record.short_description: Automated SEO and GEO platform for visibility in Google and AI assistants like ChatGPT
record.description: Sorank is a subscription platform that automates search engine optimization and generative engine optimization (GEO) for websites. It generates and publishes AI-written articles, does keyword research, and places backlinks through a credit-based exchange network of member sites. It also uses an AI agent to fix technical SEO errors. It tracks how often a brand is mentioned in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude and Grok answers, and it sends weekly SEO and GEO reports. Reviewers describe it as an alternative to hiring an SEO agency.
record.pricing_summary: Third-party reviews list Essential at $99 per site per month (about $83 per month billed annually) with 20 articles, 300 prompts analyzed and 5 backlinks. Pro is $249 per site per month with 75 articles, 1,000 prompts and 15 backlinks, and Custom pricing is on request.
features: AI agent that auto-fixes technical SEO errors
AI mention tracking across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude and Grok
use_cases: Getting a brand mentioned in ChatGPT and other AI answers
Ranking on Google and AI search on autopilot
Alternative to hiring an SEO or GEO agency
record.notes: Search usage ran out before I could open sorank.com or its pricing page. That is why confidence is below 0.6. Everything here comes from third-party pages: Capterra, ranked.ai, best-ai-seo-software.com, thatmarketingbuddy.com, saascity.io, and a September 2026 press release. These sources agree on the $99 Essential and $249 Pro prices. Capterra also lists a starting price of €99 per month and says a free trial is available. ranked.ai mentions a 3-day trial, but its text was cut off, so this is unconfirmed. Reviewers say there is no free plan. Saascity says the platform is built in Budapest and is linked to the founder's earlier agency, Ovirank. Capterra's listing URL uses the Ovirank slug. No source says Sorank was acquired or shut down. The current blurb, 'Rank first on the LLMs (AI)', is a slogan. It also leaves out that the platform covers traditional SEO as well.

record.short_description: AI voice assistant that helps French real estate agents automate follow-ups and manage prospects
record.description: SIANA is an AI assistant for real estate agents and independent agents (mandataires), offered as a mobile app. Agents dictate voice notes after calls or visits, and the app transcribes them and updates client files. It pulls in data from emails, calls, messages and the calendar, then builds a daily action plan with prioritized prospects, follow-ups and suggested messages. It also watches local listings to spot new mandate opportunities and connects to tools agents already use.
record.pricing_summary: Third-party sources list a subscription of €34.99 per month per agent (about €35 per month after an 8-day free trial), with custom quotes and volume discounts for agent networks.
features: Automated listing monitoring (pige) for mandate opportunities
use_cases: Dictate a voice note after a meeting to update a client file
Prioritize which prospects to call and when to follow up
Detect new listings and price drops to win mandates
Prepare appointments with talking points and actions
Roll out an AI copilot across an agent network
record.notes: The current blurb is accurate. The siana.app domain is live: a 2025 blog post on siana.app showed up in search, and the Google Play app 'SIANA - Assistant IA Immo' is listed under developer SIANA in Saint-Denis, France. I could not open the homepage or an official pricing page directly because the search limit ran out. Pricing comes only from third-party sites (lesoutilsimmo.fr, mysweetimmo.com), so check it against the official site. The official blog says SIANA can be tested for free, which matches the reported 8-day trial, but no permanent free tier was found. Press names Valentin Cordier (CEO) and Augustin Cousin as cofounders. Trials ran with the Propriétés-privées.com and Noovimo networks, and SIANA was a finalist at Salon RENT. Do not mix it up with Siana ApS (siana.ai, a Danish predictive-maintenance company) or Siana Cars (UAE).

record.short_description: Generative AI service that turns text prompts into images and short videos, on the web or Discord
record.description: Midjourney is a generative AI service from Midjourney, Inc., a research lab based in San Francisco. Users type text prompts to create images, and they can also turn images into videos. Most work happens on the Create page at midjourney.com, where images appear as they generate. From there, users can make subtle or strong variations, like or delete results, and sort their work on an Organize page. The service is also available through Discord. Every plan is a paid subscription that renews automatically and is metered by GPU time.
record.pricing_summary: The plans are Basic at $10/mo (3.3 Fast GPU hrs), Standard at $30/mo (15 hrs plus unlimited Relax), Pro at $60/mo (30 hrs) and Mega at $120/mo (60 hrs). Yearly billing costs $96, $288, $576 and $1,152, and extra Fast GPU time is $4/hr.
features: Create page with real-time creation feed
use_cases: Exploring and iterating on visual concepts
record.notes: Prices come from Midjourney's own help-center plan page (docs.midjourney.com/docs/plans), but the search engine's copy of that page looks old (page_age about 1,344 days). Several recent third-party articles from 2026 list the same tiers, so the numbers appear current. Third-party sites also say there is no free plan or free trial, but I did not open an official page that confirms this, so free_tier is set to false only because all docs plans are paid subscriptions. The Billing Support docs say Turbo mode is not supported in V8.1, and Wikipedia lists V8.1 as the current release. My search-tool limit ran out, so I did not open the midjourney.com homepage directly; the domain is confirmed by the official docs, Wikipedia and Midjourney's X profile. The listed URL https://www.midjourney.com/home/ was not checked, so I set official_url to the root domain. The current blurb is broadly accurate, but it leaves out video generation and the paid-only model.

record.short_description: AI audio platform for text to speech, voice cloning, transcription, voice agents and music generation
record.description: ElevenLabs is an AI audio platform. Its main product is text to speech that turns text into lifelike speech in more than 70 languages. Users can choose from a library of over 11,000 voices. The platform also includes voice cloning, voice design, speech to text, text to dialogue, music generation and tools for building voice agents. Developers can use these features through a REST API and SDKs. A low-latency Flash model supports real-time streaming. ElevenLabs also has a mobile app for creators.
features: 11,000+ AI voices and community Voice Library
Text to dialogue with multi-speaker control
Eleven v3 model with inline audio tags
use_cases: Voiceovers for TikTok, Instagram and YouTube Shorts
Content creation for creators and influencers
record.notes: The listed website is a referral or affiliate link (try.elevenlabs.io), so the official URL has been changed to https://elevenlabs.io. The current blurb is in French and the rest of the record is in English, so the blurb may need to be translated or replaced. ElevenLabs' own pages support listing it as freemium: the text-to-speech page says it is 'Free to start', and the AI voice generator page says commercial usage rights start from the Creator plan. I could not open the official pricing page at elevenlabs.io/pricing because the search limit was reached. The plan prices I found came only from third-party sites, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are left empty. Those sites list Free $0, Starter $6, Creator $22, Pro $99, Scale $299, Business $990 and a custom Enterprise plan. These numbers should be checked on elevenlabs.io/pricing before they are published. ElevenLabs' own pages give different counts for languages and voices: the app store listing says 32 languages, and the text-to-speech page mentions both 11,000+ and 17,000+ voices.

record.short_description: AI workspace that combines docs, wikis, project management and custom agents for teams
record.description: Notion is a collaborative workspace that brings note-taking, documents, wikis, task management and project management together on one platform for individuals and teams. Its project tools include tasks and sub-tasks, statuses, assignees, due dates, dependencies and granular database permissions. The company now presents Notion as an AI workspace. Teams can build custom agents, search across connected apps and automate routine work such as weekly reporting, triaging feedback and handling support tickets.
features: Status, assignee and due date fields
record.notes: The listed_website is an affiliate referral link (affiliate.notion.so), not the official site. Replace it with https://www.notion.com/. The current blurb only covers tasks and projects. Notion now presents itself more broadly as an AI workspace for docs, wikis, projects and agents. I hit the search limit before I could open notion.com/pricing, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are left empty. Third-party sites (plaky.com, costbench.com, saascrmreview.com) list Free $0, Plus $10 and Business $20 per member per month billed annually, with Enterprise at custom pricing. Some older third-party pages list lower prices. A Notion help page confirms that paid Plus and Enterprise plans exist. The free tier is supported only by third-party sources, so check it on the official pricing page. Integrations are limited to Slack, which the homepage names; third-party sources also mention Google Drive.

record.short_description: AI writing assistant that checks grammar, adjusts tone, and generates text across apps and websites
record.description: Grammarly is an AI writing assistant that checks spelling, grammar, and punctuation, shows the tone of a piece of writing, and rewrites sentences. It also generates text from AI prompts and detects plagiarism and AI-generated text. It runs in more than 1 million apps and websites, including Google Docs, Microsoft Word, and Gmail, through browser extensions and apps. It also includes Go, an AI assistant. The product is used by individuals, students, teams, and enterprises. In 2025 the parent company renamed itself Superhuman.
record.pricing_summary: Free is $0/month and includes 100 AI prompts. Pro averages $12 per member/month on the $144 annual plan, or $30 monthly or $60 quarterly, with 2,000 AI prompts, plagiarism and AI-text detection, and a free trial. Enterprise is for larger organizations.
features: Generative AI text with prompt limits by plan
Works in 1 million+ apps and websites
Go AI assistant in Chrome and Edge extensions
record.notes: Official grammarly.com pages and Grammarly's blog say that in October 2025 the company renamed itself Superhuman. The new company brings together Grammarly, Coda, Superhuman Mail, and Superhuman Go. Grammarly still runs under its own name, so status is active, not acquired. Monthly, quarterly, and annual Pro prices come from support.grammarly.com. Grammarly's support page says Pro replaced the Grammarly Business plan. No Enterprise price was published. A search tool limit stopped me before I could re-open the plans page, so the tier details come from search snippets of grammarly.com/plans and its support pages. The current blurb, 'Improve your writing with precision,' reads like a slogan. Consider replacing it with the short description.

record.short_description: No-code automation platform connecting 9,000+ apps through trigger-and-action workflows and AI tools
record.description: Zapier is a no-code automation and AI orchestration platform that connects more than 9,000 apps. Users build Zap workflows in which a trigger in one app starts one or more actions in others. The platform also includes Tables, Forms, chatbots, and the Copilot AI assistant. Zapier MCP lets AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor take actions across connected apps, and Next Gen Zaps add advanced logic and automatic recovery when workflows break.
record.pricing_summary: Zapier's pricing page lists a Free plan at $0/month with 100 tasks per month, unlimited Zaps, Tables, and Forms, and two-step Zaps. It also lists paid Professional and Team plans and an Enterprise plan sold through Contact Sales.
features: Zap workflows with triggers and actions
Next Gen Zaps with advanced logic
AI manager agent that detects and fixes issues
use_cases: Connecting AI tools to business apps
record.notes: The listed website is the Zapier ChatGPT (OpenAI) integrations subpage, not the product homepage. I changed official_url to https://zapier.com/. The current blurb is accurate but thin. Zapier now calls itself an AI orchestration platform for 9,000+ apps. The pricing page text I could see confirmed only the Free plan ($0, 100 tasks/month) and the names of the Professional, Team, and Enterprise plans. Professional at $19.99/month billed annually ($29.99 monthly) and Team at $69/month billed annually ($103.50 monthly) appear only on third-party sites (Lindy, Activepieces, Jetadmin), so I left them out of pricing_summary. I did not verify the legal company name or the founding details.

record.short_description: AI chat assistant from OpenAI for text conversations, research, coding, image and voice tasks
record.description: ChatGPT is an AI assistant made by OpenAI. Anyone can use the free version, and paid plans add more usage, more models and more features. Individuals can choose Go, Plus or Pro. Teams can use Business, which provides a shared workspace, and larger organizations can use Enterprise. Paid plans also include Codex, OpenAI's coding agent, and ChatGPT Work. OpenAI also offers Edu plans for universities and a free plan for verified U.S. K-12 teachers.
record.pricing_summary: There is a free plan at $0. Plus costs $20/month, and Pro comes in $100, $200 or $500/month tiers. Business costs $25 per user per month billed monthly or $20 billed annually (2+ users), Business Premium seats cost $125 monthly or $100 annually, and Enterprise uses custom contracts.
features: Codex coding agent (web, CLI, IDE extension, iOS)
No training on Business workspace data
use_cases: Team collaboration in a shared workspace
Education for universities and K-12 teachers
record.notes: The listed URL chat.openai.com is out of date. OpenAI's business pricing page sends consumer visitors to ChatGPT.com, so official_url is set to chatgpt.com. The current blurb 'The world's No. 1 AI tool' is a slogan that no source supports and should be replaced. Prices were confirmed on OpenAI's own sites: developers.openai.com/codex/pricing, help.openai.com (Pro tiers and Business FAQ) and openai.com/business/pricing. The Go plan is mentioned on openai.com, but its $8/month price showed up only on third-party sites (gradually.ai, nocode.mba), so it is left out of pricing_summary. The ChatGPT.com consumer pricing page was not opened. Prices may vary by country. No integrations were confirmed from official pages.

record.short_description: AI-powered customer platform and Smart CRM with marketing, sales, and service tools for growing businesses
record.description: HubSpot is a customer platform built on an AI-powered Smart CRM. It brings marketing, sales, and service teams onto one system that covers the whole customer journey. Its free CRM includes contact management, sales activity logging, communication history, and pipeline management. Paid editions of HubSpot's product hubs come in Starter, Professional, and Enterprise tiers. HubSpot also offers live chat, lead capture forms, email templates, an Outlook integration, and a marketplace of connected apps. It markets the platform to startups, small businesses, and enterprises.
record.pricing_summary: The free CRM costs $0, has no expiration date, and covers up to two users and 1,000 contacts. HubSpot's own Sales Hub pricing guide lists Starter at $9 per seat per month billed annually or $15 monthly, Professional at $90 annually or $100 monthly, and Enterprise at $150 per seat per month.
features: AI-powered contact data enrichment and duplicate detection
Sales activity logging and communication history
use_cases: Centralizing customer data for marketing, sales, and service teams
Managing leads and the sales pipeline
Capturing website leads and syncing them to the CRM
Free CRM for startups and small businesses
record.notes: I confirmed the product, the free CRM limits (2 users, 1,000 contacts, no expiration), and the features from pages on hubspot.com. I hit the search limit before I could open the official pricing page (hubspot.com/pricing), so the paid prices come from HubSpot's own blog guide to Sales Hub pricing. They only cover Sales Hub and may differ from the current official pricing page. Third-party sites list different numbers, such as Starter at $15–$20 per seat and Marketing Hub Professional at about $800–$890 per month. Check against hubspot.com/pricing before publishing. The current blurb is a slogan and should be replaced.

record.short_description: AI website builder for designing, refining, and publishing responsive professional websites with CMS and hosting
record.description: Framer is a website builder that lets teams create responsive, professional websites from a prompt, brief, blank canvas, or early idea. Its AI agents can draft pages, propose sections, write first-pass copy, and create CMS-ready content blocks. Users then refine the design on a freeform visual canvas before publishing. The platform also includes a CMS, SEO controls, analytics, and managed hosting with SSL and CDN delivery. Framer is aimed at designers, agencies, startups, and teams who build no-code websites.
features: AI agents that draft pages, sections, and copy
CMS for dynamic pages and content blocks
Managed hosting with SSL and CDN delivery
use_cases: CMS websites, directories, and content hubs
record.notes: The listed URL has an affiliate parameter (?via=artifimedia), so I normalized it to https://www.framer.com. Framer's own AI website builder page backs up the description and has a 'Get started for free' button, so I marked it freemium with a free tier. I could not open the official pricing page because the search tool hit its usage limit. The prices I did find came from third-party blogs (awesomic.com and landerlab.io). They list Free at $0, Basic at $10/month and Pro at $30/month billed yearly, and a custom Enterprise plan. Because those are not on Framer's site, I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. The current blurb, 'Create complete websites with a single sentence', overstates things. Framer describes building sites from a prompt, brief, or blank canvas and then refining them on the canvas, so I suggest a new blurb. The AI page names 'GPT 5.6' in its interface demo, but I left it out of integrations because the page doesn't clearly say it is a supported integration.

record.short_description: Visual website builder for designing, building, hosting and managing websites with a built-in CMS
record.description: Webflow is a visual website development platform for designing, building, and hosting professional websites without writing code by hand. It now calls itself a Website Experience Platform. It covers front-end design, content management through the Webflow CMS, and hosting. Other features include Webflow AI, an MCP server, Webflow Cloud app hosting, form handling, and password protection. Workspaces let teams stage sites and invite teammates or clients to work on them together. Pricing is split into Site plans and Workspace plans.
record.pricing_summary: The free Starter site plan includes a webflow.io subdomain, limited CMS, 2 static pages, 1 GB bandwidth and 50 form submissions. The Basic site plan costs $15/mo billed yearly and adds a custom domain, 300 static pages, 10 GB bandwidth and unlimited form submissions. There is also a free Starter Workspace plan.
use_cases: Simple static sites on a custom domain
record.notes: Change the listed website: it is an affiliate/partner link (webflow.partnerlinks.io), and the official site is webflow.com. I only saw part of the official pricing page in search results, which covered the Starter and Basic site plans and the Starter Workspace. A Premium plan at $25/mo billed yearly (described as replacing the CMS and Business plans) appears only on third-party sites like flowninja.com and creativecorner.studio, so I left it out of the pricing summary. Older third-party prices ($14 Basic, $23 CMS, $39 Business) look outdated. I hit the search limit before I could open the homepage or an integrations page, so I left integrations empty. The feature list comes from the official pricing page plus a third-party guide. The current blurb is a slogan and should be rewritten.

record.short_description: AI marketing platform with agents, brand voice controls, and content pipelines for marketing teams
record.description: Jasper is an AI platform built for marketing teams. It produces text such as articles, emails, ads, and social posts, and it also creates on-brand images. Its core is Jasper IQ, a layer that applies brand voice, audience profiles, style guides, and product knowledge to everything it generates. The platform includes more than 100 specialized AI agents, content pipelines, a Canvas workspace, Studio for building custom AI apps, Grid for content at scale, and tools for tracking how a brand appears in AI answer engines.
record.pricing_summary: Jasper's pricing page lists a Pro plan with monthly billing and a Business plan for larger teams. The search results from that page did not show any prices.
features: Content Pipelines for automated content lifecycle
Canvas workspace for planning and collaboration
Studio for building custom AI apps and workflows
Jasper IQ with Brand IQ and Marketing IQ
Grid for systematic content creation at scale
Image Suite and Image Pipelines for on-brand visuals
Image APIs for background removal, cleanup, upscaling
GEO and AI search visibility measurement
use_cases: Marketing content creation (articles, emails, ads, social posts)
Governed marketing in regulated industries such as financial services and healthcare
record.notes: I only got through two searches before the search tool hit its usage limit. The official homepage, platform page, and pricing page were found and are live. Jasper has moved from the general 'create all of your content' pitch to an agent-based AI platform for marketing teams, so the current blurb is out of date. The text I retrieved from jasper.ai/pricing named Pro (Monthly) and Business plans, and its metadata also mentioned a Creator plan, but it showed no prices. Several third-party sites (eesel.ai, rankable.ai, layer3labs.io, usagepricing.com) say Pro costs $69 per seat monthly or $59 per seat billed annually, that Business is custom-priced with a 12-month minimum, that there is a 7-day free trial, and that there is no free plan. These are not confirmed on Jasper's own site, so I left the numbers out of pricing_summary. I marked the tool as paid with no free tier because Jasper's Microsoft marketplace listing says the Word add-in requires a paid Jasper subscription. No acquisition or shutdown was found.

record.short_description: Generative AI go-to-market platform with chat and automated workflows for sales and marketing teams
record.description: Copy.ai is a generative AI platform for sales and marketing teams. It started as an AI copywriting tool and now calls itself a go-to-market (GTM) AI platform. It combines Chat by Copy.ai with workflows for content, research, and outreach. Fullcast, a GTM and revenue operations software company, bought Copy.ai in October 2025, and the two are building a single GTM AI platform. Copy.ai is also available as a connector in Microsoft Power Automate, Logic Apps, Power Apps, and Copilot Studio.
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit, so I could not open the copy.ai homepage or its pricing page directly. A post on the company's own blog (copy.ai/blog/fullcast-acquires-copy-a, Oct 15, 2025) and a PR Newswire release both say Fullcast bought Copy.ai. That is why status is acquired. Pricing came only from third-party review and directory sites, and they disagree. Several list a Chat plan at $29/mo ($24/mo billed annually). Some list Growth, Expansion, and Scale plans at $1,000-$3,000/mo. One says the current page shows only Chat plus custom Enterprise, with an Agents plan at $249/mo. They also disagree on whether a free plan still exists. Because none of this came from a copy.ai page, I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty, set pricing_type to unknown, and set free_tier to false. The integrations come from Microsoft's connector documentation. The current blurb ('Write captivating blogs, emails, and posts') is out of date: the product now presents itself as a GTM AI platform, not just a copywriting tool.

record.short_description: Low-code, AI-native platform for building collaborative business apps, workflows, and AI agents on relational data
record.description: Airtable is a cloud platform from a San Francisco company of the same name. Teams use it to build collaborative apps and workflows on relational data, with AI built in. It combines spreadsheet-style databases, custom interfaces, reporting, automations and embedded AI agents. It also has enterprise governance and security controls. Airtable offers templates for things like project management, content calendars and product roadmaps. It connects with tools such as Slack, Salesforce, Claude, ChatGPT and Google Drive. Mobile apps are available too.
features: Relational source of truth for apps, agents, and workflows
Custom interfaces built from your data
Reporting to measure, analyze, and share insights
Two-way integrations with Slack, Claude, Salesforce, and CMSs
record.notes: I confirmed the official site through search-result snippets of airtable.com (the homepage, /platform, /integrations, /downloads and a guides page). I didn't get to Airtable's own pricing page because I hit the search limit. The only prices I found were on third-party blogs (Adalo, Jetadmin and others), and they disagree with each other. For example, Adalo lists Team at $24/seat/month and Business at $54/seat/month, while Costbench says plans run up to $45/user/month. So I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. Setting freemium/free_tier is based on the homepage's 'Try Airtable for free' link plus third-party descriptions of a free plan. I didn't confirm it on an Airtable pricing page. Status: Wikipedia's infobox lists 'Owner: Bending Spoons', but I couldn't find any other source for an acquisition, so I kept status as active because the site is live. Please check this before publishing. The current blurb ('Automate your CMSs and use AI') is too narrow. Airtable's site describes itself as an AI-native platform for building apps, workflows and agents, and only mentions CMSs as one of many connected tools.

record.short_description: Legal AI platform for legal research, case analysis and drafting for European lawyers
record.description: Doctrine is a legal AI platform founded in Paris in 2016. It helps lawyers and in-house legal teams automate legal research, case analysis and drafting. It combines local legal data with a firm's private data. The company says the platform is GDPR compliant, certified to ISO 27001 and used by more than 27,000 legal professionals in France, Germany, Spain, Italy and Luxembourg. Its tools include a legal chatbot, a case-law research tool and a litigation file workflow.
features: Legal chatbot with sourced answers on law and case law
Doctrine Flow for automated litigation exhibit management
use_cases: Legal research for lawyers and in-house counsel
record.notes: The search tool limit was reached, so I couldn't open the doctrine.fr homepage or a pricing page directly. The facts here come from Doctrine's own newsroom (doctrine.pr.co) and blog (blog.doctrine.fr). Search results suggest the official site doesn't publish prices. Third-party directories (logiciels.pro, appvizer, societe.tech, legal-tech.fr) list a Standard plan at €159 per user per month, but I left pricing empty because none of it is on Doctrine's domain. Those sources also disagree on whether there is a free trial. Acquisition: LexisNexis and Summit Partners say RELX (owner of LexisNexis) agreed to acquire Doctrine through a put option agreement. Wikipedia says RELX acquired Doctrine, but gives the date as September 2026, which looks wrong. Because I couldn't confirm the deal had closed, I set status to active; please check again. Doctrine has also acquired Spain's Maite.ai and taken a stake in Germany's Dejure.org. The current blurb, 'Revolutionize legal analysis with Doctrine's AI,' is a slogan and should be replaced.

record.short_description: AI rendering platform that redesigns interior and exterior spaces from photos, sketches, or text prompts
record.description: Luw.ai is an AI rendering and home design platform for architects, interior designers, and homeowners. Users upload a photo, a sketch, a 3D model image, or a text prompt and get redesigned interior or exterior visuals within seconds. Tools include Interior AI, Exterior AI, virtual staging, room and floor planning, video renders, 3D generation, render enhancement, and ArchiGPT. A free plan gives daily credits with watermarked, lower-resolution output. Paid monthly plans add 4K renders without watermarks, a commercial license, team seats, and API access.
record.pricing_summary: The free plan costs $0 and gives 2 credits per day at 512×512 with a watermark. Paid plans are Pro at $19/mo for 200 renders, Max at $39/mo for 500, Ultra at $79/mo for 1,200 with API access, E1 Studio at $299/mo for 5,000 renders and 50 seats, and E2 Agency at $499/mo for 9,000 renders and 100 seats.
features: AI render from 3D model, image, or text prompt
4K output without watermark on paid plans
Team seats on Studio and Agency plans
use_cases: Visualizing home makeovers and interior renovations
Virtual staging for real estate marketing
integrations: API access (Ultra, E1, and E2 plans)
record.notes: The listed site luw.ai is live. The homepage describes interior and exterior AI design, virtual staging, and claims 3M+ designers. Pricing comes from luw.ai/pricing, which also lists the free plan's limits: no Video AI or Enhancement and basic models only. A beta.luw.ai subdomain is also live. A third-party connector directory (glama.ai) lists a Luw.ai MCP connector. It was not confirmed on luw.ai, so it is not listed as an integration. The pages I saw did not name the company or legal entity, so company is left empty. Some directory sites show older prices, such as credit packs and a $19/month starting price, that differ from the current pricing page. They were not used. The current blurb is accurate but short. A suggested replacement is the short_description.

record.short_description: iOS app that uses AI to redesign room photos in chosen styles and give decor advice
record.description: Renovy, listed on the App Store as AI Interior Design - Renovy, is an iOS app for iPhone and iPad from developer Viktor Maric. Users take a photo of a room and pick a design style, and the app's AI shows the space redesigned in that style. Users can also ask the app design questions and get personalized advice. The listing says the app is for both design beginners and decor enthusiasts. It is free to download and offers in-app purchases.
features: AI-driven room transformation from a photo
Experiment with styles, furniture, and decor elements
use_cases: Reimagining a room in a different style
Getting advice on decor and plant placement
Trying out furniture and decor ideas before buying
record.notes: I didn't find a separate official website, so official_url is empty. The listed website is an Apple App Store page, not the product's own domain. I opened the Korean App Store page for the same app ID (id6473541903). It names the developer as Viktor Maric and says the app is free with in-app purchases, but it doesn't show prices for those purchases. A directory site (theresanaiforthat.com) says paid options start at $4.99/month. I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty because that price isn't on the product's own domain. My search limit ran out before I could open the US App Store page, so I couldn't confirm the current listing or a recent update date. I marked the status active because the app still shows up in App Store results. The current blurb ('Redefine your space with style and budget') doesn't match the App Store description I saw, so it should be replaced. Don't confuse this app with Renovo (renovoapp.ai, by Pixery), which is a different AI home design app.

record.short_description: Discontinued OpenAI video model and app that turned text prompts into generated video clips
record.description: Sora was OpenAI's text-to-video model and creative app, which generated video from written prompts. The first version reached ChatGPT Plus and Pro subscribers in December 2024. Sora 2 followed in late September 2025 as a standalone app with social media features. According to OpenAI's help center, the Sora web and app experiences were discontinued on April 26, 2026. The Sora API was scheduled to shut down on September 24, 2026. Users were advised to export their content before Sora data is deleted.
features: Sora 2 standalone app with social features
record.notes: OpenAI's help center article 'What to know about the Sora discontinuation' (help.openai.com/en/articles/20001152) says the Sora web and app experiences were discontinued on April 26, 2026, and the Sora API would be discontinued on September 24, 2026. Several third-party reports say the API shutdown happened on that date. OpenAI announced the shutdown on March 24, 2026 (NBC News, NPR). I could not find current pricing on an OpenAI page because the product is discontinued, so the pricing fields are left empty. I did not open the listed URL itself. The current blurb is out of date, and the row should be marked discontinued or removed. Launch dates come from Wikipedia and news coverage.

record.short_description: Chrome extension that uses OpenAI's API to sort open browser tabs into tab groups automatically
record.description: AI Tab Group, also called AITabGroup, is a Chrome browser extension that sorts open tabs into categories. It uses OpenAI's API, and users enter their own OpenAI key in the extension's options page. One click creates the categorized tab groups. The free plan covers automatic categorization and includes a 5-day trial of premium features. A paid monthly plan adds hierarchical tabs on one page and lets users save tabs in markdown format or as bookmarks.
record.pricing_summary: Free Plan costs $0.00 and includes automatic categorization plus a 5-day trial of premium features. Monthly Plan costs $1.99/month and adds hierarchical tabs on one page, saving as markdown, and saving as bookmarks.
features: One-click creation of categorized tab groups
use_cases: Automatically grouping related tabs to tidy the browser
record.notes: Checked the official site ai-tab.net through search result text. The site shows the pricing above. The site requires users to enter their own OpenAI key, so API costs may apply on top of the plan price. I found no company or developer name on the site. A third-party directory (LogicWeb) also mentions an Annual Plan and Edge support, but I could not confirm either on the official site, so neither is included. A Chrome Web Store listing named 'AI Tabs Group' (about 100 users, 4.4 rating) has an overview line that closely matches the current blurb. However, I could not confirm it is the same product as ai-tab.net, so it is not used as a source. I hit the search limit before I could open a separate pricing or docs page. The current blurb is accurate but vague. A better version would say it is an AI Chrome extension that groups tabs using the user's OpenAI key.

record.short_description: White-label AI motion tracking SDK that counts reps, corrects form, and gives real-time feedback in fitness apps
record.description: KinesteX AI makes a white-label API and SDK for camera-based motion tracking. Fitness, weight-loss, and digital health apps use it to add guided workouts. The AI tracks movement, counts reps, estimates calories burned, corrects form, and gives real-time feedback. Companies can use ready-made workouts, plans, challenges, and AI assessments, or build their own experience on top of the tracking. Video is processed on the device. The company says the product is HIPAA and GDPR compliant and works on Android, iOS, and web.
features: Ready-made workouts, plans, challenges, and AI assessments
use_cases: Adding AI motion tracking to fitness apps
record.notes: I checked the official homepage, the docs Getting Started page, and the product FAQ on kinestex.com. The FAQ says pricing is usage-based and set to fit each use case, and the homepage pushes visitors to 'Book demo'. I didn't find any published prices or a free tier on the official site. Third-party sites give conflicting numbers (SaaSHub: freemium at $0.55 per user per month; OpenTools: from $0.15/mo; AIToolGuru and AITopTools: about $20/mo). None of them are on the product's own domain, so I left them out. The current blurb, 'Real-time user performance optimization', is vague. It's better described as an AI motion tracking SDK for fitness and health apps. My search tool hit its usage limit before I could look for a dedicated pricing page.

I could not verify this row. My web searches never returned phrases.ai: one query returned Phrase (phrase.com), an unrelated enterprise translation platform, and another returned Engram (engram.us), a different English proofreading tool. After that, the search tool hit its usage limit, and a direct request to https://phrases.ai/ returned nothing because the sandbox has no internet access. None of the results confirmed the listed site, the company, its status, pricing or features, so those fields are left empty or set to unknown. exists is set to false because I couldn't confirm the product, not because I found evidence that it doesn't exist. Do not mix this row up with Phrase (phrase.com) or Engram. The row needs to be checked again by hand on phrases.ai.

record.short_description: AI recruiter that runs voice and video candidate interviews and reaches applicants by email and SMS
record.description: Ribbon is AI recruiting software from Ribbon AI Inc. Its AI interviewer holds spoken voice and video screening interviews with job applicants 24/7, in more than 10 languages, and scores each one against the employer's rubric. It also contacts applicants by SMS, WhatsApp and email. Recruiters get scored interviews, summaries and an analytics dashboard. Ribbon is aimed at high-volume hiring in areas such as contact centers, warehouses and education. The company says it has run more than 1 million interviews.
record.pricing_summary: With annual billing, Growth is $499/mo (2 seats, 2 roles, 100 interviews/mo), Business is $999/mo (5 seats, 400 interviews/mo) and Scale is $1,999/mo (10 seats, 1,000 interviews/mo). Extra interviews cost $4.00, $3.00 or $2.50 each depending on the plan, and Enterprise is custom priced. Every paid plan offers a 7-day free trial.
use_cases: Contact center and BPO agent hiring
Hiring instructors for education and training providers
record.notes: The listed site was ribbon.cool, but search results show the product now runs at ribbon.ai, where the pricing page is. I did not directly confirm that ribbon.cool redirects there, so the directory should consider updating the URL. The current blurb is still accurate. There is a 7-day free trial but no free plan; a free practice-interview page exists for candidates only. The named ATS integrations (Workday, Lever, Greenhouse, BambooHR) and the 45 ATS figure come from a March 2025 HR Brew article. Ribbon's own pricing page says only 'ATS integrations'. Pricing on G2 is out of date compared with the official page.

record.short_description: Free AI paraphrasing tool that rewrites essays, emails, sentences, and paragraphs in seven modes
record.description: Paraphrasing.io is a web-based AI paraphrasing tool. It rewrites essays, emails, sentences, and paragraphs while keeping the original meaning. It uses natural language processing to restructure sentences, swap in synonyms, and adjust tone. Users can pick from seven modes: Simple, Reworder, Creative, Shorten, Formal, Professional, and Academic. It supports several languages. Paid plans use a credit system that also covers an article rewriter, text summarizer, plagiarism checker, AI content detector, and AI humanizer.
record.pricing_summary: There is a free registered plan at $0. Paid plans are Basic Monthly at $5/mo (2,000,000 credits), Basic Yearly at $48/yr (1,000,000 credits), Pro Monthly at $8/mo, Pro Yearly at $58/yr (1,500,000 credits), and a one-time Lifetime plan at $65.
features: 7 paraphrasing modes (Simple, Reworder, Creative, Shorten, Formal, Professional, Academic)
Multi-language support (EN, ID, DE, FR, ES and more)
500-word limit free, 1,500 for registered users, 3,000 for premium
use_cases: Improving readability and uniqueness of content
record.notes: Checked the homepage and the /plans page on paraphrasing.io. The site is live. Neither page names the operating company, so the company field is empty. Paraphrasing.io is a different product from the similarly named paraphraser.io, and many review sites mix them up. The $9.99/mo price shown on third-party sites such as toolfi.ai was not used. The current blurb mentions avoiding plagiarism. The site does offer a plagiarism checker, but the paraphraser itself is described as rewriting text while keeping its meaning. The yearly plans list fewer credits than the monthly plan, as shown on the plans page.

record.short_description: AI image upscaler and enhancer that raises image resolution and adds detail
record.description: ClarityAI is an AI image upscaling and enhancement tool. The open-source Clarity Upscaler GitHub repository by developer philz1337x calls ClarityAI.cc the paid, easy-to-use web version of the upscaler for people who do not want to run it themselves with Cog, A1111, or Replicate. A Clarity AI 'Crystal Upscaler' model, focused on facial and portrait enhancement, is also listed on fal.ai. Nothing found describes it as a social media engagement or ROI tool.
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize engagement and ROI on social media') looks wrong. Every source found describes ClarityAI/clarityai.cc as an AI image upscaler and enhancer. The search tool hit its usage limit, so I could not open clarityai.cc or any pricing page on that domain. Because of that, the status is unknown and the company name and actual prices are not confirmed. The only pricing evidence is from outside the product's site: the GitHub README calls ClarityAI.cc 'my paid version', and fal.ai lists Crystal Upscaler at $0.016 per megapixel. Under the rules, neither counts as an official pricing source. I marked pricing_type as paid based on the README, but whether there is a free tier or trial is not verified. The integrations listed (Replicate, ComfyUI, A1111, fal.ai) are platforms where the open-source model or Clarity AI models run, found on GitHub, RunComfy, and fal.ai. They are not confirmed integrations of the clarityai.cc product. Someone should check the live site by hand before publishing.

record.short_description: AI quiz maker that turns PDFs, notes, text, or topics into graded practice quizzes
record.description: QuizWhiz is a web-based AI quiz generator for studying. Users upload a PDF, paste notes, link an article, or enter a topic, and the tool creates graded practice quizzes with explanations and instant feedback. After each quiz, it identifies key skills or concepts, tracks progress on each one over time, and gives personalized study recommendations and goal-based learning paths. It supports math equations and multiple languages. A separate MCQ generator can export questions to TXT, CSV, JSON, or PDF.
record.pricing_summary: Free is $0/month with 10 credits, all question types, unlimited practice, and 1 Focused Quiz and 1 Level Up Quiz per week. Basic costs $14/month for 1,000 credits and unlimited Focused, Level Up, and Bonfire quizzes, and Pro costs $32/month for 5,000 credits plus priority support.
features: Quiz generation from topics, PDFs, text, or article links
Skill tracking across 5-10 key concepts per quiz
MCQ generator with TXT, CSV, JSON, and PDF export
use_cases: Turning lecture notes into practice quizzes
Creating quiz content from articles or textbooks
record.notes: Prices, features, and FAQ text come from the pricing section on the quizwhiz.ai homepage and the quizwhiz.ai/tools/mcq-generator page in search results. The search tool limit was reached before I could open a separate pricing, about, or terms page, so the company name is unconfirmed. The old blurb is vague. The current site is aimed at students practicing for exams more than at teachers making quizzes. Third-party directories show older pricing that no longer matches the site, such as $9 and $18 plans with runs, and a Google Classroom integration that I couldn't confirm on the official site. Don't confuse this product with quizwhizai.com, a different study app, or the QuizWhiz Laravel script sold on CodeCanyon.

record.company: Vladyslav Klymenko (App Store developer; operates as Bliss Brain)
record.short_description: iPhone app that uses AI to generate a new personalized guided meditation for each session
record.description: Bliss Brain is an iPhone meditation app from developer Vladyslav Klymenko. Instead of offering a library of pre-recorded sessions, it uses AI to write a new guided meditation each time and narrates it with a natural-sounding voice. Users can start a session with one tap based on their profile, or describe what is on their mind and pick a voice guide, length and background music. Sessions can also use Apple Health data and a photo-based emotion scan.
features: AI-generated meditation sessions that are never repeated
Emotion scan from a photo to detect stress, fatigue and anxiety
Apple Health integration using sleep, heart rate, HRV and activity
Multiple voice guides (Rebecca, Scott, Maitreya, Sanjay)
One-tap session based on profile and intentions
Fully customized sessions from a described topic
record.notes: The listed website is a Ukrainian App Store link. The current US listing is titled 'Bliss Brain・AI Meditation App' (id6468079948, developer Vladyslav Klymenko, iPhone only, Health & Fitness). The only page I opened on blissbrain.org was its privacy policy, which says Bliss Brain operates the mobile app and gives the contact vk@blissbrain.org. I did not check the homepage itself. The App Store lists the app as 'Free · In-App Purchases', and an older Lithuanian listing mentions 7 days of free full access. I left pricing_type as unknown because I could not confirm whether there is a lasting free tier. Specific subscription prices ($1.99/week, $4.99/month, $12.99 for 3 months) appear only on a third-party directory (theresanaiforthat.com), and I found no pricing page on the product's own domain, so I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. Product Hunt shows a launch in January 2024, ranked #5 of the day. The current blurb ('Optimize concentration with tailored meditations') is too narrow. The app covers focus, sleep, stress and anxiety, and generates a new AI meditation each session. I could not run a final search to confirm the homepage and in-app prices because the search limit was reached.

record.short_description: AI coding agent and chat extension for VS Code and JetBrains IDEs, with multiple model choices
record.description: CodeGPT is an AI coding assistant and agent platform that works inside VS Code and JetBrains IDEs. Its site says the agent reads the codebase, proposes a plan the user can edit, and then writes code. Users can choose Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, or open models through Ollama and LM Studio, or bring their own API keys. Other features include MCP connections, coding rules, live context tracking, and terminal commands that need user approval. Judini makes CodeGPT.
record.pricing_summary: The Free plan costs $0/mo and includes 10 interactions a day on Economy models, a $1 welcome credit, unlimited use with your own API keys, and local models. Professional costs $10/mo, or $9/mo billed annually ($108/yr), and Teams costs $30 per user per month, or $27 billed yearly ($324 per seat per year).
features: AI coding agent that plans before writing code
Bring your own API keys (15+ providers)
Local models via Ollama and LM Studio
MCP connections to APIs, docs, and databases
Pooled team credits and admin dashboard (Teams)
use_cases: Team AI coding with centralized billing
record.notes: The listed website is the official site and is up. The current blurb 'Optimize collaborative coding' is vague and should be replaced; the site presents CodeGPT as an AI coding agent and assistant for IDEs. The company link to Judini comes from Judini's GitHub (JudiniLabs), its X profile, and its PyPI package, which call CodeGPT their product. The codegpt.co pages I opened do not name Judini directly. The homepage title also mentions Visual Studio, but I did not confirm a separate Visual Studio integration, so it is not listed. Third-party sites (Capterra, SaaSworthy, agent-finder) show older or different prices ($9.99, $7.20/$8 BYOK, $19.99), so I used only the official pricing page. That page mentions team and enterprise plans, but I found no enterprise price.

record.short_description: AI interior design app that redesigns room photos and suggests matching furniture
record.description: RoomGenius is an AI interior design app from Bitfuse UG, a company based in Düsseldorf, Germany. Users upload a photo of a room and describe the look they want. The app then creates several redesigned versions in different design styles within seconds. It also suggests matching furniture with links to real products people can buy. According to the company's own site, it uses pay-as-you-go credits after some free first designs and has no required subscription. It is available on the web and as an Android app.
record.pricing_summary: Users get a few free designs and then buy credits as they go, with no required subscription. The official pages I found did not list credit prices.
features: AI-generated room redesigns from a photo
Text description of desired room look
Furniture matching with links to real products
use_cases: Room redesign inspiration for homeowners and renters
Visualizing interior styles before buying furniture
Finding furniture that matches a design
Design concepts for interior designers and real estate agents
record.notes: Search results showed the site is live, with the imprint and blog pages on room-genius.com. The imprint names the operator as Bitfuse UG (limited liability) in Düsseldorf, represented by Jannik Niemer. The listed Google Play app (com.bitfuse.roomgenius) is from the same company. The pricing details (free first designs, then pay-as-you-go credits, no required subscription) come from the company's own blog, not a pricing page. I found no actual prices on the official domain. Third-party directories give different figures, such as $20–$40, about $1.10 per unit, or $3 per unit, so I did not use them. I ran out of searches before I could open a dedicated pricing page, and I did not open the homepage itself. The current blurb is a slogan and should be replaced with a factual description.

record.short_description: AI web tool that generates illustrations in selectable styles, with upscaling, background editing, and bulk creation
record.description: IllostrationAI is a web app from Illostration that creates AI-generated illustrations. Users pick a style from a library, describe the object they want, and get a new artwork each time. The site also offers upscaling for sharper images, background removal or replacement, and editing of selected parts of an image. Users can create illustrations in bulk by uploading a CSV file, convert vector illustrations to SVG, use a Figma plugin, and share their work in a community gallery.
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize copywriting on social media') is wrong. The official homepage describes AI tools for making illustrations, not copywriting. My search tool ran out of uses, so I only saw the homepage text through a search result and could not open the site directly. I also could not find a pricing page on illostration.com. Third-party directories (10web, toolai.io, aitoolguru) say paid plans start at $4.90/mo with a free trial, but none of these sources are official, so I left pricing blank. Some directories also quote older site text saying the product was in public beta with early-access signup. I could not check whether the site is still active, so treat 'active' as unconfirmed.

record.short_description: AI-powered PDF editor for editing, converting, annotating, signing, translating and summarizing PDF documents
record.description: Wondershare PDFelement is a PDF editor from Wondershare with tools for reading, editing, converting, annotating, signing and sharing PDFs. Its AI features are powered by ChatGPT. Users can chat with a PDF and have it translated, rewritten, proofread or summarized. It can also create presentations from PDFs and check whether text was written by AI. Other tools include OCR for scanned documents, file compression and automatic bookmarks. PDFelement runs on Windows, Mac and Android and offers a free download for trial use.
record.pricing_summary: Wondershare's French site lists PDFelement from $79.99/year up to $129.99 for a lifetime license, with a limited 14-day trial. On the official store, PDFelement for Android costs $3.99/week, $19.99/year or $39.99 one-time, and PDFelement Cloud for Windows costs $8.99/month or $89.99/year.
features: Edit PDF text, images and shapes
AI translate, rewrite, proofread and summarize
Cloud storage and certificate-based digital signatures (Cloud plan)
use_cases: Summarizing and extracting key points from long PDFs
Reading and annotating PDFs on mobile
record.notes: The listed URL works. It is the French landing page for PDFelement's AI PDF editor on Wondershare's own domain, and pdf.wondershare.com is the main official site. The current blurb, 'Optimize the editing of multilingual PDF files', is too narrow. Translation is only one AI feature, and the product is a general AI-assisted PDF editor. The desktop prices ($79.99/year to $129.99 lifetime, 14-day trial) come from a Wondershare French article, not the main store page, which I could not open. Review sites list different numbers: TrustRadius matches $79.99/$129.99, while softwarefinder lists $49/$129/$159, so check the official store before publishing. The Android and Cloud prices come from pdf.wondershare.com store pages. I found a free download, trial and free-trial option but no lasting free tier.

record.short_description: AI humanizer that rewrites AI-generated text to evade AI detectors such as Turnitin and GPTZero
record.description: AIBypass is a web-based AI text humanizer. It rewrites AI-generated content so that AI detection services are less likely to flag it. Third-party listings say it runs on StealthGPT's engines and targets detectors including Turnitin, GPTZero, Copyleaks, Originality.ai and Winston AI. It is marketed for essays, emails, papers and blogs. Tracxn lists aibypass.com as an unfunded company founded in 2023. The official site could not be opened during this check, so all details come from secondary sources.
use_cases: Rewriting papers to avoid AI detection
Making blog content read as human-written
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit before I could open aibypass.com or its pricing page, so nothing here comes from the official site. Status is therefore unknown, not active. The domain and the StealthGPT link come from Tracxn (about 388 days old), There's An AI For That (about 1005 days old) and Medium posts. Pricing appears only on There's An AI For That: Standard Bypasser $9.99/mo, Enhanced Bypasser $14.99/mo and Ultimate Bypasser $24.99/mo. That listing is old and third-party, so I left pricing_summary empty and pricing_type unknown. I found no evidence of a free tier. The current blurb is broadly accurate, but the tool is marketed for beating Turnitin and similar academic-integrity checkers, which you may want to consider for a founder directory. Re-check the live site before publishing.

record.short_description: Free online article rewriter with five rewriting modes, including word changer, paragraph rewriter and plagiarism remover
record.description: ArticleRewriter.net is a web-based tool that rewrites text, from single sentences and paragraphs to full essays and articles. Users choose from five modes: Word Changer, Sentence Rewriter, Plagiarism Remover, AI Rewriter and Paragraph Rewriter. The site says the tool keeps the original meaning while changing the wording, can be used without registering, and supports up to 10 languages. A free version is available, and paid options unlock premium modes and higher word limits. The site also offers paraphrasing, plagiarism checking, grammar checking and summarizing tools.
record.notes: I checked the official homepage through search results. It describes the pricing as 'Free (& Paid)', and the input box shows 'Only first 1500 words!' with an 'Upgrade Now' prompt. Some modes are marked PREMIUM. The homepage links to a Pricing page, but I could not open it because I hit the search tool's usage limit, so I left the tier prices empty. One third-party directory (theresanaiforthat) lists paid options starting at $7, but I did not confirm this on the product's own site. G2 lists the headquarters as Faisalabad, Pakistan, but I could not find a legal company name, so the company field is empty. The current blurb is broadly accurate, though it reads more like a slogan.

record.short_description: Free open directory comparing LLM pricing, benchmarks, AI datasets, models, MCP servers, agent skills and jobs
record.description: Metatext is a free, open directory that gathers information about the AI ecosystem in one place. Users can compare large language models by input and output cost, context window and provider, and see benchmark scores next to the price per million tokens. The site also lists AI datasets, models, MCP servers, agent skills and AI job openings. It is aimed at AI researchers, engineers and builders. It requires no account and says its data is updated continuously.
record.pricing_summary: Metatext's terms of service say the public directory is free and requires no account. The site's homepage also calls it free and open.
features: LLM pricing comparison by input/output cost, context window and provider
Benchmark leaderboards paired with cost per million tokens
use_cases: Choosing which LLM to ship based on cost versus performance
Finding datasets to train or evaluate on
Finding MCP servers or agent skills to use with Claude or Cursor
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimizing copywriting to boost visibility') is wrong. I found nothing about copywriting. The metatext.ai homepage now describes the product as a free, open directory of AI models, LLM pricing, benchmarks, datasets, MCP servers, agent skills and jobs. Older third-party listings (SourceForge, Slashdot, ToolMage, OpenTools) describe an earlier no-code NLP model-building platform with a $35/mo Starter plan and a $295/mo Pro plan. I did not confirm those prices on the official site, and an AppSumo reviewer said that earlier service seemed discontinued. An eesel.ai review says the paid tiers on the site's pricing page are template placeholders and that a paid 'Metatext Hub' is in early access. I could not open a metatext.ai pricing page to check this, so I left Hub pricing out. The terms of service refer to the service as 'metatext.io' even though the page is on metatext.ai. My search tool hit its usage limit before I could do more checks, so these findings come from search-result snippets of the homepage and terms pages, not full page reads.

record.short_description: iPhone education app with camera scavenger hunt and matching games that teach kids the ABCs
record.description: ABC Finder is an iPhone education app from developer Todd Hamilton that helps kids learn their ABCs. It has two games. In the camera game, children go on a scavenger hunt for real-world objects, and the app uses real-time AI image recognition to detect them. When an object is found, the app teaches its first letter and the sound that letter makes. The matching game is simpler and suits younger children. Both games use 3D emojis and calm music.
record.pricing_summary: The app is free to download. A Full Version in-app purchase costs $1.99.
features: Real-time AI image recognition of objects
Teaches first letter and letter sound
record.notes: I didn't find a separate product website, so the official_url and pricing source are the developer's App Store listing on apple.com, not the product's own domain. The listing names Todd Hamilton as the developer. It says the app needs iOS 17.0 or later and also supports visionOS 1.0, is rated 4+, and is in the Education category. My search found a third-party directory page (theresanaiforthat.com), but I didn't use it for any facts. The current blurb is accurate but vague. A better one would mention the AI camera scavenger hunt and the matching game. I hit a search limit, so I couldn't run more searches for a standalone site.

record.short_description: AI copywriting feature in Klaviyo that generates SMS campaign message options from brief inputs
record.description: Klaviyo SMS Assistant is an AI-powered copywriting feature built into Klaviyo's SMS campaign editor. Klaviyo launched it in November 2022. Users pick a campaign type (Promotion, Product Announcement, Newsletter, or Other), enter an optional product name and a short campaign description, and the assistant writes three SMS message options. Klaviyo says the tool is trained to follow mobile carrier rules and avoid forbidden content. Marketers can use a generated message, edit it, or treat it as a starting point for their own copy.
features: Four campaign types: Promotion, Product Announcement, Newsletter, Other
Optional product name and brief campaign description as inputs
Trained to follow mobile carrier regulations and avoid forbidden content
Opened from the star icon in the SMS message content field
use_cases: Helping marketers new to SMS write compliant messages
record.notes: Klaviyo's Nov 8, 2022 newsroom post, its blog post (klaviyo.com/blog/sms-assistant), and a help center article (help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/10039353259163) confirm the feature exists. The help article, updated about a year ago, still explains how to use it, so the status is active. I couldn't open the listed URL (/product/whats-new/sms-assistant) because I hit the search limit, so I used the blog post as official_url. The assistant is a feature inside Klaviyo, not a standalone product, and none of the Klaviyo pages I opened give a separate price for it. Klaviyo's plan prices, including a free plan for up to 250 active profiles, came only from third-party review sites (emailtooltester, Omnisend, Flowium, Plivo, FirstPier). I didn't open klaviyo.com/pricing, so pricing is left empty and free_tier is false. I also couldn't check whether the assistant is included on the free plan. The current blurb is accurate. Klaviyo's own SMS templates page describes the assistant as producing 'high-performing, on-brand copy in seconds.'

record.short_description: Collaborative AI canvas for drafting and organizing work with context-connected prompts and real-time teamwork
record.description: lxi.ai is a web-based canvas for working with AI on iterative tasks such as writing research papers, planning trips, or organizing thoughts. Instead of a linear chat, users connect relevant pieces of information to give the AI context, generate sections at a time, and revise outputs themselves. Generated content can be dragged onto the canvas, function nodes apply one prompt across multiple inputs, and teammates can collaborate on a shared canvas in real time. The site states the product is in beta.
features: Store generated content on the canvas via drag and drop
Function node applies the same prompt across multiple inputs
Connect relevant information to give AI context
Draft sections with AI and revise yourself
record.notes: I checked the official site only through the search engine's indexed copy of lxi.ai, not by loading the page live. That copy describes an AI collaboration canvas that is 'currently in beta testing', with early-access sign-up and the contact hello@lxi.ai. It does not name a company or show any pricing, so pricing_type is unknown and free_tier is false. Directory sites (SaaSworthy, There's An AI For That, LogicWeb, ToolAI, aitoolguru) describe an older version: a GPT-based tool that answered questions from your documents, with a 14-day free trial and usage-based pricing ($0.10 per MB per month and $0.0025 per question). Because those prices don't appear on lxi.ai, I left them out. The product appears to have pivoted. Status is active only because the indexed site is up; it is still in beta. The current blurb, 'Streamline drafting and planning', loosely matches, but 'collaborative AI canvas' describes the product more accurately. Not to be confused with laxi.ai, the LXI instrumentation standard, or LXIcorp.

record.short_description: AI music generator for royalty-free tracks from text or image prompts, plus a developer API
record.description: Mubert is an AI music platform that generates royalty-free soundtracks of a chosen length, mood and style from text prompts, images, genres or artist sample packs. Mubert Render is aimed at creators making videos, podcasts and other content. Mubert API lets developers add music generation and streaming to apps, games, AI agents and live streams. Through Mubert Studio, musicians can contribute loops, riffs and sample packs and get paid when their sounds are used.
record.pricing_summary: Mubert Render has a free non-commercial Ambassador plan (25 tracks/month, 5 downloads), Creator at $14/month ($11.69/month billed annually, non-commercial), Pro at $39/month ($32.49/month billed annually, commercial use) and Business at $199/month ($149.29/month billed annually). API plans are separate and start at $49/month for Build (100 generations), with Startup at $199/month and Startup+ at $499/month.
features: Track generation from artist sample packs
Custom track duration up to 25 min
200+ moods and themes in the API
use_cases: Background music for YouTube, TikTok, podcasts and video
Music generator for user-generated content apps
Musicians earning money from loops and sample packs through Mubert Studio
record.notes: The listed URL is the official pricing page but carries an affiliate parameter (?via=essor). The clean URL is https://mubert.com/render/pricing. The prices come from search-result snippets of mubert.com pages, not from pages I loaded directly. The API page snippets were partly garbled: Startup showed both $199 and $249, and Build showed $49 and $99. An official Mubert blog post confirms Build/Trial at $49, Startup at $199 and Startup+ at $499 per month, so re-check the API prices before publishing. Render's Creator plan is non-commercial only; commercial use needs Pro or Business. The current blurb, 'Generate music, use it and earn money', is vague. The earning part refers to Mubert Studio, which pays contributing musicians, not to users of the generated tracks. Suggested replacement: 'AI music generator for royalty-free tracks from text or image prompts, plus a developer API'. I found no acquisition or shutdown notice.

record.short_description: AI client intelligence platform that turns client calls, emails and chats into next-step actions
record.description: Kaizan is a London-based AI platform for client service, account management and customer success teams. It records and summarises client meetings, emails and chats in one place. It scores each account with its CARE framework, which covers client sentiment, activity, relationship strength and expansion. Its AI Helpers write follow-ups and proposals for the team to approve, warn about revenue at risk, and spot upsell and cross-sell openings. Clients are compared against benchmarks built from more than 11M client service signals.
record.pricing_summary: After a free 14-day pilot, Starter costs £99 per client per month with at least 10 clients, Growth costs £119 per client per month with at least 25 clients, and Enterprise is priced on request. All plans are in GBP on an annual contract and include unlimited users.
features: Call, email and chat capture and summaries
Follow-ups and replies drafted for approval
use_cases: Client retention and churn risk detection
record.notes: The listed blurb, 'Optimize real-time customer engagement', is vague and should be replaced. The site now describes Kaizan as client intelligence and customer success software for agencies, professional services firms and client service teams. The free 14-day pilot is a trial, not a free plan, so free_tier is false and the pricing type is paid. Third-party sites show older or different prices, such as £499 a month for Platform Access, £49 per user per month, and Team/Growth/Scale plans from £3,495 a month. Those were not used because they conflict with the official pricing page. The pricing page only says 'standard chat and CRM integrations' without naming any. A Kaizan blog post says it connects to about 1,000 tools through Nango and Composio, which are integration services, so no specific integrations are listed. Funding news reports a £2.5M round led by Pembroke VCT. No acquisition or shutdown was found. The search tool limit was reached before an integrations page could be checked.

record.short_description: AI logo maker and brand kit tool that generates logos, branded templates, and websites for small businesses
record.description: Looka is an AI-powered logo maker and brand identity tool. Users enter a business name and pick styles they like. The AI then generates logo concepts, which users can edit by changing colors, fonts, icons, and layout. Designing is free, and payment is needed to download files. Looka also sells a Brand Kit with over 300 branded templates for social media, business cards, email signatures, letterheads, and invoices, plus brand guidelines. A higher tier adds an AI-generated website.
features: AI logo generation from business name and style preferences
Logo editor for colors, fonts, icons, and layout
High-resolution and vector logo files (PNG, EPS, SVG, PDF)
Brand Kit with 300+ brand asset templates
AI-generated website with drag-and-drop builder, hosting, SSL, and custom domain support
use_cases: Creating a first logo without hiring a designer
Building a brand identity for a small business
Making branded social media templates, business cards, and email signatures
record.notes: The listed website is an affiliate link (looka.partnerlinks.io), not the official site. Swap it for https://looka.com. My searches hit a tool limit before I could open any page on looka.com, so every detail here comes from third-party reviews, and the official URL and active status are not confirmed on the site itself. I set status to active only because several recent reviews describe the product as live. Pricing seen on review sites only, so pricing_summary is left blank: Basic Logo $20 one-time, Premium Logo $65 one-time, Brand Kit $96/year, Brand Kit Web $129/year. One site lists Brand Kit Web at $192/year, and another lists a Brand Kit Web Ecommerce tier at $299/year. The sources disagree on whether there is a free tier: designing is free, but downloading needs payment. That is why free_tier is false and pricing_type is paid. The current blurb reads like a slogan, so the short_description replaces it. Check pricing and features on looka.com/pricing before publishing.

record.short_description: AI app that swaps fashion models and backgrounds in apparel product photos for Shopify stores
record.description: OnModel is an AI fashion model app for apparel and fashion ecommerce stores. It lets sellers put clothing on AI-generated models without a photoshoot. Users can swap models by gender, ethnicity, age, expression and makeup, and generate faces for cropped images. The goal is to replace generic supplier photos with unique ones and to show models that match a store's customers. It is available as a web app and as a Shopify app aimed at dropshippers, wholesalers and print-on-demand stores.
features: Change models by gender, ethnicity, age, expression and makeup
use_cases: Upgrading apparel product photos without photoshoots
Matching models to a target audience
record.notes: The official site loads at onmodel.ai, and the listed www URL points to the same domain. Its homepage confirms AI model swapping for apparel stores, a web app and a Shopify install. The current blurb is vague: the product is specifically AI model swapping for clothing photos. I found no prices on onmodel.ai, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are empty. The free tier comes from the official Shopify App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/model-swap), which says a free plan is available. Future Tools also lists it as freemium. Background changing and batch jobs are only described on third-party sites, not on pages I opened, so I left them out of features. I couldn't confirm the legal company name. G2 lists the seller only as OnModel.ai. My search limit ran out before I could open a pricing or docs page.

record.short_description: AI-powered academic search engine for finding, summarizing, and tracking scientific papers across disciplines
record.description: Semantic Scholar is a research tool for scientific literature developed by the nonprofit Allen Institute for AI and publicly released in 2015. It uses natural language processing to help researchers find relevant papers. It provides TLDR summaries for nearly 60 million papers in computer science, biology, and medicine. Users can save papers in library folders and turn on AI-powered Research Feeds that recommend new papers by email. Researchers can also claim their author pages and see influential citations.
features: AI-powered Research Feeds with paper recommendations
Claimable author pages with recent citations
use_cases: Screening papers for relevance before reading
Staying up to date with new research in a field
record.notes: I confirmed the features on the official product page (semanticscholar.org/product). I did not open a pricing page on semanticscholar.org. A McMaster University library guide calls the tool free, and several directory and review sites also describe the tool and its API as free. Because of that, pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are empty. A third-party article says API keys are now required and that use above a threshold may cost money. I could not check that on the official API pages. Wikipedia names Ai2 as the creator and gives the launch date as November 2, 2015. The current blurb is close to the product's own wording.

record.short_description: AI sales platform offering conversation intelligence, real-time call guidance, automated QA and revenue intelligence
record.description: Salesken is an AI platform for sales teams. It analyzes sales conversations to show deal risks, buyer intent and next-best actions. Its products include Quality Assurance AI, which scores every call and flags compliance risks, and an AI Sales Assistant that gives reps live prompts during calls. It also offers Revenue Intelligence AI for pipeline visibility and deal predictions, plus a meeting notetaker. Salesken logs transcripts, summaries and action items into the CRM and supports multiple languages.
features: Quality Assurance AI evaluating 100% of conversations
Revenue Intelligence AI with deal outcome predictions
CRM enrichment with auto-logged transcripts, summaries and action items
Real-time compliance and objection risk flagging
Automated email drafting and smart follow-ups
use_cases: Automating call QA and compliance monitoring
Pipeline visibility and deal forecasting for sales leaders
Real-time objection handling during sales calls
Reducing CRM data entry for reps
record.notes: The search results showed content from the official homepage and product pages, and they confirm the site is live. I found no pricing page on salesken.ai. Capterra, GetApp and Software Advice list a $99/month flat-rate plan with a free trial, and a ZoomInfo review says pricing is by custom quote. Because those are third-party sites, pricing is left empty here. Salesforce and Freshsales come from Salesken's own blog. Salesloft comes from the Salesloft Marketplace listing. ZoomInfo also names HubSpot and Zoho, but I left those out because they are third-party claims. The current blurb is accurate but incomplete: the product also does real-time call guidance, QA automation and revenue intelligence. Search tool limits stopped me from opening a dedicated integrations or pricing page.

record.short_description: AI web platform that turns selfies into professional headshots, artistic profile pictures, and interior design visuals
record.description: Rupa.AI is an Indonesian web platform that uses generative AI to transform ordinary photos. Users upload selfies to get artistic profile pictures, professional headshots for CVs and LinkedIn, Korean-style studio portraits, and AI passport photos. The platform also offers Dreamspace, which redesigns a room from an uploaded photo. According to its site, uploaded photos are used to train the user's model and are deleted within 72 hours. Refunds are not offered because of the computing cost of rendering.
features: AI headshot for professional and LinkedIn photos
use_cases: Professional profile photos for CVs and LinkedIn
Artistic profile pictures for social media
Professional portrait photography without visiting a studio
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimizing content management on social networks') is wrong. Rupa.ai is an AI photo transformation and headshot tool, not a social media content management tool, so the blurb should be replaced. I hit the search tool's usage limit, so I could not open the rupa.ai homepage or a pricing page directly. The details here come from search-result text: a page on Rupa's own domain (web.rupa.ai/en/enhance-your-photos-with-the-power-of-ai/, which covers photo deletion, the no-refund policy, and an Indonesian +62 contact number), the company's LinkedIn page, its TikTok account, and a Kompas article from December 2024. I found no prices on Rupa's own domain. Third-party directories disagree on pricing: SpotSaaS and SaaSworthy list Basic $9.99, Premium $15.99 and Premium+ $19.99. Dataconomy says per-product payments start at Rp 1.000 with limited free trials. AIChief lists a free tier and a $19/month Pro plan. Because these conflict and none is on Rupa's site, I left pricing empty or marked unknown. Several features (Corporate Headshot, Magicbooth, Pas Foto AI, the Aruna AI WhatsApp assistant) and the WhatsApp integration come only from directory sites. I marked the status active because recent sources show the product is still promoted, not because I loaded the site.
