Don't confuse this with Rupa Health (rupahealth.com, lab testing) or an unrelated 'Rupa' tool that helps creators sell digital products.

record.short_description: VR suite for sculpting, rigging and animating 3D models with a headset
record.description: Masterpiece Studio is a 3D content creation suite for virtual reality from the company formerly known as MasterpieceVR. It brings together Masterpiece Creator, which handles clay and mesh sculpting, and Masterpiece Motion, which handles rigging, skinning, posing and applying pre-made animations. Users can build and animate models by hand while wearing a VR headset. The company says the tool is meant to make 3D creation easier for people without 3D modeling experience. Its Pro edition targets animation and game content.
use_cases: 3D creation for creators without modeling experience
Concepting, sculpting and animating characters in VR
record.notes: My search tool hit its usage limit, so I could not open masterpiecestudio.com or a pricing page. The listed URL is kept because SourceForge, Slashdot and AIIndigo all give it as the product website, but I have not confirmed the site is up. Status is therefore unknown. The company's blog about Masterpiece Studio is now hosted on masterpiecex.com, which suggests the company has rebranded or moved toward Masterpiece X, a generative AI 3D product. I found no page saying Masterpiece Studio was discontinued or acquired. Road to VR reported free and paid commercial licenses at launch, and SourceForge lists a price from $19.95 per month with a free trial. Neither source is on the product's own domain, so I left pricing blank. Auganix (April 2021) reported the release of Masterpiece Studio Pro, with Jonathan Gagne as CEO. The current blurb is vague. A better one would mention that the tool is VR-based and covers sculpting and animation. Watch for unrelated businesses with similar names (themasterpiecestudio.com, masterpiecestudioz.com).

record.short_description: AI tool that generates user personas from basic project and target audience information
record.description: PersonaGen is an AI-based user persona generator listed at personagen.app. Third-party AI tool directories say users enter basic project details such as name, description, industry and keywords, and the tool analyzes the target audience to produce user personas. These listings mention support for multiple projects, target audience analysis and feature-wise personas. They also say personas can be downloaded as PDFs or shared online. The official site could not be opened during verification, so these details are unconfirmed.
features: PDF download and online sharing of personas
use_cases: Creating user personas for websites, mobile apps or other products
Understanding a target audience for data-driven decisions
record.notes: I hit the search tool limit before I could open personagen.app or any pricing page on its domain. Every detail above comes from third-party directories (domore.ai, which links to https://personagen.app/, plus findmyaitool.com, futuretools.io, toolai.io, creati.ai and aicenter.ai). I left status as unknown because I could not confirm the site is up. The current blurb ('Optimizing content strategies on social networks') does not match how any source describes the product. All of them call it an AI user persona generator, so the blurb should be rewritten. Pricing is not confirmed. Futuretools lists it as Free, toolai.io shows a price of 0, and aicenter.ai says 'Open Source' and 'Waitlist'. None of these are on the product's own domain, so I did not record them. There are several similarly named products that may be unrelated: personagen.net ('Custom User Personas in minutes', which offers free beta access), personagen.dev (a synthetic persona API) and an academic PersonaGen research tool (arXiv 2307.00390). I could not confirm whether personagen.net is the same product. The company name was not found.

record.short_description: AI website chatbot and sales agent that qualifies, converts, and follows up with leads
record.description: MagicForm.AI is an AI chatbot that businesses embed on their websites to act as a sales and support agent. It learns about a business by scanning its website and any documents uploaded to it. It then answers visitor questions, qualifies leads, and follows up with them around the clock. Users can customize the agent's introduction, personality, and suggested questions, add better answers to past chats, and watch usage statistics. Setup is done by pasting an embed code into the site.
record.pricing_summary: The Starter plan is $49/month and includes 500 messages, 1 AI agent, a website embed code, email notifications, and GPT-4o. The Pro plan is listed at $149/month next to a $99 figure and includes unlimited AI agents ($10/agent above 20) and unlimited team seats. Both plans offer a 14-day free trial.
features: Learns by scanning your website and uploaded documents
Suggested questions you can reorder or add to
Human handoff and advanced APIs on custom plans
use_cases: Customer support FAQs, order updates, and shipping questions
record.notes: The official site is up at magicform.ai. The listed URL includes an affiliate parameter (?via=thibault), so the clean URL is used instead. The pricing comes from a search-result snippet of the magicform.ai homepage, which shows a © 2024 footer. I couldn't open a dedicated pricing page because the search tool limit was reached. The Pro price is unclear: it shows both $99 and $149/mon, possibly a struck-through price. Third-party directories (toolsforhumans.ai) mention a free Starter plan with 50 conversations, $99 Pro, and CRM integrations. These don't match the official site, so they weren't used. The current blurb is a slogan and should be replaced. Don't confuse this with magicform.app, an unrelated Google Forms add-on. Crunchbase lists the company under the slug 'titan-x', but I didn't confirm the legal entity name.

record.short_description: OCR API that pulls structured data from receipt and invoice images
record.description: ReceiptUp is described by third-party sources as a receipt OCR API. It extracts data from images of receipts and invoices, including total amounts, transaction dates, tax details, and merchant information, and turns it into structured digital data. Directory listings say it supports multiple languages and can extract data by region. It is aimed at automating expense tracking, bookkeeping, and other financial workflows. The official website could not be opened to confirm these details.
features: Extracts totals, dates, tax data, and merchant details
record.notes: I could not open or confirm the listed site (https://www.receiptup.com/). A direct fetch from the sandbox returned nothing, and none of the search results came from the official domain. Everything in this record comes from third-party pages: Tracxn, TAAFT, creati.ai, bai.tools, aikaptan, and Cloudbooklet. Tracxn calls ReceiptUp an unfunded OCR API platform for turning receipts into digital data. The only prices I found were on directory sites, and they don't match each other: TAAFT says 'Free + from $33.00/mo' and Cloudbooklet says freemium starting at $39. Because neither comes from the product's own domain, I left pricing empty and marked the free tier as unconfirmed. The TAAFT listing is about 971 days old. I found no page saying the product was discontinued or acquired, so status is unknown. The current blurb broadly matches the third-party descriptions, but it's vague. These sources describe a receipt and invoice OCR API, not general document digitization.

record.short_description: AI business builder that generates websites and offers marketing, SEO, and CRM tools for entrepreneurs
record.description: Durable is an AI business builder for independent entrepreneurs and small business owners. Its website builder uses AI to generate a site with copy and images in under 30 seconds. Users can then customize the design. The platform includes hosting, SSL certificates, and basic CRM functionality. It also offers Discoverability tools for SEO and GEO, an AI Studio that creates logos, social posts, posters, and website images, and an AI Partner assistant.
features: AI website generation in under 30 seconds
AI Studio for logos, social media posts, posters, and website images
use_cases: Getting a small business online quickly
Building a website without coding or design skills
Generating marketing images and social posts
record.notes: The listed URL is durable.co. Durable's own blog and launch post are now on durable.com, and I used that as the official URL. I could not confirm that durable.co redirects there. I did not open an official pricing page because I ran out of searches. A Durable blog post on durable.com, about 283 days old, says pricing 'starts at $15/month', but it is not a pricing page. Third-party sites disagree with each other. B12 and Software Finder list Starter $15 and Business $25, plus a top tier of $95 (Mogul) or $99 (Scale). Seldonframe lists Free, Launch $25/mo ($22/mo annual), and Grow $49/mo ($41/mo annual). B12 and Seldonframe both report a free plan, but no official page confirmed it, so pricing_type is unknown and free_tier is false. Invoicing appears only on third-party reviews (Cybernews, B12), not on the official pages I saw. I have left it out of features, and the current blurb's invoicing claim should be checked. The blurb also predates the rebrand as a 'complete AI business builder' with Discoverability, AI Studio, and AI Partner.

record.short_description: AI-native property management system for short-term rental operators and boutique hotel managers
record.description: Jurny is an AI-native property management system for hospitality, built for short-term rental operators, property management companies, and boutique hotels. It runs on its own platform, jOS. NIA, its Network of Intelligent Agents, handles guest messaging, reservations, dynamic pricing, upsells, reviews, and maintenance coordination. Other tools include a unified AI inbox, smart-lock self-check-in, branded digital guidebooks, a custom guest app, and branded booking websites. Jurny connects with OTAs such as Airbnb, Vrbo, and Expedia.
record.pricing_summary: The required jOS AI base plan costs $19.00 per unit per month when billed monthly, or $13.30 per unit per month when billed annually (30% off). Add-on modules are offered on top of the base plan.
features: NIA multi-agent AI (communication, pricing intelligence, concierge & upsells, review management, data science)
use_cases: Scaling a rental portfolio without adding staff
Reducing reliance on OTAs through direct bookings
record.notes: The current blurb ('AI for the management of your real estate assets') is too broad. Jurny is specifically a hospitality and short-term rental PMS, not general real estate asset management. The base-plan price comes from Jurny's official STR pricing page. Add-on prices (e.g., AI-Powered PMS $29, Smart Device Hub $4/unit/month) appeared only on third-party directories (SoftwareFinder, GetApp), so they were left out. Capterra and Software Advice describe 'custom pricing' for operators with 15–500+ units, which may mean pricing differs by portfolio size. Capterra and Software Advice AU say there is no free version or free trial. The integrations list comes from a 2023 Business Wire partnership release and a Turno blog post. A PrivCo page showed M&A entries that appear to be placeholder data about unrelated companies, so no acquisition is recorded. Search tool limits prevented opening further official docs pages.

record.short_description: AI-powered site search and shopping assistant chat for e-commerce stores and enterprise websites
record.description: Zevi is an AI-driven site search and discovery platform for online stores and enterprise websites. It combines neural search, which interprets shopper intent, with a ChatGPT-like shopping assistant that answers product inquiries. Plans include AI spell and synonym checking, trending products and suggestions, campaign redirection, merchandising controls, review- and revenue-based ranking, and search analytics. Higher tiers add vernacular and mixed-language search. The company says the product is available for enterprises and Shopify stores.
record.pricing_summary: The official pricing page lists a $0/mo plan (up to 25 products/records, 7 days of analytics), Basic at $29/mo (500 records), Premium at $99/mo (1,000 records), Pro at $499/mo (1,000+ records), and a custom Enterprise tier. Yearly billing saves up to 15%.
use_cases: Increasing site search conversions and sales
Answering shopper inquiries via chat assistant
record.notes: The homepage and pricing details come from search-indexed copies of zevi.ai, which had no dates. I could not load the live site directly, and my search quota ran out before I could confirm it is up. One directory (chatableapps.com) says zevi.ai has been unreachable in weekly checks and moved it to its graveyard on Sep 14, 2026. Another (tooldirectory.ai) lists a 'Zevi' workflow automation tool as shut down in April 2025, which may be a different product. I found no official page saying the product was discontinued or acquired, so status is unknown, not shutdown. Some third-party sites show older or different prices ($16/$49/$250 tiers, or 'starts at $29'). I ignored those. The current blurb is roughly accurate, but it skips the core product, which is AI site search plus a shopping assistant chat for e-commerce. Recheck the site before publishing.

record.short_description: AI design tool for making logos, t-shirts, stickers, posters, and social media graphics from text prompts
record.description: Playground is an AI graphic design studio. Users can type a request or start from templates in 24 categories to make logos, t-shirt graphics, stickers, posters, wallpapers, cards, and social media posts. Its editing tools include style swap, object removal, mockups, and smart layers, and every edit can be undone. Playground offers several image models, including its own Playground v3 and Muse Image as well as GPT Image 2, Nano Banana, and Seedream. It runs on the web and has an iOS app.
record.pricing_summary: Free plan: up to 10 images every 3 hours plus 3 monthly generations on premium models. Pro: $15/mo, or $12/mo billed annually ($144/yr), with up to 75 images every 3 hours, 150 monthly credits, editing up to 2K, and a commercial license. A Pro Plus tier is also listed.
features: AI image editing, resizing, and extending up to 2048×2048
SVG vector export with built-in vector editor
Commercial use license on paid plans
Multiple AI models in one place
use_cases: SVG cut files for cutting machines
record.notes: The homepage and pricing page at playgroundai.com are live and up to date. They brand the product as 'Playground' and pitch it as an AI design studio for logos, merch, and posters. The pricing page names a Pro Plus tier, but its price did not appear in the page content I saw. Third-party sites say Pro Plus costs $45/mo, or $36/mo billed annually, so I left that price out. A third-party review says the product rebranded from 'Playground AI' to 'Playground' in August 2024 and moved to playground.com. The company's X and Hugging Face profiles list playground.com, so the directory URL could be updated, but playgroundai.com still serves the site. The company name 'AI Playground, Inc.' comes from the Apple App Store listing, not the official site. The integrations listed are AI models built into the product, not outside app integrations. The current blurb is a slogan. A more factual option: 'AI design tool for logos, t-shirts, stickers, posters, and social media graphics'. A tool limit stopped further searches.

record.short_description: AI dating assistant that wrote pickup lines, bios and messages for dating app users
record.description: Meet Millie was an AI-powered web tool for people using dating apps such as Tinder. Users entered details about themselves and their match. The tool then wrote personalized pickup lines, custom poems, profile bios and suggested replies. It also suggested date activities based on the user's city and picked the user's best-performing profile photos. Its stated aim was to raise response rates and lead to deeper conversations. It launched around January 2023 and appears to be offline now.
features: Date ideas based on city location
use_cases: Breaking the ice on dating apps
Getting more responses and deeper conversations with matches
record.notes: meetmillie.app no longer hosts the AI tool. It now runs a dating-advice blog called 'Meet Millie – Real advice for real connections' (posts on first dates, heartbreak recovery and similar topics), with no product, app or pricing pages. Because the domain no longer hosts the original product, I left official_url empty. Everything about the original tool comes from third-party directories: futuretools.io, toolhunter.ai, aiawesome.com, videosdk.live and dang.ai. Dang.ai says Meet Millie was 'marked as closed, shutdown or acquired' and has an article asking why MeetMillie.app shut down. That is the basis for the shutdown status, but it is a third-party claim and no official shutdown notice was found. The directories disagree on pricing: futuretools and toolhunter say Paid, dang.ai says Freemium with a free trial, and none give prices. No pricing appears on the product's own domain, so pricing is unknown. The current blurb broadly matches the original tool, but the listing should be removed or marked discontinued. Note that meetmillie.ai is an unrelated AI social media manager product. My search budget ran out before more checks were possible.

record.company: Windsurf (formerly Codeium, previously Exafunction); acquired by Cognition
record.short_description: AI-native code editor with an agent called Cascade, formerly sold as the Codeium code-completion extension
record.description: Windsurf is an AI-native code editor first released by Codeium in November 2024. It is built around Cascade, an AI agent that can edit several files at once, run terminal commands, and use context from the whole codebase. The editor is a fork of VS Code and runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Codeium started as a free AI code-completion extension for many IDEs. In April 2025 the company renamed itself Windsurf, and Cognition then agreed to buy it.
use_cases: Agentic code editing from natural-language instructions
record.notes: This row is out of date. Codeium renamed itself Windsurf in April 2025 (Neowin and other sources). Cognition's own blog (cognition.com/blog/windsurf, July 14, 2025) says it signed a definitive agreement to buy Windsurf, including its product, IP, and trademark. Status is set to acquired because that page names the buyer. I didn't open windsurf.com or codeium.com myself. Third-party articles say windsurf.com/pricing now redirects to Devin's pricing page and that the product is now called 'Devin Desktop', but no official page I saw confirms this. Every price I found came from third-party blogs (they cite Free $0, Pro $20/mo, Max $200/mo, Teams $80/mo plus $40 per seat, and custom Enterprise), so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are left empty. pricing_type is unknown and free_tier is false for the same reason, not because there's no free plan. I ran out of search calls before I could open the official pricing page. Suggested changes: rename the listing to Windsurf, update the website, and replace the blurb 'The free toolkit for developers.'

record.short_description: AI platform for building apps, websites, and creative assets, with a library of 40,000+ AI tools
record.description: Vondy is a web-based AI platform where teams describe what they need and get working websites, apps, dashboards, and internal tools. Builds can include payments, authentication, and pushes to GitHub. The platform also generates images, video, 3D elements, icons, and other assets, with access to 48+ models. It sits on a library of 40,000+ AI tools covering design, programming, writing, translation, audio, and marketing. A separate service, Vondy Forge, builds custom software for clients.
record.pricing_summary: Pro is $20/mo for 10,000 credits, Pro+ is $60/mo for 35,000 credits, and Ultra is $200/mo for 100,000 credits. Each plan includes unlimited downloads, the Vondy AI Assistant, and a project workspace. Enterprise is custom-priced and adds unlimited seats, SSO, and SLAs.
features: Push to GitHub with version tracking
Image, video, 3D, and icon asset generation
use_cases: Build websites, apps, dashboards, and internal tools
Founders launching a first version faster
Generate images and visuals for app projects
Logo, book cover, and game art design
Custom software for operational workflows (Vondy Forge)
record.notes: The current blurb ('Your assistant that helps you automate your work') is outdated. The official homepage now presents Vondy as an AI builder for apps, websites, and creative assets, backed by a library of 40,000+ AI tools. The listed URL has an affiliate parameter (?via=artifimedia), so the clean official URL is used instead. The official pricing page lists no free plan. However, some vondy.com tool pages say users can create a free account and get a free trial, and a few generator pages say they are free. Because the pricing page itself shows no free plan, free_tier is set to false; this should be rechecked. Third-party sites show older prices ($19/$49/$99 plans), which no longer match the official page. The Enterprise tier lists 'custom integrations' without naming any. Pages were read through search-result extracts of vondy.com, not a full browser load.

record.short_description: App that generates personalized, adaptive soundscapes to help users focus, relax, and sleep
record.description: Endel is an app that generates personalized soundscapes for focus, relaxation, sleep, and physical activity. The company says its patented technology changes the sound in real time based on time of day, weather, heart rate, location, and step cadence. It runs on iOS, Android, macOS, and the web, has a standalone Apple Watch app, and works with Amazon Alexa. Premium soundscapes include colored noise and work made with artists such as James Blake, Grimes, and Richie Hawtin.
record.pricing_summary: Endel's own checkout page lists Endel Premium at $6.99 per month, $19.99 for 3 months, $39.99 per year, or $249.99 for lifetime access.
features: Adapts to time of day, weather, heart rate, and location
Focus, Relax, Sleep, and Move modes
Autoplay that picks a soundscape for your current state
use_cases: Mindful movement during walks and runs
record.notes: The site is live and the product is actively updated: the official X account posted about the new Custom Scenarios feature in Nov 2025. The listed blurb is roughly accurate, but Endel calls its output personalized soundscapes, not music. The prices come from payment.endel.io, a subdomain of endel.io. Third-party sites say app store prices differ by platform and region. I could not confirm a free plan or free trial on an official page. The X bio says 'Try Endel for free' and review sites mention a 7-day trial and a limited free plan, but free_tier is set to false. PitchBook says Warner Music Group bought Endel on 2022-04-05. That looks like a mix-up with Endel Engie, an unrelated French industrial company bought by Altrad Group around the same date, and no official page confirms it, so status is active, not acquired. Wikipedia names Endel Sound GmbH as the developer.

record.short_description: AI meeting recorder and notetaker that records, transcribes, and summarizes Google Meet, Zoom, and Teams calls
record.description: tl;dv, short for "Too Long, Didn't View," is an AI notetaker for online meetings on Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams. It records calls, either with a bot that joins the meeting or through a bot-free desktop app. It also produces transcripts with speaker labels and AI summaries in 30+ languages. It is built for sales, customer success, and internal meetings. It can pull insights from many meetings at once, offers sales coaching, and connects to CRMs and thousands of other tools.
record.pricing_summary: A tl;dv blog post says there is a freemium plan with unlimited recording and a Pro plan at $18 per user per month, billed annually. The same post lists a sales-focused Business plan at $35 per seat per month, billed annually.
features: Meeting recording for Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams
record.notes: The listed website (tldv.cello.so) is a Cello referral link, not the official site, which is https://tldv.io/. The current blurb is too narrow: the product also supports Microsoft Teams and does AI summaries and insights, not just transcription. I could not open the official tldv.io/pricing page. The prices above come from a tldv.io blog post comparing tl;dv with Gong, which may be out of date. A third-party site (claap.io) lists Business at $59 per user per month billed annually, and also says Pro is $29 per user per month if paid monthly. Those numbers conflict with the blog post, so the prices should be checked on tldv.io/pricing. The legal company name was not confirmed.

record.short_description: AI content detector that flags ChatGPT and other LLM-written text, alongside a set of writing tools
record.description: ZeroGPT is a web-based tool that estimates whether text was written by a person or produced by ChatGPT and other large language models. It can check whole documents, paragraphs and single sentences, and it shows probabilities and statistics. The site also offers a plagiarism checker, AI humanizer, paraphraser, summarizer, grammar and spell checker, translator, citation generator, and AI image and video detectors. ZeroGPT says it is built for educators, businesses and content creators.
features: AI-generated text detection at document, paragraph, and sentence level
AI Chatbot and AI Email Assistant
use_cases: Teachers checking essays for AI-generated content
record.notes: Sources were the zerogpt.com pages /welcome, /faq and /ai-image-detector. The welcome page says users can detect ChatGPT content for free, and the site footer has a Pricing link, so pricing_type is set to freemium. The search tool hit its usage limit before I could open zerogpt.com's own pricing page, so no tiers are recorded. Third-party sites list prices that don't agree with each other: Cybernews (Aug 2025) gives Pro $7.99/mo, Plus $13.99/mo and Max $18.99/mo billed annually, and Capterra lists $8.29/mo. Neither is on the official domain, so I left both prices out. I could not confirm who owns the product, so company is empty. Several unrelated look-alike sites exist (zerogpt.net, zerogpt.tech, zerogpt.org, zerogpt.plus) and should not be confused with zerogpt.com. The current blurb is accurate, but the product now also covers plagiarism checking, humanizing and image/video detection.

record.short_description: AI writing assistant for rewriting, paraphrasing, proofreading, generating text, and summarizing content
record.description: Wordtune is an AI-powered reading and writing assistant from AI21 Labs. It rewrites and paraphrases text, corrects spelling and grammar, switches between formal and casual tones, and makes sentences longer or shorter. It can also generate text from prompts or templates in a style that matches the user's writing, and help make AI-generated content sound more natural. Wordtune also summarizes documents, articles, webpages, and YouTube videos. It is offered through a web editor, a browser extension, and an iOS app.
record.pricing_summary: Basic is free with 10 rewrites and AI suggestions per day, 3 AI summaries per month, and unlimited spelling and grammar checks. Advanced costs $6.99/month ($4.89/month billed annually) for 30 rewrites per day and 15 summaries per month, and Unlimited costs $9.99/month ($6.99/month billed annually), both with a 3-day free trial.
features: AI text generation from prompts and templates
Summarize documents, articles, webpages, and YouTube videos
record.notes: The listed website is correct and live. The current blurb, 'Accelerate your professional tasks,' is vague and reads like a slogan, so it should be replaced. AI21 Labs is named as the maker in AI21 press releases on PR Newswire and in news coverage. The prices come from search-result text of wordtune.com/plans, which may be an older cached copy, so they should be rechecked against the live page. Third-party sites show other prices, including a team price, but those were not confirmed on wordtune.com and were left out. The Google Docs and iOS/Siri integrations come from AI21 press releases and news coverage. The browser extension is mentioned in Wordtune's own guide.

record.short_description: AI tool that summarized YouTube videos, with timestamps, chat-based Q&A and a saved video library
record.description: Tammy AI was an AI tool for YouTube viewers. It was offered as a web app and a Chrome extension. It made two kinds of video summaries. Basic Summary gave chapters and key points. Pro Summary added timestamps and an overview. Users could also ask questions about a video in a chat, explore videos and save summaries to a personal library. Its listed domain, tammy.ai, now shows a GoDaddy page offering the domain for sale, so the product no longer appears to be running.
features: Basic Summary with chapters and key points
Pro Summary with timestamps and overview
use_cases: Jumping to key moments in a video using timestamps
record.notes: Search only, no pages opened beyond results: I hit the search tool limit, so I couldn't check further, including the Chrome Web Store listing. The search result for https://tammy.ai is a GoDaddy page saying the domain is for sale for $124,999, so I left official_url empty. I didn't find any working official product page or pricing page. The domain-for-sale result is the only sign that the product is offline. The result is listed as old, so the current state of the domain should be checked by hand. I set status to unknown, not shutdown, because no official page says the product was discontinued. The only mention of a shutdown is the title of a third-party directory page (dang.ai), which asks why it shut down. Pricing from third parties (allthingsai, aibucket.io, tenereteam) mentions a free plan and a Premium plan at about $9 to $9.90 a month. None of that is on the product's own domain, so I left pricing_summary, pricing_source_url and free_tier empty or false. The features listed come only from third-party directories and a demo video transcript. The current blurb is in French and is a slogan. I recommend marking this listing as inactive or removing it.

record.short_description: AI resume and cover letter builder with ATS-friendly templates and AI writing tools for job seekers
record.description: Kickresume is an online resume and cover letter builder for job seekers. Users choose a template and use AI tools to write, rewrite, tailor and check their documents. The AI can build a resume from a job title or a pasted job ad. It can also generate summaries and work experience sections and format content for applicant tracking systems. Users can upload an existing resume to edit it. The product also includes a personal website builder, and students and teachers can get Premium free.
record.pricing_summary: There is a free plan with unlimited resumes and downloads, 4 resume and cover letter templates, and 1 website template. Premium costs $24 per month billed monthly, $18 per month billed quarterly, or $8 per month billed yearly, and students and teachers get 6 months of Premium free.
features: AI resume builder from job description
use_cases: Tailoring a resume to a specific job ad
record.notes: I found this through web search results only and didn't open any pages directly. A second round of searches was blocked by the tool's usage limit. Pricing comes from a Kickresume help-center article indexed 7 days ago, not the pricing page itself. Kickresume's own pages disagree on price: an older help-center FAQ lists $19, $13 and $7 per month, while newer pages list $24, $18 and $8. A third-party review says the pricing page is in euros, not dollars, so check the currency. Other third-party sites list LinkedIn/PDF import and Career Map, but I didn't record them because I didn't confirm them on Kickresume's own site. The legal company name wasn't confirmed. The current blurb 'Create an attractive CV using AI' is accurate but narrow: the product also covers cover letters, ATS checks, resume tailoring and personal websites.

record.short_description: Stability AI's family of text-to-image diffusion models, offered as open weights and through a paid API
record.description: Stable Diffusion is a family of text-to-image models from Stability AI, a UK company. It was first released publicly in August 2022. Stability AI published the model weights, model card and code, so people can run the models themselves. It also sells hosted access through its Developer Platform API, which uses credits. The API covers image services such as Stable Image Ultra, which is built on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, along with other generative services like Stable Audio.
record.pricing_summary: The Developer Platform API uses credits, with 1 credit = $0.01, and new users get 25 free credits. Stable Image Ultra costs 8 credits per generation, and more credits can be bought from the account page.
features: Publicly released model weights and code
Stable Image Ultra based on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large
use_cases: Adding image generation to applications through the API
record.notes: The current blurb ('Generate your images with Stable Diffusion Online') looks like the wording of a third-party Stable Diffusion web app, not Stability AI's own site. It should be replaced. Stability AI's ownership of stability.ai is confirmed through its verified GitHub organization. Pricing comes from the official platform.stability.ai/pricing page, which also lists other services. Prices for each model (for example SD3.5 Large at 6.5 credits) and the Community License's free self-hosting under $1M revenue only appeared on third-party review sites, so they were left out. The search limit ran out before the stability.ai/license and stable-image pages could be checked directly.

record.short_description: Machine learning platform providing predictive personalization and search for ecommerce and hospitality businesses
record.description: Aidaptive is a Cupertino, California company founded by former Google engineers who worked on AI and machine learning infrastructure for Google Ads and Payments. It offers predictive engines for the ecommerce and hospitality sectors. These engines use machine learning to show customers relevant products or services and to improve engagement and conversion rates. For vacation rental property managers, it offers an AI search capability, which is available natively to BizCor customers who use Streamline. CB Insights lists the company as alive.
use_cases: Driving direct bookings for vacation rental property managers
record.notes: I couldn't open aidaptive.com or any pricing page on Aidaptive's own site because my search limit ran out before I could. These details come from secondary sources: CB Insights, LinkedIn, X, a company press release quoted by CB Insights, and directory and review sites. The X, LinkedIn and CB Insights profiles all link to aidaptive.com. CB Insights lists the company as alive, with a $16M seed round. A review site (toolsforhumans.ai) says pricing is custom and quote-only, but that isn't confirmed on Aidaptive's own site, so I left pricing empty. The current blurb about AI conversion optimization roughly matches the sources. However, recent sources describe a focus on hospitality and vacation rentals as well as ecommerce. Before publishing, someone should check the official homepage and pricing page.

record.short_description: AI code writing assistant with code completions and function generation for data scientists and analysts
record.description: CodeSquire is an AI code writing assistant for data scientists, engineers, and analysts. It suggests and completes code as users type, turns written comments into code, and writes whole functions using well-known libraries, so users do not have to look up methods and parameters. The official site says it is built for data science use cases and supports Jupyter, VS Code, PyCharm, and Google Colab. It is installed as a Chrome extension.
features: Code completions and suggestions as you type
Entire functions generated by AI tailored to data science use cases
use_cases: Creating charts such as Plotly bar charts from comments
Writing functions without searching for library methods and parameters
record.notes: The official homepage (codesquire.ai) appeared in search results and describes the product as an AI code writing assistant for data scientists. It says the tool supports Jupyter, VS Code, PyCharm and Google Colab and offers a Chrome extension download. I could not find a pricing page on the product's own domain. Third-party directories disagree on price: one says paid plans from $10/mo with a free trial, others call it freemium or free, and another says it is paid. Because of that, I left the pricing fields empty or set to unknown, and free_tier is false. The LinkedIn company page lists Dubai as headquarters and a team of 2-10 employees. I hit the search tool limit before I could open a docs or pricing page or check recent activity, so status 'active' rests only on the homepage being indexed. The current blurb is close to the site's headline, 'Turn your thoughts into code', but it leaves out that the product is aimed at data scientists.

record.short_description: AI chatbot offering CBT-based mental health support; its Woebot app was retired on June 30, 2025
record.description: Woebot Health is a San Francisco company founded in 2017 by clinical research psychologist Dr. Alison Darcy. It built Woebot, an AI-powered relational agent delivered as a smartphone chat app. Woebot used structured conversations and tools drawn from cognitive behavioral therapy to help people manage symptoms of anxiety and depression. Recent App Store listings required an access code from a provider, employer, or partner. According to several industry news reports, the company retired the Woebot app on June 30, 2025.
features: Structured conversations based on cognitive behavioral therapy
Access codes issued through providers, employers, or partners
use_cases: Managing symptoms of anxiety and depression
Chat-based mental health support for patients and members
Adolescent mental health support through healthcare partners
record.notes: I set status to shutdown because the Woebot app itself has been discontinued. Behavioral Health Business (Apr 23, 2025), MobiHealthNews, and several other outlets report that it was retired on June 30, 2025. Users could download their conversation history until then, and the company said it would anonymize account data after July 31, 2025. The woebothealth.com homepage still loads but only says 'We are making important updates to user accounts' and doesn't clearly confirm the shutdown. I couldn't tell whether any enterprise or partner offering is still running. I found no pricing on the official domain. A University of the Free State LibGuide calls it free, but that isn't an official source, so I left the pricing fields empty. A Leaps by Bayer investment of $9.5M (March 2022) appears on woebothealth.com, but that was an investment, not an acquisition. The listed blurb is out of date, and the directory should mark this listing as discontinued. I wasn't able to finish a follow-up search of the official site because my search limit ran out.

record.company: Limitless (formerly Rewind AI), acquired by Meta
record.short_description: Discontinued Mac app that recorded screen and audio activity so users could search their past
record.description: Rewind was a personal memory app for Mac. It recorded the text and audio that passed through a user's screen and speakers, indexed it, and let users search that history in natural language. The company renamed itself Limitless in 2024 and moved toward a cloud service and a wearable Pendant. Meta bought Limitless in December 2025. After the deal, the Rewind app was sunset, with screen and audio capture turned off on December 19, 2025. Pendant sales also stopped.
features: Records text and audio from screen and speakers
Search past screens, audio, and meetings
record.notes: This row is out of date. Several third-party sources agree: 9to5mac, WinBuzzer, Outlook Business, IoT M2M Council, and The Rundown. They say Rewind became Limitless in 2024, Meta bought Limitless in December 2025 (CEO Dan Siroker announced it in a blog post), and the Rewind Mac app was sunset, with all capture turned off on December 19, 2025. Pendant sales stopped, existing Pendant users get one year of support, and service ended in the EU and UK. The status is set to shutdown because the product itself was discontinued, but Meta is the named buyer of its parent company, so the record could also be marked acquired. I did not open rewind.ai or limitless.ai directly because my search tool hit its usage limit. The Rundown says the current rewind.ai domain now belongs to a different, unaffiliated AI company, so I left official_url empty. I could not check pricing on the product's own domain, so pricing is empty. The current blurb describes a product that no longer works, so consider removing the listing or marking it discontinued.

record.company: Trip Planner AI, Inc (acquired by Layla AI)
record.short_description: AI trip builder and itinerary generator that organizes flights, hotels, and activities in one place
record.description: Trip Planner AI is a web-based travel planning tool that uses AI to build personalized trip itineraries. According to its website, it gathers flights, hotels, and activities in one place so users do not need many browser tabs. It uses live data to fit itineraries to a traveler's style, budget, and timing. The site also offers optimized itineraries, personalized dining suggestions, social media insights, and a Community Trips section. Crunchbase lists the company as acquired by Layla AI.
features: Flights, hotels, and activities organized in one place
Smarter itineraries built around traveler needs
Live data matched to travel style, budget, and timing
use_cases: Planning a trip without juggling many browser tabs
Organizing flights, hotels, and activities for a trip
record.notes: The official site, tripplanner.ai, is live. Its homepage and /trips page describe the AI trip builder and itinerary generator, and the /trips page title calls it a 'Free & Customizable Travel Itinerary App'. That is why free_tier is true. I did not find a pricing page with tiers or prices on tripplanner.ai. One third-party comparison site (simular.ai) lists a $7.99/month Pro plan. Directory sites list it as free. Because neither source is on the product's domain, pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are empty and pricing_type is unknown. Crunchbase names Layla AI as the buyer and lists the operating status as Closed, but the site is still up. A Trip.com article also says it was merged under Layla. One directory (aitoolswiki) says Expedia Group bought Layla, but I could not confirm that from a primary source, so it is not recorded. The same directory mentions Skyscanner, Booking.com, and GetYourGuide booking links, but I did not confirm these on the official site, so integrations is empty. The current blurb 'Organize your trips in 1 click' does not appear in the official text I saw. Search tool limits stopped me from opening a dedicated pricing or docs page.

record.short_description: Consumer AI chatbot platform for chatting, roleplaying, and creating stories with user-made AI characters
record.description: Character.ai is a generative AI chatbot service run by Character Technologies Inc. Users chat, roleplay, and create stories with AI Characters. They can pick from millions of Characters made by the community, or design their own and publish them for others. The service is available on the web and in iOS and Android apps. It recently added free chat styles called PipSqueak 3 and ShortSqueak. The company's blog says it has started a voluntary Chapter 11 process to support a court-supervised sale.
features: Create and publish your own Characters
Image models for consistent Character visuals
use_cases: Building and sharing custom chatbot characters
record.notes: Listed URL beta.character.ai is an old subdomain. The main site is character.ai, and the About page and blog are hosted there. I ran out of searches, so I could not confirm whether beta still redirects. The current blurb is vague. The official blog says Character.ai has 'initiated a voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy process to facilitate a court-supervised sale of the company.' No buyer is named, so I did not mark it acquired. Re-check status soon. Google's August 2024 deal for about $2.7B was a non-exclusive technology license plus founder hires, not an acquisition. The free tier is supported by the official blog and the app listings. The blog also mentions a paid '(c.ai) lite' tier, but no price appears on any official page I opened. Third-party sites (eesel.ai, usagepricing.com, thesaaseducation.com) report c.ai+ at $9.99/month or $94.99/year and (c.ai) lite at $2.99/month. One says character.ai/pricing returns 404 and that prices only appear in the in-app paywall at character.ai/subscribe. Those prices are unverified on the official domain, so pricing fields are left empty.

record.short_description: AI face swap app for putting a selfie into videos and GIFs, plus AI avatars and photo edits
record.description: Reface is a mobile and web app from NEOCORTEXT, Inc. that uses AI to swap a user's face into videos, GIFs, movie stills, and character art using a single selfie. It can also animate photos, turn photos into cartoons, generate AI avatars and AI photos, preview hairstyles, create future baby images, and edit faces with retouch tools and filters. It is aimed mainly at casual users who make entertainment and social media content. Many premium features require a subscription.
features: Face swap in videos and GIFs from one selfie
use_cases: Creating memes and funny face swap videos
record.notes: The official pages reface.ai/reface/ and web.reface.ai describe it as a face-swap app and AI avatar generator, and the developer is NEOCORTEXT, INC. according to the Google Play and App Store listings. I couldn't find a pricing page on reface.ai. The App Store lists the app as free with in-app purchases, says premium features need a subscription, and shows 'Reface PRO weekly $6.99'. Because that price comes from apple.com and not the product's own domain, I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. Third-party sites like ToolFi, ToolChase and Screenrant give conflicting prices, so I didn't use them. The current blurb, 'Create original content', is vague and doesn't say that this is a consumer face-swap app. My search tool hit its usage limit before I could open a dedicated pricing page, so this record is less certain than it would otherwise be.

record.short_description: Library and generator of ready-made ChatGPT prompts for eCommerce marketing content
record.description: eCommerce Prompts, branded on its site as eCommerce ChatGPT Prompts, is a web tool for eCommerce marketers. It says it offers more than 2 million ready-made ChatGPT prompts built by prompt engineers using insights from eCommerce experts. Users pick a content type, such as a homepage headline, an SMS campaign, a WhatsApp message or a browser notification. They then set up to 10 personalization options and generate a prompt to use in ChatGPT. The site also has Prompt Ideas and Inspiration Board sections.
record.pricing_summary: The homepage invites users to 'Generate Prompts for FREE!' No paid plans or prices were found on the site.
use_cases: Setting up store and marketing campaigns
record.notes: Product details come from search-indexed text of the official homepage (ecommerceprompts.com). The page title is 'eCommerce ChatGPT Prompts', which differs from the listed name 'Ecommerce Prompt'. The existing blurb is roughly accurate, but the tool is a ChatGPT prompt library plus generator for eCommerce marketers. Company is left blank because only a third-party LinkedIn article says Moda launched the site; the official page doesn't name an operator. Pricing is marked free only because the homepage CTA says 'Generate Prompts for FREE!' No pricing page was found, so paid tiers or limits may exist. Because I hit the search limit, I couldn't open a separate pricing or docs page or confirm the site loads live. 'ChatGPT' is listed under integrations only because users paste prompts into it. I found no evidence of a technical integration.

record.short_description: AI design platform that turns product sketches into realistic renders and rotatable 3D views
record.description: Vizcom is an AI design platform for product development. On its product page, the company says the tool turns sketches into 3D renders that users can view, rotate and refine. Its tools include sketch-to-render, live rendering that updates as the user draws or edits a prompt, generating design variations, and close-up and material shots. Users can also place a quick drawing onto a photo to see the design in context. Vizcom says the platform supports work from early concept through to manufacturing.
features: Place sketches onto photos for in-context visualization
record.notes: Vizcom's product page is now on vizcom.com (https://vizcom.com/product). The listed vizcom.ai may redirect there, but I could not confirm that. I did not open an official pricing page because the search limit ran out. Third-party sites (archpulse, softwarefinder, saasworthy, spotsaas) mention a free Starter plan and a Professional plan at about $49/month, but their numbers disagree with each other ($18, $19, $25 and $40 also appear). So I left pricing as unknown and did not record a free tier. The founder details (Jordan Taylor and Kaelan Richards, San Francisco) come only from a third-party site, so I did not use them. Current blurb is broadly accurate but slogan-like; the product now emphasizes sketch-to-3D rendering for product design.

record.short_description: AI service that turns existing floor plans into 2D and 3D floor plans and 360° virtual tours
record.description: Getfloorplan is an AI-based service for the real estate industry. Users upload an existing 2D floor plan and receive 2D and 3D floor plans and 360° virtual tours that can be used to market a property. The company also offers furnished 3D floor plans, editable 3D models made from 2D plans, and custom interior styles. It serves real estate agents, developers and 3D visualization agencies. LinkedIn lists the company's headquarters as Boca Raton, Florida.
features: AI conversion of 2D floor plans to 3D
Editable 3D model from an existing 2D plan
Custom or mix-style interior design on request
record.notes: The official site is up. I saw the homepage (https://getfloorplan.com/) and the news page (getfloorplan.com/news/unique-style) through search results. I did not open a pricing page on getfloorplan.com because I hit the search tool limit, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are empty and pricing_type is unknown. Third-party directories list per-plan prices, but their numbers don't agree: Toolify, Dang.ai and TopAI list sets from $25 to $69 or $70, and SourceForge says pricing starts at $20 per plan. Some directories also say there is a free trial or free tier, and SourceForge says there is an API. I could not confirm any of these on the official site, so free_tier is false and integrations is empty. LinkedIn lists Boca Raton, FL as headquarters. The current blurb, 'Maximize Your Real Estate Sales', is a slogan and should be replaced with a factual description.

record.short_description: Open-source GPT-2 model that adds style cues to Stable Diffusion image prompts
record.description: Prompt Extend is an open-source text generation model and Hugging Face Space made by the developer daspartho. A user types the main idea for an image prompt, and the model adds suitable style cues to it. The model is GPT-2 and was trained on a dataset of Stable Diffusion prompts built from DiffusionDB. It is released under the MIT license. It can be used through a Gradio demo or loaded with the Hugging Face Transformers library. Training notebooks are on GitHub.
record.pricing_summary: There are no paid tiers. The model is open source under the MIT license and free to download and run.
features: Generates suitable style cues from a prompt's main idea
GPT-2 model trained on Stable Diffusion prompts
Training notebooks for the dataset and tokenizer
use_cases: Enhancing text-to-image prompts with style cues
record.notes: The current blurb is misleading. The tool expands Stable Diffusion image prompts with style cues. It does not improve prompts for general AI or chatbot responses. A suggested blurb is: 'Adds style cues to Stable Diffusion prompts using a GPT-2 model.' The listed Space at huggingface.co/spaces/daspartho/prompt-extend showed a 'Runtime error' when indexed, so the hosted demo may not work. The model page (huggingface.co/daspartho/prompt-extend) and the GitHub repo (github.com/daspartho/prompt-extend) are still available, and several copies of the Space by other users are running. Status is set to active because the pages are up and nothing says the project was discontinued. The project looks unmaintained: the model was last updated about 3 years ago, and the app.py file about 2 years ago. Pricing comes from the MIT license in the model card. No pricing page exists. All details come from search-result snippets of the Hugging Face and GitHub pages, because the search limit stopped further checks.

record.short_description: AI companion chatbot app for conversation, emotional support, and building a relationship with an AI friend
record.description: Replika is an AI companion app from Luka, Inc., a company based in San Francisco. Users chat with a personal chatbot that learns from their reactions and conversations, so each Replika develops its own way of talking. Users can pick a relationship status for their AI, and paid features add voice calls. Replika runs on iOS and Android and as a web app at my.replika.com. Its site describes it as an AI friend for chatting, reflection, and personal growth.
features: Learns from your reactions to its messages
use_cases: Emotional support when feeling down or anxious
record.notes: The official homepage calls Replika a free AI friend, and the help center describes the chatbot, relationship status, and 24/7 availability. The company name, Luka, Inc. of San Francisco, comes from Replika's privacy policy. Replika's own site does not list subscription prices. Third-party review sites claim Pro costs about $19.99/month or $69.99/year and Ultra about $29.99/month or $119.99/year, but those figures conflict with App Store prices quoted elsewhere, so pricing is left empty. Voice calls as a paid Replika Pro feature comes from Australia's eSafety guide, which also mentions Oculus VR access. The current blurb loosely follows an older tagline ('Always here to listen and talk'). The homepage now says 'The AI friend to do life with' and claims a user count of over 42 million. In 2025, Italy's data protection authority fined Luka €5 million under GDPR. I searched only once because the search tool hit its usage limit, so I couldn't open the help center's pricing pages.

record.short_description: AI audio and video creation platform offering voice generation, voice changing, song creation, and virtual camera software
record.description: Fineshare is a software company that describes itself as an all-in-one AI audio creation platform. It offers voice cloning, voice generation, voice changing, music and sound effect generation, and voiceover tools for individuals and businesses. Its products include FineVoice, Singify, VoiceTrans, Vora, and FineCam. FineCam is an AI virtual camera for video recording and video conferencing that can turn a phone into a webcam. Products are sold through Fineshare's online store on monthly, annual, or lifetime plans.
record.pricing_summary: The Fineshare store lists FineVoice from $8.99/month (Basic is $5.99/month billed annually at $71.99), VoiceTrans at $6.99/month, and FineCam at $9.95/month. FineCam Pro costs $9.95 for 1 month, $29.99 for 1 year, or $49.99 for a lifetime license.
record.notes: Use https://www.fineshare.com/ as the official URL. The listed URL has an affiliate referral parameter (?rfsn=...), so remove it. The current blurb is in French and only describes FineCam's video and conferencing use. Fineshare's own About page now presents the company mainly as an AI audio creation platform, so the blurb should be rewritten. Prices come from fineshare.com/store.html, fineshare.com/finecam/buy.html and finevoice.fineshare.com/pricing. No official page I opened clearly describes a free plan. The freemium label rests on FineCam's 'Upgrade for full Pro features' wording and on third-party sites (TrustRadius, Cybernews) that report free versions, so it should be checked again. Fineshare's X account posted a notice (dated Jan 19, year unclear) about a temporary site issue, listing backup links for Vora, FineVoice (finevoice.ai) and Singify. The fineshare.com pages showed up in search results, so the site appears to be up. I found nothing showing an acquisition or shutdown. No specific third-party integrations were confirmed on official pages.

record.short_description: Fully managed vector database and AI knowledge platform for search, RAG, and agent retrieval
record.description: Pinecone is a fully managed vector database for AI applications, developed by Pinecone Systems, Inc. The company describes its AI knowledge platform as covering Database, Nexus, and Marketplace products. With Pinecone, developers can store and search vector embeddings for semantic search, recommendations, chatbots, and anomaly detection. New writes become searchable within seconds and indexing is automatic. It scales from zero to billions of items, runs on AWS, GCP, and Azure, and includes an Assistant product, Dedicated Read Nodes, and a web console.
features: Writes acknowledged in under 100ms and searchable within seconds
Live index updates on add, edit, or delete
Scales from zero to billions of items
Web console for monitoring and managing indexes
SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR-ready
record.notes: The official site is live. Pinecone's own pages say it is a fully managed vector database built for AI. They also call Pinecone 'the trusted AI knowledge company', with Database, Nexus, and Marketplace products, so the current blurb 'Long-term memory for AI' looks out of date. The free tier is based on the official 'Start using Pinecone for free' wording. I couldn't open the official pricing page (pinecone.io/pricing) because I hit the search limit, so I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. Third-party sites list prices, but they don't agree with each other: a free Starter plan, a $20/month Builder plan, Standard at a $50/month minimum, Enterprise at a $500/month minimum, and older hourly pod pricing. Check these against pinecone.io/pricing. A Pinecone landing page names customers including Adobe, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Zapier, but I didn't add them to the record.

record.short_description: Online image tool that enlarges pictures and improves their quality, per the existing directory listing
record.description: Image Enlarger is listed as a tool that makes images larger and improves their quality. The listed link is a ShareASale affiliate redirect (merchant ID 92386), and it does not show which product or company it points to. Several unrelated products use the same generic name, including Picsart's Image Enlarger, Topaz Labs' Image Enlarger, and Imglarger's AI Image Enlarger, so this record could not be matched to one vendor. Pricing, features, and integrations were not confirmed.
record.notes: The listed_website is a ShareASale affiliate tracking link (m=92386), not an official product site. I could not find which merchant it points to before the search tool hit its usage limit. A web search for 'Image Enlarger' found several separate products with that name: picsart.com/image-enlarger, topazlabs.com/tools/image-enlarger, imglarger.com (AI Image Enlarger), and bigjpg.com. None of them could be tied to this affiliate link, so official_url, company, and pricing are left empty and status is unknown. The use_cases only repeat the current blurb. Next steps: resolve the affiliate redirect, or check ShareASale merchant 92386, to find the real vendor, then replace the affiliate URL with the vendor's own domain.

record.short_description: Browser-based AI tool in Adobe Podcast that removes background noise and echo from voice recordings
record.description: Enhance Speech is an AI audio tool in Adobe Podcast, Adobe's web-based podcasting suite. Users upload voice recordings and the tool removes noise, echo and reverb so speech sounds like it was recorded in a studio. Adobe released version 2 with clearer, more natural dialogue and a strength slider. The free version cleans audio files. Premium is included with the Adobe Firefly Pro plan and adds video support, bulk uploads, separate speech, music and ambience controls, and higher daily limits.
record.pricing_summary: Enhance Speech has a free version. Adobe Podcast Premium comes with the Adobe Firefly Pro plan and allows enhancement of up to 4 hours a day with files up to 1 GB. No dollar price was shown on the pages checked.
features: Removes noise and echo from voice recordings
Enhance Speech v2 for clearer, natural-sounding dialogue
Removes reverb, chatter and background music
Premium: video support for MP4, MOV and more
Premium: adjust speech, music and ambience levels
Premium: up to 4 hours a day, files up to 1 GB
Audiograms with custom themes and captions
use_cases: Fixing interview audio recorded in noisy places
Fixing recordings made in rooms with poor acoustics
integrations: Adobe Firefly Pro plan (includes Adobe Podcast Premium)
record.notes: The product is officially called Enhance Speech, part of Adobe Podcast, not 'Adobe Enhance'. The listed site podcast.adobe.com is correct, but the dedicated product page is podcast.adobe.com/en/enhancespeech. The current blurb is accurate but very thin. Adobe's own page links Premium to the Adobe Firefly Pro plan but showed no price. Third-party review sites list Premium at $9.99/month or $99.99/year, plus free-tier limits of 1 hour a day and 30-minute/500 MB files. Those figures are not confirmed on an Adobe page, so they are left out of the pricing summary. I couldn't open a helpx or adobe.com pricing page because the search limit ran out. A TIME article names Enhance Speech one of its Best Inventions of 2025.

record.short_description: AI study app that turns notes, PDFs, and lectures into quizzes, flashcards, summaries, and podcasts
record.description: School Hack is an AI-powered study app for students. Users upload notes, videos, PDFs, or lecture slides, and its AI assistant, Andy, turns them into personalized study sets with quizzes, flashcards, and summaries. It also offers interactive notes, study podcasts made from course material, an always-available AI tutor, and a collaborative mode where students share decks and track progress together. It is available on the web and as an iOS app, published by SCHOOL HACK FZ-LLC.
features: Interactive notes that quiz you back
AI tutor Andy for questions about your notes
Collaborative mode for live group study
Upload notes, videos, PDFs, or lecture slides
use_cases: Turning lecture notes into study sets
Listening to study materials as audio
record.notes: The listed website, https://charley.ai, is wrong. It belongs to a separate product, Charley AI, an AI essay-writing tool, so the URL should be changed to https://www.schoolhack.ai/. The schoolhack.ai homepage I saw in search results shows the product and a 'Sign up for free' button, but it lists no plans or prices. I did not find a pricing page on schoolhack.ai, so pricing is set to unknown and free_tier to false. The search tool hit its usage limit before I could look further. Third-party directories (theresanaiforthat, aichief, success.ai) say prices start at $9.99, and aichief also mentions a $19.99 plan. I left those numbers out because no page on the official site confirms them. The company name comes from the developer listed on the App Store. The Discord integration and the GPT-4 basis come from Australia's eSafety Commissioner guide, not the official site. Some directories describe older features such as essay writing, paraphrasing, and plagiarism checking, but the current homepage focuses on study tools. The current blurb is vague, so I suggest replacing it with the short_description.

record.short_description: No-code AI web scraper that collects data from a URL and the items you specify
record.description: Webscrape AI is a no-code web scraping tool for automated data collection. Users enter a URL and the items they want to scrape, and its AI scraper extracts the data without any coding. The site says the tool is accurate, fast, and customizable, and pitches it as an affordable option for businesses of all sizes. Higher plans add proxy support, waiting for page load or JavaScript, pagination, and bulk URL scraping. It is sold as a monthly or annual subscription.
record.pricing_summary: WebScrapeAI costs $27/month for 250 URLs per month, WebScrapeAI Pro costs $47/month for 500 URLs with proxy and JS-wait support, and WebScrapeAI Bulk costs $87/month for 1,000 URLs with bulk and pagination support. Annual billing is discounted.
features: Enter URL and items to scrape
record.notes: The official homepage content, including features and pricing, comes from a search-indexed copy that appears to be about 3.5 years old (page age about 1285 days). I could not confirm that this is the live current version. The status is marked active because the domain is indexed, but this is not verified as current. Third-party sites conflict with the official page on pricing: Dataconomy lists a free tier with 500 credits plus a Hobby plan at $27/month, a Startup plan at $99/month, and custom Enterprise pricing. ScrapeGraphAI mentions a free trial. Neither claim appears on the official page I saw, so neither was used. No company or legal entity name was found. The listed URL contains an affiliate parameter (?via=lacreme), which was removed from official_url. The current blurb, 'Automate data collection without coding', matches the site's headline.

record.short_description: Cloud-based AI tool that turns live-action footage into editable CG scenes with animated characters
record.description: Autodesk Flow Studio, formerly Wonder Studio from Wonder Dynamics, is a cloud-based AI toolset for VFX and animation. It automatically animates, lights and composites CG characters into live-action video shot on a single camera. It also generates elements for export, such as motion capture data, camera tracks, alpha masks, clean plates and character passes. These can be used in Maya, Blender, Unreal Engine or 3ds Max through USD. Autodesk bought Wonder Dynamics in 2024 and renamed the product in 2025.
record.pricing_summary: Autodesk's Flow Studio pricing guide describes a Free plan at $0 with 300 credits per month, including 3D Editor + Canvas, AI Motion Capture, Live Action Easy and Wonder 3D, subject to plan limits. Paid plan prices were not confirmed on an Autodesk page.
features: AI motion capture from single-camera video
Automatic animation, lighting and compositing of CG characters
Wonder 3D text-to-3D and image-to-3D asset generation
use_cases: Inserting CG characters into live-action footage
AI motion capture without mocap suits
record.notes: Wonder Studio by Wonder Dynamics is now Autodesk Flow Studio. Autodesk bought Wonder Dynamics in May 2024 (Wikipedia, CG Channel), and the product was renamed in March 2025. The listed website should be changed to the Autodesk Flow Studio page. The old help docs at help.wonderdynamics.com still exist and now use the Flow Studio name. The current blurb is still roughly accurate but should mention the rename. Third-party sites (80.lv, CG Channel, SaaSworthy) report paid tiers of Lite $10/month (2,100 credits), Standard $45/month (6,000 credits), Pro $95/month, plus Enterprise. Those prices were not confirmed on an Autodesk page, so they are left out of the pricing summary. In 2025 sources described the Free tier as watermarked, but Autodesk's newer guide calls it a free commercial tier. The pricing guide was seen only in a search result snippet, not opened in full.

record.short_description: ChatGPT-powered tool that generates social media posts from article links in a chosen style
record.description: PostGenius was a web tool, launched on Product Hunt in 2023, that used ChatGPT to generate social media posts. According to third-party directory listings, users pasted a link to an article and got a post back. They could pick a vibe, such as professional, choose a format, and match the writing style of an outside site or blog. Posts could be adapted for networks such as LinkedIn. The official site could not be checked, and one directory lists the tool as closed.
features: Generate posts from existing articles via a link
Match the style of an external site or blog
Customize posts for specific social platforms such as LinkedIn
use_cases: Turning blog articles into social media posts
Social media content creation for marketers, business owners, and bloggers
record.notes: I could not open postgeniusapp.com. My searches ran out before I could reach it, and no result from that domain came up. The Product Hunt listing for 'Post Genius' (launched 2023) names postgeniusapp.com as the company site. Everything else here comes from third-party directories (Product Hunt, dang.ai, aicenter.ai, listedai.co, aivalley.ai). Dang.ai says its review team marked Postgeniusapp as 'closed, shutdown or acquired', and its page title asks why it shut down. That is a third-party claim and does not name a buyer, so I set status to unknown instead of shutdown or acquired. Several directories say the tool was free with no signup, and dang.ai mentions planned paid tiers. No page on the product's own domain confirmed any pricing, so pricing and free tier are left empty or false. The company name was not found. Several unrelated products use similar names, including thepostgenius.com (Indian Trade Bird), postgenius.cogniqai.ai (CogniQ), postgenius.carrd.co, and PostGenie. None of them should be merged with this row. The current blurb is accurate but generic. A human should check by hand whether postgeniusapp.com still loads before keeping this listing.

record.short_description: AI platform from Portugal offering specialized assistants for writing, marketing, design, SEO, and business tasks
record.description: IntellibizzAI is an information technology company based in Cumieira, Vila Real, Portugal, that markets itself as a partner for AI-driven solutions. It offers a suite of specialized AI services for businesses, individuals, and creatives, such as Wordsmith Wonders, an AI chat assistant for content creation. Directory listings describe assistants for sales strategy, product marketing, keyword research, art generation, YouTube SEO, resume coaching, and email marketing. Its current X profile describes AI-powered brand identity systems.
record.notes: I hit the search limit before I could open intellibizzai.com or a pricing page on that domain, so I couldn't confirm the site is up, and status is unknown. The domain is still the right one: the company's Facebook page (Cumieira, Vila Real, Portugal; info@intellibizzai.com) and X profile both link to it, and Facebook links to intellibizzai.com/chat/wordsmith-wonders. The only prices I found were on third-party directories (daleelai.com and aiportalx.com list a free plan with 5,000 words and 5 images, plus Elite Suite and GPT-4 Turbo Suite at $19.99/month; aitoolguru.com says from $4). Pricing and free_tier stay unset until the company's own site confirms them. The features and use cases come from the company's social posts and theresanaiforthat.com. The current X bio talks about AI-powered brand identity systems, which suggests the company may have moved away from the AI tools suite. The current blurb ('Boost your creativity with IntellibizzAI') is a slogan and should be replaced. Recheck the live site before publishing.

record.short_description: AI video clipping tool that turns long videos into short clips for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts
record.description: Vizard is a browser-based AI video tool that finds the most engaging moments in long videos such as podcasts, webinars, and interviews. It turns them into short clips for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. It reframes horizontal footage to vertical 9:16, transcribes speech in 30+ languages, adds captions, and gives each clip a virality score. Users can also crop, trim, and caption clips, or add audio, images, and effects, inside the editor.
features: Multiple clips from one long video
use_cases: Turning webinars and interviews into social videos
Creating TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts
Keeping a steady posting schedule for social media managers and agencies
record.notes: Product and features were checked on vizard.ai tool pages (/tools/ai-video-clipper and /tools/clip-maker). The listed URL has an affiliate parameter (?via=essor), so the clean URL https://vizard.ai/ is used instead. I could not open Vizard's own pricing page because the search limit was reached, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are blank. Third-party sites (coldiq, contenttoolslab, saasworthy) report a free plan with 60 credits a month, 720p exports, and a watermark, plus paid Creator and Business tiers. Their reported prices conflict: about $14.50/$19.50 a month billed yearly versus $29/$39 a month. 'Freemium' and the free tier are based on those reports and on the official page title 'Free AI Clip Maker'. Vizard's pages name TikTok, Reels, and YouTube Shorts only as output formats, so no integrations are listed. The legal company entity was not confirmed. The current blurb 'Turn long videos into Shorts' is accurate but narrow; the clips also target TikTok and Reels.

record.short_description: Chrome extension that uses AI to draft and reply to emails from a goal and tone
record.description: Mailr is an AI email assistant delivered as a Google Chrome extension. Users give it the goal of an email in a few words, choose one of more than ten tones such as friendly, informal, or persuasive, and Mailr drafts a new email or reply in a single click from the browser. The Chrome Web Store listing says it is powered by ChatGPT. The official site states that Mailr has been acquired by MailWiz.
record.pricing_summary: Free Forever plan at $0 with a 2,000-word limit, new email composition and 10+ custom tones. Premium Tier at $4.99/month with 100,000+ words per month, faster email generation and early access to beta features.
features: Write and reply to emails in a single click
use_cases: Drafting new emails from a short instruction
Changing the tone of email communication for individuals and businesses
record.notes: The product at the listed URL is called 'Mailr' (also 'Mailr - AI Email Assistant'), not 'AI Mailer', so the directory name should be updated. I took the official homepage content (pricing tiers and the line 'Mailr has been acquired by MailWiz') from search-indexed copies of mailr-ai.com. I hit the search tool limit, so I could not load the page live a second time to re-check it. The site does not say whether development continues after the acquisition. The Chrome Web Store listing showed about 884 users and says the extension is powered by ChatGPT. The site gives a contact email (mailrofficialai@gmail.com) for anyone who needs more words. The current blurb 'Write emails quickly' is vague. A better one would mention the Chrome extension and choosing a tone. mailr.org is an unrelated open-source webmail project.

record.short_description: AI story planning app that generates branching plot options to help authors outline novels and scenes
record.description: Story Path is an AI story planning application for authors. According to a third-party directory listing, it generates branching plot options from minimal input and helps writers outline whole novels or single scenes. It reportedly suggests plot points automatically, explores 'what if?' scenarios, and supports genres from fantasy to mystery. Users can color-code paths, add or delete sequences, and backtrack to revise choices. Saved paths can be exported as PDF or Word documents. Story Path's official website could not be confirmed.
record.notes: This row needs a fix because the website doesn't match the product. The listed site, storyscapeai.app, belongs to a different product called StoryScape AI. Slashdot lists StoryScape AI with that website and describes it as a ChatGPT-powered app for choose-your-path stories. The current blurb, 'Dive into a world of immersive storytelling', also fits StoryScape AI, not Story Path. In this check, Story Path only showed up in a directory listing (topai.tools). That listing describes it as an AI plot-planning tool for authors that is paid 'from $6.99' and integrates with SceneOne. I left out that price because it doesn't come from Story Path's own site. My search limit ran out before I could open storyscapeai.app or find an official site for Story Path. Because of that, the company and status are unknown, and the features, use cases, and SceneOne integration come only from the directory. Someone should decide which product this row is meant to be. If it's Story Path, find its real website. If it's StoryScape AI, rename the row and check it against storyscapeai.app.

record.short_description: AI tool that pulls the best moments from long videos and turns them into short clips
record.description: 2short.ai is an AI video repurposing tool for content creators. It analyzes long-form videos, picks out the most engaging moments, and turns them into short clips for YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram Reels. Its site says every plan has full access to all features, and plans differ mainly by monthly hours of AI video analysis. Third-party sources also mention facial tracking, animated subtitles, multiple aspect ratios and 1080p exports without watermarks.
record.pricing_summary: The official pricing page lists a free Starter plan with 30 minutes of AI video analysis per month and full feature access, and a Lite plan at $9.90/mo with 5 hours of analysis per month.
features: AI extraction of best video moments
Vertical, square and horizontal aspect ratios
Branding presets with logos and overlays
Full feature access on all plans
use_cases: Repurposing long YouTube videos into Shorts
Creating TikToks and Instagram Reels from long-form content
Clipping podcasts, interviews and educational videos
Agencies producing short clips for multiple channels
record.notes: The official site 2short.ai is live, and its pricing page confirms the free Starter plan and the $9.90/mo Lite plan. Third-party sites (Siteefy, Shortzly, Fastlane) also list Pro at $19.90/mo for 15 hours and Premium at $49.90/mo for 50 hours. I couldn't see those tiers in the official page text I got, so they are left out of the summary. Capterra shows prices in euros with different hour limits.
