record.notes: I hit the search tool limit before I could open quadency.com or any pricing page on the product's own domain. Because of that, official_url, status, and pricing are unverified. Every claim in this record comes from third-party sources: QuickNode builders guide, ToolMage, CryptoSlate, CB Insights, Tracxn, Dealroom, and the reviews from Hedge With Crypto, Blockonomi, and CaptainAltcoin. Several of these say Quadency has been renamed Quad Terminal. I did not confirm the new domain, so a reviewer should check whether quadency.com still works or redirects. Some reviews mention a free Hodler account and paid subscriptions, but those prices are only on review sites, so I left pricing empty. No source named a buyer or said the product was discontinued. The listed URL has a referral parameter that should be removed. The current blurb is a slogan and should be replaced.

record.short_description: Shopify app that uses OpenAI GPT to generate ecommerce product titles and descriptions
record.description: ProductGPT - AI Text Generator is a Shopify app from the developer Related Code. Third-party directory listings describe it as an AI tool that uses OpenAI's GPT technology to write and improve product titles and descriptions for ecommerce stores, with the aim of cutting manual listing work. The Shopify App Store page now says the app is not currently available there. No standalone product website was found, and no current pricing or feature details could be confirmed from an official source.
record.notes: The listed URL (apps.shopify.com/productgpt) now says 'This app is not currently available on the Shopify App Store' and names Related Code as the developer. That page does not say the product is discontinued, so the status is unknown, not shutdown. official_url is left empty because the only official page is a third-party marketplace listing that is now delisted, and no standalone product site was found. The features and description come from a third-party AI directory (success.ai), not an official page. No pricing was found on an official page. I hit the search limit, so I could not check whether Related Code has its own site for the app. Suggested blurb update: say the app appears to be delisted from Shopify, or remove the row.

record.short_description: AI tool that turns plain product photos into generated scenes and backgrounds without prompts
record.description: Final Touch is a generative AI tool for product photography. Users upload a product photo, the tool identifies the item, and it suggests a range of relevant scenes. It then generates a complete scene with the product placed in it, and no design skills or text prompts are needed. It also has an advanced editing mode. The company says it is building an image and video solution for SMB owners and ecommerce sellers, and the product is currently offered as a free beta.
record.pricing_summary: The official FAQ says Final Touch is currently completely free for anyone to use during its beta, and asks users for feedback in return. No paid tiers or prices are listed.
features: Upload product photo with automatic product recognition
Fully generated AI scenes and backgrounds
Multiple images of the same product in different settings
use_cases: Refreshing website and social channel visuals
SMB product visuals without professional photography
record.notes: I confirmed the product with search-indexed copies of the official homepage, About, Terms, and Skincare pages on final-tou.ch. I didn't open the live pages directly, so I couldn't check that the site is up right now or whether the beta is still running. Pricing comes from the homepage FAQ, which says the tool is free for now, so this may change once the beta ends. The site calls the program both 'free beta' and 'Alpha'/'Early Access'. One third-party directory (aitoolsvault) says the team behind Cloudinary built it. No official page I found confirms this, so I left it out. The current blurb 'Optimize your product visuals!' is vague. It would be more accurate to say it generates AI product scenes and backgrounds. Final Touch Geneva (final-touch.ch) is a different company, a jewelry and candle shop.

record.short_description: Free desktop web browser from Opera with Aria, a built-in AI assistant, and a customizable interface
record.description: Opera One is a desktop web browser made by Opera. Opera says it was the first browser to ship with a built-in browser AI, called Aria. Users can open Aria from a command line with Ctrl+/ or Cmd+/, rework its answers with a Refiner tool, and write content from ready-made prompts. Third-party listings say it also includes a built-in VPN, an ad blocker, a battery saver, YouTube pop-outs, Speed Dial shortcuts and support for extensions. It is listed as freeware.
features: Command line access to Aria (Ctrl+/ or Cmd+/)
Refiner tool with Reuse and Rephrase
record.notes: The search tool hit its limit after the first round, so I could not open the listed URL (opera.com/fr/one) or any opera.com product or pricing page. The Aria AI details come from Opera's own investor news release (investor.opera.com). The 'free' price, the Windows freeware/ad-supported label, and the VPN, ad-blocker, battery-saver, pop-out and Speed Dial features come only from a Softpedia download listing. Because that is a third-party site, pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are empty. Status is set to active because Opera's domain is live and still promotes Opera One, but the product page itself was not checked. The current blurb is vague: it calls the browser 'modular', which the pages I saw did not mention. A better blurb would name the built-in Aria AI.

record.short_description: K-12 writing practice platform with teacher-led, curriculum-aligned lessons and classroom reports
record.description: Curipod is a K-12 classroom platform from a Norway-based company that now presents itself mainly as a writing practice tool. Teachers run whole-class lessons aligned with district curricula such as HMH Into Reading and Amplify CKLA, and students read, write and discuss together. Each lesson produces reports that help teachers spot learning gaps and adjust instruction. The site says it is FERPA, COPPA and GDPR compliant, that students do not need accounts, and that it works with ClassLink, Clever and Google sign-on.
features: Reports and insights from every lesson
Single sign-on via ClassLink, Clever and Google
use_cases: Tier 1 and Tier 2 instruction alongside core curriculum
Spotting learning gaps and differentiating instruction
record.notes: Search results included the curipod.com homepage, which is live and titled 'Writing Practice Students Love'. It offers 'Sign Up For Free' and a separate School or District option. The current blurb ('Animate your classes with interactivity and AI support') is out of date: the site now focuses on curriculum-aligned writing practice rather than general interactive slides. I couldn't open curipod.com/pricing, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are empty. Pricing figures appear only on third-party sites. Older sites list a $9/month or $7.50/month Premium plan. Newer ones say there are now only two tiers: a free plan with weekly sessions and a School & District plan priced by quote. Freemium is inferred from the free signup and the school/district offer on the homepage. The About page names Jens Seip as CEO. LinkedIn lists the headquarters as Bergen, Norway. I found no evidence that the product was acquired or shut down.

record.short_description: Generative AI platform that automates research and deal workflow tasks for M&A, VC and PE teams
record.description: Eilla AI is a London-based generative AI platform for professionals in mergers and acquisitions, venture capital and private equity. It automates routine deal-workflow tasks such as building company profiles, market mapping, buyer selection and competitor analysis. It pulls data from trusted providers and turns it into industry-style documents. Third-party sources say it anonymises sensitive data. The company was founded in 2022, raised a $1.5M seed round in November 2023 led by Eleven Ventures with Fuel Ventures, and officially launched in November 2024.
features: Document creation such as one-pagers and executive summaries
use_cases: Venture capital deal sourcing and due diligence
record.notes: My search tool hit its usage limit, so I could not open eilla.ai or a pricing page on its domain. Everything here comes from third-party pages: the Orrick and EU-Startups funding coverage (Nov 2023), the Maddyness launch article (Nov 2024, which lists the Crunchbase, Capital IQ, Beauhurst and LinkedIn integrations), and Dealroom, Tracxn, Capterra, TechBriefly and ToolPilot. Because of that, status is set to unknown and pricing is left empty. The pricing found elsewhere conflicts and is only on third-party sites. Software Advice says pricing is available on request. TechBriefly and AIChief describe a success-fee M&A advisory service for SMB sellers with no upfront fees, which may mean the product has pivoted. xpay.sh claims a $37/mo plan plus a free tier, but it files the product as an AI writing assistant, which looks unreliable. The current blurb broadly matches older third-party descriptions. Someone should check the live eilla.ai homepage and its /pricing page before publishing.

record.short_description: AI tool that generates and explains Excel and Google Sheets formulas from plain-language descriptions
record.description: Sheet+ is an AI tool for people who work in Excel and Google Sheets. Users describe what they need in plain English and get a formula back. They can also paste in an existing formula to get an explanation or help finding errors. Directory listings say it offered Google Sheets and Excel add-ons and traced it to sheetplus.ai. That domain is now listed for sale, and no live official site for the product could be confirmed.
record.notes: The listed website, formulagenerator.app, does not appear to be Sheet+. In search results it is a content page about AI prompts for formulas. G2 links that domain to a different product called FormulaGenerator, and no page tied it to Sheet+. Several directories, including Brandfetch, bestofai.io and dang.ai, show Sheet+ at sheetplus.ai. Brandfetch says sheetplus.ai is now a domain for sale. dang.ai marked SheetPlus as shut down on Apr 16, 2024, but says it 'may have closed, been acquired, or moved.' No official discontinuation notice was found, so status is unknown rather than shutdown. All prices came from third-party sites only, and they disagree: SourceForge says from $5.99/mo, dang.ai says $6.49/mo or $51.99/yr, and buildfastwithai says $4/mo. No price was found on the product's own domain, so pricing is left empty. Features and integrations also come from third-party directories. I could not open these pages directly, and the search tool hit its usage limit before more checks could run. The current blurb is a vague slogan. Recommend removing the listing or replacing the URL until a live official site is confirmed.

record.short_description: AI writing and copywriting platform with 150+ tools for blogs, ads, and social content
record.description: Nichesss is an AI writing and copywriting platform. It generates blog posts, ads, social media content, business ideas, and poems from short inputs. Third-party listings say it offers more than 150 writing tools, including author bios, blog post outlines, book titles, and descriptions. They also mention a long-form editor and an AI Art Prompt Helper for DALL-E 2 or Stable Diffusion. Other features reported are niche and Reddit research, API access, webhooks, a Chrome extension, and image generation.
use_cases: Writing product descriptions and email content
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit before I could open nichesss.com or its pricing page directly, so every detail here comes from third-party pages: futuretools.io, theresanaiforthat.com, softwarefinder.com, coldiq.com and thelifetimedeal.com. The product name is spelled 'Nichesss' (three s's), not 'Nichess' as in the row; theresanaiforthat also lists it as 'Nichess'. Pricing appears only on review and directory sites (softwarefinder: Rookie $19/mo, Intermediate $39/mo, Pro $99, Lifetime $1188; coldiq: from $19/mo with a trial; thelifetimedeal: a $59 AppSumo lifetime deal). I left pricing fields empty because none of these prices are confirmed on the product's own domain. A free trial or starter allowance is mentioned only by third parties, so free_tier is set to false. A thelifetimedeal.com review (about 142 days old) says the site is live with a 2026 footer and founder Malcolm Tyson. No formal company name was found. Status is unknown because I couldn't check the site myself, and no page says it was shut down or acquired. The current blurb loosely matches the reported tagline 'Write anything 10x faster with AI.' Re-check the official homepage and pricing page before publishing.

record.short_description: AI assistant built into Microsoft 365 work apps, with chat and agents for business users
record.description: Microsoft 365 Copilot is Microsoft's AI assistant for work. It is built into the existing Microsoft 365 experience and combines large language models with an organization's own data. Microsoft's pages list AI chat, Copilot inside its apps, ready-made agents for work, and tools for building custom agents. Copilot Studio covers building apps, workflows, and agents. Through its Copilot Adoption Hub, Microsoft also offers onboarding resources such as the Copilot Success Kit, which includes enablement guides, readiness guides, and planning checklists.
record.pricing_summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot Business is listed at $18 per user/month paid yearly (originally $21), or $25.20 per user/month on a monthly plan. Bundles include Business Standard with Copilot at $23.50 per user/month paid yearly, and no-Teams versions of Business Standard with Copilot at $20.30 and Business Premium with Copilot at $28.80 per user/month paid yearly.
features: Copilot Studio for building apps, workflows, and agents
use_cases: Rolling out Copilot to employees and tracking adoption
Sales work in the flow of Microsoft 365
record.notes: The listed website (adoption.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/) is Microsoft's Copilot Adoption Hub. It offers rollout and training resources, not the product or pricing page, so official_url was changed to the Microsoft 365 Copilot product page on microsoft.com. I did not open that root product URL directly. I inferred it from the /business and /pricing-without-teams subpages I did open. Prices come from Microsoft's business pricing pages, and the Business tier is described there as a limited-time discount. Third-party sites mention a $30/user/month Enterprise add-on and a free consumer Copilot, but I did not confirm either on a Microsoft page, so they are left out and free_tier is false. Microsoft's Copilot branding covers several products (consumer Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Copilot Studio), so this row should state which one it means. The current blurb fits Microsoft 365 Copilot. My search budget ran out before I could open an Enterprise pricing page.

record.short_description: AI mind mapping and brainstorming tool from the Xmind team that builds mind maps through chat
record.description: Chatmind is an online AI mind mapping and brainstorming tool made by the Xmind team. Users describe what they want or chat with an AI assistant, and Chatmind builds and edits mind maps from that conversation. Its official homepage says it is powered by ChatGPT and can produce a mind map in minutes. Several third-party sources say the product has since been renamed Mapify, still under Xmind. This could not be confirmed on an official page.
record.notes: I found the official homepage (home.chatmind.tech) only as a search result snippet, which describes Chatmind as a free online AI mind map tool from the Xmind team. I could not open the page directly to confirm it is still up or to read pricing, because my search tool limit was reached. Prices on third-party sites disagree: SaaSworthy and SourceForge list $3.99/month, and other sites list Basic at $9.99 and Pro at $19.99. None of these come from Chatmind's own domain, so pricing is left empty. Third-party sources (UPDF, ConversionGems) say Chatmind was renamed Mapify under Xmind. This looks like a rebrand, not a sale, so status is not set to acquired. Someone should check whether chatmind.tech now redirects to Mapify and update the listing. The current blurb is a slogan and should be replaced.

record.short_description: AI-powered platform that scores, analyzes, and helps founders validate startup and business ideas
record.description: ValidatorAI is an AI-powered platform for validating startup ideas. It was created by entrepreneur Aron Meystedt and has been running since 2022. Founders answer questions about an idea and get a score and analysis. The platform helps them clarify the value proposition, analyze competitors, find target customers, simulate customer feedback, and test assumptions. It also suggests next steps. An AI mentor called Val helps users come up with ideas, and the site publishes founder-behavior data and a weekly newsletter.
record.pricing_summary: A ValidatorAI article says the AI validator tool is free. Users who want more can book phone calls with Val, listed at $49 for 3 calls.
features: Startup idea scoring and analysis in 15 seconds
use_cases: Validating a startup idea before building
Companies thinking through ideas they want to implement
record.notes: The site is up at validatorai.com (the listed www URL is the same site). The current blurb 'Validate your business projects' is vague and should be updated. I didn't open a dedicated pricing page. A third-party site (anygen.io) says chat.validatorai.com/pricing lists a free Standard plan and a PRO plan at $25/month, but I couldn't confirm that on the official domain, so it isn't in pricing_summary. The $49-for-3-calls price comes from a dated article on validatorai.com and may have changed. I found no integrations. My searches hit the tool limit before I could open the docs or pricing pages.

record.short_description: No-code AI chatbot platform for automating sales and support on WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook
record.description: Chatfuel is an AI chatbot platform that lets businesses automate customer conversations on WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook. Its AI answers customer messages around the clock and can qualify and score leads, sell products in the chat, reply to post and Reels comments, send bulk WhatsApp campaigns, and book meetings. It also syncs WhatsApp with CRMs and sends WhatsApp conversions to Meta Pixel. There is a Business plan for single companies and an Agency tier for running AI assistants for multiple clients.
record.pricing_summary: Chatfuel's pricing page lists the Business plan at US$18 per month billed yearly (US$216 per year), with US$20 in AI credits each month. An Agency tier is also offered, and every plan starts with a free trial.
features: AI replies to customers 24/7 on Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook
Selling products and services in the chat
Automatic replies to post comments and Reels comments
Sending WhatsApp conversions to Meta Pixel
Monthly AI credits included in plans
Chatfuel MCP for running bots from Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor
use_cases: Agencies running AI assistants for clients
record.notes: I could only use one round of searches. Everything here comes from a search snippet of chatfuel.com/pricing; I could not open the homepage or the docs, and I did not find a separate monthly-billing price on Chatfuel's own site. Third-party sites quote conflicting prices: $20 per month billed monthly, a $69 standard rate, older $39 to $279 contact-based tiers, and $23.99. One also says the help center lists a $0 free plan. None of these were confirmed on chatfuel.com, so I set free_tier to false. A GitHub page called 'Chatfuel-AI' looks like a third-party SEO page, not the official one. The current blurb is accurate but narrow: the product also covers Instagram and Facebook, not just WhatsApp.

record.short_description: AI notetaker that records, transcribes, and summarizes Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams meetings
record.description: Fathom is an AI meeting assistant made by Fathom Video Inc. It joins Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams calls and records video, audio, and a searchable transcript. When a call ends, it produces summaries and action items. Users can make clips and playlists, search across past calls, and ask questions about their meeting history with Ask Fathom. Paid team plans add CRM field sync, deal summaries, coaching metrics, and admin and security controls. Mac users can also record without a bot joining the call.
record.pricing_summary: Individuals: Free at $0, and Premium at $16/user/month billed annually or $20 monthly. Teams (2-user minimum): Team at $15/user/month annually or $19 monthly, Business at $25/user/month annually or $34 monthly, plus an Enterprise tier with SSO/SCIM and custom data retention.
features: Clips, playlists, and search across calls
use_cases: Sales call intelligence and CRM updates
record.notes: The listed site, fathom.video, works, and its pricing page loaded. Fathom also publishes product pages on fathom.ai (overview, integrations, comparisons), so that may now be the main domain. I did not confirm whether fathom.video redirects to it. The pricing page showed an Enterprise tier with an unclear '$34' figure and no clear per-user price, so I left that number out. Reviews describe the Free plan's advanced AI summaries as limited to 5 calls per month, but the official page I opened did not confirm this. Asana comes from third-party sources and fathom.ai pages. HubSpot, Salesforce, Close, and Zapier are listed in Fathom's own Trustpilot company description. The company name comes from the Chrome Web Store developer listing. The current blurb 'Improve your meeting productivity' is vague and could be replaced with the short description.

record.short_description: AI code review and test generation platform with IDE plugins and pull request review tools
record.description: Qodo is the company formerly called CodiumAI. It renamed itself in September 2024. It started with an IDE extension that wrote meaningful tests and explained code for developers. Its products now cover more: Qodo Gen, an IDE plugin formerly called Codiumate, gives context-aware help with writing code and tests. Qodo also offers AI code review, including a VS Code plugin that lets developers review their own local changes and fix issues before they commit code.
features: Context-aware code generation in the IDE
Self review of local code changes before commit
use_cases: Catching bugs before code is committed
Maintaining code quality in AI-driven development
record.notes: CodiumAI renamed itself Qodo in September 2024. The official qodo.ai blog post confirms the rename, so the listed website (codium.ai) is out of date. Update the name and URL to Qodo / https://www.qodo.ai. This was a rebrand, not an acquisition, so status is active. My search tool hit its usage limit before I could open the official qodo.ai pricing page. Pricing is therefore left empty. Third-party sites (dev.to, costbench, mstone.ai, trystackd) report a free Developer tier, a Teams plan at $30/user/month, and custom Enterprise pricing with a credit system. None of that is confirmed on qodo.ai, so free_tier is false and pricing_type is unknown. The VS Code Marketplace listing (publisher qodo.ai) shows the extension as Free. JetBrains support comes from a third-party source only. The old blurb ('code tests') is out of date because the product now focuses on AI code review as well as tests. Don't confuse it with Codium/VSCodium, which is an unrelated open-source build of VS Code.

record.short_description: AI tabletop RPG platform inspired by D&D 5e, with an AI Game Master named Franz
record.description: Friends & Fables is an AI-powered tabletop roleplaying platform inspired by Dungeons & Dragons 5e. Players can explore thousands of worlds made by other players or build their own, then play campaigns run by Franz, an AI Game Master who adapts the story to their choices. The platform includes worldbuilding tools, character sheets, turn-based combat and multiplayer campaigns. Friends can join a subscriber's campaign for free. Paid plans add unlimited turns, text to speech and larger parties.
record.pricing_summary: The official pricing page lists Legend at $39.95/month (unlimited standard turns, 6-player campaigns, text to speech, 600 bonus monthly credits) and a Pro tier with 5-player campaigns and 300 bonus credits. A late-2025 post on the company's blog lists Free at $0 (5-25 AI turns per day, up to 3-player campaigns), Starter at $19.95/month and Pro at $29.95/month, with lower yearly rates.
features: AI Game Master (Franz) that adapts to player choices
Multiplayer campaigns where friends play free
use_cases: Playing TTRPG campaigns solo without a human DM
Running group campaigns without scheduling conflicts
AI text adventure inspired by D&D
record.notes: The site is up at fables.gg (the listed URL uses www). The current blurb is accurate but brief. The homepage claims more than 100,000 players and world builders. Search results only showed part of the official pricing page: Legend at $39.95/month and some Pro features. The Free, Starter ($19.95) and Pro ($29.95) prices come from the company's own blog comparison posts dated late 2025, so they may have changed. Prices on third-party sites didn't match each other or the official page, so I didn't use them. The company name, Side Quest Labs, comes from a competitor's article that quotes the product's About page; I didn't open the About page myself. I found no integrations on official pages. Further searches were blocked by a tool limit.

record.short_description: Discontinued AI voice platform for text-to-speech, voice cloning and a developer TTS API
record.description: Play.ht, also known as PlayHT and later PlayAI, was an AI voice platform that turned text into speech. It offered AI voices, voice cloning and a text-to-speech API with a Python SDK for developers. Meta acquired the PlayAI team in July 2025. Several sources say the API went offline in late July 2025 and the platform shut down for good on December 31, 2025. They also report that accounts, voice clones and saved audio were deleted at that point.
record.notes: Change the row to discontinued. Bloomberg reported on Jul 11, 2025 that Meta acquired PlayAI, the company behind PlayHT. Several third-party pages say the platform shut down permanently on Dec 31, 2025 and all data was deleted: Inworld migration guide, notevibes, anyspeech, theplanettools and voiceaispace. One source says play.ht no longer resolves. I could not open play.ht or find a shutdown notice on the product's own domain, so the shutdown status comes from third-party sources. Prices on TrustRadius, SaaSworthy and review blogs conflict and are not from the official domain, so I left pricing empty. playht.co and playht.app look like unrelated lookalike sites and should not be used. The listed URL is an affiliate link (?via=artifimedia) and should be removed. Features come from the archived official GitHub repo, the pyht package and third-party profiles.

record.short_description: Desktop AI image enhancement app for upscaling, denoising, sharpening and restoring focus in photos
record.description: Topaz Photo, formerly called Topaz Photo AI, is a desktop application from Topaz Labs that uses AI models to improve photo quality. It can sharpen details, restore focus, remove noise, upscale, adjust lighting, balance color and recover faces, and an autopilot mode can pick settings to start from. It runs on Mac and Windows and supports both local and cloud rendering. Topaz Labs, based in Addison, Texas, also includes Topaz Photo in its Topaz Studio subscription bundle.
record.pricing_summary: The official Topaz Photo page lists the plan as starting at $17/mo, billed annually. Topaz Photo is also included in the Topaz Studio subscription bundle.
use_cases: Upscaling and preparing images for print
record.notes: Topaz has renamed the product from 'Topaz Photo AI' to 'Topaz Photo', so the directory name should be updated. The listed website (topazlabs.com) is the company homepage. The product page is /topaz-photo. The current blurb works, but it's slogan-like. The 'From $17/mo billed annually' price comes from the official product page, but the search index has that page as about 395 days old, so the price may be out of date. Third-party sites quote different prices: $199/yr, $58/mo or $252/yr, and $39/mo with no commitment. I couldn't open the official pricing page to check, so treat the price as unconfirmed. An old topazlabs.com shop page lists 'Topaz Photo AI Monthly' at $35/month, which looks like a legacy listing. A third-party site mentions a demo mode and says perpetual licenses ended in September 2025. I couldn't confirm either on the official site, so free_tier is set to false. Lightroom/Photoshop plugin support wasn't confirmed on any page I opened, so integrations is left empty. I hit the search limit before I could check the pricing page or the docs.

record.short_description: AI tool that swaps photo backgrounds for realistic scenes matched to the subject's angle and lighting
record.description: ZMO.AI Background Changer is an AI photo editing tool from ZMO.AI, part of its ImgCreator suite. Users upload a photo and either pick a background filter or type a text description of the scene they want. The AI then generates a realistic background that matches the angle and lighting of the original subject, including shadows. The same suite also includes a background remover, a Magic Remover for unwanted objects, and an Image Variation tool. The product is aimed at product and portrait photos.
features: Realistic background generation matching foreground angle and lighting
Free background remover usable without logging in
Magic Remover for watermarks and unwanted objects
record.notes: I couldn't open pages directly because the search tool hit its usage limit, so this record is based on search-result snippets. The ZMO.AI page at zmo.ai/imgcreator/background-changer says the Background Remover is free and that high-resolution results need a Pro membership, which supports listing it as freemium with a free tier. The listed URL imgcreator.zmo.ai/background-changer did not show up in results. The matching page found was www.zmo.ai/imgcreator/background-changer, and zmo.ai/imgcreator/tools-background-changer also exists. I found no pricing page on zmo.ai. Prices only appeared on third-party directories, and they disagree with each other. They include a Starter plan with 300 credits a month, and fashion-model plans of either $49/$149/$599 or $59/$199/$799. So I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. One directory, startupstacked, says the main zmo.ai domain now redirects to Creati while the older ImgCreator pages still work. I couldn't confirm this or find any buyer named, so status is active, not acquired. The current blurb is accurate but narrow. The tool works on portraits as well as product photos.

record.short_description: E-commerce platform for building online stores and selling online and in person, with built-in AI tools
record.description: Shopify is a commerce platform that lets businesses build and run an online store, take payments, and sell online and in person. Its plans run from entry-level stores up to Shopify Plus for high-volume brands. Shopify Magic is a set of free AI features built into Shopify's products. It writes text such as product descriptions. Sidekick is an AI assistant in the Shopify admin that takes plain-language commands to answer store questions and carry out tasks.
features: Sidekick AI assistant in the Shopify admin
Multi-storefront and wholesale on Shopify Plus
use_cases: Scaling high-volume e-commerce with Shopify Plus
record.notes: The listed website (shopify.pxf.io/artifimedia) is an affiliate tracking link, not the official site, so the official URL should be https://www.shopify.com. The official Help Center (help.shopify.com) confirms that Shopify Magic is a suite of free AI features. My search quota ran out before I could open shopify.com/pricing. The only prices I found came from third-party sites: Basic $39/mo, Grow $105/mo, Advanced $399/mo, Plus from $2,300/mo, with some sites also listing a $5 Starter plan. Those numbers are not confirmed on Shopify's own domain, so I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. I marked the pricing type as paid based on third-party sources. I did not confirm a free tier or trial terms on shopify.com. The current blurb's claim of 'World's No. 1' is marketing, not something I verified, and should be replaced.

record.short_description: AI video generator that turns product pages or descriptions into product videos with AI presenters
record.description: Oxolo is an AI-powered video creation platform for producing product and marketing videos without editing experience. Users can enter a product URL, write a product description, or start from a template. The AI analyzes the product page, pulls out key selling points, writes a script, and picks visuals and music. It then produces a finished video with AI-generated presenters and voiceovers in multiple languages. A built-in editor lets users adjust scenes, add branding, and upload their own media.
features: Generate video from a product URL
Generate video from a written product description
use_cases: Scaling video marketing across a product catalog
Marketing videos for WooCommerce store owners
record.notes: My search tool limit ran out before I could open oxolo.com or its pricing page. That means the official site, its current status, and its pricing are all unconfirmed, so status is set to unknown. The official_url is the listed website, and third-party pages (AppSumo, OMR) also point to oxolo.com. The features come from third-party sources: a wbcomdesigns review (about 146 days old), the AppSumo listing, and Capterra. I could only find prices on review sites, so pricing_summary is left empty and free_tier is set to false. G2 (last updated Oct 2024) lists a free plan with 15 credits, Basic from $24.99/month for 300 credits, Business from $149/month for 2,400 credits, and a custom-priced Enterprise plan. OMR shows older yearly prices, and Capterra lists a starting price of $12.50 per user per month. Pricing and the free plan should be checked on oxolo.com/pricing before publishing. The current blurb roughly fits, but the sources describe Oxolo more broadly as AI-generated product videos with AI presenters and voiceovers. I found no evidence that Oxolo was shut down or acquired, but my search for that turned up no relevant results either way.

record.short_description: Email warm-up and deliverability monitoring tool from lemlist for mailboxes used in cold outreach
record.description: Lemwarm is an email warm-up and deliverability tool made by lemlist. Users connect a mailbox and set a target daily volume and a ramp-up increment. Lemwarm then raises sending volume gradually and tracks a deliverability score. lemlist says it handles authentication setup, matches providers such as Gmail to Gmail, and offers a dashboard with alerts and mailbox-level audits. Users can start, stop, and monitor warm-up from a lemwarm workspace. lemlist says lemwarm is included with every lemlist seat.
record.pricing_summary: lemlist says lemwarm is included with every lemlist seat at no extra cost, and warm-up is available during lemlist's 14-day trial. No standalone lemwarm price was confirmed on an official page.
features: Configurable warm-up volume and ramp-up increment
Start, stop, and monitor warm-up from lemwarm workspace
use_cases: Warming up new mailboxes before cold outreach
Rebuilding sender reputation after a deliverability incident
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit, so I could not open lemwarm.com directly. The listed URL is kept but not confirmed. Its status (active) and the details here come from lemlist's own help center (help.lemlist.com, updated about 39 days ago) and lemlist.com blog posts. Third-party review sites (mailreach.co, mailivery.io, salesdorado.com) list standalone plans: Essential at $29 per inbox per month and Smart at $49 per inbox per month, with lower prices on annual billing. These prices were not confirmed on an official lemwarm or lemlist page, so they are left out of pricing_summary. lemwarm can be used during lemlist's 14-day trial, but that is a trial, not a free tier. The current blurb, 'Avoid spam and double your revenue', is a slogan, and the revenue claim was not verified. I suggest replacing it.

record.short_description: AI-powered tool for writing, scheduling, and analyzing posts to grow an audience on X (formerly Twitter)
record.description: Tweet Hunter is a growth and monetization tool for creators and brands on X, formerly Twitter. It offers a searchable library of viral tweets and staff-picked tweets for inspiration. It also includes AI writing for tweet suggestions, rewrites, and thread ideas, along with tweet scheduling and analytics. Higher plans add an X CRM, Auto-DMs, and a ghostwriting mode for managing multiple accounts. Tweet Hunter was founded by Thibault Louis-Lucas and Tom Jacquesson and was later acquired by lempire, the maker of lemlist.
record.pricing_summary: The pricing page lists Discover at $29/mo with 1 X account, Grow at $49/mo with 5 X accounts plus the AI writer and CRM, and Enterprise at $200/mo with unlimited accounts, 15,000 Auto-DMs/month, ghostwriting mode, and priority support. Each plan starts with a 7-day free trial, and there are monthly and yearly billing options.
features: Viral tweets library (3M+ on homepage, over 12M on pricing page)
Tweet Hunter X sidebar Chrome extension
use_cases: Generating sales, subscribers, and clients through X
Scheduling a month of tweets in one sitting
Managing multiple X accounts for professionals
record.notes: The official site and pricing page are live. Prices come from a search snapshot of tweethunter.io/pricing, which also showed a 50% off limited-time deal and a monthly/yearly toggle, so the amounts shown may depend on the billing period. Third-party sites list older prices ($49/$99), which conflict with the current page. The viral-library size is inconsistent across pages: the homepage says 3M+ and the pricing page says over 12M. Status is set to acquired because lempire's own blog and Indie Hackers say lempire (maker of lemlist) bought Tweet Hunter and Taplio in 2022. The product still appears active. There is no free plan, only a 7-day free trial. The current blurb is accurate but mentions Twitter; the product now brands itself around X.

record.short_description: AI assistant offering specialist copilots for legal, health, finance and career questions across browsers and mobile
record.description: Copilotly is an AI assistant that offers specialist copilots across professional areas such as legal, health, finance and career. Its homepage lists 131 specialist copilots across 20 domains, cites sources inline, and compares itself with general-purpose chatbots. It is available as a Chrome extension, iOS and Android apps, and a desktop app for Mac and PC. The site says its answers are for educational purposes and do not replace a lawyer, doctor, financial advisor or therapist.
record.pricing_summary: The pricing page lists a Free plan at $0/month (8,000 GPT-4 words and 15,000 GPT-3.5 words per month), a $29/month plan (150,000 GPT-4 words, 5 team members) and a $59/month plan (300,000 GPT-4 words, 10 team members), with extra words at $0.50 per 5,000 on the paid plans.
features: 131 specialist AI copilots across 20 professional domains
Free plan with no card required
integrations: Desktop app for Mac and PC
record.notes: I found the official site and pricing page through search results. The pages may not have been fetched live, so the text could be a cached copy. The homepage now says 131 copilots across 20 domains and mentions a 'Pro' plan, but the pricing page still lists '50+ copilots' and word limits for GPT-4 and GPT-3.5. That suggests the pricing page is out of date, so the tiers should be checked again. Crunchbase and CB Insights (not the official site) say the company is in Bangalore, India, was founded in 2022, and lists Deepak Muni. Copilotly.net is a different product, a meeting assistant, and is not related. The current blurb is vague and should be replaced; the product is now pitched as a set of specialist copilots, not a general task assistant. aitoolguru.com lists paid plans from $29/mo, which matches the official page.

record.short_description: WebKit-based Mac web browser that organizes tabs into workspaces and includes an AI assistant called Airis
record.description: SigmaOS is a web browser built for work. It sorts tabs into separate workspaces, such as one for each project, and lets users group pages, split the screen, snooze pages and switch between logins. Its AI assistant, Airis, can chat about the page that is open, find information and explain paragraphs. The browser also has an ad blocker and a focus mode. It uses Apple's WebKit engine and can run Chromium extensions. The basic version is free, and a paid Pro plan is available.
record.pricing_summary: The official site's FAQ says SigmaOS Personal is free forever and SigmaOS Pro, which adds unlimited Airis usage, starts at $20 a month. Students and educators get 50% off Pro.
features: Airis AI assistant (chat with any website)
use_cases: Organizing browsing by project or role
Multitasking with two pages at once
Staying focused on one page at a time
record.notes: I found the official site through search results and didn't open it directly, so all details come from search snippets. The pages I saw don't say the product is shut down or acquired. Pricing sources conflict. The homepage FAQ says Pro starts at $20 a month. An older docs page (docs.sigmaos.com/common-questions) lists Personal Pro at $10 a month, or $8 a month billed yearly, with a 14-day trial and 50% off for students. I used the homepage figure because it appears to be newer, but neither price was confirmed on a live pricing page. AlternativeTo names the developer as SigmaOS Software Limited (UK), but I couldn't confirm that on the official site. Third-party sites call it Mac-only, which the official pages I saw didn't state. The old blurb 'Transform your browsing with SigmaOS' is a slogan and should be replaced.

record.short_description: AI lip-sync platform for translating, correcting, and regenerating spoken dialogue in existing video content
record.description: Deepshot is an AI lip-sync platform that changes the spoken dialogue in existing videos. Users upload their footage, write a new script, and Deepshot creates matching speech and lip movements. This lets them translate videos into other languages, fix mistakes without reshooting, make alternative hooks for ads, and keep training material up to date. It is aimed at content creators, marketers, and teams. The subscription plans are credit-based and include voice creation, a commercial license, and HD output.
record.pricing_summary: There are four monthly subscription plans: Tester at $10/month (1,000 credits, about 10 min of SD video), Starter at $25/month (2,500 credits, HD), Creator at $50/month (5,000 credits) and Pro at $100/month (10,000 credits, beta model access). Every plan includes a commercial license.
features: Dialogue replacement from a new script
use_cases: Creative testing of hooks and ad variants
record.notes: The site at deepshot.ai is up and calls the product an AI lip-sync tool for translating, reshooting, testing and reimagining video content. The current French blurb ('generate your videos easily') is vague and should be replaced. Pricing came from deepshot.org/subscriptions. That page is titled as Deepshot's own pricing page and is written in the first person, but I could not confirm that deepshot.ai links to it. Check that deepshot.org is an official Deepshot domain before publishing the price. Third-party directories list a 'free trial' or a free tier (Capterra, There's An AI For That) and different starting prices ($5, $15, $35, $79). None of this was confirmed on an official page, so it is not included. The pricing page FAQ says only that some plans add free weekly credits. No integrations were found. A search tool limit stopped further checks.

record.short_description: AI clip generator that turns long videos, streams and podcasts into captioned short-form social clips
record.description: Spikes Studio is a browser-based AI video tool that repurposes long-form content, such as Twitch streams, podcasts, webinars and YouTube videos, into short vertical clips. Its AI looks for engaging moments, then adds captions, reframing and transitions. It can also generate titles, hashtags and descriptions. The platform includes a social media scheduler and analytics for publishing to TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. It is aimed at streamers, podcasters, marketers and agencies.
use_cases: Turning podcasts into short video snippets
Creating TikTok, Reels and YouTube Shorts from long videos
record.notes: I couldn't open the official site (spikes.studio) or its pricing page because the search tool hit its usage limit, so everything here comes from third-party directories and review sites. Several of those sites point to spikes.studio as the product's domain. Status is set to active only because of recent third-party activity: a review from about 18 days ago, and xpay.sh says it read spikes.studio/pricing live in May 2026. Neither confirms the site is up today. The free plan is reported by many directories, but not by a page on the product's own domain. I left the price fields empty because the only prices I found are on third-party sites, and those sites disagree. xpay.sh and MakerStack list Free; PRO+ at $32.99/mo or $14.09/mo billed annually; and Enterprise at $115.99/mo or $56.34/mo billed annually. Other sites list $12.99, $19, $5 or $2 starting prices. MakerStack also says the company is a Tel Aviv team founded in 2020, but I haven't verified that. The current blurb matches how sources describe the product, but it reads like a slogan. Check the official site before publishing.

record.short_description: No-code platform for building custom AI chatbots for customer support and lead generation on websites
record.description: Chatling is a no-code platform for building custom AI chatbots that handle customer conversations on websites. Users build chatbots in a visual drag-and-drop builder without writing code. Chatling's own pages describe using the chatbots to answer FAQs and common questions, capture and qualify leads, and handle order updates and returns. It offers customizable templates for these tasks. Its pricing has a free plan and paid plans that add more AI credits, chatbots, customization options and API access.
record.pricing_summary: A Chatling blog post lists three plans: Free at $0/month, Starter at $25/month and Ultimate at $99/month. A third-party guide lists Starter at $29/month instead, so this price may be out of date.
features: Train chatbot on documents or website link
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit before I could open Chatling's official pricing page or homepage. The details above come from chatling.ai pages that showed up in search results: a lead-generation use-case page and blog posts. The pricing figures come from a Chatling blog post that is about 190 days old, not from a dedicated pricing page. That post gives Starter at $25/month. An eesel.ai pricing guide gives Starter at $29/month ($290/year) and Ultimate at $99/month ($990/year). Check Starter's price on chatling.ai/pricing before publishing. The Zapier integration and training from documents or a website link come only from the eesel.ai guide. Remove the ?ref=essor tracking parameter from the listed URL. The current blurb matches Chatling's own wording ('Create custom AI chatbots without any coding').

record.short_description: Business account for multi-currency payments, international transfers, team cards, and spending controls
record.description: Revolut Business is a business account and finance app from Revolut Ltd. Companies use it to accept and make payments, hold and exchange money in several currencies, and send local and international transfers. Teams can get cards while the business sets spending limits and member permissions. Higher plans add more free transfers and currency exchange, bulk payments, and API access. Revolut also offers savings accounts for business cash in some regions, including the EEA. Plans range from a free Basic tier to custom Enterprise pricing.
record.notes: The listed website is a referral sign-up link (promo=referabusiness), not the product's homepage. Replace it with the official site, https://www.revolut.com/business/. I could not open that URL during this check because the search tool limit was reached, so it is based on Revolut's own social profiles and App Store listing (developer: Revolut Ltd). Plan prices came only from third-party review sites (financer.com, joinsecret.com), so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are blank. Those sites list US plans as Basic $0/month, Grow $30/month, Scale $119/month and custom Enterprise. They also say annual billing saves up to 22% and that prices vary by region. Check these on Revolut's own pricing page. The free tier and freemium label also rely on those third-party sites. The integrations list is empty because no source I opened confirmed any. The current blurb is generic; a better one would mention business accounts, multi-currency payments and spending controls.

record.short_description: AI-powered podcast player with search inside episodes, transcripts, chapters, clipping, and highlights
record.description: Fathom is a podcast player that uses AI to transcribe and analyze podcast content for search and discovery. Listeners can ask natural-language questions and get short podcast highlights that answer them. The app also offers personalized recommendations, AI-generated previews, transcripts, AI-generated chapters, clip sharing, and custom highlight feeds called stations. Fathom.fm was co-founded by Paul Bloch and Ken Miller and launched in 2022 on iPhone and the web, with seed funding from investors including LAUNCH.
use_cases: Finding specific moments or topics inside podcast episodes
record.notes: The search-indexed text for hello.fathom.fm calls Fathom a podcast player with AI-powered search, transcripts, chapters, clipping, and highlights. The listed URL is correct, and fathom.fm podcast pages are still indexed. The current blurb, 'Discover hand-picked podcasts for you', is outdated. The product is now described as AI-driven discovery, not hand-picked curation. Press releases from June 2022 and January 2023 name co-founders Paul Bloch and Ken Miller and say the app launched on iOS and the web. No pricing page was found on the product's domain, so pricing and free tier are unknown. The LinkedIn company page slug is 'fathom-labs', but the page name is Fathom.fm. No page was found that says the product was shut down or acquired. However, there are no recent news updates after early 2023, so the site should be checked again. The search tool limit was reached, so no further searches or pages could be checked. This is a different product from the Fathom AI meeting notetaker and the Fathom financial reporting tool.

record.short_description: Safety-focused generative AI voice agents for patient calls at health systems, payors, and pharma companies
record.description: Hippocratic AI builds safety-focused generative AI healthcare agents for health systems, payors, and pharma and life-sciences organizations. The agents hold voice conversations with patients and run on Polaris 5.0, the company's own model. Polaris 5.0 combines a primary model with supporting clinical, safety, language, and scheduling models. The company says it tests outputs with a network of U.S. licensed clinicians. Its agents do not diagnose or prescribe and hand calls to a licensed human nurse when needed.
features: Supervisor models for medical accuracy and safety
Escalation to a licensed human nurse
Output testing by U.S. licensed clinicians
Sampling of live calls for safety review
HIPAA compliant with HITRUST and SOC 2 certifications
use_cases: Clinical research and device trial enrollment
AI patient support and care companion
Pharma product launch and post-market monitoring
record.notes: The official site works at hippocraticai.com. The listed www.hippocraticai.com URL is the same domain, and there is also a customer portal at portal.us.hippocraticai.com. The current blurb should be fixed. It says 'security-focused,' but the company's own pages say 'safety-focused,' and the research page calls Polaris the first safety-focused LLM constellation. The official pages I checked did not list any prices. Third-party sites such as getmacha.com and emitrr.com discuss pricing, but those are not official sources, so pricing is left empty. I found no named EHR or software integrations on the official pages. Figures on the site do not match across pages: the home page says 180M+ and 250M+ interactions, while another page says 200M+, so I did not include those numbers. The status is active, and I found no acquisition or shutdown.

record.short_description: Microsoft Research diffusion model that generates detailed 3D digital avatars as neural radiance fields
record.description: RODIN Diffusion is a Microsoft Research project that uses a roll-out diffusion network to generate 3D digital avatars represented as neural radiance fields. It stores each avatar as a tri-plane of 2D feature maps and uses 3D-aware convolution to keep computing costs down. Cascaded diffusion models build detail at several scales. Avatars can be generated from an image, a text prompt, or random noise, then edited with text prompts. The resulting avatars can be viewed in 360 degrees. The work was published at CVPR 2023.
features: 3D avatar generation as neural radiance fields
Cascaded diffusion models for multi-scale modeling
Avatar generation from a single portrait
record.notes: Search results show this is a research project page with a paper (arXiv 2212.06135, CVPR 2023), not a commercial product. I found no pricing, sign-up, public demo, or code release for the original RODIN on Microsoft's domains, so pricing is left as unknown and free_tier as false. A follow-up project, RodinHD (ECCV 2024), has a separate GitHub repo. The project page was last indexed about 1264 days ago. Status is active only because the page appears to be up. No page says it was discontinued. The current blurb's word 'realistic' fits the paper's claims, but founders may not be able to use it as a tool. Don't mix this up with the commercial 'Rodin' 3D generator from Deemos/Hyper3D, which is a different product. SourceForge lists this project too, with no pricing.

record.short_description: Generative AI rendering platform that creates photorealistic interior and architectural visualizations from photos and 3D models
record.description: Spacely AI is a web-based generative AI platform for spatial design, built by a Thai team and founded in 2023. It is aimed at architects, interior designers, real estate professionals and space owners. Users upload a room photo or capture a 3D scene, choose a style or write a prompt, and get photorealistic renders they can revise right away. The company says more than 580,000 people have used it. It also offers a SketchUp extension and a Team Canvas feature for rendering together as a team.
features: Upload a photo and choose a style
Renders saved to Project Folder (SketchUp extension)
use_cases: Winning client approval without outsourcing renders
record.notes: The listed website (artificial-art.eu) is wrong. Directory listings describe artificial-art.eu as 'Artificial Art', a separate AI digital-art generator, so it is a different product. Spacely's official site is spacely.ai, so the website field should be corrected. The current blurb is a slogan and should be replaced. The spacely.ai homepage calls the tool a 'free interior design generator' with 'No credit card required'. The SketchUp extension page names Studio and Business paid plans. I did not open a pricing page on spacely.ai, so pricing_summary is empty. Third-party review sites give conflicting prices: 40 trial credits, and paid plans from about $12.75 to $102 a month, or Personal at $20 a month billed yearly. Those prices are not recorded here. The free offering may be trial credits rather than an ongoing free tier. The search limit was reached before I could open the pricing page or the artificial-art.eu site directly.

record.short_description: B2C CRM and AI marketing platform for email, SMS, WhatsApp, push, and customer service
record.description: Klaviyo is a B2C CRM and AI marketing platform. It brings customer data together and uses it to automate email, SMS, RCS, WhatsApp, and mobile push campaigns. The platform includes pre-built email templates and flow automations, drag-and-drop builders, and AI that can build segments and flows from a written description. It also offers RFM analysis for segmentation, product recommendations, reviews, and a Customer Hub. Its Customer Agent answers customer questions across chat, SMS, email, and WhatsApp. Most of its users are ecommerce and consumer brands.
use_cases: Automated customer journeys and winback flows
Unifying customer data for B2C brands
record.notes: The official homepage and klaviyo.com/platform were checked. They describe Klaviyo as 'the autonomous B2C CRM' and list email, SMS, RCS, WhatsApp, and push. The current blurb is out of date and should mention the B2C CRM positioning and the extra channels. I could not open Klaviyo's own pricing page because the search limit was reached, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are left empty. The freemium label and free tier come only from third-party review sites (SendX, Charle Agency, Emailtooltester, SalesHive). They agree on a free plan for up to 250 active profiles and paid Email plans from about $20/month. Check klaviyo.com/pricing before publishing. The Square integration comes from Square's app marketplace and Shopify/SHOPLINE from a SHOPLINE article. The 205,000+ brands figure from the Square listing was left out.

record.short_description: AI web tool that generates Arduino code from plain-language project descriptions
record.description: Duino Code Generator is a web-based tool that uses AI to write code for Arduino boards. Users describe what they want in plain language, for example asking for code that will control an LED. The tool then returns code that includes pin and interface setup. The site says the output is not always perfect. It presents the tool as a quick way to get code snippets or ideas and as a companion to the Arduino IDE. It is aimed at hobbyists and professionals.
features: AI-generated Arduino code from natural-language prompts
Code includes pin and interface setup instructions
Support for sensors, motors and other components
use_cases: Getting ideas for larger Arduino projects
record.notes: The official domain's /about page came up in search results and describes the AI Arduino code generator. That page's content confirms the LED prompt example and the 'companion to the Arduino IDE' positioning. I could not find a pricing page on duinocodegenerator.com. Third-party directories disagree on price: Toolify and others list it as Free, while topai.tools says Freemium with paid upgrades. Because no price was found on the official domain, I left pricing empty and set free_tier to false. The company name CJS Robotics and the GPT-3.5-turbo model come from directory sites (Toolify, Moge), not a first-party page I opened, so treat them as unverified. The search tool's usage limit was reached before I could open the homepage or a pricing page directly. Status is marked active because the official page is still indexed, but I did not confirm the site is live right now. The current blurb 'Simplify your Arduino programming' is accurate but vague.

record.short_description: Voice AI for students that quizzes them out loud on their own course material
record.description: Leo AI is a study tool for students. Students upload their course material, and Leo organizes it, asks questions out loud, listens to the spoken answers and corrects them in real time. The site says it works across fields such as law, medicine, prep school and bachelor's programs. It also supports flashcards, study guides, quizzes and oral exam prep. The product began as a French-language AI for students, and its English site says 900,000 accounts have been created.
record.pricing_summary: The terms of sale list a Basic plan at €9.90/month including tax, with 100 credits a month, and a Leo AI + plan at €19.90/month with unlimited access and a 2-day free trial. The homepage says new users get 3 free sessions without a credit card.
features: Voice AI that quizzes you out loud
Questions generated from your own documents
use_cases: Turning course notes into study material
record.notes: The listed blurb 'The AI powering your studies' appears on the lacreme.ai directory and is out of date. The official homepage now presents Leo as 'The AI that makes you revise out loud,' a voice-based revision tutor. Older third-party sources describe it as a writing tool for essays and theses that could get around AI detectors. Prices come from the terms of sale page (iamleo.ai/en/legal), not a dedicated pricing page, so they may not match current plans. The homepage offers 3 free sessions, which counts as a trial, not an ongoing free tier. I could not find the legal company name because I hit the search limit. Capterra, SaaSWorthy and G2 pages for 'Leo AI' cover an unrelated engineering CAD copilot and should not be used for this product.

record.short_description: AI copywriting and SEO tool that generates written content, images, and keyword insight reports
record.description: Contentedge is an AI copywriting and SEO content tool. Its official pricing page lists plans with quotas for AI-generated words, AI-generated images, and SEO Keyword Insight reports, plus team seats. Third-party directories describe it as using GPT-3 to produce human-sounding text for blogs, articles, and sales copy, with keyword tools and real-time search data for SEO. These details were not confirmed on the official site. Its stated focus is SEO content and copywriting, not content for social networks.
record.pricing_summary: The official pricing page lists Starter at $24/mo (30,000 AI words, 100 AI images, 20 SEO Keyword Insight reports, 3 users), Professional at $49/mo (75,000 words, 500 images, 50 reports, 5 users), and Expert at $99/mo (unlimited words and images, 100 reports, unlimited users). The $24/mo price may be the yearly-billed rate. Custom plans are available through a free demo.
record.notes: I couldn't open the contentedge.com homepage because I hit the search tool limit. My only official source was the search snippet of contentedge.com/pricing-2/, and that snapshot looks about 3.8 years old (indexed roughly 1,379 days ago). So current prices and whether the site is still up are unconfirmed, and status is set to unknown. I didn't find a company or legal entity name on an official page. No free tier or free trial was found; only a free demo for custom plans is mentioned. The phrases "GPT-3", "blogs, articles, sales copy" and "real-time search engine data" come only from third-party directories (futuretools.io, opentools.ai, aitoptools.com), so I used them only as unconfirmed context in the description, labeled as third-party. The current blurb, "Create content optimized for social networks", seems inaccurate: sources describe an AI SEO and copywriting tool. Suggested replacement: "AI copywriting and SEO content generation tool".

record.company: Clipdrop (Init ML), now owned by Jasper
record.short_description: AI photo tool that removes unwanted objects, people, text and defects from images
record.description: Cleanup.pictures is a web-based AI image editing tool from Clipdrop. Users drag and drop an image, brush over unwanted objects, people, text or defects, and the AI fills in the background. The site says it does not need a background reference the way traditional clone-stamp tools do. It is aimed at photographers, creative agencies, real estate agents and e-commerce sellers. There is also a developer API. The same Cleanup tool is offered within the broader Clipdrop suite at clipdrop.co.
features: AI removal of objects, people, text and defects
Remove time stamps and cracks from photographs
Reconstructs background without a background reference
use_cases: Photographers removing time stamps or tourists from photos
Real estate agents depersonalizing room photos
Social media and YouTube thumbnail visuals
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize images and photos on social media') is wrong. The product is an AI tool for removing objects, people, text and defects from photos. Social media is only one use the site mentions. The official homepage (cleanup.pictures) says you can start for free. I couldn't open an official pricing page because the search limit ran out. Third-party sites (alternatives.co, media.io, stork.ai, techbriefly) say free exports are capped at 720p and Pro costs about $3/month billed annually; media.io says $5/month or $36/year. Those prices don't come from the product's own site, so I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. The ownership history also comes only from third-party sites (webneel, nemovideo, aiwiki): Clipdrop's maker, Init ML, was bought by Stability AI in 2023, and Clipdrop was then sold to Jasper in 2024. aiwiki says cleanup.pictures is the standalone domain for Clipdrop's Cleanup tool. I didn't open any official press release confirming the sales. The cleanup.pictures search snippet was quite old, so I couldn't confirm the site's current state.

record.short_description: No-code platform for connecting generative AI models to build and share AI apps
record.description: Brancher.ai is a no-code platform that lets users connect generative AI models, such as GPT and DALL-E, to build AI-powered apps without coding. It was built by Fresh Labs, the innovation arm of Fresh Consulting. The platform offers a library of starter templates, app themes, advanced inputs, and multi-step flows. Users can share the apps they build, and the site says monetization is planned. New users get 100 free credits. Paid plans add branding removal, custom logos, and vanity URLs.

record.short_description: Cloud-based AI platform for writing, image generation, video, audio production, and transcription

Directory listings also mention video creation, audio production, and building custom chatbots. These details could not be checked on the product's own website during this review.

record.short_description: AI crypto screener with real-time alerts, trading signals, whale tracking, and top-trader insights
record.description: CoinScreener is a crypto market screening tool that tracks unusual market activity, bullish and bearish movements, and trading signals. It sends real-time alerts and uses AI analysis to explain the market context. Users can discover top traders, compare their performance, and follow their activity. A watchlist, alerts, signals, and insights sit in one workspace, with notifications through Telegram, Discord, or push. It runs as a web app and an iOS app, and its pricing page lists a free Basic tier and a paid Pro tier.
record.pricing_summary: Basic is free and gives limited insights and real-time alerts, with no credit card required. Pro is $8.25/mo, paid yearly, and unlocks trading signals plus unlimited insights and alerts.
features: Top trader discovery and performance comparison

Tracxn, a third-party site, says the company is based in Sydney and was founded in 2022; that was not confirmed on the official site. The current blurb is a vague slogan. record.short_description: AI chat app for talking with recreated historical figures and cultural icons, with voice
record.description: Eternal AI is an app for chatting with AI versions of famous people. Its website says users can talk with more than 70 figures, including Albert Einstein, Tupac, Steve Jobs, Martin Luther King Jr., Ayn Rand and Marcus Aurelius. Users can ask questions and hear each figure's voice and perspective. The site also promotes Eternal Capsule, which builds a digital version of a user from their life stories, personality and memories through conversations with an AI historian in the Eternal AI app.
features: Chat with AI recreations of 70+ iconic figures
Eternal Capsule digital legacy built from personal stories and memories

record.short_description: Browser extension that shows keyword search volume, CPC, competition and trends on Google, YouTube and Amazon
record.description: Keywords Everywhere is a browser extension for Chrome, Firefox and Edge. It shows keyword metrics such as search volume, cost per click, competition and trends while users browse Google, YouTube, Amazon and other sites. It also offers keyword ideas, SEO difficulty, traffic and ranking keywords for any URL, AI SEO reports, and gap analysis. The extension is free to install and some features are free. Keyword metrics are paid and use credits. It also has a REST API and an MCP server for AI tools.
features: SEO difficulty and Moz link metrics

Organic traffic and ranking keywords for any URL
AI SEO reports and gap analysis

record.short_description: Online travel agency for searching and booking cheap flights, including self-transfer routes that combine airlines
record.description: Kiwi.com is an online travel agency based in Brno, Czech Republic. Oliver Dlouhý and Jozef Képesi founded it in 2012 under the name Skypicker. Its flight search uses virtual interlining, which joins flights from airlines that don't partner into one itinerary. The site also offers hotels and car hire, plus 24/7 customer support. Travelers can buy an optional add-on, the Kiwi.com Guarantee, which covers disruptions. There is also a Kiwi.com Club membership with member pricing and a refer-a-friend rewards program.
features: Virtual interlining that combines airlines in a single itinerary
Search from your city to Anywhere
use_cases: Managing trips and getting travel support
record.notes: The listed website is a personal referral link (kiwi.com/fr/user/refer-friend/...), not the main site. It should be replaced with https://www.kiwi.com/. Kiwi.com's help center confirms that referral links give rewards to both the referrer and the new user, so this link would earn rewards for whoever owns it. I hit the search limit before I could open the official site directly, so this record relies on search-result excerpts from kiwi.com pages (US homepage, cheap-flights, last-minute flights, legal terms, Club terms, refer-a-friend help article), the App Store listing and Wikipedia. Searching is free and the business earns money from bookings, a Kiwi.com Service Fee mentioned in the legal terms, and the optional paid Guarantee add-on. I found no subscription or pricing page on kiwi.com, so pricing_type is unknown and free_tier is false, even though searching costs nothing. The only Guarantee price I found (about 25% of the fare) came from The Points Guy, a third-party site, so I left it out. Wikipedia lists General Atlantic as the majority owner (66.7%), but I found no page describing an acquisition, so status stays active. Wikipedia also says the company is now based in Brno. The current blurb is acceptable but generic. Kiwi.com is a consumer travel booking site, not a startup tool, so check that it belongs in this directory.

record.short_description: AI agents that automate healthcare operations workflows, plus a browser extension for repetitive tasks
record.description: Magical is a San Francisco company whose website now focuses on specialized AI agents for healthcare operations, covering work from patient access to revenue cycle. Its agents handle tasks such as referrals, benefits verification, prior authorizations, payment posting and revenue integrity, and the company says they work with any web-based system. Magical also offers a Chrome and Edge extension that speeds up repetitive tasks like messaging, data entry and form filling. One-click autofill of fields and records

record.short_description: iOS app that uses AI to build playlists for Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, and Deezer
record.description: PlaylistAI is an iOS and iPadOS app that makes music playlists with AI. Users type a mood, activity, or genre prompt, and the app picks songs and saves the playlist to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, or Deezer. It can also build playlists from festival poster photos, TikTok and Instagram Reel links, genre blends with BPM filters, an artist's related acts, or a user's top tracks. record.short_description: AI agent that finds relevant sites and drafts backlink outreach pitches for founders to approve
record.description: BacklinkGPT is a link-building service built around an AI outreach agent. The agent finds pages that rank for a site's keywords, writes pitches asking for a link, and sends them under the owner's name after the owner approves each one. It is aimed at business owners and founders who promote their own site and have no SEO team. It is not built for agencies or link resellers. New users can get a free preview with prospects and a sample draft.
record.pricing_summary: Paid plans are Starter at $149/mo, Growth at $399/mo and Scale at $999/mo. They include 1, 3 or 6 connected sender inboxes and 2,000, 6,000 or 20,000 credits, with extra credits at $0.03 and extra inboxes at $19/month. Any fees that sites charge for a link cost extra and are paid only when the user approves them.

record.short_description: Subscription service for AI-assisted storytelling and anime-style image generation using in-house text and image models

record.short_description: AI-generated face and full-body human photos, plus face and human generators and an API
record.description: Generated Photos is a service from Generated Media, Inc. that offers AI-generated, royalty-free images of people. Users can search a library of more than 2.6 million pre-generated faces and a collection of full-body humans. They can also create custom faces or humans by setting parameters in the Face Generator and Human Generator. It also offers an AI Anonymizer, datasets for machine learning, bulk downloads, and API access. The company says the images come from GANs trained on a proprietary dataset shot in its own studio.

Bulk downloads cost $9 to $1 per photo depending on quantity, and the API costs $250/month for 1,000 photos or $300/month for 10,000 photos when billed monthly.

record.short_description: AI social media tool for creating, scheduling, and automating posts across many social networks

record.short_description: AI tool that generates product photos with custom backgrounds from a single uploaded product image

record.short_description: AI-native workspace for building apps, deploying AI agents, automating workflows, and managing team projects
record.description: Taskade is an AI-native workspace platform that combines collaborative projects with AI tools. record.notes: The listed URL includes an affiliate parameter (?via=lacreme), so I removed it from the official URL. The current blurb 'Boost collaborative productivity' is outdated: the product now presents itself as an AI app, agent, and automation platform. I found no acquisition or shutdown notices.

record.short_description: Applied AI lab that makes Devin, an autonomous AI software engineering agent for engineering teams
record.description: Cognition is a San Francisco applied AI lab that builds Devin, an autonomous coding agent that engineering teams hand tasks such as bug fixes, migrations and testing. Devin works in its own development environment, where it inspects repositories, edits code, runs tests and returns pull requests for review. In 2025 Cognition acquired Windsurf, the agentic IDE. It now offers Devin Desktop, which combines a full IDE with an Agent Command Center, plus a CLI and DeepWiki. It also publishes coding models such as SWE-2.
features: Works in its own development environment
Inspects repositories, edits code and runs tests
Devin Desktop IDE with Agent Command Center for local and cloud agents
Devin Oncall for investigating alerts and bugs
record.notes: I couldn't open cognition-labs.com, the listed website. The company's X profile and blog point to cognition.com, Wikipedia lists cognition.ai, and the product lives at devin.ai. Consider changing the listed URL to cognition.com. Cognition is the buyer of Windsurf (blog post on cognition.com, 07.14.25), not an acquired company, so the status is active. I hit the search limit before I could open the official Devin pricing page. Third-party sites (lindy.ai, nocode.mba, automationatlas.io) report a Free plan at $0, Pro at $20/month, Max at $200/month, Teams at $80/month plus $40 per developer seat, and custom Enterprise pricing. I didn't confirm these on Cognition's own domain, so I left pricing_summary blank and set pricing_type to unknown and free_tier to false. I found no integrations on an official page. The current blurb is vague; a better one would describe Devin as an autonomous AI software engineer.

record.short_description: AI web tool that compares two Instagram profiles to estimate romantic compatibility and write a love story
record.description: Locket, also called LoveLocket, is an AI web tool that checks how compatible two people might be based on their Instagram profiles. A user enters any two Instagram handles. The site then generates a result showing how the couple's love story ends, and says this takes about five minutes. It is presented as a lighthearted way to test compatibility or just have fun. The site warns that it only works well with public profiles and shows example results under a Show me some Lockets option.
use_cases: Seeing how a love story ends
record.notes: I couldn't open the live page directly, so this record is based on how lovelocket.ai appears in search results. That text gives the tagline 'Are you happily ever after?', the two-handle Instagram input, the warning that it only works well with public profiles, the roughly 5-minute run time, and the contact e@lovelocket.ai. The site doesn't name a company. Some directory sites (topai.tools, nextool.ai) credit it to 'Chidwi', but I couldn't confirm that, so the company field is left empty. I found no pricing on the official domain. Directory sites disagree: Toolify says Free, Tenereteam says Freemium, and Creati.ai says there is no free plan. Because of that, pricing is marked unknown and free_tier is false. Product Hunt lists it under Dating apps with a 2024 launch. Don't confuse it with the separate Locket Widget photo-sharing app or Locket Photo (locketphoto.net). The current blurb is accurate but vague; it should say it compares Instagram profiles for romantic compatibility.

record.short_description: iOS app that generates sound effects from text prompts using AI
record.description: Sound Effects AI - Text to SFX is an iPhone app from App All Day Pty Ltd that creates sound effects from text.
