Users type or paste a prompt, and the app produces a sound effect in seconds. Prompts can describe styles such as futuristic, retro, ambient or energetic. Finished sounds can be shared directly or downloaded. The app is aimed at content creators, podcasters and people who want to add audio to messages. Premium subscribers get unlimited generation.
features: Instant text to sound effect generation
Unlimited sound effect generation for premium users
record.notes: The only source I could check was the App Store listing in another storefront (apps.apple.com/ru, Ukrainian localization), which matches the listed app ID. My search limit ran out, so I could not open the US listing or look for a developer website. No product website of its own was found, so the App Store listing is used as official_url. The listing names App All Day Pty Ltd as the developer, puts the app in the Utilities category, and says it needs iOS 17.0 or later; it also lists Mac compatibility. Version 1.1.0 (Improved UI) is dated July 10, 2024. Pricing is left out of pricing_summary because it appears only in the developer's App Store description, not on a page on the product's own domain. That description lists $4.99 per week, $9.99 per month and $44.99 per year. It also mentions a lifetime purchase but gives no price, and the yearly line is mistyped as '1 month' of access. Free users get one sound generation during onboarding, so free_tier is false and pricing_type is paid, even though the app is presumably free to download. The current blurb ('Boost your content with sound effects') is vague. It should say that the app generates sound effects from text prompts with AI.

record.short_description: Four-week cohort training program that prepares people for B2B SaaS sales development representative roles
record.description: School of SDR is a training school in Bengaluru for sales development representatives (SDRs) in B2B SaaS. Its main offering is a four-week live cohort. The course covers ICP and account research, outreach, cold calling, objection handling, AI-powered roleplays and interview preparation, with 1:1 mentoring and placement assistance. It also sells self-paced courses and digital guides, and offers free downloads. For companies, it advertises SDR hiring, team training and onsite workshops.
record.pricing_summary: The four-week cohort comes in two tiers, Starter (for upskilling) and Premium (for career transition), with MRP prices of ₹60,000, ₹75,000, ₹70,000 and ₹90,000 listed. Self-paced courses on learn.schoolofsdr.com cost ₹4,999 to ₹9,999, and guides cost ₹999.
features: Lifetime access to recorded content, assignments and quizzes
Self-paced cold calling and interview prep courses
use_cases: Start a career as a B2B SaaS SDR
Hiring SDRs, enterprise SDRs or founding SDRs
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize SaaS sales with proven tactics') is misleading. School of SDR is not a software tool. It is a cohort-based SDR training and hiring program for B2B SaaS. The company name Rahul Wadhwa LLP comes from the site footer, and Rahul Wadhwa is listed as co-founder. The homepage shows four MRP figures (₹60,000, ₹75,000, ₹70,000, ₹90,000) across Starter and Premium, but the extracted text did not show which figure belongs to which tier, or which ones are list versus discounted prices. learn.schoolofsdr.com has several free downloadable guides (for example, an SDR onboarding guide and an activity calculator) alongside the paid courses. These are lead-magnet resources rather than a free product tier, so free_tier is set to false. LinkedIn lists the company as founded in 2023 in Bengaluru. No software integrations were found.

record.short_description: No-code platform for building AI lead magnets such as quizzes, calculators and simulators
record.description: Magnetly is a no-code platform for building interactive AI lead magnets, including quizzes, calculators, simulators and AI generators. The interactive tools give website visitors something useful first and then collect their contact details. A user pastes a website URL and Magnetly generates a lead magnet that uses the site's branding. The lead magnet can then be edited, embedded or shared. Magnetly also includes conditional logic, URL scraping for AI analysis, templates, analytics and integrations.
record.pricing_summary: Free plan with all tools and 1,000 credits included; Starter €29/month (3 tools, up to 300 credits/month) and Growth €79/month (unlimited tools, up to 1,000 credits/month). Yearly billing on Starter and Growth saves two months.
features: AI lead magnet generation from website URL
use_cases: Turn website traffic into qualified leads
Interactive free tools as lead magnets
record.notes: The listed URL is an affiliate signup link (aff=g1bj9) on app.magnetly.co, so it should be replaced with the clean domain https://www.magnetly.co/. The current blurb 'Create lead magnets in 1 click' does not match the site's wording. The site positions the product as a builder for interactive AI lead magnets. Pricing comes from the homepage pricing section as shown in search results; I did not find a separate pricing page. A Make.com integration page says the Magnetly app is maintained by the vendor. OpenAI is named in a Magnetly blog post. The homepage mentions integrations but does not list them. One Magnetly blog post mentions a $29/month price and 500+ integrations, which conflicts with the homepage, so those figures were not used. Several unrelated products share the name: magnetly.us (photo magnets), magnetlyai.com (LinkedIn automation), yourmagnetly.com and magnetly.store. Company details and founders were not verified, and the search limit was reached.

record.short_description: AI tool that generates YouTube thumbnails and titles and A/B tests them for creators
record.description: Tokee is an AI tool for YouTube creators. According to third-party profiles, it generates video thumbnails from a video script and YouTube data, writes titles that follow current trends, and predicts how well a title will perform. It also lets creators A/B test titles and thumbnails. The goal is to raise click-through rates, views and monetization. PitchBook lists the company, Tokee AI, as founded in 2023, based in Wilmington, Delaware, and now out of business.
features: A/B testing of titles and thumbnails
record.notes: I could not open tokee.ai or any page on its domain, because the search tool limit ran out, so I could not confirm the site is still up. PitchBook lists Tokee AI's status as 'Out of Business', with an entry dated 03-Jul-2025. That is a third-party database, not a product page saying the product is discontinued, so status is set to unknown rather than shutdown. Recommend manually checking whether tokee.ai still loads. Prices appear only on third-party directories: aiforeasylife lists Free $0, Start $30/mo, Grow $50/mo and Scale $120/mo, and lacreme.ai lists euro tiers. These were excluded under the rules. One directory mentions a 7-day free trial, which is also unverified. genai.works credits the build to DEVBRAIN. The French blurb matches lacreme.ai's English tagline 'A/B Test your YouTube titles and thumbnails'.

record.short_description: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings into structured minutes and action items
record.description: Upmeet is an AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes conversations. It covers in-person meetings through its mobile app, video calls on Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet, and imported audio files. After a meeting, it writes a report with discussion points, decisions, and action items. Users can search past meetings, ask questions about them, and rewrite, translate, or share recaps. It connects to calendars so it can join meetings on its own, supports more than 20 languages, and offers custom summary templates.
record.pricing_summary: Monthly plan is $9.99/month, and the Annual plan is $8.33/month billed annually (save 17%). Both include unlimited meeting recordings, AI transcription, and summaries. Enterprise pricing is custom.
features: Automatic meeting reports with decisions and action items
use_cases: Consultants and lawyers documenting client conversations
record.notes: The current blurb is accurate. Pricing comes from the official upmeet.ai pricing page, which lists no free plan. The Upmeet site advertises a free trial with no credit card, and the mobile apps are free to download with a Premium upgrade. That is why the record uses paid with free_tier false. The App Store lists the developer as InHouse Software. Do not confuse this with UpMeet at upmeet.me, a separate video-call product priced in GBP. Directories like AIChief, SaaSworthy, and Toolify mix the two up. My search tool limit ran out after two searches, so I could not check further details such as the free-trial length on the main domain.

record.short_description: Mobile app that rates facial attractiveness from uploaded selfies and gives personalized appearance-improvement advice
record.description: LooksMax AI is a mobile app for iOS and Android from Mnkybrain Labs, a developer based in San Francisco. Users upload photos, the app's AI analyzes their facial traits, and it returns ratings with personalized advice on how to look better. Its Google Play listing says the app focuses on helping men improve their facial attractiveness and confidence. Third-party write-ups also describe an AI hairstyle feature and grooming tips. The app is not a social media image tool.
record.notes: I could not open looksmax.ai directly, and the search tool limit was reached before I could check the official site or the App Store. The Google Play listing (com.looksmax.ai) links to looksmax.ai/terms and looksmax.ai/privacy and names Mnkybrain Labs as the developer. That listing says it was last updated on Apr 4, 2024. Status is unknown because I could not confirm the site is up. The listing describes the app as rating faces and giving advice, not as optimizing your image on social media, so the current blurb is inaccurate and should be replaced. Prices appear only on third-party review and directory sites, and they disagree: about $3.99/week on Android, and $9.99/week or $29.99/month on iOS. One source also mentions a free basic score, while others say the score is paywalled or unlocked through referrals. Because none of this comes from the official domain, I left pricing and the free tier unrecorded. looksmaxai.org appears to be an unofficial look-alike site, and Mogger: LooksMax AI is a separate app from a different developer.

record.short_description: AI academic writing assistant for researching, outlining, drafting, citing sources, and checking for plagiarism
record.description: Litero AI is a web-based AI writing assistant built for academic and source-based writing. It helps users research, outline, draft, cite, and polish essays, research papers, and discussion posts. Its source finder searches scholarly libraries, and its citation tool formats references in APA, MLA, Harvard, and other styles. It also includes sentence auto-suggest, an AI companion, an AI detector, a text humanizer, and a plagiarism checker. Litero presents itself as an ethical partner that writes with users rather than for them.
record.pricing_summary: The Free plan costs $0/month and includes AI commands with limited daily AI output, an unlimited source finder, and citation tools. Premium starts at $7.9/month billed annually; the site's structured data lists $19.95/month or $95/year for unlimited AI drafting, a humanizer, a plagiarism checker, and built-in ChatGPT.
features: Citation tool with APA, MLA, Harvard formatting
use_cases: Writing discussion posts and peer replies
Rephrasing writing for tone and clarity
record.notes: Checked against the official homepage (litero.ai), which includes the pricing section and FAQ, plus the product subpages for discussion posts, the AI text generator, research papers, and the citation generator. The current blurb is too narrow: the product covers research, citations, drafting, and plagiarism and AI detection, not just essay structure. The homepage shows two premium figures: $7.9/month 'if billed annually' in the visible plan, and $19.95/month or $95/year in its embedded structured data. The two may not match, so the exact price should be re-checked before publishing. The homepage also gives two source counts, '100+ million' and '10M+'. The site only uses the name 'Litero AI' and gives no legal company name; one third-party listing says it was founded in 2023 in the United States, but that is not confirmed on the official site. I couldn't open a separate /pricing page because the search limit was reached.

record.short_description: AI autoblogging tool that writes SEO-optimized blog articles and publishes them to business websites
record.description: MagicBlog is an AI blog-writing platform aimed at businesses, contractors and agencies. A user enters a core keyword and picks from suggested subtopics. The user then sets how often new articles should be created. MagicBlog writes original, SEO-optimized articles and can publish them automatically through a website or CMS integration, or save them as drafts for review. It also includes title and outline generation, writing in more than 19 languages, bulk article generation and AI image generation.
record.pricing_summary: Plans include a $0 7-day free trial, Starter at $19/month, Pro at $250/month billed monthly or $200/month billed yearly, and custom Enterprise pricing. Plans are credit-based, with 1 credit = 1 article.
features: Publish automatically or save as draft
use_cases: SEO blog content for local businesses and contractors
Agencies publishing content to client sites
Driving website traffic and inbound leads
Long-form blog writing for content writers
record.notes: The site is up. The listed blurb is accurate, but it could mention auto-publishing. Pricing comes from magicblog.ai/pricing as seen in search-result text, because I couldn't open the page directly. That page shows Pro at both $250 (monthly) and $200 (yearly, labeled save 20%). Its credit columns read 3/50/30/Custom, which looks inconsistent, so recheck it. The only free option on the official site is a 7-day trial. Third-party directories list a free plan or a $10/month starting price, but the official page doesn't confirm either. The agencies page offers 5% off 6-month billing and 15% off 12-month billing. I didn't find the legal company name.

record.short_description: AI writing platform that creates on-brand marketing content using a customized brand-voice AI
record.description: Mark Copy AI, now branded on its site as Mark AI, is an AI content platform from a Paris-based company. It builds an AI around a company's brand voice and knowledge base, and teams use it to write marketing content. The platform combines several language models and offers AI chat and workflow templates, rewriting, plagiarism detection, and translation into more than 50 languages. SEO features are sold as an add-on. It is aimed at marketing teams and enterprises that need to produce content at scale.
record.pricing_summary: The Team plan costs €750 per month for up to 5 users with unlimited content generation, and the Enterprise plan for more than 5 users has custom pricing. SEO features cost an extra $750 per month per workspace, and the page shows a discount for yearly billing.
features: AI adapted to your brand voice
Custom AI chat and AI workflows
use_cases: Scaling content production for tech and software companies
record.notes: Opened the official pricing pages (EN and FR) and the features page on markcopy.ai. The site now calls the product 'Mark AI'. PitchBook lists the company as Mark AI, formerly known as Mark Copy AI, based in Paris. No free tier or free trial appears on the official pricing page. Third-party sites like SourceForge, Capterra, and Techjockey list older prices starting at €349/$349 per month with a free trial, but the official page doesn't confirm these. Older third-party listings mention CSV bulk import and 1-click social publishing, which the official pages I opened don't confirm, so I left integrations empty. The listed blurb is roughly right but vague. The product is now pitched as a brand-voice AI for enterprise teams.

record.short_description: AI agents that automate healthcare operations such as prior authorizations, referrals, and revenue cycle work
record.description: Magical is an agentic AI automation platform. It deploys specialized AI agents that do operational work across healthcare systems, from patient access to revenue cycle. Its pre-trained agents handle workflows such as prior authorizations, referrals, benefits verification, payment posting, and records requests, and they work across browser and desktop applications. The company says AI judges put guardrails around agent execution. Magical started as a Chrome extension for text expansion and autofill. Its site now focuses on healthcare providers and payers.
features: AI judges as guardrails on agent execution
Works across browser and desktop applications
PDF data extraction into online forms
Smart data transformation and field mapping
record.notes: The current blurb is wrong. Nothing I found on getmagical.com mentions social media customer responses. The homepage and role pages now describe Magical as AI agents for healthcare operations, for both providers and payers. The text-expander page also shows a Chrome extension for text expansion and autofill, which was formerly called Auto Text Expander for Google Chrome. I could not open the listed URL https://www.getmagical.com/ai, so I used the root domain. I did not find a pricing page on getmagical.com. Third-party sites (G2 AI Marketplace, which-50, Future Tools) list a $0 Core plan or call it free, but by the rules I left pricing empty and set free_tier to false. The healthcare platform pages only offer demos and assessments. The About page names Harpaul Sambhi as cofounder and CEO. I found no acquisition or shutdown notice. A search limit stopped me before I could check pricing further.

record.short_description: AI map generator from Proxi that turns text prompts into custom maps with pins
record.description: MapsGPT is an AI map generator from Proxi that turns written prompts into custom digital maps with pins. Users pick a mode, such as Places Near an Area, Text to Map, History Explorer, Vibe Search, Freeform Prompt, or Trip Planning. They then enter a location and an email address to get an editable copy of the map. A group can add places to a shared map. The site calls MapsGPT the quick version of Proxi, whose main platform is aimed at downtowns, markets, and event teams.
record.pricing_summary: The MapsGPT homepage calls it a free AI map generator powered by Proxi. The site lists no paid tiers or prices.
features: Create a custom map with pins in seconds
Editable copy of your map sent by email
Add-a-place so groups can fill in the map
use_cases: Turning pasted text into a map
Group maps for downtowns, markets, or events
record.notes: I checked this against the mapsgpt.com homepage as it appeared in search results, and it is live. The homepage says MapsGPT is powered by Proxi, which points to Proxi as the company. A Proxi blog post says the same. I did not find a separate pricing page on mapsgpt.com. I also did not check Proxi's own paid plans, because I hit the search limit. Directory sites disagree on price: Dataconomy and HyperGPT say freemium, while Futurepedia, Future Tools, and Toolhunter say free. I used the homepage's own 'free' wording. One directory, Dang.ai, marked the tool inactive in July 2024, but the official site is up, so I set the status to active. The current blurb, 'Optimize bespoke event planning', is wrong. The product makes AI maps from prompts. Events are only one use case.

record.short_description: AI employees platform that runs inbox, social media, SEO content, lead generation and calls for small businesses
record.description: Marblism is a London-based Y Combinator (Winter 2024) company that gives small businesses a team of AI employees. Each one has a named role: Eva as executive assistant, Sonny for social media, Stan for lead generation, Penny for SEO, Rachel as receptionist, Linda as legal assistant and Walter as website builder. The AI employees handle inbox management, social posting, SEO articles, outreach and calls. They check with the user before anything goes out. An iOS app is also available.
record.pricing_summary: One plan that includes all AI employees, priced at $24/month billed annually, $33/month billed quarterly or $44/month billed monthly. It comes with a 7-day money-back guarantee instead of a free trial.
record.notes: The current blurb ('Generate efficient applications quickly') is out of date. Marblism used to generate web apps from a prompt, and its LinkedIn tagline still says so, but marblism.com now sells AI employees for small businesses. The blurb should be replaced. The prices come from Marblism's own blog post, not the /pricing page, because I hit the search limit before I could open that page. Third-party reviews give the same $24/$33/$44 figures and also mention a 50-hour monthly cap and per-seat fees, but I could not confirm those on Marblism's site. Integrations like Gmail, Outlook, WordPress and Wix appear only on third-party sites, so I left that list empty. YC lists the company as founded in 2024 by Ulric Musset. The homepage claims 40,000+ businesses.

record.short_description: AI fitness and nutrition app that creates personalized meal plans, workout programs and habit tracking
record.description: MikeAI is an AI-powered fitness and nutrition companion. It creates personalized meal plans, workout routines and supplement recommendations based on a user's goals and preferences. Workout programs include video guides and progress tracking, and an AI recipe generator creates meals that fit macro targets. The service also offers daily habit tracking with streak rewards, a Fitness GPT chatbot that answers nutrition and fitness questions, and community features for sharing progress. LinkedIn lists the company in Austin, Texas, founded in 2023.
features: Custom workout plans with video guides
Fitness GPT chatbot for 24/7 nutrition and fitness advice
use_cases: Getting instant fitness and nutrition advice
record.notes: The search result for mikeai.co showed the homepage and its features. I did not open a pricing page there. The homepage offers a free 7-day trial, but I found no listed prices or a permanent free plan. The only price I found was 'Starts at $4.99' (Fitness Premium), on third-party sites SaaSworthy and TechImply, so I left it out. The directory blurb says 'Quickly optimize your workout routines', but the product focuses as much on meal plans and nutrition as on workouts. A Google Play app called 'MikeAi' with the same features is published by Crution Private Limited, so this may be the developer, but I did not confirm it on the official site. LinkedIn lists MikeAI as based in Austin, TX. 'MikeAI (WAZ)' is an unrelated cryptocurrency, and Mike AI at mikeai.co.uk is an unrelated legal workspace product.

record.short_description: AI web app that generates titles, descriptions, tags and thumbnail ideas for online content
record.description: MetaGenieAI is a web application, listed in several third-party AI tool directories, that uses artificial intelligence to generate metadata for content. Users enter a description of their content, and the tool suggests titles, descriptions, tags and thumbnail ideas. Directories describe it as a way to make metadata for websites and social media faster to create, with output that can be adjusted to the user's language. The official site could not be opened or verified, and one directory reports that the domain now redirects to a for-sale page.
record.notes: I could not open the listed site (https://www.metagenieai.com/) because the connection failed, so nothing here comes from the official site, and I left official_url empty. One directory (domore.ai) says the domain now redirects to a GoDaddy page offering it for sale and that no active product is shown. That suggests the product may be defunct, but no official page says it was discontinued, so status is unknown rather than shutdown. Prices show up only on third-party sites: techjockey says it starts at $5, ai-locator says freemium from $5/mo, and Future Tools says it is free and calls it a Google Colab notebook. I left the pricing fields empty because the rules don't allow prices from other sites. All features come from directory listings. The current blurb roughly matches, but the tool generates content metadata rather than strictly optimizing it for SEO. Recommend removing the listing or marking it as unverified until someone confirms the domain is live.

record.company: MyInvestment-AI (site publisher listed as Sandy Tanguy)
record.short_description: AI tool that turns your finances, goals and risk tolerance into a personalized investment plan report
record.description: MyInvestment-AI is a web tool that produces a personalized investment plan. Users enter basic financial details, including income, savings, investment goals and risk preferences. The tool then analyzes this data and generates a report with an investment strategy and actionable steps. The site says users do not need to upload documents and that submitted data is deleted after the report is generated. It also states that it provides information about investment strategies rather than financial advice.
features: Analysis of financial data, goals and risk tolerance
Submitted data deleted after report generation
use_cases: Building an investment strategy without a traditional financial advisor
record.notes: I only saw the official site through search-index snippets of its FAQ and legal notice. I could not open the live page, so the 'active' status is based on the site being indexed, not a confirmed live load. The legal notice names the site publisher as SANDY TANGUY (French SIRET 902 576 859 00018) and gives hello@MyInvestment-AI.com as the support email. Prices appear only on third-party directories, so pricing is left empty. TheresAnAIForThat and LogicWeb list an Essential Investor Plan at $9.99 one-time (discounted from $14.99) and a Strategic Investor Plan at $24.99. Other directories conflict, variously calling it free, freemium or paid, so I set no free tier. Product Hunt shows one launch in 2024. The current blurb ('Reduce human error by investing') is not backed by any source I found and should be replaced.

record.short_description: AI tool that turns ideas, PDFs, YouTube videos, and web pages into visual mind maps
record.description: MindmapAI is a web-based tool that uses artificial intelligence to build visual, organized mind maps. Users can start from an idea, a PDF, a YouTube video, or a URL. The AI pulls out the main points and structures them into a map, which users can then customize with notes, links between nodes, icons, tags, and themes. The platform supports real-time collaboration, sharing through public links, export, and keyboard shortcuts for faster editing.
features: Custom notes, icons, tags and node links
use_cases: Summarizing PDF documents into mind maps
Turning YouTube videos into organized key points
record.notes: The current blurb is wrong. The mindmapai.pro homepage describes an AI mind map generator, not a social media content tool, so the blurb should be replaced. The site mixes English and Spanish text. I found no pricing page or company name on mindmapai.pro, so pricing and free tier are left as unknown/false. This is a different product from MindMap AI at mindmapai.app (which has its own $0/$3.99/$9.99 tiers) and from mindmapai.net. Don't merge their details into this row. I hit the search limit before I could check mindmapai.pro for a pricing page.

record.short_description: Self-service business intelligence platform for building dashboards and KPIs from multiple data sources
record.description: NativeBI is a self-service business intelligence platform from NativeBI Inc., a Delaware company. Business users and analysts can pull data from several internal and external sources into one place, then build interactive dashboards and KPIs with built-in charts. Users can run ad-hoc analysis in natural language through ChatGPT, set alerts on business rules, and share dashboards with their team or publicly. The site says the product is designed for non-technical users and has a short learning curve.
record.pricing_summary: There is a free lifetime plan at $0 with 1 Excel data source, 1 dashboard, 5MB per data source and 10 ChatGPT requests per day. Pro costs $25/month for 3 data sources, 5 dashboards, 3 analysts and 10 viewers. Enterprise costs $100/month for 10 data sources, 20 dashboards, unlimited alerts and unlimited viewers.
use_cases: Visualizing and analyzing business data in one place
Ad-hoc data analysis with natural language
Getting alerts when business rules are met
record.notes: Sources: search-indexed copies of nativebi.com pages (home, features, FAQ, pricing, try-for-free, terms). Those index snapshots are about 3 to 3.5 years old, and I could not load the live site directly. So the site being up today and the prices still being current are not confirmed, and status is set to active based only on the indexed official pages. The company name NativeBI Inc. (Middletown, Delaware) comes from the terms and conditions page. The FAQ also lists data sources still in development, such as MongoDB, MariaDB, Azure, Google Analytics, Google Sheets, Google Drive and Dropbox. I left those out of integrations because they were not yet supported. The current blurb is accurate but vague. A better one would mention that it is a self-service BI platform with dashboards and ChatGPT analysis.

record.short_description: B2B SaaS that converts natural-language questions into SQL so employees can query enterprise data
record.description: NLSQL is a B2B SaaS tool from NLSQL Limited, a London company founded in 2018. It gives employees an AI chat interface that turns natural-language questions into SQL queries against company databases. It runs as an AI bot app, and its site says no sensitive data has to leave the corporate IT environment. The company describes integrations with major database types, storage systems and corporate messengers, and it holds an SAP certification. Other listed products include an AI Agent and AI Anomaly Detection, distributed through Microsoft's Azure Marketplace.
features: No sensitive data transfer outside corporate IT ecosystem
Webchat for embedding in a webpage
AI Agent, AI Employee, Web App Builder AI and AI Anomaly Detection products
use_cases: Healthcare BI and clinical trial data analysis
Querying SAP data for business intelligence
Front-line employees getting data during business negotiations
record.notes: I confirmed the official site at nlsql.com, including the home, solutions, how-it-works, terms and contacts pages. The company is NLSQL LIMITED (company no. 11276867) in London. NLSQL's own pages don't show any prices. Third-party directories list conflicting prices: Capterra and Software Advice say $99/month Basic, while SourceForge says $987/month for unlimited users and points to Azure Marketplace. Because none of these are on NLSQL's domain, I left the pricing fields empty. An older NLSQL blog post mentions a free trial on SAP App Center, but I couldn't confirm a current free tier. The current blurb, 'Clarify your data for fast decisions', is vague. A clearer version would mention natural-language-to-SQL querying. The search tool limit was reached, so I couldn't search further.

record.short_description: AI-enabled lung cancer screening service for community health centers, hospitals, and imaging networks
record.description: Oatmeal Health is a virtual, AI-enabled cancer screening platform. It works with community health centers, hospitals, and imaging networks to find patients who are eligible for lung cancer screening, contact them, and get them scheduled. Its LungIQ tool searches EHR data for patients who meet USPSTF criteria. The company also offers care coordination and case management, mainly for underserved populations at FQHCs. It is developing LungAI CADx, an AI tool for assessing pulmonary nodules. LungAI is investigational and has not been cleared by the FDA.
record.pricing_summary: No price tiers are published. The FQHC page says the lung and breast cancer screening service is provided at no cost to FQHCs and patients.
features: LungIQ EHR mining to identify screening-eligible patients
Annual lung and breast cancer screening coordination
use_cases: Closing lung cancer screening gaps at FQHCs
Early cancer detection for underserved populations
Improving UDS and HEDIS quality metrics
Reducing staff burden of running screening programs
record.notes: I checked the official site's homepage, About page, FQHC page and press page. The current blurb is reasonable, but it is too broad: the company focuses on lung cancer screening, and the FQHC page also mentions breast cancer screening. The homepage says LungAI is investigational, not FDA-cleared and not commercially available in the US. A Google Cloud case study says it 'will be among the first FDA-cleared' AI solutions. The site does not list B2B pricing for health systems. Google Cloud is listed as an integration only because the Google case study names it as the company's cloud infrastructure provider.

record.short_description: Generative AI cloud platform for creating personalized images and videos from a brand's own assets
record.description: OHMYSYNT is a generative AI cloud platform for marketers and brands. Its core technology, AI-SYNT, lets users train custom AI models on their own brand assets, such as products, styles and brand ambassadors. Those models can then generate new images and videos. Users can place digital copies of people or products into new scenes using text prompts. The company says this speeds up production and lowers costs. Dealroom lists a December 2022 launch, a Wilmington, US headquarters and a team of 2 to 10 people.
features: Custom AI model training on brand assets (AI-SYNT)
Digital copies of people or products placed into new scenes via text prompts
Proprietary fine-tuning engine for AI models
Initial results from a single photo during registration; full training uses 20-30 images
use_cases: Reducing traditional production time and cost
record.notes: The web search tool hit its usage limit after one successful query. Because of that, I could not open ohmysynt.io or any pricing page on that domain. All details come from third-party listings: Dealroom (app.dealroom.co/companies/ohmysynt), which links to ohmysynt.io, and the Product Hunt launch page. The Dealroom page is about 1,415 days old, so the information may be out of date. The status is set to unknown because I could not confirm the site is still up. No pricing was found. The current blurb is broadly accurate but vague; a better one would say it trains custom AI models on brand assets to generate personalized images and videos. The official site and pricing should be checked by hand before publishing.

record.short_description: AI painting app for Windows that turns simple brushstrokes into realistic landscape images
record.description: NVIDIA Canvas is a Windows painting application from NVIDIA that uses AI to turn simple brushstrokes into realistic landscape images. Users paint with materials such as sky, mountains, river and stone, change the look and lighting with built-in styles, and keep elements separate on layers. A Panorama mode creates images that can be imported into 3D applications such as Blender and NVIDIA Omniverse USD Composer. NVIDIA offers the app as a free beta, and it requires an NVIDIA RTX-class GPU.
record.pricing_summary: NVIDIA calls Canvas a free beta app for anyone with an NVIDIA RTX GPU. It has no paid tiers.
features: AI turns simple brushstrokes into realistic landscape images
Materials ranging from sky and mountains to river and stone
Panorama mode for images importable into 3D apps
AI model based on GauGAN2 research
use_cases: Archviz designers drafting backdrops and environments
record.notes: Official product page (served at nvidia.com/en-us/studio/canvas.html) shows Version 1.4, a 'Download Beta' button, Windows only, and requires a GeForce RTX, NVIDIA RTX or TITAN RTX GPU, 4 GB RAM for Standard or 6 GB for Panorama, Windows 10, and driver 522.06 or later. The product page text I saw does not state a price. 'Free beta' comes from NVIDIA's own blog (2022), which may be out of date. Feature details came from the product page, the NVIDIA forum beta thread (PNG/PSD export), and the NVIDIA FAQ (use cases). I found no NVIDIA page saying the app was discontinued, so the status is active, but I could not run more searches to confirm recent updates. The current blurb is broadly accurate, but the official wording is 'brushstrokes' rather than 'sketches'. Suggested blurb: 'Use AI to turn simple brushstrokes into realistic landscape images'.

record.short_description: AI ad generation platform for creating, launching, and analyzing image and video ads across channels
record.description: Omneky is a San Francisco-based AI creative advertising platform. It uses generative AI to make image ads, video ads, UGC-style avatar videos and ad copy from product photos, briefs or brand guidelines. It scores creatives for predicted performance. Marketers can then launch and manage campaigns on Meta, Google, TikTok, LinkedIn and Reddit from one dashboard. The platform also includes brand controls, an AI agent, automations and performance insights. It offers plans for brands, agencies and enterprises.
record.pricing_summary: Lite costs $29/month (200 credits, 1 brand), Standard $99/month (1,000 credits, 3 brands) and Pro $249/month (4,000 credits, 5 brands). Billed yearly, they cost $24, $79 and $199 a month. Enterprise is custom, and Lite, Standard and Pro start with a 7-day free trial.
features: AI ad scoring for predicted performance
use_cases: Generating on-brand ad creatives at scale
Launching campaigns across multiple ad platforms
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize your brand consistency') is too narrow. Brand consistency is one feature, but Omneky is mainly an AI ad generation and campaign launch platform. The homepage and the omneky.com pricing page back up the pricing and feature details. The 7-day trial is not a permanent free tier, so free_tier is false. Some third-party review sites list different seat counts and plan names than the official pricing page. I relied on the official page.

record.short_description: iOS voice chat app for natural, expressive spoken conversations with an AI companion
record.description: Oliver, listed on the App Store as Voice AI Chatbot by Oliver, is an app for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Vision from SPATIAL AI LABS LTD. It lets people have spoken conversations with an AI. Its voice replies can show emotion and laughter, and it supports about 15 languages. Conversations can be shaped around goals such as language practice, life coaching or brainstorming. The app is built on the ChatGPT API, and users can add their own OpenAI API key for unlimited access.
features: Expressive voice AI with emotion and laughter
Conversations shaped around the user's goals
Generous rate limits with priority response times
Bring your own OpenAI API key (BYOK) for unlimited access
record.notes: I couldn't find a separate product website. The only source I could confirm is the App Store listing (id6447604485), so official_url is empty. On the App Store, the app has been renamed several times: 'Oliver, Voice Chat with AI', then 'Voice Chatbot by Oliver AI', then 'Voice AI Chatbot by Oliver'. The seller is SPATIAL AI LABS LTD. An older listing showed the copyright as ASK AI AND CHAT LTD. The latest version I saw was 5.2.1, dated Oct 22, 2025. The App Store says 'Free' with 'Offers In-App Purchases', which is why it's marked freemium. The only specific paid price I found, from $14.99/month, comes from directory sites (theresanaiforthat.com, techbriefly.com), not the product's own domain. So pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are empty. The current blurb ('Optimize the writing and translation of content') is outdated. An old Android listing called it a 'Writer Assistant', but the current App Store listing presents it as an expressive voice AI companion. I recommend updating the blurb. I hit the search limit before I could check the in-app purchase price list or look further for a developer website.

record.short_description: AI portrait retouching software that detects faces and automatically smooths skin and enhances eyes and teeth
record.description: ON1 Portrait AI is portrait retouching software from ON1. It uses machine learning to find every face in a photo and applies retouching to the skin, eyes and mouth. It can also batch-process whole folders. Edits are non-destructive. Users can also work manually by adjusting eye and mouth positions, refining skin masks and brushing out blemishes. It runs as a standalone app on Mac and Windows or as a plugin for other editors. It is also built into ON1 Photo RAW.
record.pricing_summary: A perpetual Portrait AI 2023.5 license is listed at $29.99, marked down from $69.99, for 2 computers. A Photo RAW MAX subscription with all ON1 apps is $89.99/year for 3 computers, with a 30-day money-back guarantee.
features: Manual eye, mouth and skin mask controls
record.notes: The listed name 'On1' is the company. The product is ON1 Portrait AI, and the listed URL is the official product page. The current blurb reads like a slogan and should be replaced. The $29.99 price is shown as a markdown from $69.99, and the page says signed-in customers may see different prices. ON1's store page for Portrait AI 2023 shows a different price ($39.99), so the price may be out of date. The download page offers a 30-day full-featured free trial with no credit card needed. That is a trial, not a free tier. The current version is listed as Portrait AI 2023.5.

record.short_description: Multimodal AI search that indexes video, audio, documents, and text so site content becomes searchable
record.description: Omnisearch is an AI search product that makes the content on a website searchable, including audio, video, text, documents, and presentations. Its multimodal AI can find faces, logos, scenes, and spoken words inside media, and it returns time-stamped results. Customers can use it through an API or through an admin dashboard. The company aims it at EdTech platforms, media portals, and security footage monitoring. It was founded by Croatian competitive programmers and reports raising $1.5M in venture funding.
features: Multimodal search across audio, video, text, documents and presentations
Find faces, logos and scenes in video
Scalable architecture across servers and cloud environments
use_cases: AI search for EdTech and e-learning platforms
record.notes: The official site omnisearch.ai is live. Its homepage, About Us, education, and security pages describe multimodal AI search for video, audio, and documents. The current blurb ('Optimize cloud-based media content management') is inaccurate: Omnisearch is a search and indexing product, not a content management tool. I did not find a pricing page on omnisearch.ai. Third-party directories (Capterra, Software Advice, Tekpon, SpotSaaS) list plans from $49/month (Basic), $99 (Standard), and $199 (Advanced), plus a free trial or free version. Because none of that is confirmed on the official domain, pricing was left empty and free_tier set to false. The search tool limit was reached, so I could not check further. The About page lists investors: GoAhead Ventures, SQ Capital, Apertu Capital, and David Richardson. LinkedIn lists Vancouver, BC as headquarters. No acquisition or shutdown was found. The 'LMS integration' entry comes from an Omnisearch blog post. No specific integration partners were named.

record.short_description: Los Angeles AI consultancy that builds and runs AI agents for small and medium businesses
record.description: OLY.AI is a Los Angeles company that builds and runs AI agents for small and medium businesses. The agents work from a "second brain" built from each client's own files. The company says its team previously worked at Amazon, NBC, Fox and MLB, and its CEO and founder is Michael Galluppo. It offers managed service with weekly impact reporting and no long contract, and clients can export their data. OLY.AI began as a QuickBooks-based financial intelligence tool for bookkeepers and SMBs.
record.pricing_summary: The homepage lists $1,500 setup plus $500/mo for the managed service, $8,500 for self-managed, and $5,500/mo for enterprise. A separate /pricing page still shows the older QuickBooks plans: Free at $0, Starter at $50/mo and Pro at $120/mo, billed yearly.
features: AI agents built on a second brain from your own files
Managed build and operation of AI agents
No long contract; data exports on request
Ask financial questions in plain English (legacy QuickBooks product)
Instant closing reports and budget creation (legacy)
use_cases: Automating SMB workflows with AI agents
Real-time financial insights for bookkeepers and fractional CFOs
Financial reporting and budgeting from QuickBooks data
record.notes: The site seems to have changed direction. The homepage now presents OLY.AI as an AI consultancy that builds AI agents for SMBs. A December 2025 press release on oly.ai describes it as a real-time financial intelligence platform for SMBs. The /pricing page still lists the older QuickBooks-based SaaS tiers: Free (2,500 tokens/month), Starter $50/mo and Pro $120/mo, billed yearly. Because the homepage and pricing page don't agree, I based pricing_type and free_tier on the homepage, since it is the main offering. The current blurb, "Optimize financial decision-making", fits the old product and should be updated. QuickBooks and Google Docs integrations come from the legacy pricing page.

record.short_description: iPhone app that uses AI to log meals from photos and track calories, macros, and nutrition
record.description: MealSnap is an iPhone meal diary and calorie counter from SimpliXio Pte. Ltd., sold through Apple's App Store. Users take a photo of a meal or drink, and AI estimates its nutrition. The developer says the app goes beyond counting calories. It shows food processing indicators, nutrition scores, and health analytics, and it keeps a meal history. Recent versions added meal search by day, meal ratings, logging streaks, achievements, and weekly progress recaps. The store listing now uses the name Food & Macro Tracker: MealSnap.
features: AI food recognition from meal photos
Search meals within a selected day
Meal logging streaks with grace days
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit partway through, so I checked fewer pages than usual. Everything here comes from the US, Bermuda, and Singapore App Store listings for app ID 6475162854, which all name SimpliXio Pte. Ltd. as the developer. The app has been renamed. Depending on the country, it now appears as 'Food & Macro Tracker: MealSnap', 'Food Tracker & Macro: MealSnap', or 'MealSnap: AI Food Log & Tracker', so the directory name is out of date. I didn't find a developer website. mealsnap.ai also offers a photo-based nutrition app called MealSnap, but no page I opened connects it to SimpliXio, so I didn't use it as the official URL. I left the pricing fields empty because the only prices are on apps.apple.com, not the developer's own domain. The US listing shows a free download with in-app subscriptions: Foodie Weekly $3.99, Foodie Monthly $7.99, and Foodie Yearly $59.99. That listing also says advanced AI features need a subscription. However, one version-history note says all logging and tracking features now work with no subscription, so the current pricing model is unclear. The old blurb 'Manage your nutrition in one click' sounds like a slogan, and I couldn't confirm it on any listing. I left out third-party pages (genai.works, techbriefly) because they only repeat the store description.

record.short_description: AI photo restoration tool from ONERECOVERY that repairs blurry, pixelated, damaged, and old photos
record.description: OneRecovery Photo Restoration is an AI-powered feature of ONERECOVERY, a data recovery software brand for Windows and Mac. Its website says it repairs corrupt photos and fixes blurry, grainy, pixelated, overexposed, and old images. It also removes scratches and sharpens detail. It uses AI recognition to find imperfections while leaving undamaged areas untouched, and it adapts its repair method instead of using fixed templates. A free online version lets users upload JPG, PNG, and other formats. The brand also offers data recovery, video repair, and file repair tools.
features: AI recognition and analysis of photo details
Adaptive repairing method instead of fixed templates
Fixes blurry, grainy, pixelated, and overexposed images
Old photo restoration and scratch removal
Free online photo restoration with drag-and-drop upload
Supports JPG, PNG, and other formats
use_cases: Repair corrupted photos that will not open
Repair photos from smartphones and professional cameras
record.notes: The listed URL works and goes to an official ONERECOVERY page called 'Photo Restoration with AI'. The site also has a separate page for the free online tool at /photo-restoration-online. ONERECOVERY is mainly a data recovery suite, and photo restoration is one of its features. The same ONERECOVERY content also shows up on tinyfrom.com, and the site menu links to 'TinyFrom WhatsApp Transfer', so the TinyFrom name seems to be connected to it. The company name MAX&MINI TECHNOLOGY LIMITED comes only from directory listings (Slashdot and Crozdesk), not from a page on the official site. I could not find prices on the official domain. Third-party sites give prices that don't match each other ($4.99 lifetime on Tekpon, $45.95/month on SourceForge, $49.95/year on Slashdot, and $24.95/month for video repair on TechBriefly), so I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. The site has a 'Pricing' menu link and paid desktop products, which is why I marked the tool as freemium. The current blurb is accurate but very short. I hit the search limit before I could check the official pricing page.

record.short_description: AI translator for text, images, documents, speech, and websites in over 100 languages
record.description: OpenL Translate is an online AI translation service. It translates text, images, screenshots, PDFs, Word files, audio, and websites in more than 100 languages, and the company describes its output as context-aware. It also handles scanned PDFs, image-to-image translation, and MP3 transcription with translation. A Chrome and Microsoft Edge extension lets users select text on any web page to translate it or open longer content in a side panel. A free tier uses daily credits, and paid subscriptions raise the limits.
record.pricing_summary: The Free plan gives 40 Fast Credits per day. Paid plans billed yearly are Starter at $8.9/month, Pro at $9.9/month (listed at 50% off, with 1,000 Advanced Credits per month), and Ultimate at $29.9/month, and all three include unlimited Fast Credits.
features: Chrome and Edge extension with side panel
record.notes: I confirmed the product, its features, and its prices from search-result snapshots of openl.io and openl.io/pricing. I didn't open the live pages directly. I couldn't find the legal company name because I hit the search limit before checking the terms or about pages, so that field is empty. The current blurb is in French and is a generic slogan, so it should be replaced. A third-party site (callin.io) lists an older $7.90/month price, which differs from the current official pricing.

record.short_description: AI-powered domain name generator that suggests only available .com domains from a project description
record.description: Only.Coms (Onlycoms.com) is an AI-driven domain name generator that only suggests .com domains. A user types in a description of a project or idea, and the tool uses ChatGPT to come up with fitting names. It then checks which of those names are still available to register. It also has a Random idea option that asks ChatGPT to make up business ideas. A Namecheap blog post says software developer Sandis Klakovskis built it and that it connects to Namecheap for registration.
features: AI-generated .com domain name suggestions from a project description
Checks whether suggested domains are available to register
Random idea feature that generates business ideas
use_cases: Finding an available .com domain for a new project or startup
Brainstorming domain names for side projects
record.notes: I couldn't open the official site (onlycoms.com) because my search tool hit its usage limit. Every fact here comes from third-party pages, mainly a Namecheap blog post about Onlycoms and a few AI-tool directories. Because the site isn't confirmed to be up, status is set to unknown. The directories disagree on price: one says Free with no signup, another says a $20–$40/mo subscription, and another says no free plan. No pricing page on onlycoms.com was found, so pricing is left empty and free_tier is false. The Namecheap post names Sandis Klakovskis as the developer, but I found no company name. The current blurb is accurate but could mention that it uses AI and checks availability.

record.short_description: macOS desktop app for chatting with local LLMs via Ollama using a Ctrl+Space shortcut
record.description: Orac Interface is a desktop app for chatting with a locally hosted large language model without interrupting ongoing work. Pressing Ctrl+Space anywhere on the system opens a chat input. Its GitHub repository states it currently runs on macOS and depends on Ollama, so users install Ollama and pull a local model before installing the app from a .dmg file. Planned additions include Linux support, saving LLM responses, and customizable shortcuts.
features: Ctrl+Space shortcut to open from anywhere
Integrated into your workflow without interruptions
use_cases: Asking an AI questions without interrupting work
Using local LLMs privately on macOS
record.notes: The search tool limit was reached before I could open orac-interface.vercel.app directly, so this record rests mainly on the official GitHub repo (github.com/hamzal0/orac-interface). That repo links to the listed Vercel site and says a demo is available there. I did not confirm that the Vercel site is currently up. Status is set to active because the repo is public. The product appears to come from an individual GitHub developer (hamzal0), not a named company. No pricing was found on the product's own pages. The repo offers a .dmg download but does not state a price or license. The directory sites LogicWeb and Revoyant call it open source; I did not use that to set pricing. AIChief lists paid plans from $9 and describes it as a web-integration and automation tool. That conflicts with the repo, so I ignored it. The current blurb is slogan-like. The repo describes the tool more concretely: 'Easily chat with your local LLM.' Planned items listed in the repo, such as Linux support, response saving, and shortcut changes, are not shipped features, so I kept them out of the features list.

record.short_description: AI sales intelligence platform that automates lead research and prioritizes accounts using buyer signals
record.description: Oppwiser is a sales intelligence platform that uses AI to automate lead research and prioritization. Third-party listings say it monitors buyer signals across the web to find accounts that are ready to buy and help sales teams reach decision makers. Listed tools include an AI Lookalike Company Finder and an AI Opportunity Scanner. The company is reported to be based in Riga, Latvia, and to collect firmographic, technographic, and company online activity data.
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit after one query, so I couldn't open oppwiser.com or a pricing page. Everything in this record comes from third-party listings: G2 and ZoomInfo. ZoomInfo lists the website as www.oppwiser.com, which matches the listed URL. Status is unknown because I couldn't confirm the site is live. I found no pricing on the official domain, and ZoomInfo describes the company's activity as very low. The current blurb ('Optimize targeted prospect detection') is vague, so a rewrite is suggested. Re-check the live site before publishing.

record.short_description: AI platform for higher education that gives real-time writing feedback, grading support, and AI-moderated discussions
record.description: Packback is an instructional AI platform for higher education, built by educators. Its Packback Writing product gives students real-time feedback tied to the instructor's rubric, a digital research assistant, and originality and AI-risk reports. Instructors get an AI grading assistant that checks writing mechanics. Packback Questions is an AI-moderated discussion platform that scores posts with a Curiosity Score. The platform connects to learning management systems through LTI, with single sign-on and gradebook sync.
features: Real-time AI writing feedback aligned to instructor rubrics
AI grading assistant for writing mechanics
Digital Research Assistant with source credibility checks
Automatic APA or MLA citation support
Originality AI Risk report and Fingerprint analysis
Writing Process Report showing drafting timeline and revision history
AI-supported discussion moderation with Curiosity Score
Flags for profanity, repetitiveness, and other concerns
LTI single sign-on and gradebook sync
use_cases: Improving student writing in college courses
Supporting academic integrity in the age of generative AI
Tracking student engagement and retention at institutions
record.notes: The official site is up at packback.co, which is the same site as the listed packback.co with www. The About page says Packback Questions launched in 2016 and Packback Writing in 2022. No pricing page on packback.co was found. The only prices came from third-party sites: Capterra, GetApp, and Software Advice list $25 per feature, and a Baylor University help page mentions a $29 student access fee. Those prices were left out of the record. I ran out of searches before I could check Packback's help center for pricing, so pricing_type is unknown. No free tier was found. Suggested blurb: AI writing feedback, grading support, and discussion tools for higher education.

record.short_description: AI voice and WhatsApp agents that answer calls, route callers, book appointments, and capture messages
record.description: Paka AI is a web-based service that provides AI agents to handle business phone calls and WhatsApp conversations. The agents act as an AI receptionist, answer common questions, and route callers to the right person or department based on what they need. The service also has a message center that captures customer messages and emails them to the team. It can book appointments through calendar integration and handles time zones. Plans are billed by the month and based on call minutes.
record.pricing_summary: Basic costs $25/month with 40 call minutes and 1 bot, Advanced costs $90/month with 400 minutes and 2 bots, and Expert costs $500/month with 3,500 minutes and 3 bots. Extra minutes cost $0.20, $0.15, or $0.10 depending on the plan, and optional WhatsApp add-ons cost $5, $30, or $100 per month.
use_cases: Routing callers to the right department
record.notes: The listed URL https://www.paka.ai/ points to the official site at paka.ai, which is up and lists features and pricing on its homepage. The current blurb is vague. A better one would say the product offers AI phone and WhatsApp agents for call answering, routing, scheduling, and message capture. I found no free plan. The site says 'No credit card required for setup,' but I did not find a free trial stated, so I didn't list one. The site does not name a specific calendar provider. One third-party source (getlatka) ties the company to learnwithpaka.com. I could not confirm the legal company name on the official site.

record.short_description: AI financial planning software, with a client app for automating personal finances and getting AI insights
record.description: Parthean is an AI-powered finance product from a New York startup founded in 2020. The client app page on its site, titled Money Automated, says it automates finances with AI tools. It gives AI insights about linked accounts, supports unlimited accounts, transfers and automations, and helps users manage credit card utilization to build credit and earn points. Several third-party profiles now describe Parthean mainly as an AI financial planning platform for advisors, covering client onboarding, data extraction and AI paraplanning.
record.pricing_summary: Parthean's client app page lists a Parthean Membership at $14.99 per month or $119.99 per year, with a 1-month free trial that can be canceled at any time.
use_cases: Optimizing credit card points and building credit
record.notes: The search tool limit was hit early, so I could not open the homepage or a dedicated pricing page directly. The pricing comes from a search snapshot of parthean.com/client-app, about 668 days old, so it may be out of date. Third-party sources (CB Insights, Toolspedia, topai.tools, dang.ai) say Parthean has shifted to an AI financial planning platform for advisors (onboarding, form builder, data extractors, AI paraplanner), but I could not confirm this on the official site, so the description mentions it only briefly. The current blurb, 'Automatically optimize your budget,' looks outdated and doesn't describe the product well. Directory sites give conflicting prices ($8.99, $9.99, $15) and a 7-day trial; I ignored these. CB Insights lists the company as alive, with $1.6M raised. I found no sign that it was acquired or shut down.

record.company: Paymefy (legal name per Crunchbase: HappyDay Events, S.L.)
record.short_description: AI-powered debt collection and accounts receivable software that automates payment reminders and payment links
record.description: Paymefy is a Barcelona-based software company founded in 2019. It sells an AI-based debt collection and accounts receivable management platform. The software uses machine learning to build notification workflows that contact debtors through channels such as SMS and email. It aims to send the right message at the right time. It also generates unique payment links so debtors can pay in one click. The goal is to help businesses recover unpaid invoices faster and at lower cost.
features: Automated payment reminders via SMS and email
Branded notifications with the company's visual identity
Feedback from customers who refuse to pay
use_cases: Reducing collection costs and recovery time
record.notes: I hit the search tool's usage limit before I could open paymefy.com or any pricing or docs page on it, so nothing here is confirmed from the official site. The listed URL is the same one given on EU-Startups and Crunchbase. Company details come from those third-party pages: founded 2019, based in Barcelona, and raised about €1.2M from Encomenda, Successful Ventures, MNext and Emergia (reported by Nordic9). The feature descriptions come from Capterra and Future Tools. I couldn't find pricing on Paymefy's own domain. Capterra shows a free version and free trial but lists no prices, and Future Tools calls it Paid. Neither is allowed as a pricing source, so pricing is left unknown and free_tier is set to false. I found no page saying the product was acquired or shut down. Status is set to active only because current third-party listings show it as active; I didn't check whether the site is up. The current blurb ('Efficiently optimize debt collection') matches what the sources say the product does, but it is vague. Someone should re-check by opening the official site.

record.short_description: Client onboarding tool listed at pascal.vartion.ai, not verified because web searches failed
record.description: Pascal is listed in the directory as a client onboarding tool at pascal.vartion.ai. The domain suggests it is made by a company called Vartion, but that could not be confirmed. Every web search attempt failed with a tool usage limit error, so no official page, pricing page or docs page was opened. The product's existence, features, pricing, status and company details are all unconfirmed and should be checked by hand before publishing.
record.notes: Not verified. Every web search attempt returned 'Server tool use limit exceeded', so I could not open the listed website (https://pascal.vartion.ai/) or any other source. Because nothing was opened, official_url, company, pricing and features are left empty, and exists is set to false, meaning not confirmed rather than confirmed missing. The domain suggests the company is Vartion, but I could not confirm this. From memory, Vartion's Pascal may be an AI tool for KYC/AML checks such as adverse media screening during client due diligence, but no page I opened supports that, so it is not recorded. The current blurb 'Accelerate effortless client onboarding.' reads like a slogan and should be replaced after a manual check of the official site and any pricing page. Re-run verification when search is available.

record.short_description: AI essay writing platform that generates structured academic essays plus outlining, paraphrasing, and citation tools
record.description: PerfectEssayWriter.ai is a web-based AI writing tool aimed mainly at students, educators, and professionals. Users enter a topic, word count, and essay type, and the tool produces an essay draft. Alongside the core essay writer, the platform offers an essay outliner, paraphrasing tool, citation generator, grammar checker, and summarizer. A Chrome extension pairs the AI essay writer with an AI content detector. The site describes its output as plagiarism-free, and users can start with a free account.
record.pricing_summary: The official homepage's structured data lists an offer price of $9.99. Its title also advertises a free AI essay writer, but I could not confirm the full tier breakdown on an official pricing page.
use_cases: Drafting academic essays by topic, word count, and essay type
record.notes: I confirmed the official site from a search result for perfectessaywriter.ai, but I hit the search limit before I could open a dedicated official pricing page. The homepage metadata shows only a $9.99 offer price, with no billing period given. Third-party sites disagree on the plans. GoodFirms and SaaSworthy list Free (1,500 words), Basic $9.99/mo, Pro $14.99/mo, and Advanced $99.99/yr. G2 lists $29.99/mo and $179.99/yr, and TechBriefly lists $29.99/mo and $249.99/yr. Because of that, I left the tier details out of the summary, and they should be rechecked on the official pricing page. Some features, like the outliner, grammar checker, summarizer, thesis generator, and live editor, come from review and directory sites and the Chrome Web Store listing rather than an official feature page. I found no company legal name beyond the 'PerfectEssayWriter.ai' creator name in the site metadata. The site also markets its essays as undetectable by AI, which may matter for an academic-integrity review. The current blurb ('Succeed easily in academic writing') is a slogan and should be replaced.

record.short_description: Voice-based AI mock interview platform that generates questions from job descriptions and gives instant feedback
record.description: PracticeInterview.ai is a web platform where job seekers practice for interviews. Users paste in a job description, and the tool generates interview questions tailored to that role and job level. Users answer out loud, and the AI returns scores and personalized feedback. The site describes the experience as a realistic mock interview simulation that users can do at their own pace, with the aim of reducing anxiety and building confidence before real interviews.
use_cases: Practicing answers to role-specific interview questions
Reducing interview anxiety and building confidence
record.notes: The official homepage loads and describes the product. Its FAQ includes a 'How much does it cost?' question, but the search snapshot cut off the answer, and I could not find a pricing page on practiceinterview.ai. Prices only showed up on third-party sites, and they don't agree with each other: There's An AI For That says there is a free trial and paid options from $9 per unit, pay-as-you-go, and a coupon/review site (tenereteam) lists one-time plans at $29, $39 and $59. Because neither source is the product's own site, I left the pricing fields empty and set free_tier to false. The company or operator behind the product is not named on the pages I found. A search tool limit stopped me from running more searches. The current blurb is vague. A clearer version would be: 'AI voice mock interviews with feedback, tailored to a job description.' This is a different product from practiceinterviews.com.

record.short_description: AI photo editor for background removal, photo enhancement, object removal and product image generation
record.description: PicWish is an AI-powered photo editor available on the web and as iOS and Android apps. It removes image backgrounds, with batch processing of up to 30 files, and unblurs and enhances photos. It also removes unwanted objects such as text, logos and watermarks. Its chat-based designer edits images from natural-language prompts and generates e-commerce product shots and model images. PicWish also sells developer APIs for background removal, photo enhancement, object removal, ID photos, compression and OCR.
features: Batch editing of up to 30 files
Photo colorization and old photo restoration
record.notes: The official site is up and calls the editor 'Free to use'. It also mentions a Pro app and paid API services, so I marked it freemium. I couldn't find a pricing page on picwish.com. The only prices I found were on directory sites (SourceForge and Slashdot list $6.99/month or $49.99/year for the app), so I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. Slashdot names the company as Wangxutech, but I couldn't confirm that on the official site, so company is empty. The current blurb is too narrow: the product does much more than e-commerce image optimization. That includes background removal, enhancement, AI editing and APIs.

record.short_description: Link-in-bio and mobile website builder for creators with digital product sales, payments, and email collection
record.description: Portaly is a link-in-bio and mobile website builder for visual creators and businesses. It is based in Taipei. Users build a customizable bio page from building blocks and can turn an existing website or profile into a link-in-bio page using AI. The platform also handles selling digital products, payments, donations, email list collection, and analytics. It can embed video and audio from platforms such as YouTube, TikTok, Twitch, and Vimeo. There is a free plan and a paid Premium plan.
record.pricing_summary: The Free plan costs $0 a month and includes 12 blocks, 1 page, 10 email collections, and a 12% fee on donations and products. Premium is $5.99 a month billed annually ($71.88 a year, shown against an $18 list price) with the first 14 days free, and adds unlimited blocks and pages, a custom domain, SEO tools, GA/GTM/Pixel tracking, and a 6% fee.
features: Customizable link-in-bio page with building blocks
record.notes: Pricing comes from Portaly's own pricing page (portaly.cc/en/pricing). The page also offers monthly billing, but I could not find the actual monthly price. The legal name Real Engine Inc. and the Taipei location come from Crunchbase, not Portaly's own site. Integrations come from Portaly's own blog post (Q1 2023) and pricing page. The current blurb is too narrow: Portaly now pitches itself as an all-in-one tool for creators who want to make money, with payments, digital products, and email collection, not just a page of social links. My web search limit ran out partway through, so I only read the English homepage through search snippets, not directly.

record.short_description: AI presentation maker that turns prompts or uploaded documents into designed, editable slide decks
record.description: PowerPresent AI is a web-based tool that builds presentations with AI. Users enter a prompt or upload a PDF or Word document, and the tool writes and designs a full deck. Decks can be edited in the browser and presented from there. The free plan includes watermarked PDF downloads. Paid plans add editable .pptx export with native charts and document upload. Users can also upload their own templates or pay for professional presentation design help.
record.pricing_summary: A free plan allows unlimited creating, editing and presenting, with watermarked PDF downloads. Paid options include one-time credits ($5 for 1 presentation, $19 for 10, $49 for 40), monthly plans at $9, $29 and $49, and a $499 lifetime option.
features: Full deck generated from a prompt
Turn uploaded PDF or Word documents into slides
Create, edit and present in the browser
Watermarked PDF export on free plan
record.notes: The site is up and was confirmed through own-domain pages: Terms (updated October 2025), blog, and Hire Professional. A dedicated pricing page could not be opened because the search tool limit was reached. Pricing comes from a recent blog post on the official domain. Prices on the official domain conflict with each other. The Hire Professional FAQ says $2 per presentation, a 7-deck bundle for $12, and a free first presentation. A Prezi comparison post lists a $2 Starter, a $19/month Pro plan with 15 credits, a $49/month Power plan with 40 credits, and a $99/year plan. Pricing should be checked again before publishing. Google Slides export is mentioned only on third-party directories (SourceForge, LogicWeb), so it was not listed as an integration. Third-party deal sites list a lifetime subscription for $79.99 (MSRP $240). The current blurb is accurate but vague.

record.short_description: Mobile photo and video editing app with AI effects, filters, retouching tools and templates
record.description: Prequel is a photo and video editing app for iOS and Android from Prequel Inc. It offers more than 800 effects and filters, including D3D, AR objects and captions. Its AI-powered effects can turn selfies and portraits into artwork or comic-style images. The app also includes retouching tools for smoothing skin, whitening teeth and reshaping faces, plus color correction, templates, music and stickers. Users can edit for free, and a paid Prequel Gold subscription unlocks the full collection of effects and tools.
record.pricing_summary: The app is free to download and use with some features. The paid Prequel Gold subscription unlocks all filters, effects and tools, billed weekly, monthly or annually, but the company's own site does not list prices.
features: AI-powered effects for selfies and portraits
Retouching: skin smoothing, teeth whitening, face reshaping
D3D effects, AR objects and captions
Color correction with vintage, retro and Y2K styles
use_cases: Editing photos and videos for social media
Turning selfies into AI art or comic-style images
record.notes: I confirmed the official site (prequel.app), Prequel Inc. as the company, and the Prequel Gold subscription policy on prequel.app. App Store and Google Play listings confirm the app is free with in-app purchases and has weekly, monthly and annual plans. Prequel's own site gives no prices. Review sites (Common Sense Media, Filmora, SoftwareFinder) mention figures such as $4.95 to $7.99 per week and $34.99 per year, but I left these out because they don't come from Prequel's site. The App Store also lists free trials. The current blurb, 'Enhance your images to captivate your audience,' is vague and leaves out video editing and AI effects. A separate AI selfie page also exists at ai.prequel.app. My search limit ran out after the first two searches, so I relied on page excerpts from those results.

record.short_description: AI language-learning app where learners practice speaking with lifelike AI tutors and get instant feedback
record.description: Praktika is a mobile language-learning app that teaches speaking through real conversations with lifelike AI tutors. The tutors listen, reply and coach learners in real time, and can explain things in the learner's native language. The app gives feedback on pronunciation and grammar and offers personalized lessons. It started as an English-only app but now covers several languages. A business plan gives teams access to the full language catalogue, a pronunciation score and a monitoring dashboard. The site reports 30M+ learners.
record.pricing_summary: For business, Starter (10–49 seats) costs $12 per user per month and Growth (50–99 seats) costs $10 per user per month, with lower per-seat pricing at 100+ seats. A Praktika blog post puts individual plans at about $8 per month.
features: Real-time feedback on pronunciation and grammar
Tutor speaks in your native language
use_cases: Building speaking fluency through everyday conversation
record.notes: The official site is up. The homepage says 'Try it for free!' but does not say whether that is a free plan or a trial. A third-party review (copycatcafe.com) says Praktika offers a limited free version in the mobile app, but I did not confirm this on Praktika's own site, so free_tier is set to false and pricing_type to paid. The consumer price of about $8/month comes from a blog post on praktika.ai. Review and directory sites give the same figure, and one review says the price can change after onboarding. The 100+ seat business price was not visible. The current blurb is outdated: Praktika now covers multiple languages (the Google Play listing says 11), not just English. A suggested replacement is 'Learn languages by speaking with AI tutors.' Note that softwaresuggest.com lists an unrelated dental software product also named Praktika.

record.short_description: AI coding assistant that generates, optimizes, reviews, and debugs code across many programming languages
record.description: ProgramAI is an AI-powered coding assistant offered as an online subscription service. Its website says it writes code in one click and can produce full web apps and games. It works with languages such as JavaScript, Python, Java, C#, C++ and Swift. The site lists real-time code optimization, error detection, automated code review and testing, codebase analytics, and a personalized learning assistant. ProgramAI says it integrates with major IDEs. It is aimed at users ranging from students and beginners to experienced developers and enterprises.
record.pricing_summary: The Basic plan costs $49.99/month and the Professional plan costs $399.99/month. The site says users who request access can qualify for a $7, 7-day trial.
features: Learns from user coding style with tailored suggestions
use_cases: Creating full web apps in one click
Writing code for a full game
Learning to code for students and beginners
Code review and debugging for developers and enterprises
record.notes: The product details and pricing come from search-result snippets of programai.co. I could not open the site directly, and the search tool limit was reached before I could search further. I found no company or legal entity name on the official site. Trustpilot lists a contact location in Colombia.
