Trustpilot reviews and a Medium post (medi-muse.medium.com) report a paid $7 trial that automatically becomes a recurring charge of about $49/month, along with trouble cancelling and getting support. Directories should look into this before listing the tool. Unrelated similarly named sites (programai.io, a Web3 ad tool, and Programa) are different products. The current blurb is accurate but vague.

record.short_description: Product management platform for organizing customer feedback, prioritizing features, and building and sharing product roadmaps
record.description: Productboard is a customer-centric product management platform that helps teams understand what customers need, decide what to build next, and keep everyone aligned on the roadmap. Teams can make customizable roadmaps from templates and share them with different stakeholders. They can also send prioritized features into delivery tools like Jira. For larger organizations, Productboard offers enterprise-grade security and compliance, permissions with role-based controls, open APIs, and first-party integrations. It also includes an AI chat called Spark.
features: Push prioritized features into delivery and track status
Spark AI chat with MCP connectors
use_cases: Communicating strategy and roadmaps to stakeholders
Coordinating product teams at enterprise scale
record.notes: I checked the official site (productboard.com enterprise, solutions, and integrations pages, plus support.productboard.com). It is live, so the status is active. I could not open the official pricing page because I hit my search limit. Prices only came from third-party sites, and they disagree: some list Starter free, Essentials $19, Pro $59 per maker per month, and Enterprise custom. Others say pricing changed in 2026 to plans called Spark, or Free/Plus/Business. Because of this, I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty, set pricing_type to unknown, and set free_tier to false. Someone should check https://www.productboard.com/pricing/ directly. The current blurb, 'Optimize product management through data', is vague. The official pages focus on customer feedback, prioritization, and roadmaps. Azure DevOps is listed as 'ADO' on the support integrations page.

record.short_description: Prompt optimizer that generates and refines prompts for large language models and image generation models
record.description: PromptPerfect is a prompt generator and optimizer from Jina AI. It offers an interactive way to improve prompts for large language models and image models, including GPT-4, Claude, Llama, Stable Diffusion and Midjourney. Developers can also use an API with endpoints to optimize a single prompt or up to 16 prompts in one batch. The site says that after Elastic acquired Jina AI in October 2025, PromptPerfect will no longer be available after September 1, 2026.
features: Supports GPT-4, Claude, Llama, Stable Diffusion and Midjourney
Batch optimization of up to 16 prompts via /optimizeBatch
Access through the Jina AI SDK
use_cases: Prompt engineering for large language models
Optimizing prompts for image generation models
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize social media editorial content') is wrong. PromptPerfect is an AI prompt optimizer. Both the official homepage and the /api page say Jina AI was acquired by Elastic in October 2025 and that PromptPerfect will no longer be available after September 1, 2026. I set the status to acquired because the buyer is named. If the current date is after September 1, 2026, change it to shutdown and consider removing the listing. The only prices I found were on third-party directories (Pro $19.99/month, $99.99/month for API access, plus a free plan mentioned), so I left pricing empty. My search limit ran out before I could open an official pricing page, so free_tier is false only because it couldn't be confirmed.

record.short_description: AI tools that generate real estate and Airbnb listing descriptions, house rules, and interior design images
record.description: PropertyListingsAI is a web-based set of AI tools for real estate agents, property managers, and vacation rental hosts. It writes property descriptions, titles, and supporting marketing copy. Other tools turn property photos into Airbnb listings, write Airbnb house rules, and create improved interior design images from room photos. The site also has a mortgage calculator. Pricing is a one-time credit purchase with no subscription, and the credits can be used to make listings for major real estate and vacation rental platforms.
record.pricing_summary: There is no subscription. A one-time payment of $9.99 buys 15 credits, and this is labeled the most popular plan.
features: Airbnb listing generator from property photos
Listing titles and supporting marketing copy
use_cases: Writing real estate listing descriptions for sale or rent
Creating Airbnb and vacation rental listings
Writing house rules for short-term rentals
Making improved interior design images from room photos
record.notes: The current blurb, 'Optimize ad publishing on networks,' is inaccurate. The site is an AI listing-copy and real estate tools product, not an ad-network publishing tool. I found pricing ($9.99 one-time for 15 credits) in search-indexed content from the product's own homepage. I couldn't open a separate pricing page because I hit the search tool's limit. The site says 'trusted by the best real estate agents' but names no customers. The site doesn't name the company or owner. One third-party directory (topai.tools) lists the product as freemium, but I couldn't confirm a free tier on the official site, so free_tier is set to false.

record.short_description: AI workplace assistant that searches connected company tools to answer employee questions with cited sources
record.description: Quench is an AI workplace assistant from Quench.ai for fast-growing teams. It connects to a company's internal tools and data. Employees can ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn only from that connected data, with the sources listed for each answer. If it finds no relevant information, it says so instead of making up an answer. The company says content is protected with AES-256 encryption and that access is limited to authorised users. Google Cloud describes it as a tool for breaking down knowledge silos.
features: Says clearly when no answer is found
record.notes: The official homepage (www.quench.ai, titled 'Work AI Assistant for Fast Growing Teams') is live and supports the listed blurb. I found no pricing page on quench.ai, so pricing is unknown and free tier is set to false. A third-party directory (aitoolguru) calls it free, but I did not use that. Integrations like Slack, Google Drive, Notion and Salesforce, and the claim of 60+ connected tools, come only from Dealroom, ZoomInfo and StartupIntros, not the official site, so I left integrations empty. Google Cloud's case study confirms it is an AI workplace assistant that gives instant access to internal data. Founder: Husayn Kassai (Onfido co-founder). It raised a $5M pre-seed in 2023, when UKTN described it as an AI coaching/learning platform, so the product seems to have changed focus. Do not confuse it with Culligan Quench (water coolers, acquired by Culligan) or projectquench.ai (medical record review). The search tool limit stopped me before I could open a pricing or docs page.

record.short_description: AI-powered search engine for finding, comparing, and assessing the reproducibility of experimental protocols
record.description: PubCompare is a web-based search engine for experimental protocols, aimed at scientists in academia, pharma and biotech, and lab equipment teams. Its database draws protocols from peer-reviewed publications, preprints, and patents, mainly in life sciences and chemistry. It uses AI to find similar protocols, compare protocol sections across publications, highlight critical steps, and judge reproducibility from in-protocol citations. Paid plans add Protocolyze and Product Application reports, document uploads, and API and MCP integration with lab systems.
record.pricing_summary: There is a Free plan. Premium costs €19.95/month and adds 10 Product Application Reports and 2 Protocolyze Reports (up to 20 protocols) per month, uploads of up to 100 documents, and no ads. The Organization plan has multiple seats, custom report volumes, and API/MCP integration, and no price is listed.
features: Semantic search grouping synonyms and variations
Upload own documents to enrich reports
use_cases: Comparing similar protocols to identify critical steps
Protocol research for academia, pharma/biotech, and lab equipment teams
record.notes: Pricing, plan details, and integrations (LIMS, ELN, SOP repository, licensed full text through API/MCP) come from the official pricing page at pubcompare.ai/pricing, which was reached through search results. The Premium plan is described as 'Everything in Free plus', which confirms that a free tier exists. The homepage was not opened directly. The description of what the product does (protocol search, comparison, in-protocol citation reproducibility, semantic search, hazards detection, preprints/patents sources) comes mainly from third-party directories (toolify, theresanaiforthat, moge, seektool). The operating company name was not confirmed on an official page, so company is left empty. Database size claims on directories differ (26M vs 40M+), so they were left out. Some directories list wrong prices: aichief shows $45/$99 plans, and an older 'Individual (Academic) 19.95 €' tier with a 5-day trial appears elsewhere. The official page shows neither the $45/$99 plans nor a free trial. The current blurb is accurate but short.

record.short_description: AI tool that turns long videos into short captioned clips for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts
record.description: QuickReel is an AI video clipping and editing platform for creators, brands, marketers, and teams. It turns long-form videos such as podcasts, live streams, and YouTube videos into short clips for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. It tracks the speaker and reframes footage to 16:9, 1:1, or 9:16, and it adds subtitles in 20+ languages. It also offers brand templates, a social media scheduler, voice generation, faceless video generation from prompts, team workspaces, and API access.
record.pricing_summary: The pricing page says you can start free. Paid plans are Starter at $9/month (100 credits), Pro at $29/month (promo $17.40, 250 credits), Pro+ at $49/month (promo $29.40, 500 credits), and Ultimate at $89/month promo, renewing at $99 (1,000 credits). One credit equals one minute of input video.
features: AI clipping of long videos into short clips
Auto speaker tracking and reframing for 16:9, 1:1, 9:16
Faceless video generation from a prompt
Text to video and text to speech APIs
use_cases: Repurposing live streams and YouTube videos into Shorts, Reels, and TikToks
Scaling short-form content output for teams
Generating clips at scale through the API
record.notes: The listed URL is www.quickreel.io. The official pages show up as quickreel.io, with the app at app.quickreel.io and docs at docs.quickreel.io. The prices come from search snippets of quickreel.io/pricing, which shows promo discounts with odd details: Ultimate is shown as $259 struck through, $89/month, renewing at $99. Prices may change, so recheck them. The free tier is based on the pricing page saying 'start free' and QuickReel blog posts describing a free plan. The free plan's exact limits weren't visible on the pricing page; they came from third-party sites, so they're left out. The current blurb, 'Optimize clips for more shares', is vague. A better one would say it uses AI to turn long videos into short clips. LinkedIn, PitchBook, and AppSumo (third-party) name Ayush Sharma and Ansh Vashistha as founders, with the company based in India and founded in 2022. No acquisition or shutdown was found.

record.short_description: AI-powered diagnostic practice tests that predict SAT, ACT and PSAT/NMSQT scores for students
record.description: R.test is an AI-powered diagnostic test platform that helps students gauge their readiness for the SAT, ACT and PSAT/NMSQT. Its R.test Mini format uses AI to predict a score from fewer questions than a full-length exam. The site says this takes about 40 minutes on average. Tests run in a stage-adaptive format that mirrors the official exams. Afterward, students get an analytics report on strengths and weaknesses, step-by-step explanations, and a Q Bank for targeted practice.
features: AI score prediction with fewer questions (R.test Mini)
Stage-adaptive test format like the real exam
AI-generated analytics report with 10 types of insights
Realistic test environment with navigator and timer
use_cases: Finding strengths and areas for improvement
record.notes: Both the official site (rtest.ai) and the student login page (student.rtest.ai) are indexed and live. The homepage title says 'Get your SAT/ACT Score in 40 minutes', and its FAQ says R.test Mini takes about 40 minutes on average. The time claims don't agree across the site, though: the DSAT page title says 30 minutes, the exam pages say a free score in 15 minutes for the SAT and ACT and 14 minutes for the PSAT, and a blog post says 45 minutes. The homepage FAQ looks dated because it mentions additions expected in 2023. The official pages show a free test and list accepted payment methods (credit/debit card, PayPal and Paymentwall), but I couldn't find a page on rtest.ai with actual prices. Third-party prices disagree with each other (aichief.com lists $19/month; a LearnQ comparison page lists $19.99 to $79.99), so I left the pricing fields empty. The company name Riiid, Inc. comes from toolify.ai, a directory site; I didn't confirm it on rtest.ai. Crunchbase places the company in Seoul. Suggested blurb fix: the current French blurb leaves out which exams it covers. Something like 'Tests diagnostiques IA pour prédire son score au SAT, ACT et PSAT en environ 40 min' would be clearer.

record.short_description: AI tool that writes personalized first lines and icebreakers for cold outreach emails
record.description: Quicklines is an AI cold outreach assistant that writes personalized opening lines, or icebreakers, for cold emails. According to third-party listings and its Product Hunt page, users upload a CSV of prospects and get back a sheet with lines written for each contact. The lines can then go into the first sentence of an email. Listings say it pulls prospect details from LinkedIn profiles to write the lines. Crunchbase lists the company as based in Sterling, Virginia, and founded in 2021.
features: AI-personalized first lines for cold emails
CSV upload and download of a sheet with written lines
Social scraping of prospect LinkedIn profiles
use_cases: Replacing virtual assistants who write first lines
Preparing lead lists for cold email campaigns
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit before I could open quicklines.ai or any pricing page on that domain. Everything here comes from search-result snippets of third-party pages: Crunchbase, Product Hunt, Brandfetch, BestofAI, findmyaitool and others. Pricing appears only on third-party pages, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are empty. Several of those pages, plus a maker comment on Product Hunt, describe a $59 one-time lifetime deal with 300 credits/lines per month. One review site instead claims $59/month for 500 lines, which conflicts and is unverified. Crunchbase lists the company as active and names Shahnavaz Kadirmohideen as founder and CTO. Status is unknown because I did not confirm the site is up. The current blurb is broadly accurate but vague; it could say AI-written icebreakers/first lines for cold emails. Re-check the official site and its pricing before publishing.

record.short_description: AI platform that analyzes global real estate data to find investment properties and estimate costs
record.description: RealtyOmega is an AI-driven real estate investment and asset management platform. It uses AI algorithms to analyze global data, such as city plans, growth trajectories, population trends, vacancy rates, economic indicators and local development projects, to find promising investment opportunities. It also estimates purchase costs, including down payment, closing costs, fees, taxes, HOA and insurance, and it estimates profit. An AI agent gives users personalized insights and calculations. Access to the AI engine is requested by email, and companies can request a demo.
features: AI analysis of global real estate data
Market trend analysis of city plans, population trends and vacancy rates
Cost estimation including down payment, closing costs, taxes, HOA and insurance
Personalized insights and calculations from an AI agent
use_cases: Identifying promising real estate investment opportunities
record.notes: Details come from a search-indexed copy of the official homepage (realtyomega.com). I could not open the page directly because the search tool limit was reached, and I could not reach a separate pricing or docs page. The homepage shows no prices. It mentions a '3 Months Free Trial' and asks users to email info@realtyomega.com for access to the AI engine or to request a demo. Because of this, pricing_type is unknown and free_tier is false: a trial is not a free tier. Third-party directories disagree on pricing (Tool2Mate says Freemium, Neura says Free, Creati.ai says there is no free plan). One directory (Neura) mentions an API, but the official page does not, so I left it out. Most directory listings date from 2024, and I found no proof of recent activity. The listed blurb 'Maximize your real estate gains' is a slogan and should be replaced with the short description. No legal company name was found beyond 'Realty Omega'.

record.short_description: AI tool that removes image backgrounds automatically, with bulk processing, an online editor, and API
record.description: Removal.AI is a web-based tool that uses AI to remove backgrounds from images. It finds the subject in a photo automatically and returns it on a transparent, white, or custom background. It can handle hair and furry edges and accepts more than 1,000 images in a single upload. After the background is removed, users can keep working in its online photo editor. Developers can use an API, and the site offers a free low-resolution option for personal use.
record.pricing_summary: Free for low-resolution (0.25 MP) images and personal use. Full resolution costs 1 credit per image: one-time credit packs run from 3 credits for $1.89 to 13,000 for $1,499 (valid 3 years), and monthly plans run from 100 credits for $5.99 to 90,000 for $1,650, with custom high-volume plans for 10,000+ images a month.
features: Cutouts for hair and furry edges
Online photo editor with text and effects
10 free API preview credits per month
use_cases: Automated background removal in apps through the API
record.notes: The site is up and confirms what the tool does. Prices come from removal.ai/pricing, which search tools say was indexed about 555 days ago, so they may have changed since. Older pages on removal.ai and third-party reviews list different tier amounts. The legal name REMOVAL.AI LTD comes from the official Figma plugin listing, which is on figma.com rather than the product's own site. I found no page saying the company was acquired. The current blurb ('Prepare your images for fast distribution') is vague and doesn't say the tool removes backgrounds. It should be replaced. The listed name 'Removal' should probably be 'Removal.AI'.

record.short_description: Pre-release AI tool that rewrites resumes and automates cover letters and job applications
record.description: Resume Rewriter AI is an early-stage project at resumerewriter.online. It aims to automate job hunting by rewriting CVs for each application, writing personalised cover letters and sending automated responses to job applications. The site says it is still validating the idea. Users can try a custom ChatGPT version now, which requires a ChatGPT Plus subscription, or pre-order the planned product with a one-time payment. Pre-order buyers are promised access to the closed beta, a private group with the creator and input on new features.
record.pricing_summary: A free Waiting List tier gives access to Rewrite Resume V1, a ChatGPT-based version that needs ChatGPT Plus. A $12 one-time pre-order adds Rewrite Resume V2, closed beta access, a private community and feature requests, and the site also lists a Custom tier without a price; there are no subscriptions.
features: AI CV rewriting for each job application
Job lists, resumes and prompt updated monthly (V1) or daily (V2)
Closed beta access and private creator group for pre-order buyers
use_cases: Tailoring a resume for each job application
Writing cover letters for job applications
Automating job search and application responses
record.notes: Everything here comes from the indexed text of the official homepage in search results. I could not open the page directly to confirm the site is currently live, and I hit the search limit before I could check further. The site describes a product that has not launched yet ('Validate our idea', pre-order before release). Right now it only offers a custom ChatGPT that requires ChatGPT Plus, so the free tier is not truly free to use. The pricing text in the snippet is jumbled. The $12 seems to be the pre-order price, and a 'User' tier promising endless free rewriting seems to describe the planned release, but it is unclear which tier each item belongs to. No company or owner name was found. The current blurb ('Optimize applications and response times') is vague. Do not confuse this site with resumerewriter.com, a separate product with $0/$19/$49 plans.

record.short_description: AI reputation management tool that monitors reviews across 100+ sites and auto-generates responses
record.description: RepBot.ai is an online reputation management tool for businesses. According to its pricing page, it monitors reviews from more than 100 sites and generates review responses automatically. It can also publish those responses through Google and Facebook integrations. Higher tiers add review removal, which flags reviews that break platform policies, and let users spend unused response credits on past reviews. Plans differ mainly in how many response generations are included each month.
record.pricing_summary: Lite is $25/mo for 10 response generations, Business is $75/mo for 50, and Enterprise is $150/mo for 100, as early-bird quarterly prices. The standard prices are $50, $150, and $300/mo, and each plan has a 30-day money-back guarantee.
features: Automatic Google and Facebook response publishing
Review removal: identify and flag platform violations
Apply unused response credits to past reviews
record.notes: I could only read the official pricing page as a search-indexed copy that is about 3 years old. I couldn't open repbot.ai live, so I can't confirm the site is still up or that these prices are current, and status is set to unknown. That page mentions an early-bird offer and a money-back guarantee but no free tier. Some directory sites call it freemium, but the official page doesn't back that up. No company name was found. The domains repbot.dev and rep-bot.net belong to separate products also called RepBot and should not be mixed up with this one. The current blurb is accurate but generic.

record.short_description: AI platform that turns room and exterior photos into virtual staging, redesign, and landscaping visuals
record.description: REimagineHome is an AI design platform that works from photos of real rooms and exteriors. Users upload a photo, pick a design goal or describe a change in plain language, and get photorealistic results. It handles virtual staging, redesigning furnished rooms, decluttering, and landscaping. Paid plans add a conversational design flow, reference photos, real product visualization, and batch processing for listings. It is aimed at homeowners, real estate agents, and interior designers. An Android app is also available.
record.pricing_summary: Credit-based monthly plans priced from $14 to $99/mo: Essential (30 credits/mo), Pro (200 credits/mo), Advanced (400 credits/mo), and Agency for high-volume teams. New users get 5 free designs.
features: Reference photos for scene or object guidance
use_cases: Virtually staging empty rooms for real estate listings
Generating marketing assets from real estate photos
Visualizing home improvement and renovation ideas
Refreshing curb appeal and landscaping concepts
record.notes: Official site, pricing page, and FAQ were found through search results. I hit the search limit, so I couldn't open the homepage directly. The pricing page gives a $14–$99/mo range and lists credit counts per tier, but no per-tier prices. Per-tier prices ($14/$49/$74/$99) appear only on a third-party review site, so they are not recorded here. The FAQ says plans start at $36/month for the full agentic experience. That doesn't match the pricing page, and an older official blog post lists different tiers, so pricing appears to have changed. I recorded the free offer (5 free designs for new users) as a one-time trial, not an ongoing free tier. The company name (Styldod, Inc.) comes only from a third-party directory (aigearbase), not the official site. No integrations or API were confirmed on official pages. The current blurb reads like a slogan and doesn't say what the product does.

record.short_description: AI pre-production platform that turns screenplays into script breakdowns, shooting schedules, and budgets
record.description: RivetAI is an AI-powered pre-production platform for screenwriters and film production teams. It takes a screenplay and prepares a first pass of the scene and character breakdown, script coverage, stripboard schedules, and budget topsheets. Budgets can include guild rates, tax incentives, fringes, and scenario planning. Writers get a script editor with tags, revisions, and snapshots. Production crews get scheduling and budgeting tools plus API access. Pricing is a one-time payment per project rather than a subscription.
record.pricing_summary: Free ($0): up to 5 scenes in the script editor, 1 seat, 0 AI credits. Writer costs $49.99 per project (30 AI credits, 2 seats) and Studio costs $150 per project (100 AI credits, 9 seats, scheduling, budgeting and API). Both are one-time payments per project with no subscription.
features: Script editor with tags, revisions & snapshots
AI top-sheet budgets with guild rates, tax incentives and fringes
use_cases: Moving from screenplay to shoot plan
Shooting schedule creation for 1st ADs and line producers
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize texts for social networks') is wrong. RivetAI is a film and TV pre-production tool, not a tool for social media copy. The official site, LinkedIn, and Medium all describe it as an AI copilot for pre-production. Pricing comes from the official rivetai.com/en page. Some third-party directories list older $49/month subscription or 14-day trial pricing, but the official site now says pricing is pay-once per project. Crunchbase lists the legal entity as Rivetai Inc. (Culver City, CA), with CEO Debajyoti Ray. The legal name was not confirmed on the official site, so the company field uses RivetAI. Third-party sites mention FDX, CSV, PDF, and XLSX exports, but the official page I saw did not confirm them, so they were left out. RivetAI is not related to Ironclad's open-source Rivet or the Rivet creator CRM.

record.short_description: AI agent platform that resolves customer support tickets across email, chat, voice and WhatsApp
record.description: Robylon is an AI customer support platform for building and deploying multilingual AI agents without code. The agents resolve queries, qualify leads and take actions across chat, WhatsApp, email, tickets and voice. They can work on their own or alongside an existing helpdesk, and they act inside connected tools, for example by starting a return in Shopify or updating a Zendesk ticket. Teams build each agent from a knowledge base plus workflows and tools. Pricing is based on AI credits rather than seats.
record.pricing_summary: The free Starter plan includes 300 AI credits a month (about 40 conversations), and Pro starts at $25/month for 500 credits. Business ranges from $180 to $300/month for 4,500 to 10,000 credits, yearly billing is 10% off, and optional live agent seats cost $19, $49 or $89 per seat per month.
features: Omnichannel support across chat, WhatsApp, email, tickets and voice
Human escalation inbox with live agent seats
record.notes: I checked the official homepage, pricing page, platform overview, blog and guides.robylon.ai. The current blurb is too narrow. Robylon is an AI agent platform for support and pre-sales across several channels, not just a ticket management tool. Prices on G2 and SaaSworthy (Pro $35-$39, 250/2,000 credits) and AlternativeTo (one-time $199-$3,999) are older or don't match the official pricing page, so I ignored them. AlternativeTo names the developer as Zooid Tech Inc., but no official page I opened confirmed that, so the company field uses the brand name Robylon AI. The integrations list is drawn from Robylon's own pages, including a Robylon blog post, not from a dedicated integrations directory.

record.short_description: Former AI web tool for restoring old photos, fixing blurry faces, and colorizing black-and-white images
record.description: Restore Photos One was described by third-party directories as a free online AI tool for repairing old or damaged photographs. According to those listings, it restored blurry face photos, retouched faces in high definition and colorized black-and-white images, with no registration or software download required. The listed domain, restorephotos.one, no longer appears to host the product. Search results show it with an unrelated online slot gambling title and recipe content. No current official product page could be confirmed.
record.notes: The listed website, restorephotos.one, no longer appears to host this product. In search results, www.restorephotos.one had the title '12NAGA: Situs Slot Online Thailand Gampang Maxwin Hari Ini' (an online slot gambling site), and the indexed page showed unrelated Hawaii recipe content. The domain looks lapsed or repurposed. I could not confirm this from a live page because I ran out of searches, so this is based on search results only. No page says the product was discontinued, so status is set to unknown rather than shutdown. The features, use cases and description come only from third-party directories (genai.works and saashub.com), which described the tool as free with no registration. That free claim appears only on directory sites, so pricing is left empty. Do not confuse this product with similarly named tools: restorephotos.io (the open-source Nutlope project), restorephotos.me, restorephoto.net, restoreoldphotos.io and restorephotosapp.com. The current blurb, 'Revive your old photos in one click', is not supported by any live official page. I recommend removing the row or marking it inactive.

record.short_description: AI writing assistant and language model API for grammar checking, autocomplete, and AI detection
record.description: Sapling is an AI writing assistant and language model API toolkit for enterprises, developers, and customer-facing teams. It offers grammar and spell checking, autocomplete, rephrasing, snippets, and AI content detection. Teams can use it through a browser extension, through Google Docs, Outlook, and Word, or through its API and SDK. Its Sapling Suggest product recommends chat responses on messaging platforms, using OpenAI models. Sapling says its team comes from the Berkeley and Stanford AI labs and that it is backed by Y Combinator.
record.pricing_summary: The Free plan costs $0/month and allows AI detector checks of up to 2,000 characters. Pro costs $25/month, or $12/month billed annually, with checks up to 100,000 characters; the API is metered with a one-time $5 minimum, and Enterprise starts at 10 seats at $15/seat/month.
use_cases: Adding language model features to web applications
record.notes: I confirmed the details from sapling.ai search snippets, including the homepage, /about, /pricing, /docs, /openai, and /grammar-check, but the search tool hit its usage limit before I could open any more pages. The current blurb is outdated: the product is now presented mainly as an AI writing assistant, AI detector, and language model API, with customer communication as only one use case. The Crunchbase and Kallidus acquisition pages refer to a different company, Sapling HR (saplinghr.com), not Sapling.ai, so I did not mark it as acquired. A third-party review mentions a free one-month Pro trial, but I left it out because no sapling.ai page I opened confirmed it. I did not confirm which messaging platforms Sapling Suggest supports, such as Zendesk.

record.short_description: Online resume and cover letter builder with templates, pre-written bullet points, and resume scoring
record.description: ResumeNerd is an online platform that helps job seekers build resumes and cover letters. Users choose a template, enter their details through a guided step-by-step process with recruiter tips, and download the result as PDF, MS Word, or TXT. The builder suggests pre-written bullet points based on job title and offers ATS-friendly templates. It also scores resume quality and includes a job matcher. The company says it has built career tools since 2016.
record.pricing_summary: ResumeNerd offers a 14-day introductory trial for $2.75 that includes the cover letter builder, resume score, and job matcher. The builder can be tried for free, but downloading a resume requires a paid plan.
features: Expert-written bullet points suggested by job title
AI resume scoring with improvement suggestions
Guided step-by-step process with recruiter tips
Download in PDF, MS Word, or TXT format
use_cases: Tailoring a resume to pass applicant tracking systems
Matching a resume to job openings
record.notes: The official site is live. The company name Specter Technologies Limited, with a Grand Cayman address, comes from structured data on resumenerd.com/contact-us. The only price found on ResumeNerd's own domain is the $2.75 14-day trial. I left out the recurring prices because they appear only on third-party pages: $23.75 every four weeks in reviews and in ResumeNerd's reply on BBB, and $99.95 a year in reviews. ResumeNerd's resume-builder page says a paid plan is needed to download. Zapier and other sites say TXT downloads are free, so pricing_type might be freemium. I could not run more searches to check this. The current blurb says CV, but the product is mainly sold as a resume and cover letter builder. A suggested blurb: Build ATS-friendly resumes and cover letters with templates and pre-written bullet points.

record.short_description: AI web app that creates personalized stories, storybooks, meditations and lullabies starring children
record.description: Scarlett Panda is an AI web app that writes personalized children's stories. Parents set a character's name, age, appearance, interests and the moral of the story, and the app writes the story with images. Stories can feature up to four characters and are offered in 74 languages. It also offers scheduled bedtime stories, 10-chapter storybooks, meditations, lullabies, learning adventures and audio narration. Families can read stories in the app, save them to a library, or ask for printed copies.
record.pricing_summary: Free stories with no credit card required. Scarlett Panda Premium costs USD $9.90 per month (no trial) or USD $79 per year, and the annual plan includes a seven-day free trial.
features: Personalized stories with up to 4 characters
Printable coloring sheets and activity workbooks
record.notes: The listed website is live, and the story app runs at app.scarlettpanda.com. The site footer and refund policy say Scarlett Panda is a trading name of Incremento Ltd (UK company 12997528). However, the app footer reads '© 2026 Scarlett Panda, Singapore', and a third-party directory names Levels Media Inc. as the provider, so the owning entity may have changed. Pricing comes from the official pricing and refund pages. A third-party listing showing $49/year is out of date. The FAQ says there is only a web app for now, with a Google Play app in development. No integrations were found. The current blurb is vague. A suggested replacement: 'AI-personalized children's stories, storybooks, meditations and lullabies featuring your child'.

record.short_description: AI writing suite with story generator, summarizer, paraphraser, headline generator, and content APIs
record.description: Sassbook is a web-based AI content automation service with several writing apps: an AI Writer for general text, an AI Story Writer for fiction in multiple genres, an AI Summarizer, an AI Paraphraser, and an AI Headline Generator. In the Story Writer, users can choose a genre first or use an "Original" mode to write in their own style. Sassbook also offers developer APIs for generating content, summaries, and headlines. The APIs are billed per 1,000 tokens and are available to commercial plan subscribers.
features: AI Story Writer with selectable fiction genres
"Original" mode for writing in your own style
AI Writer for general text generation
Content, summary, and headline generation APIs
use_cases: Writing stories or books in multiple genres
Composing emails or social media posts
record.notes: The current blurb ('Manage your social media posts effectively') is wrong. Sassbook is a set of AI writing tools, not a social media manager. Its homepage only says the AI Writer can help draft social media posts. The listed URL (sassbook.com/ai-story-writer) goes to just one product, the AI Story Writer, so official_url is set to the main domain. The site's learn-more page calls it a 'Free AI story writer', and the API page mentions 'commercial plan subscribers', which supports listing it as freemium with a free tier. I couldn't find subscription prices on sassbook.com, and the official API pricing page I saw didn't show numbers. Third-party sites list different prices (OMR: Free / Standard $39 / Premium $59 per user per month; SourceForge: from $15/month), so pricing_summary is left empty. Everything here comes from search-result text of sassbook.com and blog.sassbook.com pages, not from opening the pages directly.

record.short_description: AI-powered visual web scraper desktop app that extracts website data without writing code
record.description: ScrapeStorm is a visual web scraping tool that uses AI to extract data from websites without code. It runs as a desktop app on Windows, Mac and Linux. Smart Mode finds lists, tables and pagination buttons on its own. Flowchart Mode lets users build rules by clicking on a page and simulating actions such as typing, scrolling and looping. Scraped data can be saved to local files, databases, WordPress or Google Sheets. The tool also supports scheduled scraping, IP rotation, an API and webhooks.
record.pricing_summary: There is a free Starter plan with 10 tasks and 100 exported rows per day. The Business plan costs $199.99 per month, or $159.99 per month billed annually. Professional and Premium plans are also listed, but I could not see their prices.
features: Smart Mode automatic identification of lists, tables and pagination
Simulation of input text, click, scroll, loop and conditions
Export to Excel, CSV, TXT, HTML
File download of images, video, audio and documents
Windows, Mac and Linux desktop app
use_cases: Extracting prices, emails, phone numbers and images from web pages
Monitoring website data on a schedule
record.notes: Product details come from scrapestorm.com pages: the product page, a landing page, a tutorial and the pricing page. The search snippet of the pricing page cut off before the Professional and Premium prices. Capterra lists Professional at $49.99/mo and Premium at $99.99/mo, and ColdIQ says Professional is $39.99/mo billed annually. Those figures are only on third-party sites, so they are left out of pricing_summary. The pricing page also mentions a 5-day money-back guarantee. The current blurb 'Accelerate web data extraction' is vague. A better one would say it is a no-code AI visual web scraper. A search tool limit stopped further page checks.

record.short_description: Browser extension that records a process on screen and turns it into a step-by-step guide
record.description: Scribe is a documentation tool that records a user's screen as they work through a process. It then turns the recording into a step-by-step guide with screenshots and text. It is used to make tutorials, how-to guides, SOPs and training manuals. Users can edit the text and screenshots, then share a guide by link or embed code. A ChatGPT integration writes titles for guides. Paid plans add desktop capture, redaction of sensitive information and custom branding.
features: Screen capture with auto screenshots and text
Share via link or embed code
Auto-generated guide titles via ChatGPT integration
use_cases: Sharing process documentation with teams or customers
record.notes: The listed domain, scribehow.com, appears to have moved to scribe.com. A Scribe-branded guide-generator page is live at scribe.com/tools/how-to-guide-generator, and third-party pricing articles cite scribe.com/pricing. However, I did not open scribehow.com or scribe.com/pricing directly before my search limit ran out. I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty because every price I found came from third-party sites (Supademo, Dubble, Supered, Trainn, Vendr). Those sites list a free Basic plan, Pro Personal at $25/seat/mo billed annually ($35 monthly), Pro Team at $13/seat/mo billed annually with a 5-seat minimum, and custom Enterprise pricing. Vendr and Docsie give older or different figures. Scribe's own page calls the guide generator free, and a Montgomery College page describes a free Basic plan and a paid Pro plan, so I marked it freemium. Suggest updating the blurb and checking the official URL.

record.short_description: Edinburgh- and London-based AI, ML and data science consultancy whose applications include semantic CV matching
record.description: Semafind is an independent research and development consultancy based in Edinburgh and London. It works on AI, machine learning and data science, and builds custom algorithms for businesses. Its website lists several applications. One is Semantic CV Matching, a machine learning algorithm that compares resumes with job descriptions and recommends jobs based on skills and experience. Another is an AI tool that identifies spare parts from images. The site also shows automatic semantic knowledge graph creation. It says it offers products and APIs to existing users.
features: Personalized job recommendations based on skills and experience
Custom algorithms in data, AI and ML
use_cases: Matching candidates' CVs to job descriptions
Helping engineers identify spare parts for maintenance and repair
Applied AI/ML research and consulting for businesses
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit, so I could not run follow-up searches for a pricing page. I used the search-result text for semafind.com, /about and /contact rather than opening each page in full. The current blurb is misleading. The official site describes Semafind mainly as an AI/ML/data science R&D consultancy. Semantic CV Matching is only one of the applications on its homepage, and the site describes it as giving job recommendations to candidates, not as a recruiter tool. Directories such as Product Hunt also list a separate Semafind product, Semafind Knotes, an AI knowledge-management platform launched in November 2023. I could not confirm Knotes on the official site. I found no pricing on semafind.com. Third-party sites disagree: one says free, one says paid plans from $8/mo, and one says contact for pricing. I left pricing empty and set it to unknown. I recommend rewriting the blurb to describe the consultancy, or the specific product being listed.

record.short_description: Enterprise conversational AI platform for building multilingual virtual assistants and voice assistants
record.description: Senseforth.ai is a conversational AI company whose main platform is called A.ware. Large enterprises use it to build multilingual AI virtual assistants and voice assistants that handle customer conversations across digital touchpoints. According to third-party profiles, the platform combines intent-recognition engines with analytics modules, ticketing and routing, and a command center for managing bots. The company also offers speech analytics, semantic search, and agent-assist tools. It was founded in 2017 and lists a New York address. In 2021, Fractal Analytics led a $14 million funding round in the company.
features: Intent identification from natural language input
Conversation, customer profile, and agent performance analytics
use_cases: Automating customer experience across digital touchpoints
record.notes: I hit the search tool limit before I could open senseforth.ai or any pricing page. So the official URL, the site's status, and the pricing are not confirmed directly. The domain is the one listed on Crunchbase, ZoomInfo, and CB Insights. CB Insights marks the company as 'Alive', but status is set to unknown because I could not confirm the site is up. Features come from a 2021 ITPro article about the funding round and from CB Insights and ZoomInfo profiles. The AiDOOS marketplace says pricing is 'Tailored to you', but that is not on the company's own domain, so the pricing fields are left empty. Fractal Analytics backed the company through a strategic investment, but no page I found says it was acquired. The current blurb about 'social media' engagement is wrong: Senseforth is an enterprise conversational AI and virtual assistant platform, and the blurb should be replaced.

record.short_description: iOS camera app that uses AI to create real-time AR filters and effects from text prompts
record.description: Shader is an iOS camera app from a San Francisco startup founded by Darya Sesitskaya, a former Snap design lead. Users scan their face and type a text prompt, tap controls or use their voice to generate a personalized AR mask, filter or effect. They can then record and share videos wearing it. Other features include photo transformation and a drawing mode that reimagines selfies from sketches. The terms of service describe a free plan and paid subscriptions.
record.pricing_summary: The terms of service describe a free plan with no subscription fees and a paid Monthly subscription. No specific prices were found on the official site.
features: Create effects with text, taps, or voice
Record and share videos wearing filters
Shader Drawing: reimagine selfies from doodles
use_cases: Creating custom face filters for selfies and videos
Making AI effects for social media content
Making holiday cards and videos with AI masks
record.notes: I hit the search tool limit before I could open the shaderapp.com homepage. The only official-domain page I saw was the terms of service, which mentions a free plan and a paid Monthly subscription but gives no prices. Other details come from TechCrunch (Feb 2024), the official X account, and Crunchbase. On X, the latest posts are from 2024, and one post contains wording that may be a farewell message. I couldn't confirm a shutdown, so status is set to unknown. Please check that the site is still live before publishing. Crunchbase lists the company as Shader Inc., while Softonic lists the iOS developer as Znichka Inc. TechCrunch says a premium subscription was planned. The current blurb, 'Quickly customize images and avatars', is close but doesn't mention the main product, a real-time AI/AR effects camera. Don't confuse this app with shaders.com or the Shade app, which are different products.

record.short_description: AI image recognition apps that identify dog, cat and horse breeds from smartphone photos
record.description: Siwalu Software GmbH is a German company based in Havixbeck that builds AI-based image recognition for animals. Its mobile apps are Dog Scanner, Cat Scanner and Horse Scanner. They work out a pet's breed, including mixed breeds, from a photo taken with a smartphone in a few seconds, as an alternative to DNA testing. Dog Scanner recognizes more than 370 dog breeds and includes a breed database. The company's site also lists advertising and API offerings for businesses.
use_cases: Identifying a pet's breed without a DNA test
Learning about breed characteristics and traits
record.notes: The site is up, but the search snippets for its pages are several years old. The listed blurb is accurate but narrow: it covers dog, cat and horse breed apps (Dog Scanner, Cat Scanner, Horse Scanner). I found no pricing page on siwalusoftware.com, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are left empty. The freemium rating comes from the Apple App Store listing for Dog Scanner, which shows the app as free with in-app purchases: All Access at $1.49 and $2.99, and Dog Scanner Premium at $13.99. That listing says Premium removes ads and gives faster results. The site's navigation lists an API and advertising for businesses, but I didn't open those pages, so they are not listed as integrations. The search tool limit was reached before I could check them further.

record.short_description: AI shopping assistant app that scans barcodes and receipts to compare prices and track spending
record.description: Shopilot is an AI-powered shopping assistant mobile app published on the Apple App Store by developer KEUNHWA KI. Users scan product barcodes to compare prices, or photograph a product with a Lens feature when its barcode is not found. The app also scans receipts to track spending, sends deal alerts, uses GPT for shopping advice, and suggests recipes with ingredients and instructions. It keeps shopping and scan histories. Product Hunt lists a launch on December 11, 2023.
features: Lens search by taking a photo of a product
use_cases: Comparing prices while shopping in a physical store
record.notes: I could not open tryshopilot.com, and my search limit ran out before I could check it, so I could not confirm the site is up. Status is unknown for that reason. The official URL comes from the listing and from the Product Hunt page (launched December 11, 2023), which links to tryshopilot.com. Most details come from the App Store listing (id6471922117, developer KEUNHWA KI). The latest update I saw there was version 1.2 from 27/12/2023, so the app may not be actively maintained. The App Store shows an in-app purchase called 'Shopilot' for USD 5.99. AigoTools, a directory site, says there is a free version and a premium subscription. Neither source is on the product's own domain, so I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty, set pricing_type to unknown, and set free_tier to false. The current blurb, 'Optimize your purchases by scanning a barcode', is accurate but leaves out receipt scanning, deal alerts and recipes.

record.short_description: Picsart's standalone iOS app that uses generative AI to turn sketches or photos into artwork
record.description: SketchAI is a standalone app from Picsart, launched in January 2023, that turns sketches and existing images into new AI-generated art. Users draw a simple sketch or upload a photo, can add a text description to guide the result, and pick an artistic style such as ink drawing, pencil sketch, da Vinci or van Gogh. The app then generates several versions to choose from. Picsart says it is available on the iPhone, iPad and Mac app stores.
features: Draw a sketch or upload a photo
Optional text description to guide results
Artistic styles including ink drawing, pencil sketch, da Vinci and van Gogh
Generates multiple versions to choose from
use_cases: Turning hand-drawn sketches into AI art
record.notes: Search limits stopped me from opening the listed App Store page, so I couldn't confirm the app is still live. Status is therefore unknown. The product details come from Picsart's own launch blog post (picsart.com/blog/meet-sketchai-a-new-app-to-turn-your-drawings-into-ai-art/, Jan 5, 2023) and a Business Wire press release. The official_url is the listed App Store URL, which I have not verified. Voicebot.ai, a news site, reported pricing: five free uses, then a $6 weekly subscription, discounted to $18 a month or $70 a year. That source is not Picsart's own domain, so I left the pricing fields empty. The current blurb ('Create high-quality digital artworks') is vague. A more accurate one: an AI app that turns sketches or photos into styled artwork.

record.short_description: Open-source engine for federated SQL query, data acceleration, hybrid search, and LLM inference for AI agents
record.description: Spice is an open-source SQL query, search, and LLM-inference engine from Spice AI, Inc. It is written in Rust. Applications and AI agents use one SQL endpoint to query databases, data warehouses, and data lakes without ETL. Spice can store datasets locally in memory or on disk for faster queries, and it can keep a real-time analytics replica of operational databases using CDC. Teams can run it themselves under the Apache 2.0 license, use the managed Spice Cloud Platform, or deploy Spice Enterprise.
record.pricing_summary: Spice.ai Open Source is free under the Apache 2.0 license. Spice Cloud costs $19/month for the Developer plan (1 user, 5 apps) and $99/month for Pro for Teams (unlimited users, 10 apps, commercial license), and Enterprise is a separate plan with dedicated infrastructure.
features: SQL query federation across databases, warehouses, and data lakes
Data acceleration and materialization in memory or on disk (Arrow, DuckDB, SQLite, PostgreSQL)
Hybrid SQL search combining vector, full-text, and keyword search
OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway and local model serving
Deploy locally, at the edge, or on managed cloud
use_cases: Grounding AI agents in enterprise data
Real-time analytics on operational data without ETL
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize SQL queries and their responses') is off. Spice is a federated SQL query, acceleration, search, and LLM-inference engine for apps and AI agents, and the homepage now calls it an open data lakehouse for AI agents. Prices come from spice.ai/pricing/cloud. That page's search snippet also mentions a free trial, but I didn't confirm the terms. The Enterprise price wasn't shown. docs.spice.ai/pricing/plans also lists plan limits. Integrations are taken from the docs and blog.

record.short_description: AI law firm offering attorney-verified contract review and redlining for businesses, focused on construction
record.description: Superlegal calls itself an AI law firm for builders. Its patent-protected AI engine reviews commercial contracts, flags risk and generates market-standard redlines. A commercial attorney then checks the work before it goes back to the client. The company says this costs much less than outside counsel and can turn contracts around within about 24 hours. It now focuses on construction contracts, including prime contracts, subcontracts, purchase orders and vendor agreements. It also has pages for marketing agencies and healthcare and life sciences.
features: Proprietary, patent-protected AI engine trained on legal language
use_cases: Construction contract review (prime contracts, subcontracts, purchase orders, vendor agreements)
Marketing contract review (agency agreements, influencer contracts, media buying, co-marketing, sponsorships)
Healthcare and life sciences contract review
record.notes: I checked the homepage and two of the site's industry pages: construction and marketing agencies. The homepage tagline is 'AI Law Firm for Builders' and it offers 'Book Meeting' and 'Login'. The current blurb ('Accelerate the approval of secured contracts') is vague and does not match how the site describes the product, so it should be replaced. I did not find or open a pricing page on superlegal.ai, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are empty. I marked pricing_type as paid because outside sources describe paid plans. A press article (citybiz) says prices start at $117 per contract. A competitor comparison page (haqq.ai) says Superlegal's own pricing page lists Essential at $999/mo, Advanced at $1,999/mo and Premium from $3,499/mo, all billed annually. Other directories give different figures: $799/mo on GetApp and Software Advice, and $1,665 to $4,160/mo on SoftwareFinder. The marketing-agencies page shows a 'Start for free' button, but I could not confirm a free tier, so free_tier is false. I found no integrations on official pages. Press coverage says Noory Bechor and Ilan Admon founded the company, which raised a $5M seed round in May 2024. The web search limit stopped further checks.

record.short_description: AI platform that transcribes audio and video, then machine-translates transcripts into 54+ languages
record.description: Sonix is a browser-based AI platform for transcribing, translating, subtitling and analyzing audio and video. Users upload a file or import it from cloud storage. Sonix produces a timestamped transcript with speaker labels, which users can edit before translating it into 54+ languages. Translations appear side by side with the original and keep the same timecodes. The platform also exports subtitles in SRT and VTT formats, generates AI summaries and offers sentiment and topic analysis.
record.pricing_summary: Pay-as-you-go costs $10 per audio hour, and each language you translate into costs the same rate. Subscriptions are Core at $25/mo for 5 hrs, Advanced at $50/mo for 20 hrs and Pro at $80/mo for 40 hrs, or $275, $550 and $880 per year, with extra seats at $25/mo each.
features: Upload existing transcripts for timestamp sync
use_cases: Translating audio and video into other languages
Transcription for legal teams, researchers and media organizations
record.notes: The listed URL https://sonix.ai/translation is a live Sonix page about translation. The current blurb roughly matches it: the site says translation is 'one click', but you have to transcribe first and translate second. Prices come from sonix.ai/buy-premium and sonix.ai/how-much-does-transcription-cost. New accounts get 30 free minutes with no credit card required. That is a trial credit, not a permanent free plan, so free_tier is false. The site gives 53+, 54+ and 55+ as the language count on different pages. Zapier and Loom integrations appear only in a third-party review, so they are left out. Customer logos on the site are not listed here.

record.short_description: Automated crypto investing app that uses dollar-cost averaging and sells gains to cover spending
record.description: Soon is a consumer app for automated cryptocurrency investing. It moves money from a linked bank account and invests it using dollar-cost averaging, so users do not have to decide when to buy. When a user spends, Soon is notified and sells the user's highest gains to cover the purchase. It also sends earnings back to the bank every week. Soon says it holds exactly the amount of each crypto shown in the app in the user's wallet.
features: Sells highest gains to cover spending
Automated bank transfers in and out
Weekly earnings transfers back to bank
use_cases: Paying for everyday spending with crypto gains
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit, so I could not open the current soon.app homepage, a pricing page, or the docs. The product details come from an indexed page on the official domain (soon.app/old-home-3), which looks like an archived homepage, plus the company's LinkedIn page, which mentions an on-ramp partnership with Astra. Product Hunt describes a 'Soon Smart Debit Account', so the product may have been repositioned. Directory sites list conflicting prices: theresanaiforthat lists it as freemium, aichief says from $19.99/mo, and aitoptools says from $5.95/mo. None of these are on Soon's own site, so I left pricing blank. A directory also names Fortress Trust as the custodian; I could not confirm this on soon.app. Status is unknown because I could not confirm the live site, and I found no page saying it was shut down or acquired. The current blurb ('Optimize cryptocurrency transactions') is vague; 'automated crypto investing' is more accurate. Don't confuse it with other products called Soon: soonapp.co (a watchlist app by Beginner AB), soon.works (shift scheduling), and soon.dating.

record.short_description: AI-powered English speaking practice and assessment platform with CEFR level tests, IELTS simulation, and mock interviews
record.description: SmallTalk2Me is an AI-powered English assessment and training platform. Individuals can practice speaking through short lessons and get instant AI feedback on pronunciation, grammar, and fluency without a teacher or speaking partner. The platform also offers CEFR-aligned level tests, IELTS speaking and writing simulators, AI mock job interviews, and Business English training. For businesses, it automates English-level assessment in hiring, onboarding, and training. Learners can use a free plan or a paid Pro subscription.
record.pricing_summary: There is a Free plan with limited use, such as 2 IELTS mock tests, 1 CEFR level-test attempt, and 15 minutes of Speech Analyzer. Pro costs €30/month billed monthly, €81 per 3 months, €144 per 6 months, or €216 per year (€18/month).
features: AI feedback on pronunciation, grammar, and fluency
Custom IELTS speaking and writing tests
record.notes: The site and pricing information came from search-result extracts of smalltalk2.me, smalltalk2.me/about, and app.smalltalk2.me/pricing. The search tool limit was reached before I could do more searches, so I did not separately check business pages such as business.smalltalk2.me (linked from LinkedIn). B2B pricing was not confirmed on the official domain. Directory sites mention $10 per-test pricing, and Capterra mentions API/ATS integration, but I left both out because the official site did not confirm them. A third-party site gives the legal name as SmallTalk Inc., but the official site did not confirm it. The pricing page says payment by card, Apple Pay, or Google Pay, and that PayPal is not accepted. The current blurb is a slogan. A more accurate description would be an AI English speaking practice and assessment platform.

record.short_description: Visual AI workspace where parallel agents across 300+ models research and produce reports, slides, and spreadsheets
record.description: Spine is an agentic platform from Spine AI, a San Francisco company in Y Combinator's Summer 2023 batch. On a visual canvas, a swarm of AI agents uses more than 300 models to run deep research in parallel and turn the results into reports, slides, spreadsheets and dashboards. Users can inspect each agent's steps and intermediate outputs. Spine also offers a pay-as-you-go REST API, and its site has pages aimed at founders and consultants.
record.pricing_summary: The Free plan costs $0 a month and includes 2,000 credits. Starter is from $16/mo billed annually or $20/mo monthly, Max is from $80/mo billed annually, and Enterprise is custom-priced. The separate API is pay as you go at $1 per 1,000 credits, with $10 of free credits to start.
features: Parallel AI agent swarms on a visual canvas
Generates slides, documents, spreadsheets, and reports
Auditable agent task trees and intermediate outputs
Team workspaces with shared credit pool
use_cases: Fundraising and go-to-market research for founders
Market sizing, competitor, and pricing research
Consulting desk research and client-ready deliverables
record.notes: Live web search ran; results came from getspine.ai, docs.getspine.ai and app.getspine.ai. The current blurb ('Analyze trends without overloading the team') is vague and doesn't describe the product. Spine now positions itself as a multi-agent research and deliverables workspace. Older third-party profiles (Crunchbase, PitchBook) describe an earlier AI copilot product. Spine's own pages don't agree on plan names and prices. The pricing page lists Starter at $16/$20 and Max from $80/mo annual. The docs list Pro at $20/month or $192/year and Max at $100/month or $960/year. The API docs page says $5 in free credits, but the API landing page says $10. research.getspine.ai has a separate, older-looking credit pricing page. A follow-up search for third-party app integrations hit the search limit, so the integrations list only covers coding-agent surfaces and AI models named in the sources.

record.short_description: No-code enterprise platform for building, deploying, and governing AI agents and back-office workflow automations
record.description: StackAI is an enterprise platform for building, deploying, and governing AI agents. Teams use a visual drag-and-drop builder to create AI workflows. These workflows connect knowledge bases, LLMs, and business systems through what the company says are 500+ enterprise integrations. Agents can be deployed to chat, forms, APIs, and internal teams, with access controls and observability. StackAI was founded in 2023 and backed by Y Combinator. It targets finance, risk, and operations teams, and Y Combinator's company page says Asana acquired it in May 2026.
features: Connect knowledge bases, tools, and business systems
Deploy agents to chat, forms, APIs, and internal teams
Support for the LLM of your choice
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize content creation for social media') is wrong. StackAI is a no-code platform for building enterprise AI agents and workflows. The listed domain, stack-ai.com, still shows up in search results, but the company's current site and docs are on stackai.com (docs.stackai.com), so official_url is set to that. The acquisition comes from Y Combinator's company page ('Acquired by Asana (NYSE:ASAN) in May 2026') and a LinkedIn post. I hit the search limit before I could find an announcement on stackai.com or asana.com. Pricing is left empty because I never opened a pricing page on the official domain. Third-party review sites (marketermilk, SourceForge, getmacha) say there is a Free plan at $0/month with 500 runs, 2 projects, and 1 seat, plus a custom-priced Enterprise plan. Check stackai.com/pricing before setting pricing_type to freemium. Other integrations named only on third-party sites (Salesforce, Snowflake, AWS, Notion, Confluence, HubSpot, Google Workspace) were left out of the list.

record.short_description: AI bookkeeping and accounting platform for startups, with support from a dedicated human finance team
record.description: Zeni is an accounting platform for fast-growing startups. It pairs AI bookkeeping software with guidance from human accounting experts. The product covers AI bookkeeping, accounts payable, financial reporting, month-end close, bill pay, and expense reimbursements. Zeni also offers an interest-bearing business bank account and a zero-fee credit card. Its outsourced accounting services include preparing financial statements and annual tax filings. Add-on services include tax support, fractional CFO work, and payroll management.
record.pricing_summary: The AI Bookkeeping plan starts at $799/month, or $719/month billed annually, and includes a dedicated finance team. Enterprise has custom pricing. Zeni says prices depend on bookkeeping complexity, monthly expenses, and annual revenue.
features: OCR for invoices, receipts, and statements
Tax support, fractional CFO, and payroll add-ons
use_cases: Financial statement and annual tax filing preparation
record.notes: Verified on zeni.ai: the startup accounting software page, the outsourced accounting services page, and the pricing page. I hit the search tool limit, so I couldn't confirm any third-party integrations. That's why integrations is empty. I didn't use review-site pricing. Zeni Bill Pay is listed as free and included in all plans. The current blurb, 'Optimize real-time accounting management', is vague. A better one would say Zeni does AI bookkeeping with a human finance team for startups.

record.short_description: AI car photography and image editing platform for dealerships and automotive marketplaces
record.description: Spyne is an AI-powered visual merchandising platform for the automotive industry, built for car dealerships, marketplaces and retailers. Its guided capture app helps staff photograph vehicles with a smartphone, with angle guidance and quality checks. Its Studio AI then turns raw photos into studio-style images through background replacement, lighting correction, shadow rendering and branded overlays. The platform also offers 360-degree virtual tours and number plate masking. Spyne is headquartered in Gurugram, India, and raised a $16M Series A led by Vertex Ventures in February 2025.
features: Real-time angle guidance and quality checks
Car color changer and wrap previews
record.notes: I confirmed the product through spyne.ai pages (blog posts, FAQ, and the funding announcement) and its App Store and Google Play listings. I did not open the homepage or a pricing page directly because my search limit ran out. The FAQ on spyne.ai mentions a 14-day free trial, subscription plans, and a Pricing tab, but I found no tier names or prices on Spyne's own site. Third-party sites disagree on price: Capterra says from $15 per user per month, Capterra India $0.07, and SourceForge and Software Advice say custom or on request. Because none of these are on Spyne's domain, I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. Directories also say Spyne works with '50+ automotive platforms', but no named integrations appeared on official pages I saw, so integrations is empty. The current blurb is accurate but narrow. Third-party descriptions now present Spyne as a broader AI dealership platform that also includes conversational AI. Company details came from news coverage: Gurugram-based, investors Vertex Ventures, Accel, Storm Ventures and Alteria Capital. Older data lists the vendor as Eventila Technologies.

record.short_description: All-in-one AI app with chat, writing, image, audio, and video tools powered by multiple AI models
record.description: 1minAI (1min.AI) is an all-in-one AI platform that puts tools for text, writing, images, audio, and video in one app. Users can chat with several AI models, including GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, and Mistral, and mix models in one conversation. The writing tools include a grammar checker, summarizer, rewriter, paraphraser, and keyword research. The image tools include an image variator and a text remover. It runs as a web app, a Chrome extension, and iOS and Android apps.
record.notes: The official homepage is up. It says the platform is free to try and mentions 'All Plans', but it lists no prices, so pricing_summary is empty. Prices do appear on other sites: the App Store lists Pro at $8/month or $78/year and Business at $12.5/month or $120/year. G2 and Software Finder give different numbers, and lifetime deals are sold on StackSocial and DealFuel. None of these are on 1min.ai, so they are not recorded. I couldn't confirm a company name. The Google Play listing gives an individual developer contact in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The model names (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral) come from the company's own description on Trustpilot. The current blurb, 'Make SEO content creation easier,' is too narrow. The product is a general multi-model AI app, and keyword research is only one of its writing tools. One more search for an official pricing or docs page was cut off by the search tool's limit.

record.short_description: Browser-based AI platform that generates 3D models from text or images using multiple AI models
record.description: 3D AI Studio is a browser-based toolkit that turns text prompts or images into textured 3D assets. It puts several third-party 3D generation models in one workspace, including Meshy, Tripo, Hunyuan3D, Rodin and Trellis. It also has tools for refining, rigging, animating, texturing, remeshing and LOD generation. Models can be exported as GLB, OBJ, FBX or STL for game engines and 3D printing. Usage runs on credits, and developers can call the same features through a REST API.
record.pricing_summary: New users get free credits with no credit card. Monthly plans are Basic at $19 for 1,000 credits, Studio at $29 for 3,500 credits and Pro at $149 for 18,000 credits, or $12, $23 and $139 a month billed annually. One-time packs that never expire cost $34 for 2,000 credits, $69 for 5,000 and $399 for 35,000.
features: Export in GLB, OBJ, FBX, STL
Multiple AI models in one studio
record.notes: The listed site is live and redirects to www.3daistudio.com. Prices come from the official pricing page, the homepage and the docs FAQ at docs.3daistudio.com/faq. The pricing page snapshot did not show every monthly price clearly, so the monthly figures are taken from the docs FAQ. The pages disagree on free credits: one page says '100 free credits monthly', while the docs only say new users get free credits. No legal company name was found, so company is left empty. The Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor integration (through MCP) comes from the official X account. Blender, Unity, Unreal, Godot and Roblox are export targets, not confirmed native plugins. The existing blurb is accurate but vague; it could mention that models are made from text or images.

record.short_description: Flight comparison site that lets travelers search many booking and comparison sites for flight deals
record.description: AI Deal Finder is a flight search tool from Compare Flights at compareflights.io. Compare Flights describes itself as a flight comparison website that searches the internet for deals from major booking platforms. It compares prices from several sources and links users to searches on sites such as iWantThatFlight, Kiwi, Skyscanner and eDreams, so they can see their flight options in one place. A third-party AI directory lists AI Deal Finder as an AI-powered flight deal finder that works across sites.
features: Links to search on iWantThatFlight, Kiwi, Skyscanner and eDreams
use_cases: Comparing flight prices across booking platforms
record.notes: I found the compareflights.io homepage in search results, and it describes a flight comparison site. I could not open the listed /ai-flight-search/ page itself because I hit the search tool limit. Only the There's An AI For That directory confirms that this tool is called 'AI Deal Finder', calls it AI-powered, and calls it a 'flight deal finder across all sites'. That directory also says it is '100% Free', but I found no pricing on compareflights.io, so I left pricing empty and set pricing_type to unknown. The company name 'Compare Flights' comes from the site's own wording. I found no legal entity name. compareflights.net and compareflights.co.uk are different sites. The current blurb ('Optimize the planning of your trips') is vague. It would be more accurate to describe this as a flight deal comparison or search tool.

record.short_description: Online AI icon generator listed at aiicon.pro; product details could not be verified
record.description: AI ICON Online is listed in the directory as an AI tool for quickly creating unique icons, with a listed website of aiicon.pro. Web searches did not return the aiicon.pro domain or any page for a product called AI ICON Online. A direct request to the listed URL also returned no content. So the product's features, pricing, operator, and current status could not be confirmed from any official source.
record.notes: I couldn't verify this listing. Web searches for 'AI ICON Online aiicon.pro' and 'aiicon.pro pricing' did not return the aiicon.pro domain. The results showed only products with similar names on other domains: aiicon.io (an SVG icon generator), aiicongen.com, aiappicon.com, appicons.ai, aiicon.org (an AI conference), and icon.com (an ad tool). None of these is confirmed to be the same product. A direct fetch of https://www.aiicon.pro/ returned an empty response, though the sandbox may not have internet access, so the site might still be online. I hit the search tool's usage limit before I could run more queries. official_url is left empty because the site couldn't be confirmed. exists=false means 'not verified', not 'confirmed gone'. Before publishing, someone should open aiicon.pro by hand to check whether it's live and still the same product. The current blurb, 'Create unique icons quickly', has no source supporting it.

record.short_description: Mobile app for recording phone calls on iPhone and Android and getting AI transcripts
record.description: Acallrecorder, also called Call Recorder & Transcriber, is a mobile app from AnswerSolutions LLC that records incoming, outgoing and ongoing phone calls on iPhone and Android. Users can ask for AI transcription of recorded calls, with timestamped text in English, Spanish, French and other languages, and share the audio and transcripts. The app uses pay-as-you-go pricing instead of a subscription. New users get 60 credit minutes and can buy more. The service currently works only for +1 country code numbers.
features: Record incoming, outgoing and ongoing phone calls
Record conference calls by merging lines
Transcription in English, Spanish and French
Share audio and transcripts by email
History and playback of recorded calls
record.notes: I confirmed the official site (acallrecorder.com) and the company name from a search snippet of the homepage. That snippet mentions 'Fair pay-as-you-go pricing' but gives no prices. I couldn't open a pricing page on the product's own domain because I hit the search tool limit, so pricing_summary is empty. The Google Play listing says new users get 60 credit minutes, there is no subscription, and extra minutes are bought as needed. I treated the 60 minutes as starting credits, not an ongoing free tier. A directory site (theresanaiforthat.com) lists 'from $4.99/month', which doesn't match the no-subscription model, so I didn't use it. The Play listing says the service only works for +1 country code numbers. The current blurb, 'Optimize the management of your transcriptions', is vague; a call recording and transcription description fits better. Features come from the Google Play listing and the homepage snippet.

record.short_description: Web-based AI comic generator that turns text descriptions of characters and scenes into comic panels
record.description: AI Comic Factory is an online comic book generator. Users describe characters, styles and scenes, then pick a layout and captions, and the AI generates comic panels without any drawing. Users can upload reference images to add their own characters and settings, and they can create single-panel comics or single and double pages. The site says it generates comics using a Hugging Face Space and supports the FLUX.1 model. Finished artwork can be saved as a JPG file.
record.pricing_summary: There is a free plan at $0/month, a Starter plan at $9.99/month with 600 credits and a Premium plan at $13.99/month with 1,200 credits. One credit generates one panel image, and annual billing is also offered.
features: Comic generation from descriptions of characters, styles and scenes
Upload reference images for custom characters and settings
Custom caption language and caption editing
record.notes: Checked on the live web. The search tool hit its usage limit, so this record is based on one round of searches.
