The listed site, aicomicfactory.com, is live, and its homepage, pricing page, blog and explore page all appeared. No company or operator name was shown in those results, so company is blank. Important caution: AI Comic Factory began as an open-source Hugging Face Space by Julian Bilcke (jbilcke-hf). That project's GitHub README names aicomicfactory.app as the official website, not the .com. The GitHub repo was archived on Oct 31, 2025. So aicomicfactory.com may be a separate hosted service rather than the original project. Other look-alike sites also use the name: aicomicfactory.ai, aicomicfactory.org and comicfactory.ai. Review sites mention a $34.99/month Advanced plan with unlimited credits, but it was not in the pricing page text I saw, so I left it out. The pricing page shows the free plan with '0 Credits' while also saying the service can be started for free. The current blurb is accurate but very short.

record.short_description: AI-powered debugging assistant that fixes and explains broken code and answers questions about codebases
record.description: Adrenaline is an AI-powered developer tool. Its maker first described it as a debugger built on the OpenAI Codex that fixes broken code and explains the errors. Later descriptions say it combines static analysis, vector search and large language models to explain code and answer questions about a codebase. Users can import repositories from GitHub or GitLab. Product Hunt shows a launch on March 28, 2023. CB Insights lists the company as founded in 2023 and based in Brooklyn, New York.
features: Static analysis, vector search and LLMs for code explanations
Imports codebases from GitHub and GitLab repositories
record.notes: The current blurb is wrong. Every source I found, including Product Hunt, GitHub, CB Insights, Future Tools and Medium, describes Adrenaline at useadrenaline.com as an AI code debugging and codebase Q&A tool for developers, not a social media tool. 'Json' in the name looks like a data artifact; the product is called 'Adrenaline'. I could not open useadrenaline.com directly because outbound HTTP failed in the sandbox, and I hit the search limit before I could find a page on the official domain. Status is therefore 'unknown', not 'active'. Product Hunt (page about 48 days old) and CB Insights ('Alive') suggest it is still running. Pricing on third-party sites conflicts: Future Tools says paid, Cloudfindr says free, AIToolHouse says freemium from $5/mo, and Zack Proser says $10/mo with a free tier. One scraper (webclaw.io) says the domain now targets content creators and video editors, with Starter at $49/mo, Pro at $199/mo and Enterprise. That may mean the domain has been repurposed. None of these prices came from the product's own pricing page, so I left pricing empty. The company name is unclear: CB Insights says Adrenaline, Zack Proser says Adrenaline Tech, and Medium mentions GetAdrenaline working with 7code. Someone should open the live site by hand to confirm the current product, status and pricing.

record.short_description: AI image tool from ZMO.AI's ImgCreator for designing and editing images with text prompts
record.description: AI Designer is an image design and editing tool from ImgCreator, a product of ZMO.AI. Its Product Hunt launch, dated January 23, 2023, describes it as a way to design and edit images using only text. The ImgCreator site describes a broader platform with an AI image generator, an AI image editor, and AI portraits. The generator supports text to image, image to image, and swapping objects. The editor includes an AI photo studio, background removal, and a magic eraser.
features: Design and edit images using text
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize your images to convert better') doesn't match the sources. Product Hunt describes AI Designer by ImgCreator as designing and editing images using only text, so the blurb should be rewritten. The official ImgCreator site (imgcreator.zmo.ai) appeared in search results and says users can try it for free. I could not open the listed /editor URL or a pricing page on zmo.ai, and the indexed copy of the site is old, so current status and pricing are not fully confirmed. Paid plan prices (for example, a $10 Starter plan) appear only on third-party directories like Techjockey, so I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty. The freemium label is based on the official site's 'for free' wording and on reviewer mentions of premium popups, not on a verified pricing page. Some Product Hunt reviewers report complaints about billing, cancellation, and support. Search tool limits stopped further checks.

record.short_description: iOS and iPadOS app that creates custom device wallpapers with AI from text prompts
record.description: AI Wallpapers Generator is an iPhone and iPad app from BridgeTech Solutions Limited. It makes wallpapers from a word or phrase that the user types in. Users can publish their images to a public gallery and browse wallpapers that other people have made. The app can also make new images from favourite prompts while the phone is idle and charging. Image generation works only on certain newer iPhone and iPad models, and the app requires iOS 16.2 or later.
record.pricing_summary: The App Store lists the app as Free, and the listing shows no in-app purchases.
features: Public gallery for publishing and discovering wallpapers
Automatic image creation from favourite prompts while idle and charging
Reporting of offensive content in the public gallery
use_cases: Sharing AI art with a community
record.notes: Everything here comes from the Apple App Store listing (App ID 1662227892), the only product page I found. The developer is BRIDGETECH SOLUTIONS LIMITED, based in London, with support email support@bridgetech.io. I couldn't check bridgetech.io because the search limit ran out, so official_url and pricing_source_url point to the App Store listing on Apple's domain, not a separate product site. The rules ask for a page on the product's own domain, so you may want to clear the pricing fields. The App Store says Free and shows no in-app purchases. Version 1.4 (9 Oct 2023) is the latest update. Status is set to active because the listing is still live, but the app hasn't been updated since then. Image generation needs specific newer devices (iPhone 12 Pro and later Pro models, iPhone 13 Pro and later, plus some iPad Pro and iPad Air models) and iOS 16.2 or later. The current blurb, 'Visually customize your screen with one click', doesn't match the source: the app generates wallpapers from text prompts, and the listing doesn't mention one-click customization. The listing's tagline is 'Style your device with AI Art.'

record.short_description: Web3 AI image generation platform that also offered Bitcoin Ordinal inscriptions paid for in ETH
record.description: AiBlocks describes itself on its X account as a free Web3 AI image generation platform focused on helping communities create content. The account, which joined in November 2022 and links to aiblocks.app, also promoted a service for inscribing any image onto special sats on Bitcoin. Users paid in ETH and received an Ordinal in their BTC wallet. The official website could not be opened to confirm its current offering, so the product's current status is unclear.
features: Inscribe any image onto special sats
Pay with ETH and receive an Ordinal in a BTC wallet
record.notes: I could not open aiblocks.app or find any pricing or docs page on that domain. The only source tying the domain to the product was the @aiblocks_net X profile, which is about 4 years old. It calls AiBlocks a free Web3 AI image generation platform and promotes Ordinal inscriptions paid in ETH. One post mentions a single inscription costing about $30 (0.019 ETH). That claim comes from X, not the product's own domain, so I left pricing empty and set free_tier to false. The current blurb about optimizing processes and social media content is not supported by anything I found and looks inaccurate. Search results also turned up unrelated companies with the same name: aiblocks.io (a blockchain ledger) and aiblocks.in (an AI hardware company in India). Status is unknown because I could not confirm the site is still up.

record.short_description: Web service that trains an AI model on your uploaded photos to generate stylized profile pictures
record.description: AI Profile Pictures is a web service, described on its site as being in beta, that creates AI-generated profile pictures. Users buy credit to generate more than 200 images. They then upload 10 to 20 photos of themselves or another subject, and the service trains an AI model on those photos. Sample styles on the site include anime, neon, viking, officer and fantasy portraits. Users who are unhappy with the results can ask for more photos within 7 days. Refunds are not given after photos are submitted.
features: Custom AI model trained on your uploaded photos
Upload 10-20 photos of yourself or your subject
7 days to generate additional photos if not satisfied
Multiple styles such as anime, neon, viking, officer, and fantasy
use_cases: Creating stylized avatars from personal photos
record.notes: The official homepage is up and labels the service as beta. It says users purchase credit before uploading photos, so I marked it as paid. The homepage I opened shows no price. A third-party review site (tenereteam) lists a one-time $30 purchase, but I left pricing empty because that figure is not on the product's own domain. The company name was not found, and the terms page says 'Under construction'. I could not confirm the '3 hours' turnaround in the current blurb on the official page. Softonic, a third-party site, says results arrive in 2 to 3 hours. I hit the search limit, so I could not run any further checks.

record.short_description: AI content platform for generating articles, blogs, ad copy and images using OpenAI models
record.description: AI Majic is a software-as-a-service platform for generating content with AI. Its own blog says it uses OpenAI technology to produce text such as articles, blogs, advertisements and other media content in 53 languages. The blog also lists AI image generation using DALL-E and Stable Diffusion and an AI chat system with 42 bot assistants. The blog names marketers, writers, legal experts and artists as target users. A recent third-party listing reports that the domain is now for sale.
features: AI text content generation in 53 languages
AI image generation with DALL-E and Stable Diffusion
Interactive AI chat with 42 bot assistants
use_cases: Creating visuals for websites, social media and marketing campaigns
record.notes: I couldn't open aimajic.com directly because the sandbox has no direct web access. The only official page I found was a search snippet of an aimajic.com blog post, indexed about 934 days ago. The features and integrations above come from that post. A topai.tools listing indexed about 197 days ago says aimajic.com is now a domain name listed for sale. That suggests the product may no longer be running, but I didn't find any page saying it was discontinued, so status is unknown. Any prices I found came only from directory sites, not from aimajic.com, so pricing fields are left empty. Those sites were SourceForge and findmyaitool, which list plans from $15/mo with a free trial, and shrug.ai, which lists plans from $1.97/mo. The current blurb, 'Write high-quality articles in seconds', is close to directory descriptions, but someone should check whether the site is still live before keeping this row. I reached the search limit before I could check further.

record.short_description: AI tool that turns plain-English requests into SQL, and also explains, fixes, optimizes and formats queries
record.description: AI2SQL is an AI SQL query generator. Users describe the data they need in plain English, and it writes dialect-aware SQL based on their database schema. It can also explain existing queries, fix errors, optimize performance and format SQL. Users can connect their own databases through a local connector or a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, so credentials stay on their own machine. AI agents can also query data through MCP. Supported databases include MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB and BigQuery.
record.pricing_summary: The pricing page lists three monthly plans: Start at $9/mo (100 SQL queries, 10 tables), Pro at $24/mo (300 queries, 50 tables, database connectors) and Business at $39/mo (1,000 queries, unlimited tables). Each plan has a 7-day free trial. The homepage also lists Start at $7/mo billed annually and a free plan with 3 queries a day on a demo database.
features: Local connector for Windows, macOS and Linux
use_cases: Non-technical users querying databases without knowing SQL
Querying private or local databases securely
record.notes: The site works at ai2sql.io, and the www URL in the listing points to the same site. The web app is at web.ai2sql.io. The current blurb ('Optimize your SQL queries quickly') is too narrow, because the product is mainly a text-to-SQL generator and optimization is only one of its features. The prices on AI2SQL's own pages don't agree. /pricing says Start $9, Pro $24, Business $39 and also says plans start at $19/month. A blog post on builder.ai2sql.io says Start $9, Pro $19 (unlimited queries), Team $39 for 5 users. The homepage says there are three plans with Start at $9, or $7/mo billed annually. The free plan (3 queries a day on a demo database) is mentioned in the homepage's structured data and in that blog post. The company name comes from a copyright footer on ai2sql.io/text2sqlai that reads 'Cross Regions Technology' with a Florida address. LinkedIn lists Istanbul as headquarters. Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor support comes from the builder.ai2sql.io blog post. I couldn't run more searches to settle the price differences, so the prices should be checked again by hand.

record.short_description: Web tool that uses DALL-E 3 to generate posters from text prompts
record.description: AI Poster Generator is a browser-based tool that creates posters from prompt words using AI. Its site says it runs on DALL-E 3. Users enter a description on the dashboard and get a generated poster. The site presents it as a cheaper option than hiring a designer or buying design software, and suggests it for brand promotions, films, and advertising posters. There is an Explore gallery of example posters. Generations are paid for with credits, and payments are processed through Stripe.
record.pricing_summary: There is a Free Plan ($0, 1 credit). One-time credit packs have no subscription: Starter is $5 for 25 credits, Premium is $9 (listed down from $11) for 55 credits, and Advanced is $20 (listed down from $24) for 120 credits.
use_cases: Creating posters without hiring a designer
record.notes: The official homepage lists the pricing. Its FAQ says refunds are not offered and that card details are not stored because Stripe handles payments. The site does not name the company that runs it. G2 also shows no company or HQ, and its profile is unclaimed with 0 reviews. The current blurb, 'Create high-quality posters without a designer,' matches how the site describes itself. Do not confuse this product with poster.sh or NoteGPT's AI poster generator, which are different products with similar names.

record.short_description: Cloud contact center software with calling, SMS, power dialing, AI voice agents, and CRM integrations
record.description: Aloware is cloud-based contact center software for sales and support teams. It handles inbound and outbound voice calls, text messages, and broadcasts. The product includes a power dialer, ring groups, and call routing, plus AI features under the AloAi name such as voice analytics, transcriptions, call summaries, and an AI voice agent. It runs in the browser, on desktop and mobile apps, or inside a connected CRM. Native integrations include HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho, and Salesforce, and there is an API for custom connections.
record.pricing_summary: Per-user plans with unlimited agent calling and SMS: iPro + AI at $30/user (10-user minimum; $40 on the non-discounted cycle), uPro + AI at $60/user (5-user minimum), and xPro + AI at $85/user. A 3-user package costs $199 per account per month, and the AloAi Voice Agent starts at $0.10 per minute.
features: Unlimited inbound and outbound agent minutes and SMS
Browser, desktop, and mobile softphone apps
record.notes: The site is live. Pricing comes from the search-result text of aloware.com/pricing, which the search engine had indexed about 528 days ago. An Aloware blog post from about 73 days ago backs up the $30/user iPro + AI price (on quarterly billing) and the AloAi Voice Agent price of $0.10/min. The pricing page says it offers a 7-day free trial with no credit card required. A third-party directory says the trial is 14 days and lists older prices of $40/$70/$100, which I didn't use. I found no free plan. I couldn't open the homepage and pricing page directly because I hit the search-tool limit, so prices may have changed. The current blurb is a vague slogan and should be replaced with the short_description.

record.short_description: AI audio separation tool that splits recordings into music stems, dialogue, and effects tracks
record.description: AudioShake is an AI audio separation platform. It splits finished recordings into separate parts such as vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, dialogue, music and effects. It also offers lyric transcription and copyright-compliance models. Labels, publishers, producers, post-production teams and developers use it for remixing, mastering, immersive mixes, dubbing, localization, captioning and AI training data. Users can work in the web-based AudioShake Studio, through a credit-based REST API, or with an on-device SDK that does real-time separation.
record.pricing_summary: AudioShake Studio has a Free plan with 200 starting credits, MP3 export and files up to 10 minutes. Starter costs $20/mo for 500 credits a month and Pro costs $40/mo for 1,500 credits a month, both with WAV/FLAC/MP3 export and files up to 2 hours. Enterprise pricing is custom.
features: Instrument stem separation (vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, strings, winds)
REST API with async processing, webhooks and batch support
Processes MP4 and MOV video files directly
Private deployment in a customer's own cloud or offline
integrations: Local Inference SDK (iOS, macOS, Android, Windows, Linux)
record.notes: The site is live and the product exists. The current blurb, "Optimize audio mixing and subtitling", is off: AudioShake's main product is AI stem and dialogue separation. Mixing and captioning are use cases, and it does not make subtitles. Studio prices come from studio.audioshake.ai; one tier label didn't line up in the page text, so the $20 and $40 plans may be worth a quick check. The developer API is billed separately in credits, charged per minute of source audio for each model. It gives 10 free credits at signup, and per-model rates are on developer.audioshake.ai. Third-party sites show older or different prices (for example, Indie plans priced per stem), but I ignored them. I found no named third-party integrations or acquisition information.

record.short_description: AI search feature in Slite that answers team questions using the workspace knowledge base
record.description: Ask is an AI-powered search and answer feature in Slite, a knowledge base for teams. Users ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn from their Slite documentation, which saves them from digging through pages by hand. According to Slite, the assistant cross-checks sources so its answers are accurate. Slite says it built Ask in 2023 as a retrieval-based AI search for private knowledge bases. Ask now comes with Slite's paid plans, and the Basic plan limits it to Slite docs.
record.pricing_summary: Ask comes with Slite's Basic plan at $10 per user/month billed yearly, which covers unlimited docs, Ask, doc verification, and MCP/API access. The Pro plan costs $20 per user/month billed yearly and adds the Slite Agent and search across connected tools.
features: Connects knowledge base with external sources
record.notes: The listed URL slite.com/ask is live, and that page describes Ask as AI-powered knowledge access. Ask isn't a standalone product anymore. It's a feature of Slite, and on the Basic plan it only searches Slite docs. A Slite blog post says Super, Slite's cross-tool search, merged into Slite as the Slite Agent on the Pro plan. The same post says both plans come with a 14-day free trial, no credit card required. The pricing page I opened shows no free plan, so free_tier is false. Third-party directories (Future Tools, Docsie) describe Ask or Slite as free, but those listings look outdated, so I didn't use them. Softonic mentions a Chrome extension and automatic answers in Slack channels. I couldn't confirm either on Slite's own pages, so I left integrations empty. My search limit ran out before I could check the docs or integrations pages. The current blurb, 'Optimize access to useful information,' is vague. Something like 'AI answers from your team's Slite knowledge base' would describe it better.

record.company: Wizco Group, Inc. (Ava asset acquired by Atlantic Energy Solutions / CognoGroup, a Nixxy subsidiary)
record.short_description: AI interview coach that simulates real job interviews and gives personalized feedback and performance insights
record.description: Ava is an AI-powered interview coach first built by Wizco, a New York company that offers mock interview preparation. It runs practice interviews that copy real interview scenarios and adjusts each session to the user's industry, role and target company instead of drawing from a generic question bank. Users type their answers and get feedback, performance analytics, an action plan and communication tips. In March 2025, Atlantic Energy Solutions, a subsidiary of Nixxy, acquired the Ava software asset.
features: Sessions tailored to industry, role and company
Typed responses at your own pace
Integration into partner environments for their users
use_cases: Mock interview practice for job seekers
Interview coaching for students and applicants offered by universities or organizations
record.notes: The current blurb is wrong and should be replaced. Ava is an AI interview coach, not a tool for optimizing content to target and convert. Search results from Wizco pages (tribe.wizco.io and uni.wizco.io/pages/meet-ava) describe interview coaching. The listed URL wizco.io/ava is the Ava link Wizco gave in its press release and LinkedIn posts, but I could not confirm that it currently loads. Status is marked acquired because a March 7, 2025 press release from Nixxy (published on Nasdaq.com) says Atlantic Energy Solutions, a subsidiary being renamed CognoGroup, bought the Ava software asset from Wizco Group. I could not find out where the product is hosted now or whether it is still sold. I found no pricing on Wizco's own pages. A 2023 press release invited users to try Ava for free, LinkedIn posts mention freetrial.wizco.io, and the directory site genai.works lists it as Free. None of these are official pricing pages, so pricing_summary is empty, pricing_type is unknown and free_tier is false. My search budget ran out before I could check a pricing page.

record.short_description: Cloud-based AI APIs for image processing, including OCR, background removal, and content moderation
record.description: API4AI provides ready-to-use AI and computer vision services through cloud-based HTTP web APIs that share the same RESTful design. Its catalog includes text recognition (OCR), background removal, NSFW content moderation, image labelling, face analysis, brand mark recognition, image anonymization, object detection, alcohol label recognition and virtual try-on. Developers can use the APIs through the API4AI Developer Portal or through the RapidAPI marketplace. The company also builds custom AI solutions for businesses with specific needs.
record.pricing_summary: The API4AI Developer Portal uses pay-as-you-go pricing: users top up a balance and spend it on any API. API4AI also sells subscription plans, including free plans, through RapidAPI. No specific prices were found on api4.ai.
use_cases: Adding image processing to apps and websites
Extracting text from images and PDFs
Hiding faces and license plates in images
Custom computer vision solutions for businesses
record.notes: The current blurb, 'Optimize inventory management efficiently', does not match the product. API4AI is a set of cloud computer vision and image processing APIs, not an inventory management tool, so the blurb should be replaced. The api4.ai/docs page confirms the pricing models (pay-as-you-go via the Developer Portal; subscriptions with free plans via RapidAPI), but I found no price amounts on api4.ai. Per-API plan prices seem to be listed only on RapidAPI, which is not the product's own domain, so I left them out. The site footer says 'Powered by Proml', and the legal name in the site's structured data is API4AI, with an address in Concord, CA. The X account also mentions a related product called CRken, an AI code review tool for GitLab, and newer APIs (Fashion and Image Upscale) that I did not check on api4.ai. My search limit ran out before I could find a dedicated pricing page.

record.company: LimeWire (acquirer); BlueWillow was originally founded by Ritankar Das
record.short_description: AI image generator that turns text prompts into logos, characters, digital artwork, and photos
record.description: BlueWillow is an AI image generator that creates images from text prompts. Users describe the image they want, and the tool produces graphics such as logos, characters, digital artwork, and photo-realistic images. It was designed so that people with any level of experience can use it, and it built a large community on Discord. In September 2023, LimeWire announced that it had acquired BlueWillow. LimeWire planned to keep the Discord presence and add the BlueWillow model to its AI Studio.
record.pricing_summary: The official homepage says BlueWillow is free to try, but it lists no paid tiers or prices.
record.notes: LimeWire named itself as the buyer in a post on its official blog (blog.limewire.com/limewire-acquires-bluewillow), and TechCrunch reported the deal on 2023-09-19, so the status is set to acquired. The company field now names LimeWire as the owner. I only saw the bluewillow.ai homepage through a search-result snapshot that may be old. I could not confirm that the site is still live or what it shows now. One third-party directory (tooldirectory.ai) says the BlueWillow brand was retired after the acquisition. No official page confirmed that, so the status is not marked shutdown. Paid plans such as $5/month and a $0-$20/month range appear only on third-party review sites like SourceForge, OMR, and NemoVideo. They are left out because no official page confirmed them. The current blurb is vague; the suggested short_description is a replacement.

record.short_description: AI plugin for Adobe Premiere Pro that creates animated captions, short social clips, and vertical reframes
record.description: Brevidy is an AI plugin that runs as a panel inside Adobe Premiere Pro. It is aimed at editors and creators who make short videos for social media. It writes and styles animated captions word by word, with 700+ presets. Its AutoCut feature turns long footage like podcasts and interviews into short captioned clips. AutoCrop reframes wide footage to vertical and follows the person speaking. The panel also has a stock media browser, AI emoji and media suggestions, and shared team presets.
record.pricing_summary: Brevidy's own site lists the Captioner plan at $14.99/month billed yearly, with 100 caption minutes a month. The Producer plan adds unlimited captions. There is a 7-day free trial with no credit card required.
features: Shared team preset library and admin roles
use_cases: Repurposing podcasts and interviews into social clips
record.notes: The current blurb is too vague. Brevidy is specifically a Premiere Pro plugin for AI captions and clipping. The search tool limit ran out before the homepage or pricing page could be opened directly, so these facts come from indexed brevidy.pro pages (/alternatives and /alternatives/brevidy-vs-firecut) plus third-party sources. Brevidy's own comparison table calls its free option 'Trial only', so free_tier is false. A third-party site (Kompozy) mentions a free sample caption. Prices seen only on third-party sites were left out of pricing_summary: Captioner at $17.99 monthly (CineD, captionplug), and Producer at about $35.99/month (Kompozy) or $29.99/month billed yearly (aescripts). Adobe's video partner directory lists Brevidy as a partner. No company or legal entity name was found.

record.short_description: AI chatbot builder for businesses that captures leads and answers customer questions around the clock
record.description: Boon is a web-based tool for building custom AI chatbots for businesses. According to its sign-up page, the chatbots keep a business responsive when staff are offline, so leads are not missed and customer service continues. Third-party listings say users can train the bot on their own PDF and Word files and brand it with their logos, colors and messaging style. Those listings also say it collects visitor contact details, stores chat data for analytics, and connects to Zapier.
features: Training on uploaded documents such as PDFs and Word files
Brand customization with logos, colors and messaging style
use_cases: Answering website visitor inquiries outside business hours
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit after the first round of searches, so I could not open the www.boonbot.com homepage or a pricing page. The only page I found on the product's own domain is app.boonbot.com/sign-up. It describes building custom AI chatbots that keep a business active when you're not there, so you never miss a lead. The features, Zapier integration and document training come from third-party directories (SourceForge, Softonic, Creati.ai), not from the official site. Those directories call Boon subscription-based, but I found no prices or tiers on boonbot.com, so pricing_type is unknown and pricing_summary is empty. I found no company or legal entity name. Boon is easy to mix up with other products: Boon AI (getboon.ai, construction), boon.ai (a GTM platform), Boon Health (coaching), Boon (employee referrals) and Boon Solutions (boon.com.au). The current blurb, 'Maximize your sales with an optimized chatbot', is a slogan. The sign-up page focuses on lead capture and customer service more than on sales.

record.short_description: Note-taking and personal knowledge management app that organizes ideas as connected objects instead of folders
record.description: Capacities is a note-taking and personal knowledge management app from Capacities Labs GmbH, a bootstrapped company based in Freiburg, Germany. Instead of files and folders, it stores ideas as connected objects. It offers custom object types, bi-directional links, backlinks, a graph view, daily notes and tags. Paid plans add an AI assistant, smart queries, tasks and calendar integration. It runs on web, Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS and Android, keeps data in the EU and is built for individuals rather than teams.
record.pricing_summary: Capacities has a free plan with unlimited spaces, objects and blocks. Pro costs $11.99/month or $119.88/year, and Believer starts at $14.99/month or $149.88/year.
features: Quick capture via WhatsApp, Telegram, email
record.notes: The listed website is correct and the site is up. Prices come from Capacities' own Facts page (capacities.io/about/facts). I could not open a dedicated /pricing page because I hit the search tool limit. Third-party sites such as SaaS Radar, Costbench and noteapps list older prices ($9.99/month Pro, $12.49/month Believer), so I did not use them. The Facts page says a Pro free trial is available in the app with no credit card required. It also says there are no team plans and no lifetime plan. The current blurb is vague. A clearer version would be: object-based note-taking and knowledge management app. Readwise, Kindle and MCP integrations are listed as Pro features on a Capacities blog page about European note-taking apps.

record.short_description: AI agents that estimate motor vehicle accident case values and capture leads for personal injury firms
record.description: CaseYak is a Denver-based legal tech product that predicts the value of motor vehicle accident claims. It uses neural network models trained on more than 10 years of jury verdict data. It sells AI lead magnets to personal injury law firms. These are LLM-powered agents that run as a website chatbot, a standalone form, or an SMS phone agent. They collect accident details from potential clients, give an estimated case value, and send lead reports to the firm. A developer API for case value estimates is also offered.
record.pricing_summary: Website MVA AI Agent costs $249.99/month or $2,999.99/year, and SMS MVA AI Agent costs $999.99/month or $9,599.99/year, both for standard traffic. A Developer API plan is listed but its price was not visible.
features: Neural network models trained on 10+ years of jury verdict data
Motor vehicle accident case value predictions
Customization to match website look and feel
Developer API for case value estimates
Models trained on a firm's historical settlement data
use_cases: Lead generation for personal injury law firms
Turning website traffic into qualified case leads
Adding case value estimates to applications via API
Agencies launching intake across client firm sites
record.notes: The official site caseyak.com is live. Its privacy policy names the operator as Griffn Inc. d/b/a CaseYak. The current blurb is outdated and reads as consumer-facing. The product is now sold mainly to personal injury law firms as AI intake and lead-generation agents for motor vehicle accident cases. A legacy domain, thecaseyak.com, describes an earlier form-based version that included Spanish support. The WordPress.org plugin listing confirms the $249.99/mo subscription. I found no free tier or free trial on the official site. One third-party directory says consumer evaluations are free, but that is not confirmed on caseyak.com. The Developer API price was not visible in the content I retrieved.

record.short_description: AI symptom checker that asks questions about symptoms and suggests possible causes and appropriate care
record.description: Buoy Symptom Checker is an AI-based tool from Buoy Health, a Boston company founded in 2014. It asks users a series of questions about their current symptoms. From the answers, it suggests possible causes and points them to an appropriate level of care, such as self-care, a doctor visit, urgent care, or the emergency room. Buoy also sells its symptom-checking and triage engine as an API, so organizations can build it into their own websites and mobile apps and customize it.
features: AI symptom checker using a series of questions
Guidance to the appropriate level of care
Symptom-checking and triage engine via API
use_cases: Deciding between self-care, a doctor visit, urgent care, or the ER
Adding symptom checking to a mobile app or website
Helping customers find the right level of care and schedule appointments
integrations: Buoy API for websites and applications
record.notes: The search tool limit was reached before I could open the listed multi-symptom-checker page or any pricing page on buoyhealth.com. The only official-domain page I could confirm is buoyhealth.com/developers, which describes the Buoy API. The symptom checker is called free on findtherightcare.org, a third-party site labeled 'Powered by Buoy Health', and on directory sites. Because none of that is on Buoy's own domain, I left pricing_type as unknown and free_tier as false. I found no page naming a buyer or saying the product was discontinued. The current blurb is vague: the product is a symptom triage tool, not a symptom management tool. Recheck the listed URL and consumer pricing directly before publishing.

record.short_description: AI article writer that researches keywords and generates and publishes SEO-optimized articles at scale
record.description: Byword is an AI content platform that produces SEO-optimized articles at scale. It researches keywords, writes in a brand's voice using models such as GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, and publishes directly to WordPress, Webflow and other CMSs. A product called Byword CMS deploys programmatic SEO pages on a customer's domain and handles schemas, rendering, hosting and deployment. The site also offers free writing and SEO tools. Byword says more than 85,000 content teams use it.
record.pricing_summary: Starter costs $99/month for 25 articles, Standard $299/month for 80 articles, and Scale $999/month for 300 articles. New users can start free with 5 articles.
features: AI article writing in brand voice
Choice of GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, and Gemini 3.1 Pro
Programmatic SEO pages via Byword CMS
Managed schemas, rendering, hosting, and deployment
Free AI writing and SEO tools for titles, schema, readability, and metadata
record.notes: The listed blurb is out of date. Byword is now an AI article writer and SEO content generator, not a general text optimizer. Findings come from search-result snippets of byword.ai pages (home, pricing, connect, cms, tools). The pages were not opened in full because the search tool limit was hit. On the pricing page, '5 free articles' reads like a starter allowance, not an ongoing free plan, so free_tier is set to false. Third-party review sites also mention an Unlimited tier ($1,999 to $2,499/month) and pay-as-you-go pricing, but the official snippet does not confirm either, so they are left out. LinkedIn lists the company as Byword, founded in 2022 with 2 to 10 employees. CB Insights says it is based in London. This product is unrelated to the Byword Markdown editor app at bywordapp.com.

record.short_description: Indonesian conversational AI company offering chatbots, voicebots, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and omnichannel customer service tools
record.description: Botika is an Indonesian artificial intelligence company that builds chat assistants using machine learning and natural language processing, with a focus on everyday Bahasa Indonesia conversation. Its products include the Chatbotika chatbot platform, a GPT-based chatbot, the OmniBotika omnichannel customer service and call center tool, voicebots, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and a multilanguage LLM. Businesses use its chatbots to automate customer service and tasks such as billing, queuing, banking, travel, and commerce across chat messengers. Developers can also build chatbots and voicebots on the Botika Platform.
record.pricing_summary: Botika Text to Speech is free for up to 1,000 characters, with lifetime character packs at IDR 49,000, IDR 74,000, and IDR 149,000, and Enterprise API access priced on request. Botika LLM costs Rp 34,000 per 1 million input tokens and Rp 66,000 per 1 million output tokens.
features: GPT chatbot that remembers previous conversations
Access to external API data, OCR, STT, TTS
Omnichannel customer service and call center (OmniBotika)
Web-based platform for developers to build chatbots and voicebots
record.notes: The official site botika.online is live, with product pages for Chatbotika, Chatbot GPT, the products overview, About Us, Text to Speech, and omni.botika.online. The current blurb ('Real-time customer satisfaction optimization') is vague and doesn't describe the product; it is really an Indonesian AI chatbot, voicebot, and TTS/STT provider. I found no public price for the core chatbot or OmniBotika plans. The prices above are only for TTS and the LLM. OmniBotika's page says 'Start a free trial now', but I couldn't confirm the trial's terms. The messaging-channel integrations (LINE, WhatsApp, Messenger, Telegram, Slack, web widget) come from Botika's LinkedIn page and chatbots.org, not a page on botika.online. The Voicebotika Google Play listing names the company as PT Botika Teknologi Indonesia. Don't mix this up with the unrelated fashion AI photo tool also called Botika. The $22-$230/month prices on review sites belong to that product, not to botika.online.

record.short_description: Multimodal AI platform for searching, tagging, and analyzing large video, image, and audio libraries
record.description: Coactive AI offers the Coactive Multimodal AI Platform, which turns video, image, and audio content into searchable, taggable data for media companies, publishers, and other enterprises. Customers index their content once, and applications such as search, ads, recommendations, and moderation all draw on that same index. The platform works with any AI model, connects to cloud storage, and provides APIs for existing systems. Context Studio is its first flagship application. The company is aimed at enterprise media rather than small teams.
features: Multimodal AI Platform for video, image, and audio
Index content once, power every downstream application
Custom tag concepts and zero-shot tagging
Model-independent infrastructure: bring your own or chain models
Semantic Engine with yes/no feedback for concept customization
Petabyte-scale ingestion; P95 under 500ms queries on 50M+ assets
use_cases: Content moderation of uploads at scale
Content search and discovery for media libraries
Creative intelligence and tagging for agencies
record.notes: The official site (coactive.ai) is up and describes the product as a multimodal AI platform for media, so the current blurb ('Automatically optimize visual metadata') is outdated and too narrow. I found no pricing page on coactive.ai. A third-party blog (eesel.ai) cites an enterprise plan of $75,000 per 12 months and says Coactive publishes no pricing, but that is not on the official domain, so I left the price fields empty. I saw no free tier or trial. Customer examples on the site include Fandom (auto-moderation), and the blog features NBCUniversal. Third-party sources name the legal entity as Coactive Systems Inc., based in San Jose. I reviewed the official pages only through search-result extracts, and the search tool hit its limit before I could check the docs or integrations pages.

record.short_description: AI content generation, social media tracking, and audience analytics tools for media and gaming companies
record.description: ClevrAI is an AI-powered digital marketing platform that markets itself to media and gaming companies. It includes AI generators for social posts, product descriptions, blog posts, and emails. It also offers keyword and domain trackers, domain and page authority checkers, a meta tags analyzer, audience insights, and predictive churn reduction tools. ClevrAI says these tools help businesses improve engagement, manage ad spend, and track metrics across digital channels. It sells three tiered monthly subscription plans.
record.pricing_summary: The ClevrAI homepage lists three monthly plans: ClevrStart at $49, ClevrEngage at $99, and ClevrOptimize at $149. Each higher plan includes everything in the plan below it.
use_cases: Tracking media and gaming metrics across digital channels
record.notes: Search results showed a snippet of the clevr.ai homepage, which is dated about 696 days old. That snippet gave the plans and features above. I could not open a separate pricing page because I hit my search limit. The homepage title advertises 'free' AI content generator tools, but the only plans shown are paid. I found no free plan or trial on the official site, so free_tier is set to false. Third-party directories list different prices ($10/$25/$40, from $49.99, and from $249.99/mo). These look out of date and were not used. Crunchbase lists CLEVR AI Inc. in Scottsdale, AZ, and gives its operating status as Active. The site lists a Menlo Park, CA address. The current blurb is broadly accurate but leaves out content generation and the media and gaming focus. There are unrelated products with similar names: Clevr AI: Homework AI on the App Store, clevr-ai.com, and CleVR panoramas.

record.short_description: Discontinued free nonprofit tool that detected AI-written text in essays and emails
record.description: CheckforAi was a free web tool that checked whether essays and emails had been written by AI. Directory listings say it combined OpenAI's RoBERTa-base GPT detection model with its own models to reduce false readings. The project's X account says it was a free nonprofit project for individuals. It also says the team has sunset the service to focus on new projects. A comparison page reports that checkforai.com now shows a sunset notice and that the detector is offline.
features: AI-written text detection for essays and emails
Combines OpenAI's RoBERTa-base GPT detection model with proprietary models
record.notes: Change the status to discontinued. The project's own X account (x.com/checkforai) says CheckforAi 'was a free nonprofit project for individuals' and that the team has 'sunset the service to focus on new projects.' The scanforai.com comparison page quotes the same notice from checkforai.com. LogicWeb also lists the tool as discontinued, and Dang.ai marked it inactive on Jul 30, 2024. I could not open checkforai.com directly because I hit the search tool limit. No pricing page exists on the product's domain. The 'free' label comes from the project's X statement and third-party directories, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are left empty. The free tier no longer applies because the service has ended. The current blurb ('Optimizing writing and social network engagement') is wrong: this was an AI-text detector. No company or legal entity name was found. Do not confuse this with checkfor.ai, a separate API product that has its own pricing page.

record.short_description: AI chatbot that answers legal questions and gives guidance to individuals and businesses
record.description: ChatLegal is an AI chatbot that answers legal questions. Its terms of service say it is provided by LawThor OÜ, and third-party profiles place the company in Tallinn, Estonia. The product is called an AI Legal Helper. It is available 24/7 and gives real-time, personalized guidance without booking an appointment. The company says it can help with drafting a contract, intellectual property questions, and landlord-tenant disputes. It is aimed at individuals, companies, and legal professionals who want faster, cheaper answers to legal questions.
use_cases: Finding answers to legal questions for individuals and companies
record.notes: The name, domain, and company were confirmed on the official site. Search results showed chatlegal.io's contact, terms, and blog pages. The terms name LawThor OÜ as the provider and have an effective date of 14.06.2023. The homepage and a pricing page could not be opened because the search tool limit was reached, so status is inferred from the indexed site pages. No prices were found on chatlegal.io. The contact page only says 'Try ChatLegal for Free'. A directory site (theresanaiforthat.com) lists a free trial with monthly billing but no amounts, so it was not used for pricing. Dealroom lists Tallinn, Estonia, founded 2023, and 1 employee. The listed blurb is vague. A better one: an AI chatbot giving 24/7 legal guidance. Watch for name collisions: chatlegal.ai and Plainly Legal's ChatLegal™ are different products.

record.short_description: Enterprise agentic AI platform for building voice and chat customer service AI agents
record.description: Cognigy is an enterprise conversational and agentic AI platform for customer service, now operated as NiCE Cognigy after NiCE completed its acquisition in September 2025. Its Cognigy.AI platform lets contact centers deploy AI Agents across phone, chat, and 30+ digital channels, powered by the Cognigy Nexus Engine, which combines foundation models with orchestration. The site cites support for 100+ languages and 110+ prebuilt tools and integrations. Cognigy Live Agent adds an AI-assisted omnichannel workspace with Agent Copilot for human agents.
features: Agentic AI Agents for phone and chat support
Cognigy Nexus Engine multi-layered AI core
Cognigy Live Agent omnichannel agent workspace
record.notes: The listed website works and its pages are branded 'from NiCE Cognigy.' NiCE closed its acquisition of Cognigy on September 8, 2025. Sources for this are a NiCE press release filed with the SEC, NiCE's FY2025 Form 20-F, CX Today and Call Centre Helper. NiCE said it will keep selling Cognigy on its own as well as inside CXone Mpower. I found no official pricing page. Third-party sites list different numbers: Capterra and GetApp show $2,500/month usage-based, Vendr shows about $115K/year on average, and some competitor blogs say custom enterprise pricing with no free tier or trial. Because of that, pricing is left as unknown and free_tier is false, which is unverified. I hit the search limit before I could look for a pricing, trial or full integrations page on cognigy.com, so the integrations list is incomplete. The current blurb is vague and out of date. It should mention agentic AI agents for enterprise contact centers and the NiCE ownership.

record.short_description: AI writing tool that helps founders and marketers create SEO-friendly blog posts and marketing copy
record.description: ContentBot.ai is an AI writing platform for founders and marketers. Its main tool, the AI Blog Writer, generates SEO-friendly blog posts. These posts can include internal and external links, keywords chosen by the user, facts drawn from sources the user picks, and HD AI images. ContentBot also offers a WordPress plugin. The plugin's tools cover product descriptions, blog ideas and outlines, rewriting and tone changes, summaries, ad copy, landing page content, and copywriting formulas such as AIDA and PAS.
features: SEO-friendly blog posts with internal and external links
Data-driven blog posts using sources the user specifies
Blog topic ideas, intros, outlines and conclusions
Ad copy for Adwords and Facebook
Copywriting formulas such as AIDA, PBS and PAS
Brand names, startup ideas and slogans
use_cases: Blog content creation for founders and marketers
record.notes: I confirmed the official site (contentbot.ai) through its AI Blog Writer page (contentbot.ai/ai-blog-writer). Features also come from the official ContentBot WordPress plugin listing on wordpress.org. I could not open the official pricing page because my search limit ran out, so pricing_summary, pricing_source_url and pricing_type are left empty or set to unknown. Third-party sites give conflicting prices. Newer ones (ColdIQ, GitHub gists) list Prepaid at $0.50 per 1,000 words, Starter $9/mo, Premium $29/mo and Premium+ $49/mo. Older ones (SaaSworthy, Tekpon) list $1 per 1,000 words, $19, $59 and $99. Third-party sources also say there is no free trial, only 10k free words on the first purchase. Check this against contentbot.ai's own pricing page. The current blurb, 'Optimisez effortless content creation.', mixes French and English and reads like a slogan, so it should be replaced. Some GitHub pages that offer 'ContentBot download' for Mac and Windows do not look official and were ignored.

record.short_description: AI coding agent and pair programmer for code generation, debugging, automated code reviews, and PR review
record.description: CodeMate AI is an AI pair programmer and coding agent from CodeMate AI. It builds an ongoing understanding of a codebase and its documentation, and uses that context to find logical, syntax, and runtime issues, suggest fixes, and automate debugging, testing, and code review. Its products include CodeMate Build, which turns prompts and Figma designs into apps, CORA, a coding agent inside the IDE, an AI terminal, and a PR Review Agent. It is pitched as a private, self-hosted alternative to tools like GitHub Copilot and Cursor.
features: AI terminal for running code and scripts
CodeMate Build: prompts and Figma designs to deployable apps
Design Mode for UI components and layouts
CORA end-to-end AI coding agent in the IDE
Custom AI Skills for team coding standards
PR Review Agent with security analysis
Codebase-aware detection of logical, syntax, and runtime issues
use_cases: Shipping code faster with AI assistance
Automating manual code review and debugging
Turning Figma designs into working code
Automating pull request reviews and security analysis
Secure AI-assisted development for enterprises that need data sovereignty
record.notes: The official site (codemate.ai) and docs (docs.codemate.ai) are live. The listed URL https://www.codemate.ai/ works. The current blurb 'Optimize the code to reduce bugs' is too narrow: the product is now a full-stack AI coding agent with Build, CORA, an AI terminal, and a PR Review Agent. I could not open an official pricing page, so pricing is left blank. Third-party sites disagree with each other: Capterra says contact vendor, SaaSworthy and SpotSaaS say from $8/month, Milestone AI lists Pro at $20/month and Teams at $37/user/month, and F6S says from $59/month. None of these are used here. The VS Code Marketplace lists the extension as free, but that is not on CodeMate's own domain, so free_tier is set to false and pricing_type to unknown. The homepage mentions an enterprise partnership with Maruti Suzuki. My search tool hit its limit before I could check a pricing or integrations docs page.

record.short_description: AI tool for job seekers that creates tailored resumes, optimized resumes, and cover letters
record.description: CoverQuick is an AI job application assistant for job seekers. It creates resumes tailored to a job posting, optimized resumes, and cover letters. Users can make unlimited documents, exports, and folders. The free plan includes a set number of AI credits, and the paid plan adds unlimited credits and AI editing. An Enterprise plan for teams offers white labeling, single sign-on, and custom integrations. Its LinkedIn page says the company is a small team with two co-founders.
record.pricing_summary: The Free plan costs nothing, needs no credit card, and includes 500 AI credits for tailored resumes, optimized resumes, and cover letters. Pro costs $20 per month and adds unlimited AI credits and AI editing, while Enterprise pricing is by contact and adds white labeling, a custom domain, and SSO.
features: Folders and tabs for organizing documents
use_cases: Tailoring a resume to a specific job description
Writing cover letters for job applications
Offering a white-labeled resume tool to teams or organizations
record.notes: The current blurb is wrong. CoverQuick is not a social media content tool. It is an AI resume and cover letter generator for job seekers. The pricing page has a leftover tagline about 'content creation and management', which may explain the old blurb. The pricing facts come from coverquick.co/pricing as shown in search results. The homepage was not opened directly because the search tool hit its usage limit. Third-party sites (SourceForge, intrico.io) mention a job application tracker and interview prep, but these were not confirmed on the official site, so they are left out. The only official mention of integrations is 'Custom Integrations' on the Enterprise plan, with no named tools. coverquick.app is a separate site with different pricing ($4.99 for 7 days, $9.99/month, $49.99 lifetime) and should not be confused with this product. The LinkedIn page lists the co-founders as Tosin Kuye and Divine Adekanmbi. CB Insights says the company was founded in 2022 and is based in Sherwood Park, Canada.

record.short_description: AI tool that drafts personalized LinkedIn comments to help professionals gain visibility and generate leads
record.description: Commenter AI is a web-based tool from Commenter AI LTD that uses AI to write personalized LinkedIn comments. Users can edit each draft to match their own voice. It is aimed at founders, consultants, marketers, and sales teams who want more profile views, impressions, and leads without posting every day. Users can comment through the web platform, a companion Chrome extension called Social Post Mate, or iOS and Android mobile apps. The privacy policy also mentions LinkedIn and Gmail integration.
features: Context-aware comments customized to your tone
Engage with important connections and keywords
Secure post viewer for connected LinkedIn account
use_cases: Turning comments into leads, DMs, and calls
Personal brand building for founders and consultants
record.notes: The official homepage, About page, privacy policy (Commenter AI LTD), and blog posts were all found and confirm the product is active and focused on LinkedIn commenting. The homepage says no credit card is required, and a blog post mentions signing up for a free trial or a paid plan. I could not open a pricing page on commenter.ai. Third-party prices conflict: ColdIQ says $149 to $1,970 per year, aimojo says $17 to $197 per month, and several 2026 sites say Signals $99, Workflow $149, and Teams $350 per month with a 7-day trial. So I left pricing empty and set pricing_type to unknown. Some third-party sources say the product has pivoted toward managing LinkedIn sales conversations (DMs, email, meetings), but I could not confirm this on the official site. The current blurb is too broad: the product is LinkedIn-specific, not general social media content optimization. The search tool limit was reached before I could check the pricing page directly.

record.short_description: AI writing and study tool that helps students draft essays with citations
record.description: Cramly is an AI writing tool for students. Its official X account says it drafts essays with real citations. On LinkedIn, the company says it gives students AI tools to help them learn more efficiently and get more value from their study time. The company blog lists a long essay generator, an essay outline tool, and an essay paraphraser. LinkedIn lists the company under e-learning, with headquarters in Cheyenne, Wyoming. It is aimed at academic writing, not social media content.
record.pricing_summary: The company blog says Cramly is not a free tool. It offers a 7-day free trial before a paid subscription, and this page gives no prices.
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize content creation for social media') is wrong. Every source describes Cramly as an AI writing and study tool for students, so the blurb should be replaced. I hit the search limit before I could open the cramly.ai homepage or its pricing page directly. The facts here come from the company's own blog (blog.cramly.ai), its X profile, and its LinkedIn page. Status is marked unknown because I could not confirm the site is up. Recent third-party pages suggest it is still live. Prices differ across third-party sites. One site (anygen.io) says the official pricing page lists $20 monthly, $4/month billed yearly, and $110 lifetime. Older reviews list $9.99/month and $59.88/year. I did not check any of these on cramly.ai, so I left them out. Some directories also mention a free plan, but the company blog says there is only a 7-day trial. Don't mix this up with a separate iOS app called 'Cramly AI' (developer Albaraa Taher Zeinoglu, website cramly.org). It is a different product.

record.short_description: Online plagiarism checker that scans pasted text or uploaded documents against web sources for duplicate content
record.description: Duplichecker is a web-based plagiarism checker. Users paste text or upload .docx, .txt, or .pdf files, and the tool scans the content against online sources for duplication. Its reports show the share of unique content and list matching sources. The homepage says scans can cover up to 25,000 words per search on higher plans and also offers a free checker. The site sells plagiarism plans, paraphrasing plans, and a separate reverse image search product.
record.pricing_summary: The official reverse image search pricing page lists a Lite plan at $16.98/week and a Basic plan at $39.28/month. Prices for the plagiarism checker plans were not confirmed on the official site.
features: Plagiarism checking by paste or file upload
use_cases: Checking assignments, essays, and theses for plagiarism
record.notes: The official homepage is live. It describes a free plagiarism checker plus paid Plagiarism Plans, Paraphrasing Plans, and Reverse Image Search. The only prices confirmed on duplichecker.com came from its reverse image search pricing page (/ris-pricing), so the pricing summary covers only that product. Third-party sites (SaaSworthy, Scribbr, alternatives.co, others) give different plagiarism plan prices, from $5/week to $10, $19.99, or $25/month. These conflict with each other and were not confirmed on the official site, so they are left out. I hit the search limit before I could open an official plagiarism pricing page. Integrations were not found. The current blurb is a slogan and should be replaced with a plain description.

record.short_description: AI tool that turns documents, pasted text, and YouTube videos into practice tests
record.description: CreateMyTest is a web-based study tool that uses artificial intelligence to turn documents, pasted text, and YouTube videos into tests in seconds. Students can turn their notes into tests and then check what they remember using the test results. The site says users can test themselves through unlimited sessions at no additional cost, and it presents this as a way to get better marks and reduce test anxiety. Support is offered by email.
record.pricing_summary: The official homepage lists a Free plan: one-time, 200 words, no credit card required. Paid plan prices were not visible on the official page.
features: Paste text content or a document
Test results to confirm retained knowledge
use_cases: Turning class notes into practice tests
record.notes: The official homepage is live, and it supports the blurb, the free plan details (one-time, 200 words, no credit card), and the support email help@createmytest.com. A search tool limit stopped me from opening a separate pricing page or docs page. Directory sites (topai.tools, opentools.ai) list paid plans at $10, $30 and $50. Those prices are not on the official domain, so I left them out of pricing_summary. I set pricing_type to freemium because those directories show paid tiers, but the official site only shows the free plan. February 2024 press releases (Newswire/ACCESSWIRE, Toronto) describe the app. They mention multiple choice, true/false, matching and fill-in-the-blank question types and PDF input, but I did not confirm these on the official page. I could not find the name of the company behind the product. The current blurb is accurate, but 'optimized' is not wording the site uses. Suggested wording: 'Convert documents and YouTube videos into tests in seconds using AI.'

record.short_description: AI noise-cancelling desktop app for online calls, with screen recording and meeting minutes
record.description: CrystalSound is a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux. It uses AI to remove background noise and other people's voices from both sides of online calls. It also records the screen and both sides of the call audio, and it is adding meeting minutes and insights. Audio is processed on the user's device for privacy. A premium feature called My Voice Only registers the user's voice and keeps only that voice. The company also sells a speech enhancement SDK for developers and device makers.
record.pricing_summary: The pricing page lists an Enterprise plan with no published price, a Premium plan billed per user per year whose price did not load, and an Elite plan marked coming soon at $228 USD per user per year. It also runs a promotion: buy one Premium subscription and get a second free.
features: Noise cancellation and speech enhancement SDK with WebAssembly support
use_cases: Taking calls in noisy places such as cafes
Adding speech enhancement to audio devices and web apps
record.notes: The site is up, with homepage, pricing, download, installation guide and developer SDK pages on crystalsound.ai. The listed blurb is accurate but narrow. The product also does screen and call recording, meeting minutes, and offers a developer SDK. On the pricing page, the Premium price did not show up in what I retrieved. Only the Elite price ($228/user/year, coming soon) appeared, and Enterprise has no public price. The homepage says 'Try it free' and the download page says download for free, but I found no clearly defined free plan or trial length, so free_tier is set to false and pricing_type to paid. The Zoom, Skype, Teams, Discord and Slack compatibility comes from the company's own 2023 blog post. The company name is taken from how the developer page refers to itself (CrystalSound.AI); I found no legal entity name or location. A search-tool limit stopped further checks.

record.short_description: AI stock analytics platform that rates US and European stocks and ETFs with an explainable AI Score
record.description: Danelfin is an AI-powered stock analytics platform for investors. It analyzes more than 10,000 features per stock each day and gives each stock an AI Score from 1 to 10. The score estimates the probability that the stock will beat the market. The AI is explainable, so users can see the fundamental, technical and sentiment alpha signals behind each score. The platform also offers stock and ETF rankings, trade ideas, AI price forecasts and portfolio tracking with broker sync. API access is available too.
record.pricing_summary: Website plans billed monthly: Plus is $29/month, Pro is $79/month and Elite is $179/month (Elite includes API Expert with 10,000 calls/month). A separate API Free plan is $0 forever with 500 calls/month, and paid plans have a 30-day money-back guarantee.
features: AI Score (1-10) for probability of beating the market
Explainable AI with transparent alpha signals
Fundamental, technical, and sentiment alpha signals
Portfolio tracking with automatic sync to U.S. broker accounts
use_cases: Identifying the best moment to invest in favorite stocks
Programmatic access to AI scores via API
record.notes: Checked danelfin.com, danelfin.com/pricing/monthly and danelfin.com/pricing/api/annual. The pricing page mentions a Free website tier ('Everything in Free'; Free: Top 10 in rankings), but the excerpt I retrieved did not show its full limits. The API Free plan is confirmed at $0 forever with 500 calls/month. Some third-party review sites list different prices, such as annual-billing equivalents ($22/$59/$134) or old tier names. Only the monthly prices from the official page are used here, and annual billing is shown as -25%. The pricing page mentions a trial ('skip trial'), but I could not confirm its length on the official site. The specific brokers supported for sync were not confirmed. The current blurb 'Optimize portfolios with precise data' is vague; the product is mainly an AI stock-picking and rating tool.

record.short_description: Cloud-based vocal synthesizer plugin that turns typed notes and lyrics into sung vocals
record.description: Emvoice One is a vocal synthesizer plugin from Emvoice that creates sung vocals without recording. Users enter notes in a piano-roll editor and type lyrics, with each note matched to a syllable. The melodies are sent to a cloud engine, which rebuilds them from deeply sampled human vocal recordings and sends the vocal back to the DAW. It runs as a VST, AU, or AAX plugin on Mac and PC. It needs an internet connection, and voices are licensed through in-app subscriptions.
record.pricing_summary: One Voice Monthly is $7.99/month and All Voices Monthly is $11.99/month, with an introductory 50% off for the first two months ($3.99 and $5.99). Subscriptions are bought inside the plugin, and the official site also offers a free demo download.
features: Enter notes and type lyrics to create vocals
Pronunciation options and custom words from phonemes
use_cases: Creating vocals without a microphone or recording
Songwriting and demo vocal lines in a DAW
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize the workflow in copywriting') is wrong. Emvoice is an AI/sampled vocal synthesizer plugin for music production and has nothing to do with copywriting. Pricing comes from search-result text for the emvoiceapp.com homepage, which shows Pricing and Download sections. It lists $7.99/month (one voice) and $11.99/month (all voices), with 50% off for the first two months, and says to subscribe in-app. Prices may change with promotions. The free tier is a demo: KVR and press coverage say unlicensed voices are limited to a small range of notes (about seven or eight). Older third-party sources mention one-time voice licenses ($59–$199), but those look like they were replaced by subscriptions. The DAW names (Logic Pro, Pro Tools, Ableton Live, etc.) come from a Gearspace article, not the official site. The search tool limit was reached, so no separate docs or manual page was opened.

record.short_description: AI text-to-video platform for making avatar-presented training videos in 75+ languages
record.description: Elai.io is an AI video generation platform built mainly for corporate learning and HR teams. It turns text, URLs, and PowerPoint files into videos narrated by AI avatars, without cameras, studios, or actors. The platform supports more than 75 languages and 450 accents, voice cloning in 28 languages, video translation, interactive quizzes, and templates. It also offers an API for creating videos in bulk and integrations with learning and automation tools. Third-party sources report that Panopto acquired the company in 2024.
features: Custom selfie, studio, photo, and animated mascot avatars
record.notes: I confirmed the official site through these elai.io pages: home, learning-development, integrations, enterprise, and getting-started-with-api. I hit the search tool limit before I could open elai.io's own pricing page, so I left pricing blank. Third-party sites list prices that don't agree with each other and may be out of date. TheRundown lists Free (1 rendered minute), Creator at $29/mo or $23/mo billed annually, Team from $125/mo or $100/mo billed annually, and custom Enterprise pricing. G2 and SoftwareFinder show different numbers. The official site says 'Try Elai for Free', and its API page mentions a trial. I couldn't tell from the site whether that means a lasting free plan or just a trial, so I set free_tier to false and pricing_type to unknown. I set the status to acquired because third-party pages name Panopto as the buyer: checkthat.ai gives a date of Oct 23, 2024, and G2 and TheRundown call Elai Panopto's product. I didn't open any Panopto or elai.io page that confirms the acquisition. The current blurb is accurate, but it could mention that the product focuses on corporate training and AI avatars.

record.short_description: No-code platform for building chatbots and WhatsApp automation across messaging channels
record.description: Engati is a cloud-based conversational AI platform for building and deploying chatbots without coding. Its low-code visual builder uses drag-and-drop elements and prebuilt templates to set up chatbots and automated workflows. The company says bots can engage customers in more than 50 languages and can be published across about 14 messaging channels, including WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Slack, Telegram, and website chat. Engati also offers templates for WhatsApp marketing campaigns and is aimed at customer service and engagement.
record.notes: Engati's own content now appears on engati.ai. I did not confirm whether the listed engati.com redirects there. The search tool hit its usage limit before I could open Engati's own pricing page, so pricing is left empty. Third-party sites give conflicting prices: one (getmacha) cites Engati's pricing page as saying 'less than $1 a day' with a 7-day free trial, while others list $79/month, $99/quarter, $15/user, or custom pricing, and some mention an old free Starter plan. None of these were checked on engati.ai. The parent company and acquisition status were not checked. The current blurb ('Manage 24/7 customer experience with chatbots') is broadly accurate but vague; the platform's own pages now stress WhatsApp and omnichannel automation.

record.short_description: Website for comparing electric vehicles by specs, prices, range, and AI-generated review summaries
record.description: EV Intersection is a website for people shopping for an electric vehicle. Its homepage says it compares 67 EVs from 26 brands, showing specs, prices and AI-generated review summaries side by side. Users can browse by brand or by category, such as SUVs, trucks, longest range, fastest 0–60, or price bands. They can also compare two models head-to-head. Model pages list trims, EPA range, starting price, horsepower and federal tax credit details. Developer Chris Betz built it in 2023.
features: Head-to-head comparison of any two EVs
Browse by category (SUVs, trucks, sedans, longest range, fastest 0–60, under $30k/$40k/$50k)
Per-model trim pages with EPA range, price, 0–60, horsepower
use_cases: Finding an EV by range, price, brand, or 0–60
record.notes: The listed URL redirects to the official site at www.evintersection.com, which is live. The current blurb ('Optimize automotive performance analysis') is wrong. The site is a consumer tool for finding and comparing EVs, not a performance-analysis tool. The site has no pricing page, and none of the pages I found say whether the service is free. TAAFT and success.ai list it as free, but those are directory sites, so I left pricing empty and set it to unknown. The company is based on Chris Betz's portfolio page (cbetz.com), which credits him with design and engineering in 2023; no company entity is named. The site's homepage did not list any integrations. My search limit ran out before I could open more pages.

record.short_description: Agentic AI pentesting platform that continuously tests attack surfaces and validates exploitable vulnerabilities
record.description: Ethiack is an Adversarial Exposure Validation platform from a company based in Coimbra, Portugal. Its AI agent, Hackian, keeps testing an organization's attack surface. It checks whether each finding can really be exploited and provides proof-of-exploit, which the company says removes 90% of scanner noise. Results are ranked by real impact, so teams know what to fix first. Ethiack sells one-off on-demand pentests with compliance-ready reports and annual continuous testing subscriptions. Fixes are retested automatically with unlimited retesting.
record.pricing_summary: On-Demand Pentest costs €3,000 per test. Continuous Core covers up to 50 assets and is listed at €9,000 per year, marked down 25% from €12,000. Enterprise is priced on request and has a guarantee offer: it is free unless a validated, exploitable vulnerability is found.
features: Prioritization by exploitability rather than CVSS
use_cases: Ongoing validation for fast-shipping tech companies
Reducing scanner noise and manual triage
record.notes: The homepage and pricing page were both found on ethiack.com. The homepage offers a 30-day free trial with no commitment. That is a trial, not a free tier, so free_tier is false. The pricing page shows €9,000 next to €12,000 with a 25% off label. I read this as a discounted price but have not confirmed it. Enterprise pricing is not published. SourceForge lists a different starting price of €1,790 per year that may be out of date, and it was not used. No integrations were confirmed on the official site. Gartner's listing mentions CI/CD pipeline integration but names no specific tools. Gartner gives founding year 2022 and HQ in Coimbra, Portugal. The current blurb is accurate but generic. A better one would say it is AI-driven continuous pentesting that confirms which vulnerabilities can be exploited.

record.short_description: AI-powered travel recommendation app that suggests places to visit based on destination and preferences
record.description: Explorify is an AI-powered travel recommendation app. Its onboarding flow starts by asking which city the user wants to visit. A founder profile on a startup directory says the user enters a destination and preferences such as culture, cuisine or adventure. The AI then suggests places to visit, including lesser-known spots. The same profile says Explorify was founded in 2023 by a founder named Gabriel, is based in Belo Horizonte and has 1 to 5 employees.
use_cases: Discovering off-the-beaten-path places in a new city
record.notes: I hit the search tool limit, so I couldn't open the live homepage or a pricing page. The only official page I found was a search-indexed copy of tryexplorify.com/onboarding, titled 'What city - Explorify', which calls the product 'the #1 AI-powered travel recommendation app.' That confirms the domain belongs to this product, but not that the site is up now, so status is unknown. Founder name, founding year (2023), location and team size come from a founder-submitted profile on startupanz.com, which links to tryexplorify.com, not from the official site. No company name was found. Features and use cases come from third-party directory text (startupanz.com, bai.tools, toolpilot.ai) plus the official onboarding snippet. Third-party directories list paid pricing, for example an 'Individual' plan at $19 on bai.tools and toolpilot.ai. That couldn't be checked on the product's own domain, so pricing is left empty. Toolpilot.ai lists integrations (ChatGPT, SimilarWeb, Twitter) that the official site doesn't confirm, so none are recorded. Several unrelated products share the Explorify name: a Minecraft datapack, a UK primary-school science resource and a Spotify history tool. The current blurb ('Optimize the planning of unique trips') is vague. Something like 'AI travel recommendations based on your destination and interests' would be more accurate.

record.short_description: Adult AI companion platform for romantic and NSFW roleplay chat with custom AI characters
record.description: Erogen is a web platform for chatting with AI companions. It is built around romance, love, and adult (NSFW) roleplay. Users can browse characters in different styles, create and share their own companions, and download characters. The founder's launch post says the AIs can change their avatar images during a conversation and offers customizable AI voices. The platform has also run character contests and an affiliate program. Free messages are available after signing up, and paid plans are listed separately.
features: Dynamic avatar images based on conversation
record.notes: I couldn't open erogen.ai or plans.erogen.ai directly before I hit the search limit, so I left status as unknown. These facts come from the founder's Show HN post (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=39389887) and the official @erogen_ai account on X. The newest X posts I saw were from December 2024. The HN post describes the product as NSFW, romance-focused AI companionship. The current blurb ('Customize avatars to engage your audience') is misleading: it makes the product sound like an audience-engagement or marketing tool, so it should be rewritten. Prices only appeared on third-party directories, and they disagree: TechBriefly says from $5/month and There's An AI For That says from $15/month. I left pricing_summary empty.
