On HN, the founder said paid plans are at plans.erogen.ai and that free messages are available after signing up. erogen-ai.org is a different, lookalike domain and isn't the official site. StartupHub lists the company in London, UK.

record.short_description: AI tool that filters user feedback, questions, and bug reports out of YouTube comment sections
record.description: Feedby is an AI tool that pulls useful user feedback out of the comment sections of YouTube videos. Its site says that sorting through thousands of low-value comments by hand takes too long. Feedby instead uses AI to find feedback, questions, and bug reports and sends them to the user's inbox. It also shows how viewers feel about a video. Independent developer Dani Gleba built it, and it launched on Product Hunt in 2024.
record.pricing_summary: The official site lists usage-based pricing of $1 per 1,000 comments, with the note "For anything over $1".
features: Pulls out user feedback, questions and bug reports
Sends filtered feedback to your inbox
Shows how users feel about a video
use_cases: Collecting user feedback from YouTube video comments
Finding bug reports and feature requests from viewers
Building products based on what users say
record.notes: I didn't open the official page directly. All details come from web search snippets of feedby.danigleba.com, which still showed the headline, how it works, and the $1 per 1k comments price. The pricing note "For anything over $1" is unclear and may mean a $1 minimum charge. The search results showed no free tier. The current blurb, "Optimize the sorting of YouTube comments", is vague. The product actually filters comments to find user feedback, questions, and bug reports. The Product Hunt listing (launched 2024) links to the same domain and a GitHub repo. The developer seems to be independent maker Dani Gleba, who is not a formal company. No page said the product was shut down or acquired.

record.short_description: AI photo culling and editing software for high-volume event, wedding, sports and conference photographers
record.description: FilterPixel is AI software that culls and edits photos, with desktop apps for Mac and Windows. Its DeepCull mode uses genre-specific models for weddings, conferences, sports and concerts. It scores each photo on ten criteria, groups bursts, and flags blur, closed eyes and duplicates. FilterPixel Edits learns a photographer's editing style from past work and applies it across a gallery. Selections can be exported to Lightroom Classic or Capture One, and RAW files stay on the user's computer.
record.pricing_summary: The pricing page lists Standard at $14.99/mo ($180/yr) with 20 DeepCull shoots a year and Pro at $34.99/mo ($420/yr) with 70 DeepCull shoots, plus extra shoots at $7.99 each. Another FilterPixel page lists Studio at $64.99/mo ($780/yr) and a free plan with 4 projects.
use_cases: Applying a consistent editing style across large galleries
record.notes: The official site is up. Pricing comes from search snippets of filterpixel.com/pricing (Standard and Pro) and filterpixel.com/filterpixel-vs-aftershoot (Free and Studio). The Studio tier did not show in the pricing-page snippet. The free offer is described differently across FilterPixel pages: 4 free projects forever, a trial with 3 DeepCull projects, and an older 14-day trial page. Older pricing pages (/pricing-old, app upsell) show outdated prices and a $599 one-time license. No legal company name was found. Photo Mechanic export was mentioned only on an Imagen comparison page, not confirmed on FilterPixel's site. The current blurb is vague and should mention AI culling.

record.short_description: Chrome extension and web tool that finds email addresses from LinkedIn and drafts outreach emails with ChatGPT
record.description: FinalScout is an email finding and outreach tool published by Anewstip Limited. It is offered as a Chrome extension and a web app. It pulls valid email addresses from LinkedIn profiles and search results, including Sales Navigator searches, group members, and event attendees. It also finds emails from a company domain, an article, or a LinkedIn URL. The tool uses ChatGPT to write personalized emails based on LinkedIn profile information. It includes contact management with tags, email statuses, and CSV export, and it says it follows GDPR and CCPA rules.
features: Export emails from LinkedIn regular search
Export emails from LinkedIn Sales Navigator search
Export emails of LinkedIn group members and event attendees
Find emails by company domain, article, or LinkedIn URL
Contact management with tags, email statuses, and CSV export
use_cases: Turning LinkedIn searches into email lists
record.notes: The search tool hit its usage limit, so I could not open finalscout.com or a pricing page on that domain. The finalscout.com domain comes from SourceForge, and the publisher name, Anewstip Limited, comes from chrome-stats.com's record of the Chrome Web Store listing. The features listed here come only from third-party pages (textify.ai, saasworthy, futuretools, chrome-stats), and they need to be checked against the official site. Third-party sites give prices that disagree with each other. Some say a free plan plus $29/month. Others say Lite/Solo $50, Standard $100, and Pro $300 to $1,000. ColdIQ says $35. Because no price came from the official site, I left the pricing fields empty, set pricing type to unknown, and set free tier to false. I set status to unknown because I could not confirm the site is up, though reviews from 2026 suggest the product is still being sold. The listed website should be changed from the Chrome Web Store link to the official site, once that site is confirmed. The current blurb is a slogan and does not say what the product does.

record.short_description: AI toolkit for swapping faces in photos and videos, with anime, portrait and aging tools
record.description: FaceHub, listed in this directory as FaceMod, is an online AI toolkit at facengine.ai for editing photos and videos. Its face changer finds faces in a video or image and swaps them with one the user picks. It can swap several faces at once. Users can pick from preset video and photo templates or upload their own media. The site also has an AI portrait generator, an AI anime generator, an AI baby generator and an aging filter.
record.pricing_summary: The face swap page says face swapping is free and credits cost $9.99 for 20. No other tiers were confirmed on the official site.
features: AI face swap for videos and photos
use_cases: Advertising posters and marketing promo videos
record.notes: The listed site works but now uses the name FaceHub, not FaceMod. The FaceMod name still appears on third-party review and directory sites that link to this domain, so the directory name should probably change to FaceHub. The current blurb's phrase 'time savings guaranteed' does not appear on any page I opened. It reads like a slogan and should be replaced. The official pages I saw do not name the company. An App Store listing names YEABO LIMITED as the developer of a FaceMod iOS app, which AppBrain says is no longer available. I could not confirm it is the same company, so the company field is empty. Third-party sites list weekly ($9.99 billed monthly) and yearly ($39.99) plans, but I did not use them because they are not on the official domain. I checked a limited number of pages because the search tool hit its usage limit.

record.short_description: No-code platform for building AI agents, formerly an AI skin-analysis product recommendation API
record.description: Finiite is a New York-based software company, founded in 2020 according to third-party profiles. It first offered a cloud API for online retailers. The API used AI and computer vision to predict a shopper's skin type from a selfie and recommend matching products from a store. Recent third-party profiles and the company's X account now describe it differently: a no-code agentic AI platform for building and deploying LLM agents for customer support, lead capture, and HR onboarding.
features: Virtual skin analysis from customer photos (earlier product)
use_cases: Personalized product recommendations for online retailers
record.notes: I hit the search limit before I could open finiite.com or a pricing page on that domain, so this record relies only on third-party sources. finiite.com is still linked as the company site on its X profile (@FiniiteInc, posts from July 2025), Crunchbase (which lists it as active), and ZoomInfo. The current blurb is out of date: it describes the old skin-analysis recommendation API. The company now presents itself as an agentic AI agent-builder platform. Sources disagree on status. PitchBook lists Finiite as 'Out of Business', while Crunchbase and recent X posts suggest it is still operating. I set status to unknown because I couldn't check the official site. Prices only show up on directory and review sites: $55/$170/$250 per month for the old API on SoftwareSuggest and FinancesOnline, a DealFuel annual deal, and a 14-day trial claim on ColdIQ. I left pricing_summary and pricing_source_url empty for that reason. Someone should open finiite.com and recheck the record.

record.short_description: AI relationship intelligence workspace and CRM for fundraising, sales, and partnerships, built around investor pipeline management
record.description: Finta is an AI relationship intelligence workspace and CRM. It began as a fundraising platform for startups and now also covers sales, partnerships, and advisory work. Its AI assistant, Aurora, organizes context and keeps follow-ups moving. The platform includes an AI-driven CRM, deal rooms, data rooms, a prospects database, investor update drafting, and warm-introduction mapping. Finta also offers Finta Elite, a hands-on fundraising service, and a Powered by Finta program that lets accelerators and funds give the platform to their portfolio companies.
record.pricing_summary: Launch costs $29 per seat per month billed monthly, or $20 billed annually, and comes with a 14-day trial. Pro costs $59 per seat per month billed monthly, or $41 billed annually, with a 3-seat minimum. Elite is priced on request.
features: Unlimited Deals, Documents and Team Members (Pro)
use_cases: Sharing pitch decks and data rooms with investors
Accelerators and VC funds supporting portfolio companies
record.notes: The site is live and now positions Finta more broadly as AI relationship intelligence for fundraising, sales, and partnerships. The current blurb ('Optimize your relationships with investors') is close but narrower than that. The two pricing sources I found disagree. The pricing page result showed Launch, Pro, and Elite with a 14-day trial, and that is what the pricing summary uses. The homepage result instead mentioned 'Finta Pro at $99/mo' and a '7-day free trial, credit card required.' The pricing page may be cached or out of date, so these numbers need a manual check. I found no free plan on Finta's own site. Capterra lists a free version and a $15 starting price, but that is a third-party source and was not used. The homepage mentions inbox and calendar consolidation but does not name any integrations, so the integrations list is empty. LinkedIn gives the headquarters as Buffalo, NY, and Crunchbase says New York, NY. I could not run follow-up searches because the search limit was reached.

record.short_description: AI financial intelligence platform that analyzes social media and news data for real-time market insights
record.description: Finalle.ai is a financial intelligence platform that uses generative AI and new-media data sources, such as social media and news, to analyze financial markets. It collects and analyzes financial information to give investors a real-time view of the market and the forces moving it. Third-party profiles say the company was founded in 2023 and is based in Tel Aviv, Israel. They also describe it as serving financial institutions with stock market news analysis for decision-making, customer journeys, and compliance.
features: AI-generated insights from new-media and social media data
AI analysis of stock market news
use_cases: Following market trends and what drives them
record.notes: The current blurb ('Optimize content to engage more effectively') looks wrong. Every source I found describes Finalle.ai as a financial and market intelligence platform, not a content optimization tool. I could not open finalle.ai or any pricing page on its domain because my search budget ran out, so I have not confirmed that the site is live, and status is set to unknown. The official_url matches the domain cited by several directories (BetaList, Future Tools, ToolAI). Pricing appeared only on directory or review sites, so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are left empty. ToolAI lists Personal (free), Savvy Investor ($49/month), and Startup ($179/month). Several other directories list it as free, and a G2 review mentions a free version limited to five signals. None of this was checked on the official domain, so free_tier is false and pricing_type is unknown. Founding year and Tel Aviv location come from Tracxn and StartupHub.ai. I found no integrations on reliable sources. One directory mentioned 'botika AI', but I could not confirm it, so I left it out.

record.short_description: AI-powered strength training app that sets your sets, reps and weights and adjusts them as you progress
record.description: FitnessAI is a mobile app for iOS and Android that builds strength training workouts with AI. It sets the sets, reps and weights for each exercise and changes them as the user logs workouts and gets stronger. The company says its model is trained on more than 100 million sets from about 6 million workouts. The app includes guided exercise demos, progress tracking, adaptive recovery, Apple Watch syncing and a 3D body scan. It supports both gym and home training.
features: AI-powered workouts built from millions of real training sessions
AI-driven progressive overload that adjusts in real time
Smart progression of weights and reps
Guided videos and muscle visuals for correct form
Progress tracking of strength, volume and PRs
record.notes: The official site (fitnessai.com) and its landing page (get.fitnessai.com) are live. They describe an iOS/Android app but show no prices. Subscription prices appear only on third-party sites (Adapty paywall library, Newswire, review blogs), so pricing_summary and pricing_source_url are blank. Those sites cite App Store listings: $3.99/week, $9.99-$19.99/month, $44.99/quarter and $59.99-$129.99/year, with a trial whose length varies by source. A developer reply on the Google Play listing mentions a base subscription and says Body Scan is an extra feature not included in it. That supports a paid model, but no free tier was confirmed. The company name 'Appex Group' comes from the Google Play listing, not the official site. The current blurb ('Optimize your workouts for fast results.') is a slogan. Be careful not to confuse this app with unrelated products such as 'FitAI', 'WorkoutAI' or a 2025 one-time-purchase 'FitnessAI' sold on makreview.com.

record.short_description: Enterprise AI agents that automate customer service, KYC verification, and accounts payable workflows
record.description: Freeday builds enterprise AI agents, which it calls digital employees, that handle whole workflows in customer service, finance, and compliance. The agents work across voice, chat, email, and WhatsApp. They can answer customer questions, take actions in CRM and other business systems, process documents and invoices, and check identities for KYC. An orchestration layer coordinates several agents and provides monitoring, human escalation, and audit trails. Freeday says deployments take about four weeks. It charges by outcome, not by seat.
record.pricing_summary: Customers pay per resolved conversation, verified document, or processed invoice, with no subscriptions or licenses. Rates are custom, based on volume and complexity, and the vendor guarantees at least 75% automation.
features: Voice, chat, email, and WhatsApp channels
record.notes: The current blurb about customer management and KYC is too narrow. Freeday sells AI agents ('digital employees') for customer service, KYC verification, and accounts payable. Sources were freeday.ai pages (home, /ai-agents, /platform, /solutions, /pricing), read through search result excerpts. Pricing is custom and outcome-based; no list prices, free tier, or free trial were found. The site also offers a free ROI calculator. No named third-party software integrations (CRM or ERP brands) were confirmed. The integrations listed are channels taken from the platform page. The site names TUI, Bitvavo, and BUX as customers. A follow-up search for integrations and company status could not be run because the search limit was reached.

record.short_description: AI document processing platform that extracts structured data from documents through an API and web portal
record.description: FormX.ai is an AI document processing platform. It pulls structured data out of documents such as receipts, invoices, bank statements, ID documents, passports and medical forms. Users send JPEG, PNG or PDF files through an Extract API or a web portal, and the extracted data comes back as JSON. The Workspace feature lets teams upload documents, manage the results and download them in batches as Excel files. Plans range from pay-per-page usage and a monthly Starter subscription to custom Enterprise deployments.
record.pricing_summary: Pay-as-you-go costs $0.30 per page with no minimum commitment, and the first 100 pages are a free trial. Starter costs $299 per month per extractor for 3,000 pages, then $0.10 per page, and Enterprise has custom pricing.
features: Workspace for uploading and managing documents
Batch download of results as Excel
Accuracy Center for bulk dataset management
Converters for PDF to CSV, XML and JSON, and image to Excel
record.notes: Confirmed on formx.ai: the homepage, pricing page, What's New page and blog, plus the help.formx.ai docs. The help docs list three plans: Pay-as-you-go, Starter and Enterprise. The 100 free pages are a trial, not an ongoing free plan, so free_tier is false and pricing_type is paid. Directory sites show older or conflicting prices ($149 Business, $10,000 Enterprise, $299 Basic), which I ignored in favor of the official pricing page. The listed operator is the FormX.ai brand. No official page I saw named a parent company. The site mentions connecting to third-party platforms but names none, so integrations is empty. The current blurb is vague and could be replaced with the short_description.

record.short_description: AI video platform that builds a professional twin to draft and post LinkedIn videos
record.description: Gemelo is an AI video platform focused on LinkedIn. It builds an AI twin of the user's face and voice in about five minutes. The twin reads material from Slack, calls and documents, then drafts LinkedIn videos. Nothing is published until the user approves it with one tap. Higher plans add comment and DM drafting, a real-time meeting agent, CRM and calendar handoff, team twins, and MCP/API access. The company also publishes a public API for video twins and voice cloning.
record.pricing_summary: The pricing page lists Starter at $29.99/month (30 approved videos), Creator at $49.99/month (100 videos), Pro at $99.99/month (300 videos) and Studio at $199.99/month (unlimited videos), plus usage credits.
features: AI twin of face and voice
Grounded on your docs and posts
Weekly or daily content proposal engine
use_cases: Posting LinkedIn video daily without recording
record.notes: The listed website charactr.com could not be checked because the search limit was reached. The official site found is gemelo.ai. Capterra names Charactr as the vendor and an AI directory refers to the product as Charactr, so Charactr looks like the earlier brand. However, no page on the official site confirms a rebrand or an acquisition. The current blurb ('Manage your social media content effectively') is too generic and inaccurate: the product is an AI video twin for LinkedIn, not a general social media manager. The pricing page has a conflict. Its visible tiers are $29.99, $49.99, $99.99 and $199.99. Its embedded structured data lists different tiers: $19, $49 and $149. The visible tiers are recorded above. The pricing page shows no free plan. A separate app at app.gemelo.app says in its page metadata that a free tier is available. Review sites list other prices, such as $59/month and Free/Enterprise, which are probably out of date and were not used. The product appears to have shifted from a general voice/video twin API to LinkedIn-focused video automation.

record.short_description: AI-native biotech company using foundation models and physics to discover small molecule medicines
record.description: Genesis Molecular AI, formerly Genesis Therapeutics, is an AI-native biotechnology company that discovers small molecule medicines, with a focus on ligand binding. It pairs AI researchers with drug hunters and builds Pearl and GEMS, an AI platform that its researchers use to run their molecular design workflows. The platform combines foundation models with physics-based methods. It powers the company's own drug programs and work with pharma partners such as Gilead and Incyte. Genesis is a drug discovery company, not a self-serve software product, and it does not publish pricing.
features: GEMS (Genesis Exploration of Molecular Space) AI platform for molecular design
Generative and predictive AI for molecule generation and optimization
Language models, diffusion models and physical simulation
use_cases: Drug discovery for difficult or data-poor protein targets
record.notes: I found the listed site live under the name 'Genesis Molecular AI'. Its homepage mentions Pearl, GEMS, and partnerships with Gilead and Incyte. Tracxn cites an Endpoints report (Oct 29, 2025) saying Genesis Therapeutics rebranded, so the directory name should probably be updated to Genesis Molecular AI. This is a rebrand, not an acquisition. No buyer is named anywhere. Genesis is a biotech that runs its own drug programs and partners with pharma companies. It is not self-serve software. I did not see a pricing page, and no pricing is published. The feature list comes from the homepage and from company descriptions in press releases (Business Wire, Gilead): GEMS combining language models, diffusion models and physical simulation, plus the wet lab in San Diego. Older press releases also name past collaborations with Genentech, Eli Lilly and NVIDIA (NVentures investment). The current blurb 'Speed up drug discovery' is too vague. I hit the search tool's limit, so I could not open a separate docs or company page.

record.short_description: AI tweet generator that helps tech influencers write tweets on ready-made topics
record.description: Graham AI, also styled Graham.ai, was an AI tool for tech influencers that generated tweets. Its own tagline offered to help users tweet like a tech influencer. Third-party listings say it came with a set of ready-to-use topics, so users could quickly post tweets on technology subjects. A startup database lists it as a seed-stage company founded in 2022 with about five employees and says it ceased to operate in Q4 2023.
record.notes: I couldn't open the official site at grahamai.co because I hit the search tool limit. The domain is confirmed only through a 2023 LinkedIn post and the IVC startup database. IVC (ivc-online.com) says Graham.ai 'Ceased to Operate Q4/2023', and the shutdown status is based on that third-party page. I found no pricing on the product's own domain. An aitoptools.com directory page mentions analytics and reach optimization, but I didn't confirm those claims, so I left them out. The current blurb, 'Optimize posts and creativity on social media,' is vague and misleading. The product was specifically an AI tweet generator for tech influencers. Before publishing, someone should check by hand whether grahamai.co still loads.

record.short_description: AI-powered career platform for resume building, cover letters, LinkedIn reviews, and interview practice
record.description: Hiration is an AI-powered career platform that helps users build and improve resumes, cover letters, and LinkedIn profiles. Its tools include a ChatGPT-powered resume builder with ATS-friendly templates, instant AI resume review, and a job-match score that compares a resume against a job description. It also offers mock interview practice. Hiration now focuses on university career services and edtech teams, which give their students and alumni free access. Individual users can also use a free resume builder plan with paid premium upgrades.
record.pricing_summary: Hiration's own blog says its free plan lets users build resumes with templates marked FREE and download them as PDFs, while premium templates and advanced features require a paid plan. A resume-writing page on hiration.com lists writing packages from $75 for students to $225 for 15+ years of experience.
use_cases: Tailoring a resume to a specific job description
University career services for students and alumni
record.notes: Hit the search tool limit before I could open the homepage or a dedicated pricing page directly. The record relies on hiration.com subpages (the blog, resume-rewrite, and terms pages), Hiration's LinkedIn page, and university career-center pages. Subscription prices ($19.99/month, $39.99/quarter, $69.99/year per TrustRadius; other directories list different numbers) appear only on third-party sites, so I left them out. The resume-writing package prices come from a hiration.com page that may be old. Hiration now presents itself mainly as a platform for university and edtech career services, priced in modules by student population. G2 lists the vendor as CMAS Systems Consultants, but I could not confirm this. The current blurb ('Optimizing your profile...') is vague and should be replaced.

record.short_description: AI customer support platform with a shared omnichannel inbox, AI assistants, live chat and help center
record.description: Hoory AI is a customer support automation platform built on conversational AI. Businesses connect messaging channels such as Messenger, Twitter, Telegram, WeChat and WhatsApp to one shared inbox. There, agents own and resolve conversations, and AI assistants handle routine requests. The platform also offers contact management, agent roles, private notes, canned responses, real-time team performance reports, a help center and multilingual support. Each plan includes a set number of AI conversation credits and charges a per-conversation fee once those credits run out.
record.pricing_summary: Personal costs $6 per user/month, Startup $16 per agent/month, Team $26 per agent/month and Business $42 per agent/month. These plans include 50, 100, 200 and 300 AI conversation credits respectively, with additional AI conversations billed at $0.40 each, and all plans come with a 14-day free trial.
use_cases: Managing customer conversations across messaging channels from one place
record.notes: I confirmed the pricing tiers on hoory.com/pricing. The pricing page says 'Start for Free' and offers a 14-day free trial on all plans, but I found no permanent free plan, and Capterra also says no free version is included. The channel list and the canned responses and reports features come from the app.hoory.com login page. I could not open the homepage directly because the search tool limit was reached, but the site is up based on the pricing and app pages. Crunchbase lists the company as Hoory Inc in Glendale, California. One third-party review site names Soft Construct LLC as the owner, but I did not verify this on Hoory's own site. The current blurb is accurate but generic, and it leaves out the AI support and omnichannel focus.

record.short_description: AI grocery list app that turns spoken requests and food photos into shared shopping lists
record.description: HoneyDo is an AI-powered grocery list app for Apple devices developed by Konstantin Gonikman. Users speak their shopping needs naturally, and the app transcribes the voice memo into an organized list that captures quantities, brands, and notes, while keeping the original recording for playback. A "Pic to Pick" feature identifies ingredients from photos of meals, recipes, or pantries. Lists can be shared and synced with partners or roommates through iCloud, and one subscription can be shared with up to five family members.
features: Original voice memos saved for playback
Pic to Pick ingredient identification from photos
Family sharing with up to 5 members
use_cases: Sharing shopping lists with a partner or roommate
Building a shopping list from a photo of a meal or recipe
record.notes: I found the official site, heyhoneydo.com, through search. It describes the voice-to-list feature, Pic to Pick, shared lists with iCloud, family sharing for up to 5 members, and says it is 'Powered by OpenAI'. It shows no prices. The listed App Store page (Apple's domain, not the product's own) names Konstantin Gonikman as the developer. It says the app is free to download with up to 5 voice memos and 3 Pic to Pick images, and that a paid auto-renewing PRO subscription unlocks unlimited use. That supports freemium, but the page gives no PRO price, and it is not on the product's domain, so pricing_summary is left empty. A directory site (TAAFT) lists 'from $12.99', but this is unverified and not used. The newest App Store version I saw was 2024.2.2 from February 2024, so the app may not be actively updated. It runs on iOS/iPadOS 16+, Apple silicon Macs and visionOS, in English and German. Don't mix this up with other apps called HoneyDo: HoneyDo App by HoneyDo LLC (household text reminders), Honeydo Tasks by Benjamin Rericha, and an older HoneyDo to-do app from High Five Labs. The current blurb is accurate but leaves out photo-based lists and list sharing. Suggested website change: use heyhoneydo.com instead of the App Store link.

record.short_description: AI company offering a conversational shopping assistant for e-commerce and a paid expert feedback platform
record.description: Glov builds AI products that help businesses engage customers and help experts earn money from what they know. Its Agentic Commerce product is an AI-powered shopping assistant that turns visitors into buyers through conversations, conversational product discovery and proactive recommendations. The homepage sends users to gengage.ai for this product. Glov also runs an Expert Feedback Platform that matches senior executives and domain experts with startups that want product validation. Experts are paid to review SaaS products.
use_cases: Converting e-commerce site visitors through intelligent conversations
Startups seeking product validation from domain experts
Experts earning money by reviewing SaaS products
record.notes: The glov.ai homepage is live, but I only saw it through search result snippets and could not open it directly. Glov now presents itself as a company with several AI products. The shopping assistant ('Agentic Commerce') points to gengage.ai, so the commerce product may have been rebranded or moved there. I could not check gengage.ai. Glov also runs an Expert Feedback Platform that pays experts $130-$2,000 to review SaaS products. That is what experts earn, not what customers pay. I found no customer pricing on glov.ai. Third-party directories (creati.ai) mention a pay-for-results model, but that is not confirmed on the official site, so I left pricing empty. Crunchbase lists 'glov (closed)', apparently an Istanbul entity. The official site does not say the product is discontinued, so I kept the status as active. The current blurb fits the commerce assistant but leaves out the expert feedback platform and the possible move to gengage.ai. The site advertises a '2.6x conversion lift'; this is the company's own claim.

record.short_description: AI headshot generator that turns uploaded photos into professional business portraits in chosen styles
record.description: Headpix is an AI headshot generator that turns ordinary photos into professional business headshots. Users pick a style and upload their photos. The service then builds a personalized AI model from those images and returns a set of high-resolution headshots. Headpix says its results are curated by professional headshot photographers so they look closer to studio portraits. It covers many industries, including media, IT, real estate, finance and consulting, and presents itself as cheaper and faster than a studio shoot.
record.notes: The official homepage at headpix.ai is live. It describes the AI headshot service and has a 'Price for Professional Headshots' section, but the search excerpt I could see stopped before any prices appeared, so I did not verify prices on the official domain. Third-party sites (unite.ai, yepic.ai, xpay.sh) list one-time plans: Starter $29 for 100 headshots, Basic $39 for 200, Premium $59 for 300. I left these out of pricing_summary under the rules. unite.ai also says there is no free plan and mentions a 14-day money-back guarantee. The company or legal entity name was not found. My search limit ran out, so I could not open the pricing anchor (headpix.ai/#pricing) on its own. The current blurb is accurate but reads like a slogan.

record.company: Hour One (acquired by Wix.com Ltd. in May 2025)
record.short_description: AI video generator that turns text scripts into presenter-led videos with lifelike AI avatars
record.description: Hour One is an AI video creation platform founded in 2019 and based in Tel Aviv. Users type a script, pick an AI avatar and voice, and the platform produces a video with a virtual human presenter. It supports many languages, dialects and voices, and it offers designed templates, brand customization, team collaboration, a screen recorder and an API. Businesses use it for training, educational and marketing videos. Wix announced in May 2025 that it had acquired Hour One.
record.pricing_summary: The official pricing page lists a $0 Free Trial for businesses with 3 minutes of video and a Lite plan at $30/mo billed monthly for 10 minutes per month; the page also says plans start at $25 per month. The Business plan starts at $112/mo billed monthly for 20 minutes per month, with 30- and 40-minute options.
features: Share via link and download without watermark
record.notes: Status is acquired because Wix's own press room (May 23, 2025) announced the acquisition of Hour One. I didn't find a page saying the hourone.ai product has been discontinued, and I couldn't confirm what the site looks like now. The pricing comes from the search-indexed copy of hourone.ai/pricing, which is about 690 days old, so prices may have changed or been removed since the acquisition. That page calls the $0 tier a 'Free Trial' with 3 minutes, so free_tier is set to false and pricing_type to paid. Third-party sites list different prices (for example $95, $235 and $29/$99/$299) and an Enterprise plan; these were not used because they don't match the official page. A Canva integration appears only on a third-party site and was left out. The current blurb, 'Create multilingual videos in a few clicks', is accurate but leaves out the AI avatar presenters that are central to the product.

record.short_description: AI recruiting platform that automates candidate engagement, screening, interviewing, and scheduling for high-volume hiring
record.description: Humanly is AI recruiting software for hourly, frontline, and high-volume hiring teams. It engages applicants across chat, voice, and video, screens candidates through structured conversations, runs AI interviews, schedules next steps, and gives recruiters ranked candidates with transcripts and reasoning. The Seattle- and San Francisco-based company was founded in 2020. It acquired Sprockets, Qualifi, and HourWork to extend the platform into sourcing, hiring, and post-hire retention.
features: AI Recruiter for 24/7 candidate engagement, screening, and scheduling
Candidate engagement across chat, voice, and video
Outreach via SMS, email, and chat
Ranked candidates with transcripts and clear reasoning
record.notes: Confirmed on the official homepage (humanly.io). A search did not turn up a pricing page on humanly.io. The only cost figures found were on third-party review sites like hirevire.com, which describe the pricing as custom and undisclosed, so pricing is left empty. Status is active because Humanly is the buyer in its acquisitions, not the company being bought. Its own blog announces the Sprockets, Qualifi, and HourWork deals, and news coverage also reports a CareerArc deal. No named integrations could be confirmed on the official domain. Search tool limits stopped me from opening a dedicated pricing or integrations page. The current blurb, 'Optimize recruitment and save time.', is accurate but vague. A better one would mention AI screening, interviewing, and scheduling for high-volume or frontline hiring.
